The core problem is that the Consensus has been examined in a fragmented manner across legal, political, diplomatic, and humanitarian dimensions. As a result, there is no comprehensive scientific framework to identify the most sustainable strategic option. Existing literature focuses on isolated issues such as legal legitimacy, human rights concerns, or the EU’s externalization policies, yet lacks an integrated, criteria-based and expert-driven assessment. To fill this gap, the study aims to determine the most appropriate future strategy, assess the relative importance of key criteria, and offer evidence-based recommendations. It introduces an innovative hybrid model combining the Siemens network, IDOCRIW, RAM, RATGOS, and BLFS—an uncommon integration in the field. The Siemens network objectively determines expert weights; BLFS reduces subjectivity by incorporating experts’ leadership tendencies; and IDOCRIW captures multidimensional information through entropy–CILOS integration. Findings show that the most influential criteria are the EU’s commitment fulfillment level (0.191) and political cost (0.117). Among strategic alternatives, updating the Consensus (5.186) emerges as the most appropriate option. These results indicate that instead of dismantling the current framework or establishing a new externalization mechanism, a revised and more balanced version of the Consensus—strengthening commitments and enhancing burden-sharing—offers a more rational and sustainable policy direction. Overall, the study contributes to the literature by providing both a novel methodological model and actionable insights for policymakers.

title: Current trends and future directions in Japanese lexical processing: a review
abstract: Japanese lexical processing is a research area that spans across the fields of linguistics, cognitive psychology, and neuroscience. Despite significant advances, there remains a lack of reviews synthesizing the diverse strands of research within this field. This review aims to map the major research themes, identify the trend topics, and outline future directions, thereby filling a gap in the literature. Employing a mixed-methods approach, this review utilizes quantitative bibliometric analysis combined with qualitative content assessment. Data were sourced from the Web of Science Core Collection, focusing on publications from 1981 to 2024. The analysis included the detailed examination of keyword frequencies, and thematic categorizations to understand the evolution of research within the field. The analysis identified several dominant themes, including “visual word processing”, “bilingualism”, and “neurological correlates”, reflecting the core and motor themes of the research. Emerging themes such as “advanced neuroimaging techniques” and “cross-linguistic influences” were recognized as pivotal areas gaining traction. The study also highlighted significant research gaps and suggested potential new directions for future research, emphasizing the need for more integrated and technologically advanced studies. This review contributes to the field of Japanese lexical processing by providing an overview of the research landscape and pinpointing areas for further investigation. It not only synthesizes the existing body of knowledge but also sets the stage for future research endeavors, advocating for an interdisciplinary approach that bridges the gap between empirical findings and practical applications. This structured synthesis aims to inspire further research that will enhance our understanding of lexical processing in the Japanese language and beyond.

title: The effect of tactical game-based physical education lessons on students’ basic psychological needs satisfaction and self-determined motivation
abstract: By creating a structured physical activity environment, physical education teachers can enhance students’ motivation to engage in and maintain a physically active lifestyle. One promising approach to achieving this is structuring physical education lessons using a Tactical Game Approach (TGA), which may influence students’ psychological needs and support self-determined motivation. This study investigates the impact of physical education classes organized around this TGA. The research utilized a pretest-posttest model with a control group from a quasi-experimental design. The study involved two classes of 8th graders selected through random assignment at a secondary school. In the experimental group, lessons were delivered using the TGA, while the control group received instruction via the direct instruction model (DIM). The experimental group consisted of 24 students (13 boys and 11 girls), and the control group also included 24 students (12 boys and 12 girls). The data were analysed using a two-way ANOVA with repeated measures. The results indicated that the experimental group demonstrated higher scores in basic psychological needs and self-determined motivation than the control group. According to the findings, the TGA appears to support students’ basic psychological needs and may enhance their motivation toward physical education lessons.

title: CEO overconfidence and corporate greenwashing: evidence from China
abstract: Abstract This study examines how CEO overconfidence influences corporate greenwashing using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023. Drawing on the fraud triangle framework, we conceptualize managerial overconfidence as a rationalization mechanism that legitimizes symbolic environmental disclosure under regulatory pressure. Greenwashing is measured as the divergence between ESG disclosure scores and independently assessed ESG performance ratings. Using an investment-based proxy and multiple alternative measures of CEO overconfidence, we find robust evidence that overconfident CEOs significantly increase greenwashing. Mechanism analyses show that this effect operates through disclosure manipulation channels: overconfident managers engage more intensively in earnings management and increase information opacity, widening the disclosure–performance gap. The effect is mitigated by financial constraints and Big Four auditor oversight, and amplified in regions with more intensive and complex environmental regulation. Results are robust to instrumental variable estimation, selection correction, and dynamic panel models. Overall, the findings demonstrate that CEO overconfidence drives strategic ESG overcommunication rather than substantive sustainability improvements, contributing to the behavioral finance and greenwashing literature.

title: When genomics meets geopolitics
abstract: International genomic collaboration is being reorganised under growing pressure from data sovereignty, geopolitical scrutiny, and demands for fairer benefit-sharing. This Comment uses BGI Group, formerly known as the Beijing Genomics Institute, as a geopolitically salient case to examine how genomic collaboration is being renegotiated around data residency, local sequencing capacity, and jurisdictional control. It does not treat BGI as a representative case, nor does it argue that genomic science has moved from openness to national closure. Rather, BGI helps make visible a broader governance challenge: how to sustain international collaboration when sensitive genomic data is increasingly tied to national laws, regional infrastructures, and expectations of local benefit. This comment argues for sovereignty-compatible interoperability: governance arrangements that allow genomic data to remain under legitimate jurisdictional control while preserving shared standards, reciprocal access, benefit-sharing, and accountable cross-border cooperation. The policy challenge is therefore not to restore an imagined model of frictionless openness, but to build trust infrastructures that combine local legitimacy with international scientific connectivity.

title: Assessing the global food security landscape for major food staples: a systematic literature review
abstract: In the current state of our world, the three cereal crops—maize, rice, and wheat—dominate the supply of food staples and inputs for animal feeds. Yet, many countries have an insufficient supply of food staples from domestic sources, whose situations seem to be worse in recent years, largely due to the continuing population growth and unexpected events that affect the world’s food trade. The challenges of ensuring global food security have thus become more critical. To better explore the relationship between food trade and food security, a systematic review—based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)—has been conducted herein. According to 105 reviewed articles, two main themes are revealed as major threats to the world’s food security: ( i ) agricultural and environmental challenges and ( ii ) geopolitical and socioeconomic issues. Moreover, as identified by the Causal Loop Diagram (CLD), international trade, agricultural innovations, and virtual water trading are the current key approaches capable of mitigating food security problems—particularly the reduction in agricultural supply. To this end, international trade and virtual water trading can provide better access to agricultural products for low-income countries, while agricultural innovations can enhance agricultural yields for the high-income ones.

title: Boosting enterprise performance: an integrated model from market orientation and organizational capability
abstract: Abstract In today’s rapidly evolving business landscape, companies must continually adapt to shifting market conditions, technological advancements, and competitive pressures to sustain growth and achieve long-term success. A dynamic environment requires strategic flexibility, innovation, and the effective utilization of organizational capabilities. Firms that fail to respond proactively to these changes risk losing their competitive advantage. This study introduces the MOOCP (market orientation • organizational capability • performance) model, examining the impact of market orientation, organizational capabilities, and the mediating roles of brand and innovation performance on the operational performance of SMEs and large firms in the Taiwanese market. A total of 219 valid responses were collected from various industries, encompassing a range of company sizes, ages, and types. Using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS and LISREL analyses, the study examines the significance of market orientation (intelligence generation, dissemination, and response) and organizational capabilities (network ties and learning capabilities) in driving brand and innovation performance, ultimately improving operational performance. All hypotheses are supported. When a company adopts a market-oriented or adaptive strategy, it must simultaneously cultivate and enhance its business network connectivity and learning capabilities. These capabilities enable the firm to internalize market-oriented strategies and translate them into effective organizational actions, thereby achieving strong brand and innovation performance within the industry and generating solid operational outcomes. The implications of socio-organizational or cross-cultural issues are also explored to deepen the understanding of the MOOCP model’s implementations. The findings underscore the importance of aligning market orientation with organizational capabilities to attain long-term competitive advantages in dynamic environments, offering both theoretical contributions and practical implications for firm managers.

title: Understanding tourist engagement with traditional dwellings through multimodal deep learning: a case study of the Gao Family Compound, Xi’an
abstract: Abstract This study applies a multimodal deep learning approach to examine tourist engagement with traditional architectural heritage. The Gao Family Compound in Xi’an serves as a representative case. Social-media texts and images from Weibo and Xiaohongshu capture on-site experiences and expressions. Texts undergo BERT-based sentiment and topic analysis. Images are classified with a fine-tuned ViT-Large model across 31 architectural and cultural classes. The combined pipeline integrates affect, semantics, and visual attention to provide a coherent view of how tourists perceive heritage spaces. Results show a predominance of positive sentiment. Tourists focus on symbolic forms and intangible practices, including performances and crafts. Cross-modal comparison indicates strong semantic alignment between salient textual keywords and ViT-based visual classes, suggesting stable patterns of attention across media. Negative posts are few and relate mainly to service and pricing, offering direct guidance for site management. The study demonstrates how multimodal deep learning supports interpretation in heritage studies. It links the tourist gaze with affective attachment in a computational setting and clarifies which features attract attention online. The approach also informs management by identifying service frictions and by highlighting elements suited to interpretation, exhibition, and digital communication. The framework provides a basis for scalable monitoring and for future work on robustness to user-generated images.

title: Unraveling spatial distribution and co-location patterns of strategic new technologies in the Yangtze River Delta: a spatial association mining approach
abstract: Strategic new technologies are central to regional economic transformation and innovation under the Fourth Industrial Revolution. Using patent data, this study examines the spatial distribution and collaborative patterns of nine categories of Strategic new technology in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) using spatial statistical analysis, co-location pattern mining, and county classification. Three findings emerge. Spatial agglomeration and structure: strategic new technology in the YRD exhibits significant spatial agglomeration and a polycentric, networked structure. Technological collaboration patterns: five recurring co-occurrence patterns are identified; collaboration is particularly pronounced for the new materials industry, high-end equipment manufacturing industry, and energy conservation and environmental protection industry. County classification: based on technology coverage and overall spatial association strength, counties are classified into four types—core technology zones, collaborative potential zones, isolated high-intensity zones, and technological island zones—showing a clear “core–periphery” hierarchy. These results clarify the spatial mechanisms of technological agglomeration and collaborative evolution within regional innovation ecosystems and inform the design of differentiated innovation policies and the allocation of regional innovation resources.

title: Humans or Generative AI? Influence of recommendation agents on tourists’ decision-making
abstract: This study investigates whether Generative AI provides more compelling travel recommendations than humans by exploring the interaction between recommendation agents (Generative AI vs. humans) and temporal distance (near vs. distant). We conducted three scenario-based between-subjects experiments ( N = 708, recruited through Credamo, an MTurk-like platform). Participants were randomly assigned to rate their responses to Generative AI- or human-generated recommendations for three scenarios (destination, hotel, and restaurant), with temporal distance adjusted for by scenario description (e.g., “travel next week” vs. “travel next year”). Our results reveal that travel-related temporal distance affects tourists’ preferences for recommendations from humans or Generative AI. Specifically, when tourists plan a near-future (vs. distant-future) journey, human recommendations (vs. Generative AI recommendations) are more persuasive. Further, this interaction effect on tourists’ decision-making is mediated by perceived message credibility and is weakened when recommendation agents make an error. Our findings offer valuable insights into enhancing tourist experiences and promoting tourism products.

title: Smartphone software updates: delaying hedonic adaptation and sustaining satisfaction
abstract: Businesses often struggle with hedonic adaptation, a phenomenon that diminishes customer satisfaction over time. Mitigating this decline is crucial for maintaining long-term satisfaction, but the underlying mechanisms, especially in technology products, remain vague. This study examines the impact of variable features (e.g., smartphone software updates) and consumption behaviors (social interaction and enduring involvement) on thwarting hedonic adaptation. We gathered data in two waves (T0 and T1) from 173 high-end smartphone users and analyzed it with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that while variable product features have no initial impact, they become a significant driver in thwarting hedonic adaptation at T1. In contrast, the influence of fixed features on long-term loyalty intentions is negligible. Additionally, users with high levels of social interaction and enduring involvement adapt more slowly. This study provides novel empirical evidence for the temporal shift in satisfaction drivers and offers a clear strategic directive for firms to focus on post-purchase software experiences to sustain customer satisfaction and foster loyalty.

title: Exploring the quality and effectiveness of AI-generated feedback in introductory programming
abstract: Abstract Feedback is a vital but often difficult part of introductory programming courses, where standard compiler messages are vague and confusing for students. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become a promising tool for providing improved feedback in programming education, yet empirical studies on its effectiveness in real educational settings are limited. Using a design-based research approach, this study examined both the quality and instructional impact of AI-generated feedback in an introductory Python programming course. Two cohorts of undergraduate students were participants. The first cohort received data-driven feedback (DDF Group, n = 28), and the second cohort, who used an upgraded automated assessment tool, received AI-generated feedback generated by the Llama 3-8B model (AIF Group, n = 32). Quality was assessed through expert ratings using a 0–5 point rubric and student perception surveys. Effectiveness was evaluated through debugging performance metrics and final exam scores. Expert evaluation of 1,490 AI-generated feedback messages revealed concerning quality issues, with a mean rating of 1.84 out of 5 and over 40% receiving the lowest possible score. Common quality issues included excessive redundant information, content exceeding students’ knowledge scope, and misleading explanations. Students reported significantly lower perceived usefulness for AI-generated feedback compared to data-driven feedback. The AIF Group also exhibited poorer debugging performance and achieved lower final programming exam scores. Contrary to expectations, AI-generated feedback was less effective than data-driven feedback in supporting student learning. This study highlights the need for rigorous design, prompt refinement, and contextual alignment when deploying GenAI tools in educational contexts.

title: Economic footprints: mapping coin circulation and economic networks in ancient Rome
abstract: Reconstructing patterns of economic exchange in ancient societies is vital to understanding state formation, monetary systems, and interregional connectivity. This study combines spatial interaction modeling, social accounting frameworks, and archeological infrastructure data with a large georeferenced dataset of Roman Republican coin hoards (155 BCE-2 CE) to analyze monetary circulation across the Roman world. We show that coin distributions followed institutional logics shaped by administrative centers, military zones, and trade hubs. Urban civic, economic, and religious infrastructures consistently predict local coin density, while spatial clustering aligns with Roman transport networks. Over time, distance decayed as a barrier to circulation, reflecting expanding infrastructure and fiscal integration. By integrating archeological evidence with spatial-economic modeling, we uncover the systemic drivers of monetary flows in antiquity. Our findings highlight how coin circulation mirrored governance, mobility, and regional interdependence, offering new insights into the economic geography of the Roman Republic and demonstrating the value of formal methods in ancient economic history.

title: Analysis of two forms of inequality: exploitation and discrimination
abstract: This article develops an integrated framework for analysing social inequality through the concepts of exploitation and discrimination. It distinguishes Inequality of outcome from inequality of opportunity arguing that exploitation is not a unitary phenomenon, as traditionally conceived in Marxist theory, but a multidimensional one. Likewise, gender, ethnic, and generational inequalities, as well as distinctions between citizens and non-citizens, are not isolated processes but can be analytically unified within the Weberian concept of discrimination. By refining these concepts and clarifying their interplay, the article provides a mechanism-oriented approach that can be applied to empirical research on contemporary forms of inequality.

title: Incorporating geopolitical interaction effects for a more comprehensive assessment of China’s border territorial functions
abstract: China possesses the world’s longest land border and one of its most intricate geopolitical environments. Previous research, however, has frequently overlooked the distinct geopolitical characteristics inherent to border areas, thereby constraining a comprehensive assessment of their functional systems, particularly concerning the effective integration of “Openness” and “Security.” This investigation amalgamates Endogenous Support Functions with Geopolitical Interaction Functions to systematically appraise the spatiotemporal dynamics, Coupling Coordination Degree (CCD), and, using the Optimal Parameters-based Geographical Detector (OPGD) model, the driving mechanisms of five-dimensional Border Territorial Functions across 45 of China’s Land Border Regions between 2005 and 2022. The findings reveal that the External Openness Function and National Security Function, which reflect Geopolitical Interaction Effects, underwent substantial growth, emerging as pivotal drivers of border functional evolution. Nevertheless, considerable variations persist in overall functional levels and amongst different regions. Whilst the CCD amongst these five functions has shown improvement, the overall level of coordination remains somewhat modest (for instance, rising significantly to 0.43 in the Southwest Border Region, yet remaining low at approximately 0.21 in the Tibet Border Region) owing to the complexities of multi-system coupling. This suggests that achieving a high degree of synergy amongst these multifaceted functions within China’s Land Border Regions continues to present a considerable challenge. In terms of driving mechanisms identified by the OPGD, natural endowments primarily mould the Ecological Protection Function and Agricultural Production Function; socio-economic factors propel the Urban Development Function and External Openness Function; whilst geopolitical and cross-border factors profoundly influence both the National Security Function and the External Openness Function. This study contends that Geopolitical Interaction Functions ought to be regarded as a critical constituent in the assessment of Border Territorial Functions, and that the synergistic development of these manifold functions is paramount for fostering stability and prosperity in China’s frontier regions. The research furnishes a novel theoretical perspective alongside empirical evidence for understanding and optimising complex border systems.

title: Silence as a spatial practice: accented epistemology and relational dwelling in Abdulrazak Gurnah’s Admiring Silence
abstract: This article examines Abdulrazak Gurnah’s Admiring Silence (1996) by reconceptualising silence as a spatial practice through which migrant subjectivity is produced and negotiated, rather than as absence or trauma. Drawing on Henri Lefebvre’s theory of the production of space and Homi Bhabha’s notion of the Third Space, and adopting an accented epistemological perspective attentive to the politics of intelligibility (Khosravi, 2024), the article challenges linear interpretations that frame the narrator’s trajectory as a movement from marginalisation to hybrid reconciliation. Instead, it contends that the novel enacts a continual reconfiguration of spatial memory across Britain and Zanzibar, demonstrating how belonging is mediated through institutional routines, domestic rituals, bureaucratic procedures, and material infrastructures. By situating key sites, including the hospital, the Willoughby household, the immigration hall, and the domestic interior, within Lefebvre’s spatial trialectics, the article shows that margins are not pre-existing territories but are produced through everyday spatial ordering. Through the interaction of spatial practice, representations of space, and representational spaces, silence circulates across institutional, ideological, and lived dimensions of dwelling, thereby destabilising the coherence of national and racial legibility. Silence is articulated as an accented mode of enunciation that interrupts demands for transparency and exposes the epistemic conditions under which racial and national identities become intelligible. Within this framework, the Third Space is conceptualised not as a final refuge but as the ongoing condition of relational dwelling, a negotiated terrain in which identity remains provisional and spatial memory is continually reworked. Rather than presenting hybridity as a resolution, Admiring Silence frames dwelling as a practice, an ongoing engagement with entangled geographies of empire and nation-state. Through its poetics of silence, the novel reimagines diasporic subjectivity as sustained negotiation across unstable spatial formations rather than as synthesis.

title: Transportation mechanism of spatial distribution of express outlets: taking prefecture-level and above cities in China as an example
abstract: Abstract Based on data of 607,511 express delivery outlets obtained through the data crawling function of the Amap platform, this study constructs an evaluation model for transportation superiority from three dimensions: transportation network density, transportation hub influence, and location advantage. A coupling coordination model is employed to analyze the spatial coordination relationship between the spatial distribution of express delivery outlets and transportation superiority. Furthermore, a geographical detector analysis is applied to reveal the influence mechanisms and intrinsic relationships between various transportation factors and the spatial layout of express delivery outlets. The findings indicate that: (1) The number of express delivery outlets in China is vast, with extensive coverage but an unbalanced spatial distribution, showing a distinct pattern of being “denser in the east and sparser in the west.” (2) The spatial distribution of transportation superiority varies significantly, exhibiting a “core-semi-periphery” structure that diminishes outward from Central and East China. (3) There is a significant positive correlation between the spatial distribution of express delivery outlets and transportation superiority, generally characterized by a coupling coordination relationship, albeit predominantly a weak one. (4) The transportation mechanisms underlying the spatial layout of express delivery outlets manifest distinct features across regions corresponding to the three levels of coupling coordination, weak coupling coordination, and non-coupling coordination, namely: “hierarchical progression and mutual support,” “limited synergy with local conflicts,” and “negative interaction and coordination imbalance,” respectively.

title: Operationalising the people-centred approach in small-town heritage governance: mechanism making in Uchiko, Japan
abstract: Under conditions of fragmented authority, demographic decline, and limited institutional capacity, how can the People-Centred Approach (PCA) become operationally embedded in local heritage governance? This article addresses this question through a longitudinal case study of Uchiko Town in Japan, a nationally designated Traditional Buildings Preservation District. Drawing on a Critical Realist research design, the study conceptualises mechanism-making as the locally constructed configuration of institutional arrangements, relational networks, and capacity-building processes through which PCA principles are translated into durable governance practices. Empirically, the analysis combines archival materials, long-term participant observation (2017–2024), and 32 semi-structured interviews. Through iterative coding and retroductive reasoning, the study identifies three generative mechanisms underpinning PCA embedding: enabling-rule formation , through which local actors reinterpret policy instruments to create participatory governance conditions; relational brokerage , which stabilises collaboration across governmental, community, and intermediary actors; and situated capacity formation , whereby individual skills and affective people–place relations are transformed into collective action capabilities. The article contributes a mechanism-based explanatory framework that clarifies how participatory heritage discourse becomes embedded in everyday governance practices. By integrating Critical Realist mechanism analysis with PCA scholarship, the study also identifies the contextual conditions under which such governance arrangements are likely to emerge and remain sustainable in small-town settings.

title: Asymmetric impact of governance determinants and health expenditure on health outcomes in E7 countries: an empirical simulation using MMQR techniques
abstract: Despite substantial investments in health, many emerging economies continue to face challenges in achieving desired health outcomes, highlighting the need to understand how health expenditure interacts with governance quality. The present study investigates the asymmetric impacts of health expenditure and governance on health outcomes in the key E7 economies, Brazil, China, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Russia, and Turkey, over the period 2000–2023. Using Method of Moments Quantile Regression and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), the analysis examines the effects of current and government health expenditure alongside governance indicators on progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 3, which focuses on health and well-being. The findings reveal that public and private health spending positively influence health outcomes, particularly when issues of marginal efficiency at high-performance levels are considered. Governance indicators, especially regulatory quality and government effectiveness, strengthen the impact of health expenditure, whereas the role of voice and accountability is more ambiguous and often indirect. These results underscore that institutional quality is crucial for translating health investments into sustainable improvements. Overall, the study provides evidence-based insights for policymakers, emphasizing the importance of aligning governance reforms and health financing with national capacities and priorities.

title: A tale of two ‘contexts’: ideological differences in the translations of UN political speeches by human interpreters and by ChatGPT4o
abstract: This study interrogates the ideological disparities between ChatGPT4o and human interpreters in rendering Chinese political speeches delivered at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) from 2008 to 2023. Drawing on van Dijk’s socio-cognitive Context Model, it examines how ‘context’ is operationalised regarding (1) role-relation engagement through deictic pronouns, (2) the modulation of agency via modal verbs, and (3) the treatment of culturally embedded metaphors, which carry significant ideological implications. With corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis and qualitative interpretation, the study illuminates that human interpreters, informed by sociopolitical cognisance and cognitive adaptability, actively mediate discourse to align with the speakers’ ideological positioning through discursive amplification. Conversely, ChatGPT4o, limited by its token-based algorithmic architecture, tends toward literal translations in parallel with its diluting key ideological markers. These divergences underscore the epistemologically grounded differences between human cognition and algorithmic processing, pointing to the sensitivity of human interpreters in ideologically laden contexts alongside the opacity of large language models.

title: Causes of baby abandonment and associated factors: a descriptive study
abstract: Abstract Objective Newborn abandonment is a significant public health issue with both ethical and societal implications. Various socioeconomic factors contribute to the incidence of infant abandonment. The mortality rate is particularly high among infants not left in a safe environment. Many countries have developed various abandonment mechanisms to ensure the safety of abandoned newborns. Study Design: Retrospective, comparative study Setting: Tertiary referral hospital Materials and methodology: This study included 30 newborns abandoned by their families as the case group, and 24 newborns born around the same time who were not abandoned as the control group. The sociodemographic characteristics of the families and clinical data of the newborns were evaluated retrospectively. Results The rates of cigarette, alcohol, and substance use among the mothers and fathers of abandoned infants were significantly higher than those in the control group. In addition, the unemployment rate among fathers was higher in the case group. Prematurity and the need for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission were more common among abandoned infants. The rate of parents living together was significantly lower in the case group compared to the control group. According to risk analysis, parental separation was identified as the strongest risk factor, increasing the likelihood of newborn abandonment by 184.6 times. Conclusion These findings are important for identifying at-risk populations for newborn abandonment and for developing targeted preventive social and healthcare policies. The study aims to contribute to the formulation of effective strategies to prevent newborn abandonment.

title: Parental socioeconomic status modifies the association of traumatic experiences with depressive symptoms among Chinese children and adolescents
abstract: Depressive symptoms and traumatic experiences are major public health concerns among children and adolescents. While exposure to trauma and low parental socioeconomic status (SES) are established independent risk factors for depression, their interactive associations remain less well understood. This study examined whether the association between different types of trauma and depressive symptoms varied according to parental SES in a large sample of Chinese children and adolescents. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 2081 students from 12 purposively selected primary, junior, and senior middle schools in Wuhan, China, using a cluster sampling method. Depressive symptoms were assessed with the Children’s Depression Inventory. Data on recent traumatic experiences and parental SES (based on education and occupation) were collected. Additive interaction analysis was used to evaluate the additive interaction between SES and trauma. Clinically significant depressive symptoms were identified in 28.2% of participants, and 39.2% reported at least one traumatic experience in the past six months. Both low SES and trauma exposure were independently associated with depressive symptoms. Moreover, low SES demonstrated significant positive additive interaction with exposure to any trauma (relative excess risk due to interaction [ RERI ] = 3.35, P < 0.001), physical abuse ( RERI = 13.24, P = 0.020), emotional abuse ( RERI = 4.00, P < 0.001), and school victimization ( RERI = 10.65, P = 0.012). These findings suggest that the associations of specific traumas—particularly physical abuse, emotional abuse, and school victimization—with depressive symptoms were stronger among children and adolescents with low parental SES. Children and adolescents experiencing both socioeconomic disadvantage and trauma exposure may represent a subgroup with a higher burden of depressive symptoms and may warrant prioritization in prevention and support efforts.

title: Assessing Financial Performance Disparities in the Vietnam Logistics Sector Amidst COVID-19: A Hybrid MCDM Evaluation Approach Using MEREC-COBRA
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic exposed weaknesses in global supply chains, causing a 5.2% decline in global GDP and a sharp drop in merchandise trade. However, as borders reopened, global dynamics gradually recovered. The pandemic prompted strategic changes, creating opportunities for sustainable recovery. However, logistics companies faced challenges in measuring performance due to traditional methods not reflecting the complexity of modern operations. The lack of effective data integration and management hindered the adoption of digital technology. This study proposes a combined MEREC-COBRA method to assess the performance of 17 logistics companies in Vietnam, using 17 financial criteria, including liquidity ratio, financial leverage ratio, activity ratio, profitability ratio, and growth ratio. The MEREC-COBRA model is compared with methods such as TOPSIS, CODAS, and MARCOS, using Kendall's tau-b and Spearman's rho tests to evaluate the impact of the pandemic. The results show that the MEREC-COBRA model provides stable ratings, with profitability accounting for 35.48% in assessing financial performance. The study reveals the varied impact of the pandemic, with companies such as 3PL-06 showing significant performance improvements, while others maintained stability. These results indicate that while the pandemic had a strong impact, companies with adaptability and strategic flexibility recovered more effectively. This research introduces an advanced MCDM approach for evaluating financial performance in the logistics sector, providing both academic and practical value. It also offers the potential for broader application beyond logistics to other industries and regions.

title: The dynamics of international food trade: patterns of inequality and inequity from 1965 to 2020
abstract: By facilitating the redistribution of food resources, international food trade underpins the achievement of food security across nations. Although the trade’s impact has been widely studied, its inequality and inequity in supporting food security are often overlooked, as existing research frequently assumes a level playing field. In this study, we introduce a comprehensive index of the international food trade’s contribution to food security (CITFE) to analyze inequality and inequity in the international food trade’s role in supporting food security (IIFE) over the past 55 years, specifically for countries or regions with food production and demand gaps (PDGs). Our findings are as follows: First, from 1965 to 2020, the average CITFE values reveal notable disparities among food types, with soybean exhibiting the highest average value (0.0903), followed by rice (0.0760), maize (0.0669), and wheat (0.0448). Geographically, regions with high CITFE values are predominantly clustered in Europe. Second, there is significant inequality in the international food trade’s role in ensuring food security. While this inequality has decreased over time for rice, wheat, and maize, it has increased for soybean, indicating shifting patterns of trade reliance and production. Third, we identify pronounced inequity in the international food trade for low-income countries or regions, especially those in Latin America, Africa, South Asia, and Oceania. For these low-income regions, trends in trade inequity over time are strongly dependent on comparison benchmarks. Compared to high-income countries or regions, the inequity in food trade for low-income countries has shown a marked upward trend. However, when compared to middle-income or middle-and-above-income countries, inequity for low-income regions has been on a downward trend. These findings contribute to current discussions on the equality and equity of the international food trade and underscore the need for comprehensive strategies to enhance food trade practices and promote global food security across all income levels.

title: Income inequality and self-others risk perception bias: evidence from 49 countries
abstract: Abstract Self-other risk perception bias refers to the tendency for individuals to perceive their own risks as lower than those faced by others—a cognitive bias that can significantly influence decision-making and behavior, particularly in the context of health risks. This study, based on data from 42612 participants across 49 countries, investigates whether individuals tend to underestimate their own risk while overestimating the risk to others regarding COVID-19 infection, and how this bias is shaped by macro-level factors such as national income inequality and cultural orientation (collectivism vs. individualism). The results reveal a significant self-other risk perception bias. While cultural orientation (collectivism vs. individualism) was not significantly associated with this bias, national income inequality emerged as a strong predictor. In countries with higher income inequality, individuals were more likely to exhibit stronger self-other risk perception bias. This study underscores the importance of income inequality in shaping risk perception and provides new insights into how socioeconomic factors influence individuals’ assessment of risks. These findings offer valuable implications for developing targeted and effective risk communication strategies across diverse socioeconomic contexts.

title: More to the picture than meets the eye? Governors’ popularity, voters’ polarization, and political budget cycles
abstract: The use of incentives by politicians in terms of fiscal expenditures, such as engineering a political budget cycle, depends on their popularity and on the degree of polarization of the voters. In this study, we assume that this relationship is nonlinear, using data for the US governors over 30 years. Furthermore, we show that the association between popularity, polarization, and fiscal expenditures is U-shaped. The more polarized the electoral base is, the more the popularity matters, and the connection is especially significant and positive for higher levels of popularity. The relation is more visible in election years, signaling an opportunistic as well as reelection-oriented strategic behavior, rather than a partisan one.

title: Becoming a teacher through research: inquiry-based learning and identity formation in Turkish ELT programs
abstract: This qualitative study explores how pre-service English language teachers in Türkiye experience and make sense of inquiry-based learning within the Learners-as-Researchers (LAR) framework. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with thirteen participants engaged in supervised research projects, the study investigates the influence of research engagement on their professional identity development, autonomy, reflective growth, and understanding of the theory-practice relationship. Data were analyzed thematically using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase model. Findings reveal that the research process helped participants transition from passive learners to active contributors, fostering a sense of professional agency, ownership, and long-term vision. Engagement in research also supported the development of self-regulated learning skills and prompted meaningful reflections on pedagogical beliefs. While participants expressed increased confidence and alignment with professional roles, the depth of transformation varied depending on contextual factors such as institutional support, mentorship, and opportunities for autonomy. The study underscores the value of embedding inquiry-based learning in teacher education programs to support identity construction, critical thinking, and adaptive expertise. It concludes with recommendations for strengthening reflective and inquiry-oriented pedagogies and highlights the need for sustained institutional scaffolding to maximize the transformative potential of LAR-based practices in English language teacher education.

title: Developing and applying an analytical framework for visitor centres at archaeological heritage sites: the Çatalhöyük case study
abstract: Integrating visitor centres into archaeological heritage sites requires balancing conservation integrity with contemporary design, accessibility, and sustainability. While international charters provide guiding principles, systematic evaluation methods remain underdeveloped. This study develops an AHP-informed qualitative framework operationalising conservation principles into weighted criteria, applied to Çatalhöyük Visitor Centre (2024). The framework synthesises international charters (Venice 1964; Valletta 2011) and contemporary scholarship into a three-tier hierarchy: conservation principles (0.50), interpretation and engagement (0.30), and auxiliary functions (0.20). Multi-season field research (May-September 2024) employed systematic observation, photographic documentation, and behavioural analysis. The assessment reveals that Çatalhöyük employs a contrast-neutral hybrid design that achieves exemplary Tier I compliance. (minimal intervention, reversibility) and sophisticated interpretation (Tier II), while accessibility (Tier III) and community governance remain partially addressed. The study demonstrates framework transferability across World Heritage contexts, offering a replicable methodology for heritage management, policy development, and comparative evaluation.

title: Metacognitions as a predictor of short-form video use: a psychometric and network analysis study among Chinese children and early adolescents
abstract: Abstract This study was designed to construct and validate a novel instrument, the Metacognitions about Short-form Video Use Scale (MSVUS), with the objective of evaluating children and early adolescents’ metacognitive beliefs regarding their early engagement with short video content. The study also aimed to examine these metacognitive beliefs as potential predictors of the risk of short video addiction. A total of 1802 children and early adolescents from China were enrolled in the study ( M age = 12.09). The factorial structure of the MSVUS was initially delineated using exploratory factor analysis, revealing two distinct dimensions: “Positive metacognition about short video use” and “Negative metacognition about short video use”, encompassing a total of 10 items. Subsequently, the stability and structural integrity of the scale were validated through confirmatory factor analysis. The measurement invariance of the scale was rigorously tested across various demographic groups. Correlational analyses indicated that both positive and negative metacognitions were significantly and positively correlated with the propensity for short video addiction and anxiety. Further multivariate regression analyses revealed that negative metacognitions made a significant unique contribution to the variance in short-form video addiction scores, and this contribution was stronger than that of positive metacognitions. Additionally, this study explored the network structure of the scale items from a network analytic perspective, uncovering the intricate interplay between positive and negative metacognitions. The findings of this research not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of metacognition in children and early adolescent digital media consumption but also offer empirical support for the development of targeted prevention and intervention strategies for short video addiction among children and early adolescents.

title: Why do teammates hurt me? Uncovering affective and cognitive mechanisms of intra-team toxic behavior in multiplayer online battle arena
abstract: Toxic behavior is pervasive in the multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) and poses a threat to building a civil online environment. While considerable scholarly attention has been devoted to understanding the factors that predict toxic behavior, there is a paucity of research that focuses on intra-team toxic behavior and comprehensively examines its psychological occurrence mechanism from affective and cognitive aspects. To address these gaps, the present research investigates the influence of affective empathy, character attachment, and moral disengagement on intra-team toxic behavior. Findings from a survey of 548 Chinese MOBA players indicated that the propensity to hurt teammates can be weakened by affective empathy but exacerbated by character attachment. Moreover, three mechanisms of moral disengagement mediate the relationships between affective empathy, character attachment, and intra-team toxic behavior. The research offered theoretical insights into toxic behavior and gameplay studies, while also suggesting design improvements for MOBA.

title: Site selection principles and geocomputational modeling for the imperial tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in China
abstract: The site selection and construction of the Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in China strictly adhered to Feng Shui principles, reflecting the highest funeral institution of Chinese feudal society and its cosmological and philosophical views on life and death over thousands of years. In this study, the Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties of China are examined using DEM elevation data, water network data, and remote sensing images. The Feng Shui principles of the Form School related to tomb site selection were analyzed, and a geocomputational modeling of site selection principles (GMSP) based on the Maxent model was established to quantify them. The model verified the geographical characteristics involved in the Feng Shui of the Form School. The research findings indicate that: (1) the model demonstrated strong applicability and effectively characterized the site selection principles for the Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties of China; (2) among geographical environmental factors, elevation contributed the most, followed by mountain ridge, river system and slope; (3) the model’s validity and reliability were further verified using 23 tombs of Ming Dynasty princes, with most mausoleums being located in areas with a high Feng Shui Index (FSI). This study provides a novel computational approach to quantifying and expressing Feng Shui principles in the site selection of the Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties, and contributes to a deeper understanding of the ancient Chinese cosmology of the “unity of heaven and man” and the life-and-death philosophy of “serving the dead as serving the living.” The methodological framework established here not only provides a practical tool for interpreting the site selection of ancient Chinese cities and traditional villages, but also has significant implications for the preservation and transmission of traditional Feng Shui culture.

title: Evolution of carbon emissions in China’s construction industry and its influencing factors from a spatiotemporal perspective under the background of dual carbon goals
abstract: The construction industry, a key emission sector, generates a large amount of carbon dioxide at every stage of its life cycle. As a major carbon-emitting country with accelerating urbanization and a large building stock, China finds it essential to study carbon-reduction strategies for its construction industry. This paper employs life cycle assessment (LCA) to calculate carbon emissions across four key stages: raw material extraction, onsite construction, building operation, and waste disposal. Furthermore, a social network model has been developed to analyze the spatial correlation network structure of carbon emission intensity within the construction industry. The quadratic assignment procedure (QAP) regression model is employed to examine the factors influencing this spatial network structure. The main conclusions drawn from the simulation analysis are as follows: (1) the building operation stage, characterized by the highest carbon emissions, is identified as a critical factor for carbon reduction in China’s construction industry. (2) Carbon emissions and emission intensity within the construction industry demonstrate a temporal and spatial transfer pattern, spreading from the southeastern region to the eastern and central regions and subsequently to the more remote northern areas. (3) Guangdong, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, and Henan are at the center of the spatial correlation network, whereas Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia, and Xinjiang are at the periphery of the network. (4) The factors influencing carbon emission intensity in China’s construction industry, in order of impact, are spatial correlation, differences in economic development levels, and variations in industrial structure.

title: Generative AI tool usage and perceived self-regulated learning: The mediating roles of technological self-efficacy and cognitive offloading in blended learning
abstract: This study explores the connection between generative AI tool usage and perceived self-regulated learning, focusing on the mediating roles of technological self-efficacy and cognitive offloading in blended learning environments, grounded on the adapted UTAUT2 model and self-regulated learning theory. The study also examined students’ perceptions about the opportunities and challenges associated with self-regulated learning and cognitive offloading in the context of using generative AI tool usage for academic purposes. We surveyed 861 students from STEM and social science programs using a 42-item questionnaire in blended learning courses in Pakistan, China and Finland. A mixed method approach was applied with partial least square structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with qualitative content analysis. Results indicated a positive and significant relationship between generative AI tool usage and self-regulated learning, mediated by technological self-efficacy through cognitive offloading. A finding of serial mediation demonstrates that enhanced technological self-efficacy and cognitive offloading significantly associated with self-regulated learning. The results also revealed that students perceived GenAITU positively and significantly connected with SRL and cognitive offloading but highlighted some challenges like over-reliance, cognitive overload, metacognitive laziness and potential erosion of essential academic skills. The study offers practical implications for practitioners like universities, faculty, and curriculum developers to integrate generative AI tool usage to enhance technological self-efficacy and cognitive offloading, ultimately fostering improved self-regulated learning in blended learning environments.

title: Does green entrepreneurship affect sustainable economic development? Evidence from OECD nations
abstract: This study examines the impact of green entrepreneurship on economic growth in 23 OECD countries for a period from 2005 to 2024. The study employed Linear Panel ARDL model along with Cross-Sectional Dependence (CD) test, CIPS unit root test, Hausman test and Wald Test of Asymmetric Link. CUP-FM technique was utilized for robustness check. The novelty of our study is long and short run dynamics utilizing ARDL technique by exploring the Pooled Mean Group (PMG) estimator and the Mean Group (MG) estimator along with CUP-FM technique. The findings indicate that green entrepreneurship (GE) significantly enhances long-term and short-term economic growth. A 1% increase in GE increases economic growth by 8.01% in the long run. Financial technology exhibits a significant positive impact in the long run. A 1% increase in financial technology increases economic growth by 4.95% in the long run. Renewable energy demonstrates a negative but insignificant impact on long-term growth and a significant negative impact on short-term growth. It may be due to high adjustment cost in the early stages of energy transition. The study concluded that if financial technologies are implemented, they would spur the practice of industrially sustainable industries and technological development having a positive effect on long-term economic growth. The policymakers should promote green entrepreneurship, financial technology and foreign investments to leverage long-term economic benefits while carefully managing the short-term adjustment period. Our findings are closely aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 8, 9,11 and 13.

title: Co-building hyperlocal resilience: integrating the past with the present for a sustainable future—a framework for probable contextual replication from the old city of Jodhpur
abstract: In the face of escalating climate hazards, traditional urban resilience strategies often overlook the transformative potential of Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS). This study operationalises a novel, co-productive framework that bridges this critical gap by integrating IKS into climate action and disaster risk reduction, using the historical city of Jodhpur, India, as a case study. The research moves beyond a mere functional integration of traditional wisdom by employing a decolonial and feminist epistemological lens, which repositions IKS as a legitimate methodology for knowledge production and re-frames women as agents of structural change rather than passive knowledge bearers. Through a mixed-methods approach that combines hyperlocal climate data analysis, participatory action research (PAR), and evidence-driven scientific assessments, the study systematically engages with, negotiates and co-produces knowledge by treating IKS as a living, situated and performative practice that resists simple codification. Residents from multiple municipal wards participated in mutual learning spaces that revealed the critical role of women as custodians of climate wisdom, while also highlighting the systemic impediments to their meaningful participation in formal planning processes. Scientific validation, including an architectural assessment and the co-design of a low-cost, community-owned heat-humidity monitoring device, demonstrated that traditional architectural features reduce indoor temperatures by a minimum of 3°C, thereby grounding traditional wisdom in contemporary science. Key outcomes include the co-creation of Jodhpur’s first IKS-integrated Heat Action Plan and a youth-led initiative that revitalised historical water management practices through performative arts. The study’s contribution lies in its rigorous, multi-tiered framework, which offers a probable framework for contextual replication in other urban settings by foregrounding the principles of equitable knowledge co-production and empowering community members to drive their own resilient futures.

title: Enhancing electronics education in VR: a game-based learning approach in vocational high schools
abstract: The integration of digital technologies into education has been increasingly explored for its potential to support learning effectiveness. However, students often face distractions, and standardized teaching materials may fail to stimulate interest or motivation. To address these issues, this study aims to transform traditional electronics education content into immersive VR experiences through game-based learning. We developed interactive electronic learning modules by integrating game elements into VR, co-designed with vocational high school teachers to align with curriculum requirements and student needs. The results suggest that game-based VR may support learning through immersive and engaging content, potentially capturing students’ attention and supporting concentration and perceived engagement. The experimental results indicate that students who used the VR materials achieved higher learning scores than those who used conventional materials. This study suggests that game-based VR may serve as a supportive approach for enhancing student engagement and learning outcomes in electronics education. The findings highlight the potential of VR-DGBL to support electronics education by providing more immersive and supportive learning experiences.

title: Can digital technology innovation enhance the manufacturing industrial chain resilience? An empirical study from China
abstract: Abstract Digital technology innovation (DTI) is an important strategic tool in developing China’s manufacturing industry. Few studies have, however, addressed the impact of DTI on the manufacturing industrial chain resilience. Based on panel data from 2007 to 2023, this study empirically examines the impact of DTI on manufacturing industrial chain resilience in China. Results show that (1) DTI exerts a significant promoting effect on manufacturing industrial chain resilience, a finding validated using a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. (2) The enhancing effect of DTI on manufacturing industrial chain resilience is influenced by geographical location, economic development, and the profitability of the chain. Specifically, the impact is more pronounced in the central region, in less developed economies, and in lower profitability industrial chains. (3) Market integration, collaborative agglomeration of manufacturing and modern service industries, and industrial robot application all play partial mediating roles in the impact of DTI on manufacturing industrial chain resilience. (4) Digital inclusive finance can regulate the direct effect of DTI on manufacturing industrial chain resilience, and can also regulate the path of the mediating effect. The above results suggest that the government should optimize its strategy for carrying out digital technology innovation and enhancing industrial chain resilience.

title: Purpose development among high school students in an arts context
abstract: The role of an arts context in supporting adolescents’ purpose development has received little research attention, despite the prevalence and importance of arts engagement during adolescence. Using semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 51 adolescents involved in participatory arts-based activities (painting, dancing, singing, etc.), the present study explored how these adolescent artists see their art impacting the world beyond themselves. Thematic analysis identified five key themes regarding how the adolescents aim to utilize their art for societal betterment: creating emotional connection, providing social commentary and awareness, cultural representation and diversity, challenging norms and perspectives, and inspiring activity and engagement in the arts. These findings have important implications for our understanding of arts-oriented purposes and for practitioners who seek to design environments that enable adolescent artists to produce work that shapes the broader world.

title: Representation, stereotypes and change: transgender narratives in Indian advertising
abstract: Abstract Drawing on Stuart Hall’s (2013) theory of representation and stereotyping, this study critically examines how meaning is encoded in Indian advertisements and how these portrayals reflect broader ideological negotiations around gender identity. The media landscape has undergone a notable transformation in its representation of gender identities, shifting from predominantly heteronormative portrayals to the inclusion of diverse gender narratives, particularly transgender experiences. This evolution is especially evident in advertising, where brands utilise media’s expansive reach to integrate transgender representation. While such portrayals have sparked public discourse, reactions are divided; some celebrate the enhanced visibility of transgender individuals, while others question the authenticity and underlying intentions of these depictions. Within India’s historically stratified gender framework, the evolving conceptions of gender identity signify critical redefinitions. However, these representations often remain shaped by heteronormative perspectives, which can constrain their transformative potential. This qualitative analysis of select Indian advertisements featuring transgender women, including those by Ralco Tyres, Brooke Bond, Prega News, and Pathkind Labs, deconstructs reductive narratives and interrogates the stabilisation of reductive meanings, ultimately advocating for more inclusive and authentic portrayals of transgender individuals in Indian media.

title: Social comparison and segregation reveal well-being traps
abstract: Abstract The Easterlin paradox suggests that while higher income correlates with greater subjective well-being (SWB) cross-sectionally, rising incomes over time fail to yield increased SWB. Traditional explanations, focused on social comparison and hedonic adaptation, often neglect individual variability and dynamic social structures. Using an agent-based model (ABM) that incorporates heterogeneity and social relationships, we uncover several key insights. We find that social comparison significantly hinders adaptation to economic shocks, with downward comparisons enhancing resilience and upward comparisons reducing long-term SWB while increasing instability. It also functions as a double-edged sword, amplifying long-term SWB changes during localised shocks, but buffering societal impacts when shocks are widespread. Furthermore, low-income individuals are particularly prone to low well-being traps, a vulnerability partially mitigated by segregated comparison groups. We show that social comparison’s dual nature demands context-specific policies. By mitigating upward comparison risks in localised crises and leveraging downward comparisons during widespread shocks, policymakers can enhance societal resilience while addressing systemic inequities.

title: Bio-capacity dynamics in BRICS countries: assessing the role of economic and political globalization and renewable energy through panel quantile regression
abstract: The establishment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has intensified scholarly debate on globalization’s capacity to mitigate environmental degradation by 2030. BRICS nations occupy a pivotal position in this discourse, given the complex interplay between their economic expansion, political integration, demographic pressures, and renewable energy transitions. This study examines the effects of economic globalization, political globalization, renewable energy consumption, population density, digitalization, and GDP inflows on bio-capacity across five BRICS economies over 1991–2021. The primary study model is panel quantile regression, supplemented by robust regression, which captures heterogeneous effects across the full conditional distribution of bio-capacity. Preliminary diagnostics cross-sectional dependence, second-generation unit root, and Westerlund cointegration tests confirm the appropriateness of this approach. Results reveal that economic globalization, political globalization, and renewable energy consumption significantly enhance bio-capacity, with effects most pronounced at higher quantiles, indicating that ecologically endowed economies benefit disproportionately from global integration and clean energy transitions. Conversely, population density, digitalization, and GDP growth consistently exert negative pressure on bio-capacity across all quantiles. Based on these findings, policymakers should introduce differentiated renewable energy subsidies targeting high-density regions, restructure economic growth governance to redirect transfers toward green investments, align digitalization strategies with energy-efficient and sustainable infrastructure, and leverage BRICS multilateral cooperation for environmental technology transfer and climate finance mobilization. This study contributes novel, quantile-sensitive empirical evidence on the heterogeneous determinants of bio-capacity in major emerging economies, informing more nuanced environmental governance strategies.

title: Deep learning and stock returns: neural networks combining sequential information and cross-sectional information
abstract: The rise of advanced sensors, communication networks, and storage systems has facilitated the collection of high-frequency data across various sectors, including finance, telecommunications, and the Internet of Things (IoT). High-frequency data provides a greater variety of informational dimensions, thereby improving decision-making accuracy. However, the complex temporal and cross-sectional structures inherent in high-frequency data present significant challenges for conventional predictive modeling, particularly in financial markets. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel hybrid neural network architecture that utilizes a structured, staged fusion of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) models. Unlike traditional ensemble methods that process features in parallel, our approach first extracts temporal embeddings via LSTM to preserve sequential dependencies and then integrates them with cross-sectional characteristics. We apply this LSTM-MLP hybrid model to the U.S. stock market, utilizing granular intraday transaction and quotation data from the Trade and Quote (TAQ) database to accurately estimate trading costs. Our empirical analysis demonstrates that this structure-preserving design significantly reduces signal volatility, resulting in a lower turnover ratio (43.7%) compared to Random Forest (77.5%) and XGBoost (72.2%). Consequently, the hybrid model outperforms both traditional hand-engineered strategies and state-of-the-art machine learning benchmarks in terms of out-of-sample, after-cost returns. Notably, the LSTM-MLP model achieves robust profitability while maintaining a lower turnover ratio compared to alternative approaches, highlighting its practical value in real-world trading environments. Regression diagnostics further reveal that the hybrid model captures distinctive return patterns not explained by existing models, thereby offering unique insights for portfolio management. Collectively, these findings advance the theoretical understanding of deep learning applications to high-frequency financial data and provide a robust, cost-aware decision support tool for practitioners. The proposed framework also holds promise for broader applications in other high-frequency data domains such as telecommunications and IoT.

title: Unpacking societal barriers to technology adoption: a multi-theoretical analysis of user behavior in last mile delivery applications in urban developing contexts
abstract: Abstract Last-mile delivery (LMD) applications are expanding rapidly in developing urban contexts; however, technology adoption and continued use remain uneven due to societal and geographic barriers. This study investigates how digital literacy-related capabilities and constraints impact LMD app adoption outcomes in Alexandria, with a focus on user behavior as a mediator and district-level differences as a contextual moderator. A cross-sectional survey was conducted across Alexandria’s East, Middle, and West districts ( N = 2120). The measurement and structural models were evaluated using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) in AMOS, which included confirmatory factor analysis, model fit assessment, and multi-group comparisons across districts. The results indicate that digital literacy-related constructs significantly shape user behavior toward LMD apps, which in turn influences subjective well-being and social inclusion. Indirect effects reveal both beneficial and potentially adverse pathways, highlighting the paradoxical role of digital literacy. District-level comparisons indicate meaningful geographic variation in key relationships. By integrating UTAUT and SST, this study explains LMD adoption as both a technological and socially embedded process. The findings offer implications for platform design and public policy aimed at reducing intra-city adoption inequalities and strengthening inclusive digital participation.

title: Western basin, eastern rooting: localisation of growth mindset among Chinese students from a culturally comparative perspective
abstract: Cultivating a growth mindset is an important strategy for the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development to improve the core competence of adolescents. The positive driving effect of growth mindsets lies in whether the participants’ cultural context is fully considered in the actualisation process to effectively create a growth-oriented environment. To enhance the core competence of Chinese adolescents with a growth mindset, which was proposed and developed in Western culture, it is necessary to localise the theory within Chinese culture and integrate it with China’s educational practices. In terms of connotation, “mastery through diligence”, “learning for oneself”, and “seeking from within” of traditional Chinese culture align respectively with efforts, goals, and attribution of the growth mindset. Furthermore, each connotation of a growth mindset is further sublimated by “enduring persistence”, “achieving ultimate goodness”, and “unity of knowledge and action” of Chinese educational thoughts. Given this, we propose the following approaches for cultivating Chinese adolescents’ growth mindsets: Implementing meta-cognitive strategies during the process of effort, stimulating endogenous interests in self-growth goals, and developing emotional experiences through positive attribution.

title: Dual-path mechanism of AI awareness on employee job crafting: insights from the cognitive appraisal of stress and JD-R perspective
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) adoption expands across industries, employees face growing workplace challenges and decisions. Previous studies on AI awareness and employee behavior have typically relied on single theoretical frameworks. By integrating the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model with Cognitive Appraisal Theory, this research develops a comprehensive framework explaining how AI awareness influences employee behavior. Survey data from 316 manufacturing employees operating intelligent equipment were analyzed using AMOS 24, SPSS 22, and PROCESS macro (v3.3). Results indicate AI awareness positively impacts both hindrance and challenge appraisals. These appraisals, in turn, exert distinct positive effects on different job crafting behaviors while mediating the relationship between AI awareness and such behaviors. Notably, leader support moderates the mediating roles of both appraisal types. This study offers valuable insights into AI awareness-driven behavioral changes in AI-integrated workplaces and provides actionable managerial guidance for organizations implementing AI technologies.

title: Echo platforms and partisan hashtags: mapping misinformation and thematic divides in the 2024 U.S. election
abstract: Abstract Social media platforms have a significant impact on how information is produced, consumed, and trusted online, raising pressing concerns about the diffusion of misinformation and conspiratorial content, particularly during critical democratic moments such as elections. As ideologically motivated and deplatformed users migrate from mainstream networks to less regulated alt-tech spaces, these alternative environments could increasingly operate as ideologically homogeneous echo platforms, contributing to a broader fragmentation of the online information ecosystem. Drawing on two large publicly available datasets capturing activity on Truth Social and X (formerly Twitter) in the period of the attempted assassination of Donald Trump, this study analyzes the presence of questionable content and thematic patterns based on hashtags. By constructing a bipartite user–hashtag network and applying a community detection algorithm, we identify how users group around specific hashtags and assess how thematic clusters vary in terms of informational reliability. Our findings show that Truth Social hosts a highly homogeneous discursive environment dominated by low-reliability sources and repetitive partisan messaging. Conversely, X reveals greater thematic heterogeneity and community-level fragmentation, where users’ reliability scores align more distinctly with the topics they discuss. This study adds to the growing body of literature on platform-based misinformation dynamics by highlighting information diffusion and the thematic differences between mainstream and alt-tech environments.

title: Using LLMs to identify discourse derailment as a potential cue for disinformation in social media posts
abstract: Abstract Identifying disinformation in online social media is important for addressing several risks to society. However, methods for automatically detecting possible disinformation still mostly rely on low-level lexical cues, which are increasingly outdated in a world with access to generative language models. We present a new approach to the automatic detection of disinformation based on measuring discourse ‘derailment’ – messages that try to force the topic of discourse away from one topic and onto another. While this may include both malicious and benign derailment, it could serve as an important signal for early-warning systems. In this study, we implement a system for automatic detection of discourse derailment which uses a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate expected replies and compares them to the real replies. We test this system on a set of human-annotated data to show that the system outperforms various baselines and approaches the agreement between human annotators. This suggests that LLMs can be sensitive to discourse-level information. However, we also identify evidence of several limitations, including that the automatic system relies on different cues compared to human annotators, which leads to some amount of bias. Nevertheless, our project represents a considerable step towards understanding how to use LLMs to analyse discourse and a new angle on tackling disinformation.

title: A bibliometric analysis of self-forgiveness research: trends, networks, and thematic developments
abstract: Self-forgiveness has received increasing attention in psychological research because of its relevance to guilt regulation, psychological well-being, resilience, spirituality, and mental health. However, the global development and thematic structure of self-forgiveness research have not yet been comprehensively examined through bibliometric methods. This study aimed to examine the global evolution, thematic patterns, and research focus within the self-forgiveness literature. A total of 493 articles on self-forgiveness were retrieved from the Web of Science (WoS) database and analyzed using the Bibliometrix R-package and its Biblioshiny interface.
