abstract: Since tourists' environmentally responsible behaviour (ERB) has a profound impact on the overall sustainable development of a tourism destination, this research aims to examine the underlying mechanism between resident–tourist value co-creation (RVC) and ERB of tourists based on Social Exchange Theory and Stimulus-Organism-Response theory. Data were collected from 508 tourists who have visited Xijiang Miao Village within the past 3 years. PLS-SEM was adopted to test the path model. The results revealed that: (1) RVC has a positive relationship with ERB, (2) perceived value and destination identification (DI) act as mediators in the relationship between RVC and ERB, and (3) RVC indirectly influences ERB through the sequential mediation of perceived value and DI. Considering these findings, this study made achievable suggestions for tourism operators to guarantee destination sustainable development.

title: A multimodal discourse analysis of teacher discourse practices in early childhood STEM activities
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how a kindergarten teacher in Mainland China used multimodal discourse to support children’s problem-solving during STEM activities. A qualitative case study was conducted, combining systemic functional linguistics and grounded theory to analyze interactions between the teacher and 4–5-year-old children during a science-based construction task. Four discourse modalities were identified: spoken, non-spoken, instrumental, and technological. These were used with strategies such as manipulation, comparison, and linking to realize different discourse functions across the stages. The analysis identified four instructional stages: problem identification, problem expansion and solution, problem delivery, and problem representation. At each stage, specific modality-strategy combinations supported ideational, interpersonal, or textual functions. For instance, instrumental and embodied modalities helped children manipulate materials and connect experiences, fostering conceptual understanding. In the problem representation stage, structured language and tools guided children in organizing their inquiry outcomes. Interpersonal meanings were co-constructed through encouragement and shared control of talk. The findings show that coordinated use of multiple modalities can enhance children’s engagement and learning during STEM inquiry. However, reliance on question-answer routines sometimes limited deeper reasoning. This study offers practical implications for early childhood teachers in designing effective multimodal interaction in STEM settings.

title: How does GenAI support self-regulated learning? Evidence from learners' questioning behavior analysis
abstract: Generative AI (GenAI), such as ChatGPT, provides an instant and individualized learning environment that has the potential to enhance students’ self-regulated learning (SRL) compared to traditional SRL interventions. However, the impact of GenAI on student SRL remains unclear, particularly regarding how educators can best support self-regulation in GenAI-enhanced learning environments. To address this question, this study conducted an 8-week longitudinal experiment with 30 Chinese university students, combining pre- and post-test SRL questionnaires with a systematic analysis of 786 learner-GenAI dialogs. Through rigorous coding, interactions were classified into six question types (Remember, Prompt, Analysis, Reflective, Apply, and Irrelevant), mapped to cognitive, metacognitive, and motivational SRL strategies, to analyze GenAI’s impact through question type distributions, temporal pattern evolution, and cross-group proficiency comparisons. The results indicated that GenAI was effective in promoting cognitive strategy development, and that learners demonstrated increasingly sophisticated questioning behavior. However, support for metacognition and motivational regulation was limited, and the distribution of question types indicated uneven development between cognitive and metacognitive strategies. Cross-group analysis further suggested that GenAI might inadvertently widen SRL skill disparities without targeted scaffolding. These findings underscore the need for balanced intervention strategies and adaptive support tools to optimize SRL development in GenAI environments.

title: Instructional design and strategies in flipped EFL teaching: a systematic review
abstract: Innovations in technology have increasingly shaped English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instruction, and flipped learning has emerged as a pedagogical approach in recent EFL research. This systematic review examines how instructional design models, instructional strategies, and educational technology tools have been integrated in flipped EFL contexts. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the review synthesizes 21 research articles, indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, published between 2014 and 2024. Qualitative thematic and content analysis were employed to interpret the data. While prior reviews have mainly examined general trends, effectiveness, and research methodologies in flipped EFL learning, this review addresses a gap by exploring how instructional design models and instructional strategies support the planning, delivery, and enhancement of flipped EFL instruction. The findings highlight the important role of instructional design models and instructional strategies in creating more effective, efficient, and engaging flipped EFL learning experiences. Models such as Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy and ARCS provide pedagogical scaffolding and motivational support, while systematic models such as ADDIE and ASSURE guide structured instructional planning. In addition, differentiated-layered instruction, collaborative learning, self-regulated learning, the 5E PSW model, discussion-oriented approaches, and project-based learning are reported to promote communicative activities, feedback, learner autonomy, and active participation in flipped EFL learning. The review also identifies a range of educational technology tools, from video materials to immersive technologies, that support course delivery, student engagement, collaboration, and assessment in flipped EFL teaching. The findings indicate a stronger research focus on speaking and writing skills than on reading and listening, suggesting the need for further research on receptive skills, cultural adaptation, and other multifaceted aspects of EFL learning. The review offers practical implications for EFL stakeholders and recommends future research on emerging instructional design models, instructional strategies, cross-cutting technologies, and integrative approaches to maximize flipped EFL experiences.

title: Sensory-spatial pathways to risk perception in temporary nighttime urban events: the mediating roles of lighting quality and perceived crowding
abstract: Abstract Temporary nighttime urban spaces are increasingly recognized as strategic sites for economic, social, and cultural development, yet research has predominantly focused on safety, wayfinding, and lighting quality rather than their broader spatial and sensory dynamics. Despite growing investments in nighttime economies, limited research explores how sensory and spatial configurations shape risk perception and environmental experience in temporary urban settings. This study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze how lighting quality and crowding perception interact to influence sensory experience and perceived risks across different activity types in Macau. Findings reveal that lighting quality mediates risk perception, while sensory engagement moderates the impact of crowding, challenging assumptions that density universally heightens spatial discomfort. These insights contribute to temporary urbanism and nighttime spatial adaptation research, offering guidance for urban planners and event organizers in designing safe, immersive, and economically sustainable nighttime environments.

title: Impact of heatwaves on elderly depression symptoms in the context of climate change: the moderating role of community-based care services
abstract: The intensification of climate change and global warming has increased the frequency of extreme weather events, such as heatwaves, posing significant health risks to the elderly population. This study employs data from the 2005–2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS) and meteorological station records from mainland China (1974–2019) to examine associations between heatwave exposure and depression symptoms among older adults. Heatwave events are identified using the Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) index, and multidimensional heatwave indicators, including daily heatwave magnitude, single heatwave duration, heatwave frequency, cumulative heatwave days, and a heatwave exposure index, are constructed. A fixed-effects model is employed to estimate associations for event-level and cumulative exposure. The moderating role of community-based care services and heterogeneity across demographic groups and regions are also explored. The findings reveal that cumulative heatwave exposure indicators, such as heatwave frequency and cumulative heatwave days, are more consistently associated with higher depression symptoms than event-level indicators, highlighting the cumulative and repetitive stress associated with prolonged exposure. Community-based care services are associated with smaller heatwave-related increases in depressive symptoms, but effects are threshold-sensitive: a greater number of services significantly mitigates risks at lower thresholds yet attenuates and disappears under more extreme heatwaves, when older adults rely more on direct support (e.g., Personal Care Services and Neighborhood-Relation Mediation Services) than on service diversity. Service-specific patterns further indicate that Health Education is protective mainly at lower thresholds, whereas Daily Shopping Services emerges at higher thresholds. Robustness tests confirm the significance of heatwave exposure effects across conventional heatwave thresholds, with diminished significance at very high cut-offs. Heterogeneity analysis shows that individuals aged 85 and older, cohabiting older adults, and residents of North China are more vulnerable to heatwave exposure, with higher risks of psychological distress compared to other groups. This study underscores the need for targeted interventions, including enhanced community-based care services, to reduce heatwave-related mental health risks among vulnerable elderly populations.

title: Pathways to urban sustainable development from a set-theoretic perspective: evidence from the government–market–public–technology framework
abstract: Optimizing institutional environments to enhance urban eco-efficiency (UEE) remains a critical governance challenge. Given the complexity and temporal dynamics of institutional systems, this study proposes an innovative government–market–public–technology (GMPT) framework embedded with temporal dimensions, integrating complex systems theory and new institutional economics. By combining fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), necessary condition analysis (NCA), and data envelopment analysis (DEA), we conduct a configurational analysis of institutional configurations and UEE across 279 Chinese cities in 2011 and 2020. The findings reveal that no single institutional element is necessary for high UEE. Instead, governments and markets provide robust foundational support in high-efficiency configurations, while social participation and technological innovation depend on systemic synergies. Through configurational analysis, we identify seven distinct institutional patterns. This study bridges the governance dynamics layer and empirical patterns at the phenomenal layer, offering a roadmap to resolve growth–sustainability tensions in the digital era.

title: What does ideological self-placement manifest? Structural associations with basic values and issue positions
abstract: Abstract Ideological self-placement often functions as a heuristic in public discourse to infer individuals’ deeper values and issue positions. However, research suggests that the relationship among ideological self-placement, values, and issue positions may be more nuanced and less strong than these heuristics suggest. While prior research has typically examined pairwise relationships along the left-right ideological dimension with either values or issue positions, our study aimed to go beyond pairwise associations and generate a more comprehensive understanding of ideological self-placement. Specifically, we investigated ideological self-placement (left-right, conservative-progressive), basic values, and issue positions jointly and accounted for their multidimensional structure. Using data from 1006 Dutch residents during the 2023 Dutch general election, we employed two complementary approaches to assess these relationships. Multidimensional Scaling analysis (MDS) revealed that the three constructs shared a coherent two-dimensional structure and conceptual similarities, mirroring how ideological self-placements are used in public discourse. However, correlation analyses indicated that the actual strength of these relationships was relatively weak. The contrast between the structural alignment and weak correlations adds important nuance to research on the relationships among ideological self-placement, values, and issue positions. Our findings suggest that public inferences based on ideological self-placement capture meaningful patterns, but the relationships among these constructs are more modest than public discourse might assume.

title: Spatial distribution characteristics and influencing factors of traditional villages from a multi-dimensional perspective: a case study of Shanxi, Hebei, Shandong, and Henan, China
abstract: Traditional villages are vital repositories of China’s cultural heritage and rural landscape, yet their spatial patterns and associated influencing factors remain underexplored, especially from a comprehensive, multi-factor perspective. This study investigate the interrelationships between historical, natural, and social influencing factors of 1334 national-level traditional villages across Shanxi, Hebei, Shandong, and Henan provinces using ArcGIS-based spatial analysis, GeoDetector, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), and Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR) models. Results reveal that traditional villages exhibit a highly clustered and uneven distribution, primarily aligned along a southwest–northeast axis, forming a “one ring, six cores, and multiple zones” spatial structure. Road network density and average annual temperature emerged as the most significant influencing factors, with their interaction showing the highest explanatory power (q = 0.3821). Further spatial heterogeneity analysis identifies five typological village clusters with distinct topographical and cultural characteristics. The study also overlays historical transportation routes and canal systems, revealing a strong spatial correlation with traditional village distribution, thereby highlighting the combined impacts of natural geography, socio-economic factors, and historical-cultural context. This research offers a novel multi-dimensional framework for understanding traditional village distribution and provides valuable insights for regional heritage conservation and sustainable rural planning in northern China.

title: Soft and hard sciences students’ evaluation on sense of belonging and digital attitude to promote university well-being through peer education: an exploratory study
abstract: Abstract Universities are dynamic ecosystems where sense of belonging, and students’ well-being can be challenging. In an era dominated by anxiety and isolation, how can we strengthen sense of inclusion in Academia? Based on the premise that community's health thrives on active participation and mutual support, we propose an alternative model in organizational communication where students are protagonists. At university of Palermo 32 students have been appointed from various fields to participate as peer educators within a project funded by the Italian Ministry of University and Research. Researchers conducted descriptive analyses using the University Student Belonging Scale. Results have shown that students from Soft Sciences (SS) rated an overall higher Sense of Belonging than students from Hard Sciences (HS). Researchers also conducted a social network analysis to evaluate students’ activities on Instagram. Our findings highlighted the presence of Social Sciences students as opinion leaders compared to others in building connections within the social network. It follows that SS students and HS students living in collaborative settings meanwhile displaying their corporate activities on social media platform, have built a circle of common behaviours able to foster engagement and sense of community among them.

title: Marriage-divorce dynamics in Azerbaijan, 2014–2023: a time-series study
abstract: Abstract Background.: Crude marriage rates (CMR) in Azerbaijan have declined steadily during the last decade, while divorces have risen — an inversion with profound demographic and economic consequences. Objectives.: We quantify these trends with monthly micro-data, test for structural breaks around the COVID-19 pandemic, and estimate the macro-economic determinants of divorce. Methods.: Monthly civil-registry micro-files (2014–2023) from the State Statistical Committee (SSC) were aggregated to annual series. Seasonal–trend decomposition, autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) modelling, and Chow tests were applied. Multivariate autoregressive distributed-lag (ARDL) models linked divorce to unemployment and inflation; sensitivity checks included wild-bootstrap confidence intervals and heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. Results.: Marriage rates fell at –0.34 (95 % CI –0.47, –0.22) per 1 000 pop/year, while divorce rates rose at +0.08 (+0.04, +0.11). A break in 2020 (τ = –4.27, p = .01) confirmed pandemic disruption. Children born to women in unregistered unions declined 38.7 %. Inflation and unemployment jointly explained 61 % of divorce variation (R² adj = .61). Out-of-sample forecasts predict a modest uptick in marriages by 2026 if unemployment remains below 5 %. Conclusions.: Azerbaijan’s nuptiality reversal is driven by economic stress and was exacerbated by pandemic restrictions. Digitised marriage-registration services and counter-cyclical labour measures may arrest adverse demographic momentum. Contribution.: This is the first decade-long, high-resolution time-series analysis of marriage and divorce in Azerbaijan using computational econometrics.

title: ‘Too good to eat meat’: collective narcissism as the dark side of ingroup love among vegans and vegetarians
abstract: Through a pre-registered correlational study ( N = 540, 273 vegetarians and 267 vegan), we aimed at integrating the social psychological construct of collective narcissism —the belief that the ingroup is superior, but insufficiently recognized by others—into the study of vegan/vegetarian (veg*n) identities. We investigated (a) dietary motivations associated with collective narcissism and (b) how collective narcissism was related to intergroup (attitudes towards meat-eaters, collective action and behavioral tendencies), and individual (life satisfaction) outcomes among veg*ns. Contrary to our expectations, prosocially-motivated individuals and particularly vegetarians reported higher levels of collective narcissism compared to morally-motivated individuals, and vegans. As expected, veg*n collective narcissism predicted greater hostility towards meat-eaters (more negative attitudes and behavioral tendencies), as well as greater motivation to engage in both normative and non-normative collective action, whereas a non-narcissistic ingroup positivity (i.e., ingroup satisfaction) was associated with relatively more productive outcomes such as reduced negative outgroup behavioral tendencies and reduced non-normative collective action motivation. Unlike our initial suggestion, however, both collective narcissism and ingroup satisfaction contributed positively to life satisfaction, indicating the potential of collective narcissism to function as a coping mechanism among this group. These findings extend the construct of collective narcissism to a moralized lifestyle minority group and provide a nuanced account of how different forms of ingroup positivity may shape intergroup hostility, activism, and well-being among veg*ns.

title: Developing and testing a measurement of behavioral intention towards artificial intelligence in EFL/ESL learning: taking individual differences into the equation
abstract: Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education holds significant potential, yet understanding students' behavioral intentions toward AI, particularly in relation to individual differences, remains under-explored. This study addresses this gap by developing and validating a measurement scale for Chinese university students’ behavioral intentions toward AI, incorporating individual differences through Technology Readiness and Acceptance Model (TRAM). The scale includes four individual factors—optimism, innovativeness, discomfort, and insecurity—alongside traditional TAM constructs such as perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and behavioral intention. Data were collected from 401 Chinese university students, and the scale's reliability and validity were tested using Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). Results indicate that the scale is both reliable and valid, with strong factor loadings and model fit indices. Theoretical and pedagogical implications for higher education are discussed.

title: Short-term vs. long-term stability of government attention: insights for regional industrial innovation
abstract: Abstract Changes in government attention influence the pace and trajectory of policy adjustments, thereby affecting the continuity and stability of industrial policy. Such changes are crucial for fostering industrial innovation through optimized resource allocation. However, most research has emphasized the static distribution of government attention at a specific time snapshot, lacking theoretical and empirical investigations into how the stability of government attention affects innovation. This study systematically examines the extent to which the stability of local governments’ attention to a specific industry influences and shapes variations in innovation outcomes. Using China’s information and communication technology (ICT) industry as a case, we find that the short-term stability significantly enhances both the quantity and quality of industrial innovation by stimulating R&D investment, fostering a conducive market environment, and alleviating financial constraints. Conversely, long-term stability in government attention reinforces technological path dependence, thereby exerting a negative impact on innovation quality. The findings highlight the limitations of long-term stability. While short-term stability provides governments with sufficient time to optimize innovation strategies and achieve local performance peaks, it often gives rise to a capability trap. The strong alignment between governments and their immediate environmental demands restricts their ability to explore more distant alternatives, ultimately resulting in structural rigidity and institutional failure caused by long-term stability. It is essential to incorporate potential policy disruptions and fluctuations into routine adjustment cycles. To strike a balance between short-term and long-term stability, an optimal policy adjustment horizon of approximately 5 years may provide the necessary flexibility for sustaining innovation dynamics.

title: Turkish validation of the CompACT: assessing psychological flexibility among emergency aid and disaster management students
abstract: Abstract Psychological flexibility is a central construct in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and an important protective factor for mental health, particularly among individuals expected to function effectively under high stress and uncertainty, such as those in emergency aid and disaster management. Despite its relevance for this population, no Turkish version of the Comprehensive Assessment of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Processes (CompACT) had been available. The present study aimed to perform a cross-cultural adaptation of the English version of CompACT into Turkish and to evaluate its psychometric properties in emergency aid and disaster management students. The study was conducted in two phases: translation and cross-cultural adaptation, followed by psychometric evaluation in a sample of 302 students. Data were analyzed using SPSS v.21 and AMOS v.22 through exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, reliability analyses, test-retest analysis, and correlational validity testing. The exploratory factor analysis (EFA) showed that the CompACT consisted of three factors (Openness to Experience, Behavioral Awareness, and Valued Action) explaining 75.848% of the total variance, comprising 20 items. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) showed that the three-factor model provided the best fit to the data ( χ ²/df = 2.590, CFI = 0.963, TLI = 0.956, RMSEA = 0.073). The scale demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency (overall alpha = 0.843) and temporal stability (test-retest r > 0.70 across all subscales), and its expected negative associations with the Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-II ( r = −0.365) and the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 ( r = −0.403) supported its criterion-related validity.

title: Leading digital change in vocational institutions: the relationship between principals’ digital leadership and teachers’ digital competence
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies is reshaping educational practices and raising expectations for digital leadership in educational institutions. Although digital leadership and digital competence have been widely studied, evidence regarding their relationship in China’s higher vocational education sector remains limited. Grounded in ISTE∙EL (2024) and the DigCompEdu framework (2017), this cross-sectional study examines principals’ digital leadership practices, teachers’ digital competence, and their association in public higher vocational and technical colleges (HVTCs) in Sichuan Province, China. Data were collected through an online questionnaire adapted to the Chinese context. Using proportional stratified random sampling, 411 teachers were selected from a population of 12,250 across 21 HVTCs. After data screening, 349 valid responses were analyzed using SPSS 27.0 and Smart PLS 4.0. Results indicate high perceived levels of both principals’ digital leadership and teachers’ digital competence. Principals’ digital leadership was also found to be significantly and positively associated with teachers’ digital competence. Given the cross-sectional and self-reported nature of the data, the findings should be interpreted as evidence of association rather than causal effect. This study contributes context-specific evidence on digital leadership and teacher competence in vocational education and offers practical implications for leadership development, professional learning, and policy initiatives aimed at supporting sustainable digital transformation in vocational education.

title: Facilitation or inhibition? The impact of IPR protection on the quality of corporate green innovation
abstract: High-quality green innovation is a key driver in promoting sustainable development and accelerating the green transformation of economic structures. Using the National Intellectual Property Model City program as a quasi-natural experiment, this paper examines the impact of intellectual property rights protection on the quality of green innovation by employing a staggered difference-in-differences approach and leveraging data from China’s A-share listed firms spanning the years 2010 to 2023. We find that the National Intellectual Property Model City program tends to contribute to high-quality green innovation, demonstrating a gradually strengthening dynamic effect. The program shows to enhance the quality of corporate green patents through green investment driving effect, innovation environment enabling effect and resource integration synergistic effect, according to mechanism analysis. Our findings contribute valuable perspectives on how the protection of intellectual property rights can foster the trajectory of high-quality green innovation in emerging economies.

title: Newspaper discourse on translation in China: a study of topics and trends in the People’s Daily (1949–2023)
abstract: Newspapers serve as a major platform for both reflecting and shaping public opinion on a wide range of topics, including translation. Yet how translation as a general phenomenon is positioned, discussed, and represented in this medium has received little scholarly attention. This study examines newspaper discourse on translation as a distinctive form of discourse, drawing on a corpus of 1240 texts retrieved from the People’s Daily (1949–2023), the official newspaper of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party. As an authoritative publication, the People’s Daily represents institutionalized public discourse, and the findings are interpreted accordingly. To investigate the major topics and general trends in this discourse over a 75-year period, the study integrates word association analysis, co-occurrence network analysis, and corpus-assisted discourse analysis into a unified analytical framework. The study identifies period-specific topics in three periods: e.g. construction of the translation field in Period I (1949–1978), official organization in Period II (1979–2000), and cultural translation in Period III (2001–2023). On the basis of topic distribution, three overarching trends are identified: continuity in literary translation and publishing, a shift from infrastructure building to institutional and professional diversification, and a growing emphasis on cultural diplomacy and ideological outreach. This study contributes to translation studies, discourse studies, and media studies by illuminating the relationships between translation, discourse, and society in the Chinese public sphere, and offers methodological implications for the research into newspaper discourse on translation.

title: Vocational peer support for people with serious mental illness: a scoping review on mechanisms, structures, lived experience and perceived impacts
abstract: Abstract People with serious mental illness face multiple barriers to (re-)entering the workforce, including early exclusion from the labor market, stigmatization, mental health instability, and fragmented support systems. Peer support, understood as social, emotional, and practical support provided by people with lived experience of mental illness, has emerged as a promising approach to enhancing psychosocial resources and promoting recovery, yet its specific role in vocational contexts remains under-researched. This review examines peer support as part of vocational rehabilitation services, where peers support others in their vocational reintegration. This scoping review systematically examines existing empirical evidence on vocational peer support for people with serious mental illness, focusing on user perspectives regarding structural conditions, mechanisms of action, and perceived outcomes. Five databases were used for the search (PubMed, PsycArticles, PsycInfo, Web of Science, and CINAHL). Eleven empirical studies (qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods) were analyzed following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s framework was used to identify key patterns. Three thematic clusters emerged: (1) conceptualizations and structural embedding of vocational peer support, ranging from less to highly structured interventions; (2) organizational, and relational conditions of implementation, including role clarity and professionalization; and (3) user-reported effects, such as enhanced agency, stigma reduction, and vocational orientation. Peer support was experienced as emotionally empowering and socially validating, its sustainable impact on employment remains mixed and context-dependent and appears to be challenged by systemic barriers and institutional fragmentation. Peer support can complement traditional vocational services by fostering hope, identity reconstruction, and practical engagement. Sustainable effects, however, depend on its institutional embedding, role integration, and continuity across service transitions. Further research should clarify the mechanisms and contextual conditions that enable effective vocational outcomes.

title: Evolution of mental health information-seeking behavior: a longitudinal text mining analysis from the pre-pandemic to the COVID-19 endemic era
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the longitudinal evolution of healthcare consumers’ information-seeking behavior regarding mental health issues, specifically depression, across the pre-pandemic (2018), peak-pandemic (2022), and post-pandemic endemic (2025) eras. Utilizing a large-scale dataset from South Korea’s major search portals, we employed advanced text mining techniques, including word frequency, TF-IDF, and Bigram analysis, to identify shifting consumer interests and evolving psychological needs. The results reveal that while “Depression” and “Treatment” remained primary concerns throughout the entire pandemic cycle, a notable strategic shift emerged in the 2025 endemic era. Consumers increasingly transitioned from general information searching toward actively seeking professional clinical interventions, as evidenced by a surge in keywords such as “Counseling” and “Hospital,” alongside a heightened focus on adolescent-specific mental health symptoms. Furthermore, concerns regarding postpartum depression persisted as a consistent priority across all analyzed periods. These findings underscore the enduring psychological impacts of COVID-19 and highlight a critical shift in consumer demand toward formal mental health infrastructure. By identifying emerging needs for vulnerable populations like adolescents and postpartum women, this research provides empirical evidence for developing targeted public health policies and specialized community-based services in the post-pandemic landscape.

title: Breaking the cycle: longitudinal analysis of impulsivity and antisocial behavior in athletes—exploring gender-invariant mechanisms and intervention potentials
abstract: Background The relation between impulsivity and antisocial behavior are central themes in sport-related research with potential theoretical links, yet surprisingly there has been no longitudinal work on this topic. This three-wave longitudinal study aimed to explore the reciprocal relations between impulsivity and antisocial behavior in basketball, football, track and field, and table tennis ( n = 338) athletes. To better reflect the process of trait stability over time, this study employed random intercept cross-lagged modeling (RI-CLPM) to account for within-person variability. Results from the RI-CLPM indicated that impulsivity significantly predicted antisocial behavior over time (e.g., β = 0.283, p < 0.01), with the model demonstrating a good fit (χ² = 25.12, df = 9, CFI = 0.990, RMSEA = 0.073). The reciprocal effect of antisocial behavior on impulsivity was also observed, though it weakened over time. This indicates that athletes, both male and female, who struggle to control their impulsivity show increased antisocial behavior. Interventions designed to increase the effectiveness of impulse control may therefore decrease such behavior. Crucially, individual differences were found to play an important role in the stability of impulsive and antisocial behavior, with implications for interventions tailored to violent sport contexts, given both the situational conditions that are most likely to change from one interaction to another as well as dispositional characteristics, particularly among male athletes. The findings suggest that interventions targeting impulse control—such as emotion regulation training or cognitive-behavioral strategies—may help reduce antisocial behavior and promote sportsmanship in both male and female athletes. In conclusion, the longitudinal nature of this study shows that impulsivity and antisocial behavior have complex interactions over time in a sample of adult athletes, whose behavioral tendencies may reflect traits commonly associated with early-life self-regulation difficulties. These relationships should be investigated further, with a potential focus on specific moderating factors such as situational and interpersonal dynamics within sports teams that may shape the interplay of impulsivity with antisocial behavior.

title: The metaphors of wajh (face) in the Saudi media discourse: a corpus-based analysis
abstract: The reference to body parts in language is rooted in our mental cognitive system and driven by life experiences, which affect the way we perceive the world. This suggests that body parts are productive resources for expressing meanings and accomplishing discourse functions. This study aims to explore the metaphorical use of the human body part “face” in Saudi media discourse from the perspective of Conceptual Metaphor Theory (CMT). Based on corpus techniques, this study analyzed 761 concordance lines of the word wajh (face), selected from the Timestamped Arabic corpus. The results reported several metaphorical patterns; the top six of which are: WAY, CONFRONTING, APPEARANCE, SURFACE, FRONT SIDE, and PRESERVING DIGNITY, showing variations in their quantitative distributions and their cognitive mappings. Furthermore, this research demonstrated how the conceptualization of “face” in Saudi media is linked with cultural, social, and political contexts and contributes to the wider context of CMT by validating and refining the universal and culturally specific aspects of the figurative uses of “face” manifested in real discourse.

title: The impact of digital rural construction on nighttime economic vitality
abstract: As a key engine driving the high-quality development of agriculture and rural areas, digital rural construction plays a pivotal role in the structural extension of the nighttime economy from urban to rural areas. This study systematically examines the influence mechanism between digital rural construction and the prosperity of the nighttime economy by constructing a two-way fixed effects model, a threshold regression model, and a spatial Durbin model. The findings reveal the following three key insights: (1) the construction of digital rural facilities effectively drives the growth of the nighttime economy by reducing market transaction costs and fostering new consumption patterns, with this effect being particularly prominent in economically developed regions; (2) environmental quality and balanced urban–rural development exhibit nonlinear moderating effects on the enabling role of digital technologies, as when air pollution concentrations and the urban–rural income gap exceed specific thresholds, the marginal promotion effect weakens significantly; and (3) digital rural construction has a significant positive effect on the local nighttime economy, but its impact on nonlocal nighttime economies is insignificant. High-quality development of the nighttime economy can be promoted by balancing digital infrastructure, implementing differentiated environmental governance, and optimizing the urban–rural income distribution. This study provides a new theoretical perspective and research reference for rural economic prosperity in the era of the digital economy.

title: How does climate risk shock affect corporate carbon performance from the perspective of digital transformation?
abstract: Abstract The intensification of climate risk caused by global climate change presents significant challenges to corporate sustainability, necessitating urgent attention to climate resilience as a critical strategic priority. Based on resource dependence theory and dynamic capability theory, this study examines the impact of climate risk on corporate carbon performance. The panel data from Chinese A-share listed companies from 2011 to 2023 are used for empirical analysis. The findings reveal that: (1) Climate risk exerts a significant negative impact on corporate carbon performance, which remains robust after a battery of robustness tests; (2) Green innovation and corporate reputation play potential mediating roles in the relationship between climate risk and carbon performance; (3) Digital transformation has a significant negative moderating effect on the relationship between climate risk and carbon performance; (4) The effect is more pronounced in enterprises located in China’s western regions, heavily polluting industries and those with weaker cost and risk transfer capabilities. This study contributes to the existing literature on climate risk and its economic consequences, providing theoretical support and practical guidance for corporate risk management and environmental policy formulation.

title: Spatial response and interactive relationship of land space conflict to urbanization in rapidly urbanizing regions: an empirical study of Jiangsu Province
abstract: Urban expansion, as a key spatial manifestation of rapid urbanization, often triggers competition among production, living, and ecological spaces and thereby intensifies land space conflict. However, how conflict dynamics respond to urban expansion over time, and how multi-dimensional urbanization drivers shape conflict intensity, remain insufficiently clarified. This study develops an integrated analytical framework with two complementary modules: (i) a spatial-response module that evaluates how changes in land space conflict respond to urban expansion across grid units and their city-level aggregation, and (ii) an urbanization-driven module that examines how urbanization subsystems and their interactions drive conflict intensity at the city level. Taking Jiangsu Province as a rapidly urbanizing case, we analyze the period 2000–2020. Results show that land space conflict intensity (LSCI) increased continuously, whereas urban expansion intensity (UEI) and changes in LSCI (LSCIc) followed an inverted U-shaped temporal trajectory. LSCIc is positively associated with UEI, with an observable lag effect, and high-response areas shift across periods. Factor interactions among urbanization subsystems enhance the driving effect on LSCI. Based on response and driving patterns, cities are categorized into development types and corresponding spatial governance recommendations are proposed to support land-space optimization and high-quality urbanization.

title: Evolutionary game study on green finance promoting low-carbon production in manufacturing enterprises under the industrial internet platform
abstract: Industrial Internet platforms are emerging as a key driver of digital transformation and low-carbon transition in manufacturing by integrating next-generation digital technologies with industrial production. At the same time, green finance has become an important policy instrument for supporting industrial decarbonization. However, how digital empowerment and green finance jointly shape manufacturing enterprises’ low-carbon production decisions remains insufficiently understood. Here, we develop a three-party evolutionary game model involving industrial Internet platforms, platform-affiliated manufacturing enterprises, and banks based on digital empowerment theory, sustainable development theory, and evolutionary game theory. Dynamic simulations are conducted to investigate the strategic interactions and evolutionary dynamics among these stakeholders under different scenarios. We find that the initial strategic choices of all participants influence the evolutionary trajectories and equilibrium outcomes of the system. For industrial Internet platforms, the cost of providing digital empowerment services, the digital empowerment cost coefficient, and the basic empowerment cost substantially shape manufacturing enterprises’ willingness to adopt low-carbon production. On the financial side, banks’ net returns from green credit, green lending interest rates, and the additional revenue generated through green credit further strengthen enterprises’ incentives to pursue low-carbon production strategies. These results demonstrate that effective digital empowerment and well-designed green financial incentives reinforce one another in facilitating the low-carbon transformation of manufacturing enterprises. Our findings highlight the importance of accelerating the development and diffusion of industrial Internet platforms while improving the design of green financial mechanisms to promote sustainable manufacturing. The study also provides new insights into the micro-level interaction mechanisms among digital platforms, manufacturing enterprises, and financial institutions, offering theoretical support and practical guidance for optimizing green finance policies and advancing high-quality, low-carbon industrial development.

title: Color usage patterns in book cover design from a complex-network perspective
abstract: Abstract Color is a fundamental element of visual design, shaping perception, cognition, and emotional response, and plays a crucial role in communicating cultural and genre-specific meanings. Here, we conduct a large-scale quantitative study of 32,614 book covers to examine how colors are systematically selected and combined in contemporary book cover design. By integrating statistical profiling, complex-network analysis, and generative simulation, we reveal both the structural organization and distributional regularities underlying color usage. Our analysis shows that most book covers employ between 5 and 8 distinct colors, reflecting a constrained yet non-random palette structure. Modeling colors as nodes in a weighted co-occurrence network uncovers four functional groups—foundation, core, bridge, and accent—corresponding to distinct structural roles in palette composition. Beyond individual frequencies, we find that the probability distribution of color-pair co-occurrence follows an exponential long-tailed decay, indicating the coexistence of a small number of conventional color combinations with a large diversity of rare and distinctive pairings. A generative simulation successfully reproduces this decay, suggesting that such scaling behavior emerges from constrained palette selection rather than statistical artifacts. Together, these findings reveal a latent ``design grammar'' governing book cover palettes, highlight parallels between visual culture and universal patterns observed in complex natural and social systems, and offer practical implications for publishing practice and AI-assisted design, where stability supports recognition while rare combinations enable aesthetic innovation.

title: Youth migration crisis of the 21st century: a comprehensive moderated mediation analysis
abstract: The 21st century has witnessed a profound youth migration crisis, particularly in developing countries, where brain drain disrupts all sectors of society. This study examines the factors influencing youth migration, focusing on the mediating role of political factors and the moderating role of COVID-19, using a moderated mediation analysis. The study employed a quantitative approach, a cross-sectional design, and gathered data from 600 participants using convenience and snowball sampling. The analysis, conducted using SmartPLS software, revealed significant positive correlations between educational, economic, social, and political factors and youth migration. The results indicated that political factors mediate the relationships between these socioeconomic factors and youth migration. Furthermore, COVID-19 was found to moderate the indirect pathways through political factors, rather than directly moderating the relationships. The model explained approximately 31.7% of the variance in youth migration. These findings underscore the complex interplay between socioeconomic, educational, and political factors in shaping youth migration, particularly in the context of global crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. The study offers valuable insights for policymakers aiming to mitigate brain drain by addressing the root causes of youth migration.

title: Decoding birth intervals for educational attainment in sibling sequences: evidence from nationally representative surveys in China
abstract: Leveraging data from three nationally representative surveys in China ( N = 99,352), we investigate how birth intervals shape educational attainment. Utilizing a family fixed-effect model to minimize confounding factors, our findings illuminate a distinctive pattern: the birth interval preceding the index person correlates with enhanced educational attainment; the impact of the preceding birth interval is more pronounced for families with more than three children; but surprisingly, the birth interval following the index person shows no substantive impact on educational attainment. These robust results, supported by various validation methods and controls, not only contribute to the broader discourse on birth intervals but also offer empirical insights crucial for informed family planning decisions in China.

title: Mundane patient and public participation in healthcare is more important than we tend to think
abstract: Abstract This article is about mundane participation by patients and the public in healthcare. I use this term to refer to their daily, nonstrategic, and free-flowing practices that at first glance may not seem participatory and yet can make crucial contributions to the functioning of healthcare. To discern how mundane participation can contribute to healthcare, I conceptualize its operation using the notion of network and fluid relations. This notion presents healthcare as a combination of (1) network relations , that is, fixed and explicit connections between elements, such as diagnoses, protocols, medical specialists, and insurance reimbursements, and (2) fluid relations , that is, temporary, tentative, and experimental linkages that allow for adjusting fixed arrangements to fit diverse health needs and improvising temporary solutions to healthcare problems. Drawing on the notion of network and fluid relations, I suggest that mundane participatory practices are directed at developing and experimenting with fluid relations and, thus, can instill flexibility into the operation of healthcare, allow for adaptations to specific circumstances, and promote open-ended learning. I propose that the ability of mundane participatory practices to produce these benefits makes them valuable and complementary to organized participation—explicit, clearly directed participatory activities with more structure, design, and boundaries—that have received more attention in practice and scholarship to date. Current efforts to improve patient and public participation in healthcare tend to overlook mundane participatory practices. This is problematic because such practices can help make our increasingly bureaucratized and technologically complex health systems work—and work well—amid uncertainties and pressures. By theorizing how mundane participation contributes to healthcare, this article provides a platform for advocating for a shift in how patient and public participation in healthcare is acknowledged and supported.

title: When play becomes labour in the gig economy: career entry motivations of Chinese esports game companions
abstract: Abstract In today’s digital era, the boundaries between play and labor are being continuously reshaped, as platform-mediated work appeals to young people with the promise that play can pay. While the concept of playbour has long captured the blurred line between play and work, it has predominantly been conceptualized as informal and precarious. This study argues that playbour has entered a new stage of formal institutionalization through the convergence of the gig economy and state-led occupational recognition. Taking esports game companionship in China as a case, this research examines this form of gig-based playbour in which workers are paid to accompany their clients through online gameplay. This article employs the push-pull framework with a sequential exploratory mixed-methods design: qualitative interviews with 18 companions, followed by a survey of 686 respondents to examine motivations for entering this institutionalized form of work. The findings reveal a dual structure comprising three push factors (limited employment opportunities, financial pressure, and few monetizable skills) and three pull factors (passion and enjoyment, spatiotemporal flexibility, and higher earnings), with significant demographic variations. This study makes three contributions: first, it extends playbour theory by conceptualizing its transition from informal and precarious practices to formal institutionalized work; second, it applies the push-pull framework and a mixed-methods approach to an emerging digital occupation, offering a more comprehensive explanation of entry motivations; and third, it reveals how young people’s career choices reflect a tension-laden compromise between aspiration and structural constraint, with practical implications for youth employment policy.

title: Impact of carbon market trading prices on corporate green innovation
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the impact of carbon market prices on corporate market competition and green technological innovation in high-carbon industries in China. We develop a game-theoretic model to analyze the effects of carbon emission restrictions on enterprises and their market competition, measured by the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Using data from A-share listed companies in eight major regional carbon markets from 2013 to 2021, the results indicate that rising carbon prices intensify market competition by promoting substantive green technological innovation, which reduces firms’ reliance on carbon emission quotas and enhances their competitive advantage. Furthermore, we identify a threshold effect where corporate innovation capabilities significantly influence the relationship between carbon prices and market competition. Enterprises with higher innovation capabilities respond more effectively to carbon pricing, increasing their investment in green innovation. Heterogeneity tests reveal that the impact of carbon pricing is more pronounced in state-owned enterprises and firms with lower environmental responsibility scores. These findings provide valuable insights into the mechanisms of carbon market policies and their role in fostering green economic transitions. The main contributions of this research include the development of a novel game-theoretic model to examine the mechanism driving these dynamics and the identification of a threshold effect of carbon pricing, providing valuable insights into the role of carbon market policies in promoting a green economic transition.

title: The obstacles and changes in Sino-European trade routes in the twenty-first century due to climate change and geopolitical risks
abstract: In the 21st century, global climate change and geopolitical risks are interconnected, presenting new challenges and influencing the trade dynamics between China and Europe. This paper investigates the effects of climate change and geopolitical risks on the trade route between China and Europe using bibliometric analysis and review. It seeks to identify potential trends in this trade path for the 21st century. Research indicates that, influenced by climate change and geopolitical factors, trade routes between China and Europe are transitioning from traditional single trade channels to multiple trade channels, such as the joint Arctic Northeast Passage and the China-Europe Railway Express. This process generates opportunities, including enhanced efficiency and stability in Sino-Europe trade, due to the development of new trade channels. However, it introduces difficulties, including unpredictability in climate change forecasts and weaknesses arising from geopolitical tensions. This compels China and Europe to take proactive measures. The melting of Arctic sea ice presents new commercial opportunities related to climate change. Consequently, the observed variations in navigable durations and ecological sensitivity have led China and Europe to implement proactive adaptation strategies. This includes collaborative ice monitoring networks and standardized green ship technology, designed to mitigate the effects of environmental risks on supply chains. Geopolitical factors, including trade frictions and regional conflicts, have led to heightened insurance costs and disruptions at critical nodes. This scenario has caused a structural transformation within the trade system across three key areas: trade demand, logistics architecture, and trade distribution. In response, China and Europe have created strategic backup channels and enhanced multilateral mechanisms along with regional cooperation. This paper highlights the necessity of quantifying the mechanisms by which climate change and geopolitical risks influence the trajectory of China-EU trade, aiming to address blind spots in decision-making throughout the transition process. This framework facilitates the prediction of future trends in China-EU trade, considering the influence of these dual drivers. The goal is to address uncertainty, describe the trade pattern’s response, and assess and optimize the response measures of Sino-EU countries, ultimately fostering the sustainable development of Sino-EU trade.

title: Muddled governance and politics in climate change adaptation in ‘Left Behind Places’: Evidence from Gwanda and Lupane Districts, Zimbabwe
abstract: Abstract Global and national adaptation discourses often celebrate policies, funding targets, and institutional frameworks. But what happens when these narratives collide with everyday life in rural ‘Left Behind Places’? Here, adaptation is not just about glossy project reports, it is about elders reviving seed-sharing networks, women organising water rotas, and communities demanding inclusion in decisions that affect their survival. This paper peels back the layers of policy rhetoric to reveal the governance failures, political exclusions, and grassroots innovations shaping climate adaptation in places too often ignored. The paper critically examines the governance and political dynamics shaping climate change adaptation in Gwanda and Lupane - two rural districts emblematic of ‘Left Behind Places’ in Zimbabwe’s political economy. Drawing on qualitative data from key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, and policy analysis, the study reveals how adaptation efforts are constrained by politicised resource distribution, elite capture, and top-down decision-making processes. Despite the presence of formal climate policies and NGO interventions, local communities remain excluded from governance structures, with participation often reduced to symbolic performance. Yet, amid this institutional neglect, communities engage in grassroots adaptation through traditional knowledge, informal innovation, and social collaboration, what this paper conceptualises as climate citizenship from below. The findings call for a repoliticisation of adaptation governance in Zimbabwe, grounded in inclusion, transparency, and local agency. In advancing these arguments, the paper contributes to critical climate governance scholarship in Africa and offers pathways toward more just, participatory, and context-sensitive adaptation frameworks.

title: Exploring factors affecting student attitudes towards school science: a case study of ninth-grade students in a Swedish school
abstract: Abstract This study explores ninth-grade students’ attitudes toward school science in one Swedish lower secondary school, focusing on the factors shaping their interest and engagement. Using a convergent mixed-methods case study design, 63 students completed the Relevance of Science Education (ROSES) questionnaire, and 30 of these students also wrote argumentative texts taking a stance on whether school science is interesting or boring. The ROSES questionnaire is part of an international research programme that examines how young people perceive the relevance of science and science education in their lives. Thematic analysis of the texts identified three central themes: perceived difficulty of school science, perceived relevance to everyday life and future aspirations, and the role of teaching practices. Survey data from selected ROSES items supported and contextualised these themes. In this sample, 55% of the students perceived school science as difficult, 54% did not find it particularly interesting, and 59% did not expect what they learn in science to be useful in their daily lives. At the same time, some students reported a strong interest when science was connected to topics such as health, exercise, or space, and when teachers used varied, interactive approaches. By integrating qualitative and quantitative evidence within a single school context, the study illustrates how perceived difficulty, relevance, and teaching practices interact in shaping students’ attitudes toward school science. The findings suggest the importance of strengthening perceived relevance, supporting students’ expectations of success, and diversifying classroom practices to foster more positive attitudes and engagement with school science.

title: Decomposing technical efficiency in European pig farming: persistent and transient inefficiency across production systems
abstract: This study examines efficiency differences between major European pig production systems. We applied a four-component stochastic frontier model to determine the levels of persistent and transient efficiency across different pig farming systems in EU countries, using unbalanced panel data. The results revealed that persistent efficiency is more relevant for Spanish, French, and Danish farms, suggesting that structural factors are comparatively more relevant in explaining efficiency performance in these production systems. Transient efficiency is the most important component for Polish farms, suggesting that short-term managerial and operational factors may play a comparatively larger role. Our empirical findings could provide important implications for pig farm management decisions and policy measures in European countries. Improving the long-term efficiency of Spanish, French, and Danish farms may require new policies driven by country-specific factors, presumably beyond farmers’ control. Polish farms could improve short-term conditions in managerial skills and farming practices to reduce the transient inefficiency of farms.

title: Enterprises’ digital transformation investment strategies and supply chain coordination under carbon cap-and-trade policy
abstract: Digital transformation (DX) is vital for supply chain performance and environmental goals, yet optimal investment strategies under carbon policies are underexplored. This study examines a two-tier supply chain (manufacturer and retailer) under a carbon cap-and-trade policy, distinguishing between the manufacturer’s production digitization and the retailer’s business digitization. We employ game-theoretic models to analyze equilibrium across unilateral, simultaneous, and centralized DX scenarios, and propose a revenue-sharing and cost-sharing (RC) contract for coordination. The results show that production digitization and business digitization yield synergistic effects, with investment levels higher during simultaneous DX than during separate DX. The proposed RC contract achieves full supply chain coordination, ensuring Pareto improvements for both firms. Environmentally, DX reduces total emissions only when production digitization investment efficiency is sufficiently high. Notably, at moderate efficiency levels, the RC contract simultaneously advances both digitization and greening goals.

title: How do World Heritage Cultural Landscapes visually attract and educate tourists? A sentiment analysis based on eye-tracking experiments
abstract: Abstract Cultural landscapes, distinguished by their diverse structures and rich visual features, offer immersive experiences that engage visitors through high visual appeal and accessibility. As core assets in Cultural Heritage Tourism, they support regional economies and cultural identity but face ongoing challenges in balancing heritage conservation with sustainable tourism. This research examines how visual elements of five UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscapes in China shape tourists’ perceptions of heritage value. Study 1 analyzed 13,212 online reviews to build an evaluation model and developed a Richter Scale questionnaire for Study 2, which involved an eye-tracking experiment and a questionnaire survey with 24 university students to identify visual behavior patterns and preferences. Results show that different landscape elements evoke distinct visual–cognitive responses that systematically influence evaluations. On one hand, complex, information-rich elements, such as artificial structures, historic sites and activities, interior decoration, and natural plants, produce longer fixations, more frequent visual searches, and repeated visits, which are generally associated with higher perceived heritage value and satisfaction. Conversely, overly long initial processing and high cognitive load correspond to lower ratings. On the other hand, element proportions also have nonlinear effects: higher proportions can accelerate attentional capture and revisits but may reduce preference and induce esthetic fatigue in certain contexts. Among the five sites, Hani Terraces and Hangzhou West Lake achieve the highest visual attraction, perceived value, and revisit intention, while Dujiangyan and Lijiang perform less well. Overall, the findings offer practical design insights, emphasizing the need to balance artificial and natural elements, simplify transport spaces and interiors, manage crowding, and enhance interpretive media to improve visual legibility and visitor experience. This study demonstrates the value of combining online comment mining, eye-tracking, and self-reported measures to support evidence-based management and the sustainable development of World Heritage destinations.

title: Transformation, creation, regeneration: from silkworm worship to goddess fantasies
abstract: In the myths, folklore, and rituals of silk in East Asia, the Silkworm Deity is often portrayed as a female figure, representing a unique expression of ecofeminism as a modern analytical lens within Chinese culture and the broader East Asian cultural context. By integrating archeological discoveries with historical texts, this article explores the cultural origins of the Silkworm Goddess and her localized variation paths in East Asia. Employing a literary anthropology framework, the analysis draws on four key types of evidence: classical literature, excavated textual materials such as oracle bones and bronze inscriptions, folklore and ethnological references, and ancient artifacts—the Quadruple Evidence Method. It delineates the cultural compilation process from the primal essence of the silkworm to the refined silk product, highlighting the central role women have played in this construction. Analysis reveals that the worship of the Silkworm Goddess extends far beyond sericulture, encompassing fundamental religious and life beliefs related to the cycles of life and death. The transition of the Silkworm Goddess from a vibrant Mother Goddess to a specialized agricultural deity responsible for silk production raises critical feminist questions about women’s agency within political and economic structures. This article addresses these issues by analyzing the premodern cosmological beliefs inherent in the worship of the Silkworm Goddess and interpreting the manifestations of patriarchal cultural intrusion in her classical legends. It further takes the silkworm beliefs in Japan and the Korean Peninsula as comparative cases to clarify the “homology and heterogeny” of the East Asian silkworm goddess culture.

title: The impact of intrinsic and extrinsic motivation on knowledge-sharing behaviour: the mediating role of knowledge-sharing intention and the moderating role of perceived psychological safety
abstract: Knowledge-sharing behaviour (KSB) is widely recognised as an important mechanism for enhancing innovation and organisational performance in knowledge-intensive environments. However, employees may hesitate to share knowledge because of perceived personal risks, competitive concerns, and workload pressures, particularly in fast-paced e-commerce settings. To better understand the motivational and cognitive mechanisms associated with KSB, this study develops an integrated framework drawing on Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey using self-reported measures from 398 operational managers from Chinese e-commerce firms using purposive sampling. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results show that both intrinsic and extrinsic motivation are positively associated with KSI. KSI is positively associated with KSB and serves as a key mechanism linking motivational factors to behaviour. The findings further indicate that reciprocal benefits have both direct and indirect effects on KSB, whereas enjoyment in helping others, sense of self-worth, and expected organisational rewards influence KSB primarily through KSI. The results also indicate that perceived psychological safety positively moderates the relationship between KSI and KSB, strengthening the translation of intention into actual KSB. This study contributes to the knowledge-sharing literature by integrating SDT and TPB to clarify the distinct roles of motivational factors, intention, and contextual conditions in the knowledge-sharing process within Chinese e-commerce contexts.

title: Value maximization through fund raising and fund retirement: evidence from globally performing private equity companies
abstract: Abstract The companies across the world achieve value maximization of their respective companies by generating profits and/or capitalization/recapitalization. The private equity fund companies achieve value maximization by investing in unlisted high growth companies and/or capitalization/recapitalization. The private equity funds like traditional companies can maximize value by capitalization and recapitalization. The private equity funds capitalize and recapitalize by raising funds and retiring funds in the form of debt as well as equity. The purpose of study was to determine whether private equity funds maximize value by capitalization and/or recapitalization. The dynamic panel data analysis involving systems generalized method of moments as well as panel data analysis were used to determine the impact on total enterprise value. The comparative analysis was due to the fact that dynamic panel data takes into consideration lagged values of dependent variable whereas there is no such case in panel data. The dynamic panel data results showed that total enterprise value was indifferent to total equity raised, debt induced, debt retired and stock buyback. The panel data results showed that total enterprise value was highly positively influenced by debt retired and stock buyback. The research implications for investors and researchers were that the lagged values of total enterprise value don’t influence the future values and private equity funds do stock buyback and induce debt to maximize value of their respective companies.

title: From movement to motor behavior: epistemology of embodied knowledge and the limits of its digital representation
abstract: This article problematises the dominant ways in which spatio-temporal movement data are interpreted and semantically enriched in the context of intangible cultural heritage. Rather than treating semantics as a secondary layer added to already recorded kinematic parameters, the paper argues for the necessity of a preceding analysis of the knowledge realized through motor cultural practices. The study seeks to clarify the epistemological status of embodied knowledge in the context of motor cultural practices as a necessary condition for any subsequent strategy of digital representation and semantic enrichment. It proposes a distinction between movement as kinematics and movement as motor behavior — understood as an embodied and socially organized form of knowledge realized in action. On this basis, semantic enrichment is reconsidered not as an annotational technique, but as a form of epistemic mediation between the measurable parameters of movement, the research paradigm, and embodied cultural knowledge in action. Finally, the paper outlines implications for digital documentation and data collection protocols aimed at representing the conditions under which motor knowledge is realized as practice without being reduced to formal categories.

title: Key drivers and mechanisms of user satisfaction with smart wearable medical products: a mixed-methods study
abstract: Smart wearable medical products are increasingly used in chronic disease management and health monitoring. However, negative user experiences and discontinuance remain common in real-world use, and the multidimensional drivers of user satisfaction (US) and their interaction mechanisms remain insufficiently explained. This study adopts a mixed-methods design integrating qualitative identification, structural equation modeling (SEM) validation, and XGBoost–SHAP explanation. It aims to identify the core dimensions of user concern regarding smart wearable medical products, reveal their pathways of influence on US, and characterize the importance and synergistic effects of key factors within an explainable framework. First, based on 5200 valid reviews from e-commerce platforms and 13 semi-structured interview transcripts, procedural grounded theory was used to identify the key factors influencing US. Second, 391 valid questionnaire responses were collected, and SEM was applied to test the relationships among latent variables, while XGBoost–SHAP was used to analyze feature importance and nonlinear interaction effects. The SEM results show that human–AI interaction experience (HAIX), medical value factor (MV), hardware design factor (HD), and quality and performance factor (QP) all have significant positive effects on US ( p < 0.01), whereas commercial marketing factor (CMM) is not significant ( p = 0.14). The SHAP results further indicate that HAIX and QP have relatively high importance and exhibit a strong synergistic interaction. These findings suggest that US with smart wearable medical products is not determined by a single product attribute, but is jointly shaped by HAIX, MV, HD, and QP. Methodologically, this study develops a mixed empirical pathway integrating qualitative identification, SEM validation, and XGBoost–SHAP explanation. Theoretically, it introduces HAIX into satisfaction research on medical wearables. Practically, it provides actionable guidance for firms to optimize interaction design, performance reliability, and the realization of medical value.

title: When information gets dense: the role of cognitive load in corporate reporting behavior
abstract: This study investigates how financial statement complexity (FSC) affects users’ cognitive load (CL) and examines the mediating role of voluntary disclosure level (VDL). CL refers to the mental effort required to process financial information. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), it distinguishes between intrinsic CL, arising from the inherent complexity of transactions and accounting standards, and extraneous CL, stemming from presentation and disclosure choices. Using path analysis on non-financial firms listed on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX 100) from 2010 to 2018, the study examines the direct, indirect, and total effects between FSC, VDL, and CL. The results show that FSC is positively associated with VDL, suggesting that managers of more complex firms provide additional voluntary information to reduce information asymmetry. At the same time, VDL is positively associated with CL, indicating that excessive or poorly structured disclosure can increase users’ cognitive effort. VDL is also found to mediate the relationship between FSC and CL, suggesting that the effect of FSC on CL operates indirectly through disclosure behavior. The findings have practical implications for regulators, standard setters, and report preparers seeking to enhance the decision-usefulness of corporate reports. This study provides early evidence from Egypt on the links among FSC, VDL, and CL, showing how disclosure design can either alleviate or exacerbate cognitive overload in financial reporting.

title: Leveraging neuroleadership and AI-integrated capabilities: empowering entrepreneurial leaders to drive SME performance
abstract: This conceptual article applies the RBV theory and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) in SMEs, intending to offer insights into entrepreneurial leadership and SME performance relationships. The research article restructures the emerging conclusions within the existing literature of entrepreneurship, leadership, neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and SMEs. It also provides an integrated new theoretical framework that consists of entrepreneurial leadership, neuroleadership, AI-integrated capabilities, and SME performance. In addition, it responds to the extant research questions on the possible connections between constructs and puts forward several connections that might develop the present organizational literature. This research article has begun the empirical investigation of small and medium enterprises’ performance with this theoretical model. Entrepreneurial leadership applies unique resources (RBV) to boost SME performance, and neuroleadership and AI-combined talents moderate this association based on perceived ease of use and usefulness (TAM) for better performance quality. This research article also fills the gap in the literature identified. To the best of the author’s knowledge, it is the first to synthesize and develop outcomes of entrepreneurship, neuroscience, and AI literature in the SME world. It also proposes a novel, integrated method to explain the entrepreneurial leadership and SME performance relationship.

title: Exploring the impact of social media on adolescent and young adult mental health
abstract: Social media platforms offer potential benefits for mental well-being by fostering social connections, enabling self-expression, and democratizing access to mental health resources. Yet, concerns have been raised regarding their association with mental health problems, particularly among young people.
