title: Research on the deconstruction of cinematic visual grammar and narrative innovation mechanisms based on feminist theory
abstract: As an important mechanism for constructing gendered power relations, cinematic visual grammar has long formed a narrative paradigm centered on the male gaze. Based on a feminist theoretical perspective, this study undertakes a comparative content analysis of 30 feminist films and 30 traditional male-centered comparison films, matched by period, region, and genre, through the construction of a “visual-narrative-gender” analytical model, aiming to reveal the gendered encoding mechanisms of visual grammar and their deconstruction pathways. The study employs a critical mixed-methods design that integrates quantitative pattern detection with qualitative discourse analysis, treating numerical indices as heuristic tools rather than substitutes for ideological interpretation, examining the gendered characteristics of visual grammar from three dimensions: shot language, editing rhythm, and color esthetics. The research findings show that: the visual power index of male characters in traditional films is significantly higher than that of female characters (0.74 vs 0.38); feminist films effectively achieve visual deconstruction through five pathways—perspective subversion, temporal reconstruction, spatial liberation, bodily writing, and intertextual weaving—reducing the power gap by 63.2%; there exists a nonlinear relationship between visual deconstruction and narrative innovation, with diminishing innovation effects when deconstruction intensity exceeds the 0.75 threshold (read descriptively, not as a normative recommendation, and not impugning radically illegible avant-garde traditions); significant differences exist in the choice of innovation pathways across different cultural backgrounds (offered as a first-order regional approximation that intersectional follow-up research will need to refine). The coding system and quantitative indicators developed in this study provide new analytical tools for feminist film research, and the findings offer important insights for film creation, education, and critical practice, providing theoretical support and practical guidance for constructing a diverse and equal cinematic expression system.

title: Benchmarking the effects of country governance on the profitability of commercial banks: a cross-country investigation
abstract: Abstract This study aims to benchmark the effect of country governance on the profitability of commercial banks, overcoming the limited scope and context of past studies. This study uses unbalanced panel data from 126 countries, sourced from the World Bank, spanning the period from 2010 to 2021. The Pooled Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS), and two-step system Generalized Methods of Moments (GMM) estimation methods are used for the relationship analysis. Quantile regression is used for a robustness check. This study demonstrates that improvements in country governance significantly reduce the profitability of commercial banks. However, the negative effects are heterogeneous, where country governance indicators exert a greater negative impact on the upper quantiles of bank profitability compared to the lower quantiles. These findings have practical implications for formulating and implementing relevant rules, regulations, and financial policies to ensure greater competitiveness and financial efficiency in the banking sector. JEL classification: E5, E58, G1, G18

title: The branding of Sichuan-Chongqing hot pot in foodscape: semiotic dissemination and translanguaging practices
abstract: Abstract As a category of spicy hot pot, Sichuan-Chongqing hot pot (SCH) is becoming increasingly popular in China and around the world. This study examines the branding of SCH restaurants in Chengdu. By analyzing linguistic, imagery, color, and material resources, we reveal how these elements reflect the historical, cultural, and sensory characteristics of hot pot through constructing specific foodscapes. Ethnographic data, including 557 photographs from two streets and consumer-targeted interviews, demonstrate that translingual (e.g. mixed Simplified/Traditional Chinese, Chinese dialects, and English) and trans-semiotic (e.g. combining colors, materials, and imagery) choreography of multi-modality evoke a sense of nostalgia, belonging, and exoticism. This study highlights the role of multimodal semiotics in food branding, providing insights into how commodified foodscapes mediate cultural narratives and market success. Moreover, we explore how such distributed resources are selectively extracted to gradually form a series of stable and repetitive repertoires about SCH in the translanguaging space, which are continuously disseminated in meme units to promote branding. The findings highlight the role of semiotic resources in food branding, providing insights into how commodified foodscapes mediate cultural and marketing discourses. Future research could further explore the impact of meme dynamics in other culinary environments based on consumers’ behaviors.

title: Unveiling the nexus between products and influential countries in the multi-layer trade network of global lithium battery
abstract: Abstract Amid the accelerating global transition to renewable energy and the surge in electric vehicle adoption, ensuring the stability of the lithium battery supply chain has become a critical priority. This study explores the complex relationships between products and influential countries within the global lithium battery supply chain through a multi-layer trade network framework. By constructing a comprehensive network model that spans upstream minerals, midstream materials, and downstream batteries, we analyze the evolving dynamics of trade and influence from 2002 to 2022. The findings emphasize the growing centrality of lithium as a critical resource, with its influence steadily rising in both supply and demand dimensions. Furthermore, trade connections in the downstream battery layer are more robust, yet increasingly dependent on a few dominant players, particularly China, the European Union, and the United States. While China’s influence as a leading producer and exporter continues to expand, yet the declining diversity in its import structure poses risks of supply disruptions. Thus, there is urgent need for countries to diversify supply channels and closely monitor policy changes in major lithium-producing nations to ensure global supply chain stability. These findings provide important insights for understanding and optimizing the stability of the global lithium battery supply chain and provide fundamental knowledge for future research on risk transmission in the lithium battery supply chain.

title: Identifying key behavioural determinants and intervention spaces in policymakers’ climate adaptation decision-making
abstract: As climate change progresses, the urgency to adapt has increased, yet current climate adaptation efforts remain insufficient. While psychological research has explored behaviour change interventions for citizens, policymakers are often overlooked. Policymakers are central to advancing adaptation efforts as they decide which policy instruments to prioritise to increase societies’ resilience to climate risks. Despite this, the existing basis for designing context-tailored behavioural interventions to improve their decision-making remains underdeveloped. In this study, we integrate a systematic scoping review of 70 studies and an expert Delphi panel to identify key behavioural determinants of policymakers’ adaptation decision-making and to prioritise target behaviours and behaviour change techniques (BCTs). We analysed the behavioural determinants and BCTs present in research on adaptation policymaking using the Theoretical Domains Framework and Behaviour Change Technique Taxonomy. Policymakers’ context, resources, and knowledge, as well as social influences, are the most frequently reported behavioural determinants. The most commonly applied techniques to improve decisions involve setting goals, making plans, and building knowledge. The Delphi panel of behavioural science experts and Dutch climate adaptation policy professionals was conducted in two rounds ( n 1 = 47, n 2 = 32) and identified seven key behaviours, which primarily occur in intermediate decision-making phases. It also prioritised BCTs, showing that making plans, setting goals, increasing knowledge, and providing social support were rated as the most implementable and acceptable intervention techniques. Contrasting our results with the peer-reviewed literature reiterates the value of integrating behavioural, policy, and systems approaches for effective, context-tailored behavioural intervention designs. Based on the results, we were able to identify promising intervention spaces for effective, implementable behavioural interventions targeting climate adaptation policymakers within the Dutch context. We provide recommendations for future research to develop and test such interventions as well as to generalise our findings in other contexts.

title: Digital vs. Traditional Bibliotherapy: Emotion Regulation in Preschoolers
abstract: Emotion regulation is a foundational skill in early childhood, shaping children’s social competence, academic performance, and psychological well-being. Bibliotherapy-using structured storytelling to support emotional development-has shown promise, yet little is known about how delivery format affects its impact. This study examines the comparative effectiveness of digital storytelling and traditional bibliotherapy in enhancing preschoolers’ emotion regulation. Using a quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test control-group design, the study involved 91 children aged 60–72 months enroled in preschools in Türkiye. The children participated in one of three conditions: digital storytelling, traditional reading, or a no-intervention control condition. Over the course of eight sessions, children in the intervention groups engaged with specially designed bibliotherapeutic stories. Emotion regulation outcomes were measured using the Emotion Regulation Scale, based on teacher and parent evaluations. Both intervention formats produced improvements relative to the control condition according to parent and teacher ratings. In the teacher ratings, although the digital storytelling group had numerically higher adjusted mean scores at post-test and follow-up, the differences between the two intervention groups were not statistically significant. This study makes a contribution by providing comparative evidence on post-intervention and follow-up outcomes of two bibliotherapy modalities, within an extended intervention timeframe. Implications for early childhood educators and policymakers include integrating both traditional and digital methods into early learning environments to support children’s emotional well-being through evidence-based, developmentally appropriate practices.

title: Evaluating the scale-dependent impact of environmental ratings on green credit using machine learning and threshold regression
abstract: Abstract This study examines the association of environmental (E) ratings and green credit allocation among Chinese commercial banks using a panel dataset from 2010 to 2021. Initial linear models unexpectedly reveal that E ratings do not show a statistically significant unconditional association with green credit balances (GCB) once bank-level heterogeneity is rigorously controlled. To unravel this, we systematically integrate machine learning methods with econometric threshold analysis. A Hansen panel threshold regression identifies a critical institutional scale threshold (total loan volume). Crucially, E ratings exhibit a positive and marginally significant association with GCB only for banks exceeding this scale, while the association remains indistinguishable from zero for smaller banks. This provides the key to interpreting the linear model results: the association between environmental performance and green credit allocation appears strictly conditional on a minimum scale. Further analysis confirms a “scale-ratio paradox”, where higher E ratings increase the absolute volume of green credit for large banks but fail to improve, and may even reduce, its portfolio share (GCR). These findings support a risk-signaling rather than a pure efficiency-enhancement narrative, underscoring the need for differentiated, scale-contingent policies.

title: Avatar-based affective narratives in Chinese role-playing games: Genshin Impact and Black Myth: Wukong
abstract: Abstract This article examines how avatar-based affective narrative generates meaning in contemporary Chinese RPGs, using Genshin Impact and Black Myth: Wukong as case studies. Existing research on RPG narrative has often focused on player choice, branching structures, decision points, and consequential feedback. Building on this choice–consequence path, the article proposes an accumulative mode of avatar-based affective narrative and explains it through a four-layer framework: avatarial entry, avatarial translation, affective narrative sedimentation, and Yijing -oriented meaning-making. Within this framework, the avatar functions as an affective narrative mediator. It anchors a possible experiential position for the player, structures avatar-character encounters as player-borne situations, and shows how affective intensity may build through repeated exposure, processual recurrence, and ego-investment. Genshin Impact organizes affective experience through a relational network centered on the Traveler , producing an extensive world shaped by return, attachment, and memory. Black Myth: Wukong organizes affective experience through trial-based exposure centered on the Destined One , producing an intensive world shaped by combat, failure, endurance, and mythic pursuit. By connecting avatar theory, affective narrative, and Yijing -oriented aesthetics, the article shows that RPG meaning can emerge from accumulated avatarial experience and take shape as a culturally resonant felt world.

title: Urban spatial structure and ecological resilience in China
abstract: Abstract As urbanization accelerates and cities continuously expand and reshape their built environments, understanding the impact of urban spatial structure on ecological resilience has become increasingly crucial for promoting sustainable urban development. Based on grid population data and ecosystem-related data from 2007 to 2019 in Chinese prefecture-level cities, this study employs ESDA spatial exploratory analysis and entropy method to measure the degree of urban spatial structure and the level of ecological resilience. On this basis, the two-way fixed effects model, instrumental variables, and other methods are used to explore the impact of urban spatial structure on ecological resilience. We find that compact spatial structure is conducive to strengthening ecological resilience within cities. In other words, urban decentralization tends to weaken internal ecological resilience, and this effect is particularly pronounced in cities in central and western China, non-resource cities, and cities with high levels of digital development and infrastructure, and low levels of green innovation. Furthermore, mechanism tests reveal that improving climate suitability and promoting industrial sustainability are the influencing mechanisms. Finally, the study suggests that, in promoting urban construction, the government should thoroughly implement the concepts of ecological diversity protection and economic coordinated development, and reasonably plan urban spatial structure based on the current state of cities to improve the quality of living environments.

title: Quantitative identification of urban functional zones driven by POI and AOI coupling
abstract: Urban functional zones are fundamental spatial units for understanding urban structure and guiding planning interventions, yet their identification in rapidly urbanizing Chinese cities faces two persistent challenges: the opacity of multi-source data fusion mechanisms and the inadequate treatment of functional hybridization. This study proposes a quantitative urban functional zone identification framework that addresses both challenges through an “externalized fusion” paradigm—making data fusion weights explicit and traceable—coupled with a classification system that explicitly incorporates mixed functional zones. Using Zhengzhou, a rapidly urbanizing national transportation hub, as the study area and OSM road networks as spatial units, we systematically evaluated random forest, SVM, and KNN classifiers, and conducted nine controlled fusion-ratio experiments (POI:AOI from 1:9 to 9:1). The results reveal three substantive findings: (1) a stable fusion ratio of POI:AOI = 3:7 achieves optimal spatial pattern stability, quantitatively demonstrating the synergistic balance between “functional signals” (POI) and “spatial substrates” (AOI); (2) mixed functional zones predominate in Zhengzhou’s urban fabric, with residential-involved mixtures accounting for 55.5% of all zones, challenging conventional single-use zoning assumptions; and (3) a clear “core-residential versus periphery-circulation” spatial differentiation pattern emerges, directly reflecting the city’s strategic positioning as a national logistics hub. Validation against EULUC_China data shows 67.6% overall consistency (90.3% for residential zones), with field verification confirming geographic credibility. This study contributes not only a replicable methodological pathway, but more importantly, empirical and theoretical insights into how macro-level urban strategies shape micro-level land-use hybridization—offering implications for evidence-based planning in data-limited contexts and advancing the application of urban spatial theories to developing-world megacities.

title: Sustainable finance as a catalyst for environmental innovation: insights from companies listed on the London Stock Exchange
abstract: Sustainable finance promotes environmentally responsible investments that support green technologies and eco-innovation. By channeling financial resources toward sustainable projects, it enhances firms’ capacity to develop innovative solutions for long-term environmental and economic resilience. However, the impact of sustainable finance on environmental innovation remains underexplored—a gap this study seeks to address. This study leveraged stakeholder theory to examine this gap. Using purposive sampling, the study identified 143 non-financial institutions with 17 years of data (2007–2023) from Refinitiv. The Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimation model was employed to address endogeneity in the analysis. The findings indicate that renewable energy investment, environmental expenditures, and green bond issuance have a positive and significant effect on environmental innovation. Conversely, emission-reduction policies were found to have a negative and significant impact. The study also revealed that firm size positively moderates the relationship between green bond issuance, environmental expenditures, and environmental innovation. Based on these findings, firms are encouraged to invest in renewable energy, green bonds, and environmental initiatives to enhance innovation. Additionally, leveraging firm size can support sustainability goals, ensure regulatory compliance, and create competitive advantages.

title: Investigating the influential factors shaping Chinese new energy vehicle purchase intentions: evidence from Bangkok, Thailand
abstract: Abstract Thailand’s transition toward low-carbon mobility and pursuit of carbon neutrality have accelerated the adoption of new energy vehicles (NEVs), particularly those manufactured by Chinese companies. This study examines the factors influencing Thai consumers’ purchase intention toward Chinese-brand NEVs in a real market setting. Specifically, this research examines how perceived price value, performance expectancy, and environmental performance influence consumer attitudes and purchase intention. A cross-sectional quantitative design was adopted, and data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered at the 45th Bangkok International Motor Show and 27 automotive 4S dealerships across Bangkok, yielding 400 valid responses. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to evaluate the measurement and structural models. The findings show that perceived price value, performance expectancy, and environmental performance have significant positive effects on attitudes toward Chinese-brand NEVs, and that attitude serves as a strong predictor of purchase intention. The model explains 77.3% of the variance in attitude and 80.6% of the variance in purchase intention, indicating strong explanatory power. The findings suggest that competitive pricing, reliable performance, and clear communication of environmental benefits are essential to strengthening local acceptance of Chinese-brand NEVs. Moreover, they highlight the importance of structural support, particularly government incentives and adequate charging infrastructure, in fostering consumer adoption. These results offer practical insights for automakers seeking to expand market presence and for policymakers promoting the transition to cleaner transportation systems.

title: Integrating long-term bird observation data with landscape connectivity for conservation network: a case study of the Yangtze River Delta, China
abstract: The accelerated expansion of high-density urban agglomerations driven by global urbanization poses a severe threat to avian migratory networks. Focusing on the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) region of China as a representative case, this study integrated 116,102 time-series bird observation records collected over 15 years with multi-source remote sensing data, and coupled them with a three-dimensional landscape resistance model. This approach revealed the mechanisms by which urbanization degrades bird habitats and migratory routes, and further simulated optimized multi-level conservation network scenarios. The results indicated that: (1) Between 2010 and 2019, urban expansion in the YRD led to a drastic 61.39% reduction in highly suitable habitats for birds, exhibiting a cliff-like decline; although partial recovery occurred during 2020–2024, the net loss over the entire 15-year period remained substantial. (2) Vertical barriers intensified ecological corridor fragmentation, with current density within high-rise zones decreasing by up to 89%, reducing the total number of ecological corridors from 556 to 459 and causing a 35.3% decline in patch connectivity. (3) The existing protected area system neglects the vertical requirements of migratory birds, as a 211% increase in the number of buildings taller than 50 m around protected areas compelled birds to fly at considerably higher altitudes. (4) Simulations of three scenarios (status quo maintenance, bird habitat conservation, and urban expansion balance) showed that the collaborative conservation framework, which includes reinforcing the core habitats, rebuilding resilient corridors, and supplementing urban ecological functions, was more effective. By transcending the limitations of traditional two-dimensional analyses, this study leveraged dynamic data to uncover cumulative thresholds of habitat degradation and the compensatory potential of semi-natural habitats, thereby providing theoretical insights for constructing avian ecological networks in highly urbanized regions worldwide.

title: Silent voices, visible patterns: leveraging partial social interaction graph for vaccination stance detection
abstract: Vaccine hesitancy remains a major challenge for pandemic response, and understanding public stances toward vaccination is an important prerequisite for designing effective countermeasures. Existing social-media approaches mainly infer stance from users’ posts, which limits their applicability when many users do not publish vaccination-related textual content and when directly observable stance labels of some users are underused. In this work, we formulate vaccination stance detection as node classification on a partial directed social interaction graph, where edges encode observable interactions and only a subset of users have known stances. We propose GNN-SD, a graph neural network that separately models incoming and outgoing interactions and explicitly incorporates partial known user stances during inference. To benchmark this task, we construct C-VS, the first large-scale labeled social interaction graph for vaccination stance analysis on Twitter. Results show that, using only social interactions and a limited fraction of known user stances, GNN-SD consistently outperforms representative baselines and can identify a substantial proportion of anti-vaccination users without using any users’ vaccination-related textual content. Our research underscores a practical way to identify people with vaccine hesitancy, facilitating public health stakeholders to make more targeted interventions for enhancing vaccine uptake.

title: Governance through intelligence: how smart cities enhance new quality productive forces
abstract: Although digitalization has progressed rapidly, there is still a limited empirical understanding of how smart governance contributes to the evolution of new quality productive forces (NQPF) in developing countries. This study exploits the implementation of the smart city initiative as a policy shock and draws on panel data from Chinese cities spanning 2007 to 2019. The results indicate that smart city development is associated with a statistically significant increase in the growth of NQPF. Moreover, the estimated effects are stronger for new labor tools and new labor objects than for new labor force. Specifically, smart city initiatives facilitate greater governmental digital subsidy support for strategic emerging industries, significantly increasing both the breadth and depth of digital subsidies they receive. Additionally, smart city policies improve the local digital development environment while attracting digital enterprises and talent, fostering spatial agglomeration. Moreover, the influence of smart city development on strengthening NQPF varies according to a city’s degree of innovation capacity and the extent of focus it receives from both governmental agencies and the public. Notably, the policy-driven promotion of NQPF through smart city initiatives is more substantial in large urban centers, non-resource-based cities, and municipalities that do not belong to the category of old industrial bases.

title: China’s diet urgently needs to establish a sustainable evaluation system to address critical challenges
abstract: Assessing the diet’s sustainability is critical to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals. Dietary patterns have shifted from plant-based to animal-based, elevating health risks, intensifying environmental burdens, and necessitating systematic assessment and scientific responses. Current research on dietary sustainability is largely confined to national-level analyses, with few regional or provincial spatiotemporal studies. The study developed a tripartite framework integrating health, economic, and environmental indicators and applied it to 37 years of longitudinal data (1987–2023) to assess dietary sustainability at national, nine agricultural regions, and provincial scales. Nationally, the comprehensive sustainability of diets initially rose, then declined. While health and economic indicators improved, persistent environmental degradation emerged as the primary constraint. Across all nine agricultural regions, comprehensive sustainability increased, driven by gains in health and economic dimensions, despite universal declines in environmental sustainability. Provincial analysis revealed a shift in comprehensive sustainability from predominantly moderate—with some strong areas—to primarily strong, with scattered moderate areas. Notably, Tibet was the only province to register a decline. Health sustainability transitioned from a predominantly moderate pattern, marked by localized strengths and weaknesses, to an East‑West gradient, with higher levels in the East. Economic sustainability improved across all provinces, rising from weak‑to‑moderate levels to a very strong status. For environmental sustainability, all provinces except Gansu, Guizhou, Ningxia, and Shanxi showed a declining trend, with eastern regions of China experiencing pronounced deterioration. This spatial pattern shifted from a predominantly moderate baseline—encompassing both strong and weak areas—to one in which eastern sustainability falls below that in the west. Results revealed a structural contradiction from the imbalanced environmental, health, and economic dimensions’ synergies. Moving forward, coordinating the balanced development of environmental and other dimensions and reshaping the multidimensional balanced development path of the dietary system is essential.

title: Social anxiety, loneliness, and learning difficulties in primary school students: examining the roles of loneliness and AI usage frequency
abstract: This study examined the association between social anxiety and learning difficulties among primary school students, with a focus on the mediating role of loneliness and the moderating role of artificial intelligence (AI) usage frequency. A total of 800 students in Grades 1 to 6 were surveyed using the Social Anxiety Scale for Children, the Children’s Learning Adaptability Questionnaire, the Children’s Loneliness Scale, and the AI Usage Questionnaire. After data screening, 597 valid responses were retained. Mediation and moderation analyses were conducted using the PROCESS macro. The results showed that social anxiety was positively associated with learning difficulties, and loneliness partially mediated this relationship. However, AI usage frequency did not significantly moderate the association between social anxiety and learning difficulties. Its hypothesized moderating effect on weakness symptoms, defined as fatigue-related, distractibility-related, and somatic or functional strain symptoms, was also not supported. These findings suggest that social anxiety is associated with primary school students’ learning difficulties both directly and indirectly through loneliness. The results highlight the importance of emotional and interpersonal factors in understanding learning difficulties, while suggesting that AI usage frequency alone may be insufficient to buffer the negative associations between social anxiety and learning-related outcomes.

title: Chinese-language instructor support, psychological resources, and perceived AI chatbot engagement in Mandarin learning motivation among international students in China
abstract: The Chinese language has unique tonal phonology and script characteristics that pose specific problems for international students learning Mandarin, and the ways in which human and AI support can complement each other to activate students’ learning motivation are not well understood. Building on control-value theory (CVT), this study constructs models of the effects of Chinese-language instructor support on Mandarin learning motivation and of the mediating role in the process, which are then verified and strengthened through chatbot immersion in Mandarin. Based on CVT, this study constructs models of the effect of Chinese-language instructor support on Mandarin learning motivation and the role of the mediator in this process, and then verifies and strengthens these models through chatbot immersion in Mandarin. Survey responses were obtained from 406 degree-seeking students in four regional university hubs (Xi’an, Wuhan, Nanjing, and Hangzhou) and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The measurement model revealed good convergent, discriminant, and reliability. Instructors’ support had a direct effect on motivation ( β = 0.263) and an indirect effect through learning buoyancy ( β = 0.043) and self-concept ( β = 0.108), both mediations being significant. Each indirect path had a positive moderating effect of chatbot immersion, which strengthened the paths. The full model accounted for 34% of the variance in learning motivation. Results not only extend CVT to a logographic SLA setting but also demonstrate the complementary nature of human scaffolding and AI practice, providing practical recommendations for teacher training, resilience training, and technology integration in Chinese universities.

title: How does rural entrepreneurial dynamism promote common prosperity for farmers and rural areas in China?
abstract: Enhancing farmers’ incomes and narrowing income disparities are essential prerequisites for achieving common prosperity. Drawing on panel data for 1564 Chinese counties from 2015 to 2023, this study incorporates farmers’ income, the urban–rural income gap, and intra-rural income inequality into a unified analytical framework. The article simultaneously studies the results of income growth and income distribution, and explores from both theoretical and empirical perspectives how rural entrepreneurship affects farmers’ well-being and promotes the common prosperity of rural China. The results yield three key findings. First, rural entrepreneurship significantly increases farmers’ incomes and reduces both the urban-rural income gap and income inequality among farmers. These effects remain robust after addressing potential endogeneity and performing a series of robustness checks. Second, rural entrepreneurship promotes income growth and advances common prosperity by facilitating adjustments in agricultural cropping structures, expanding employment opportunities for farmers, strengthening the rural collective economy, and enhancing local innovation capacity. Third, the income-enhancing effects of rural entrepreneurship are stronger in southern regions, in areas characterized by distinctive agricultural specialization, and in regions with higher levels of rural digitalization. However, these effects may be constrained by elite capture and the digital divide. Overall, the findings indicate that fostering high-quality rural entrepreneurship and supporting the endogenous growth of farmers’ incomes are critical for advancing common prosperity in rural areas.

title: Longitudinal dyadic associations between body mass index and depressive symptoms among Chinese older couples
abstract: Obesity and depression are becoming widespread conditions among older adults. Existing studies have examined the relationship between individuals’ body mass index (BMI) and depressive symptoms, yet the findings remain quite controversial. This study aimed to examine the dyadic associations between BMI and depressive symptoms among Chinese older couples. The analytic sample consisted of 1,710 older married couples aged 60 and older from three waves (2011, 2013, and 2015) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. BMI was defined as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared, and depressive symptoms were measured using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale. Data were analyzed using the Longitudinal Actor–Partner Interdependence Model with autoregressive and cross-lagged paths in Mplus. The results showed that individuals’ earlier BMI and depressive symptoms were positively associated with their subsequent BMI and depressive symptoms across the three waves. For actor effects, husbands’ earlier BMI was negatively associated with their later depressive symptoms, whereas the reverse association was not significant. Partner effects were also found, with one’s earlier BMI being negatively associated with his/her spouse’s subsequent depressive symptoms, one’s earlier depressive symptoms being positively associated with his/her spouse’s subsequent depressive symptoms, and wives’ earlier BMI being positively associated with their husbands’ subsequent BMI. Our findings suggest a unidirectional association from BMI to depressive symptoms and highlight the complexity of dyadic associations between BMI and depressive symptoms in Chinese older couples. Couple-based interventions and programs should be taken to improve older adults’ physical and mental health conditions.

title: Studying the diachronic development of chromaticism and dissonance in Western music over three centuries
abstract: Abstract The historical narrative of increasing chromaticism and dissonance in Western music, while widely accepted, has predominantly relied on traditional close-reading analyses of individual works rather than comprehensive empirical validation. This study presents a computational analysis of a large-scale dataset—comprising over 230,000 expert-annotated harmonic labels from 1280 musical works spanning three centuries—to quantify and trace the diachronic development and co-evolution of chromaticism and dissonance. We introduce novel quantitative indices measuring chromaticism and dissonance to evaluate stylistic evolution in different musical periods. Our findings empirically validate the established narrative of a gradual rise in both chromaticism and dissonance, and further reveal a more nuanced trajectory characterized by modal differences and a persistent diatonic foundation alongside chromatic and dissonant experimentation. Adopting a “distant listening” approach, this study provides a systematic and quantitative perspective on the evolution of chromaticism and dissonance, complementing traditional musicological approaches and providing novel, data-driven insights into the evolution of Western tonal music.

title: Radical populist parties receive greater audience support on social media: a cross-platform monitoring of digital campaigning for the 2024 European Parliament election
abstract: Abstract Social media platforms play an increasingly important role in political campaigning, enabling parties to bypass traditional media and mobilize support directly. While prior research highlights the online prominence of far-right and radical populist actors, most studies are limited to single platforms or national contexts. This study presents a cross-platform analysis of digital campaign communication by 401 parties across all 27 European Union member states during the 2024 European Parliament election. Using data from Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X/Twitter, and YouTube, we examine party activity and audience engagement via likes with parties’ posts as an indicator of support. By linking digital trace data with expert surveys, we test whether populist radical right parties disproportionately succeed in raising support online. Our findings confirm strong platform-specific advantages of radical populist parties, particularly on TikTok, YouTube and Facebook. We also observe high engagement for far-left populist parties with similar emotional and anti-elitist communication strategies. Based on the linked data, we find that the more Eurosceptic positions a party holds, and the more frequently expert data estimates them as using emotional appeals or anti-elitist communication, the more audience engagement they received across several platforms. Overall, the findings highlight a disproportionate online support for radical populist parties across the European Union.

title: Rethinking the school in the Anthropocene as an ecological and democratic third place
abstract: This paper examines education in the Anthropocene as a holistic education focusing on the emergence of viable social organizations in the Anthropocene compatible with the sustainability of human life in society. The school is therefore studied as a structural frame for global behavior development, habits of thinking and acting that structure our interactions with the common world. Regarding contemporary political hurdles challenging social transformations toward sustainable societies within democratic representative governance systems, we emphasize the role of participatory democracy as an essential element for enabling maintenance and care of our shared environment. Therefore, based on the work of John Dewey, we theorize school as the place of socialization that shapes the development of collective politico-ethical habits. We take community gardens as an example for the school form, as it allows students to emerge as an active democratic and ecological community around the care of the nature of the garden as a shared environment, within the human and non-human community of life.

title: Music synesthesia or cross-modal correspondences? A systematic review of terminology and findings in multisensory research on Chinese music
abstract: This systematic review examines the use of multisensory terminology and the main findings of English-language studies on Chinese music published from 2002 to 2022. Following PRISMA guidelines (Page et al., 2021), studies were identifi ed through searches of Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and screened according to the inclusion criteria. Eight studies from psychology, cognition, and computer science were included. Deductive coding was used to examine terminology and identify underlying research concepts, while inductive coding was used to synthesize reported findings. The results showed a mismatch between terminology and research concepts. Five studies used the term “synesthesia” to describe sensory correspondences shared across participants. Synesthesia refers to stable and automatic sensory associations at the individual level, whereas sensory correspondences observed across individuals are described as cross-modal correspondences. Three factors may contribute to this terminology mismatch: historical changes in multisensory terminology, linguistic and translation practices, and language economy. The included studies examined sound–color, sound–image, sound–taste, and sound–touch correspondences. The proposed explanations involved perceptual, emotional, neural, and cultural mechanisms. The findings of this study suggest that multisensory research on Chinese music should distinguish cross-modal correspondences from synesthesia and consider cultural factors in cross-modal correspondences research. This review is limited by the small number of included studies and methodological diversity across research fields.

title: How social media shapes travel intention: insights from the elaboration likelihood model
abstract: Social media is a key channel allowing the public to access tourism information. However, given the large amount of tourism information on social media, research on how consumers transform this information into travel decisions is lacking. Accordingly, Xiaohongshu (Rednote), a representative social media platform, was selected. This study analyzed the relationship between tourism information quality, observational learning, destination trust, and travel intentions based on the central and peripheral routes of the elaboration likelihood model. Tourism information quality (value-added and timeliness) and observational learning (number of comments) positively influenced destination trust. Destination trust mediated the relationship between tourism information quality (value-added and timeliness), observational learning (number of comments), and travel intentions. These findings have important practical significance for tourism marketing organizations.

title: Revisiting the nexus between digital inclusive finance and rural revitalization: New evidence from Chinese municipal data
abstract: Recently, digital inclusive finance and rural revitalization are hot topics among academic and official groups in China. In this paper, we examine the impact of digital inclusive finance on the revitalization of the countryside using municipal-level panel data from 2011 to 2023. Endogeneity issues are dealt with by using instrumental variables in a quantitative analysis. From the results, we can see that the effects of digital inclusive finance on promoting the revitalization of rural areas mainly come out through the paths of improving technological innovation and upgrading the industrial structure. Also, the impact is moderated by conventional financial growth and digital infrastructure. Heterogeneity analysis shows differences under varied policy contexts and development situations. Based on these findings, some place-based policy recommendations are put forward to strengthen the effect of digital financial inclusion in promoting rural revitalization. This helps to understand how digital inclusive finance works and gives real-world ideas for making and checking policies.

title: The dawn of the Anthropocene: the colonial underpinnings of the green transition and post-growth alternatives
abstract: The Anthropocene marks a shift in recognising that contemporary socio-ecological crises are fundamentally anthropogenic. While the green transition is often presented as a pathway towards sustainability, this article traces its colonial underpinnings within neoliberal, growth-oriented frameworks. These dynamics unfold materially through the extraction of critical minerals and the export of waste, and discursively through narratives of ethical disposal that shift responsibility onto and reproduce guilt and shame among communities in the Global South. Furthermore, this article advances an alternative approach grounded in post-growth strategies, emphasising the need for overarching narratives that connect fragmented grassroots practices with broader governance structures. It highlights the complementary potential of such approaches for rethinking politics, responsibility, and transformation in the Anthropocene.

title: Schizo-syntax and the paranoiac guardrail: machinic schizoanalysis of AI hallucination and the conditions of a line of flight
abstract: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has intensified debate over so-called AI hallucinations: fluent outputs that are factually unsupported, logically unstable, or misaligned with a task. Mainstream engineering treats these outputs as failures to be reduced through post-training, retrieval, verification, and other control mechanisms. This article reinterprets that consensus through Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari’s Capitalism and Schizophrenia. It reads alignment as a reterritorializing apparatus and uses “schizo-syntax” for a non-clinical textual pattern of branching association under weaker referential constraint. The argument does not equate randomness, high temperature, base models, or factual error with creativity. A deviation is productively deterritorializing only when it creates context-relevant novelty, retains intelligible task constraints, and is taken up through human interpretation, selection, or verification; novelty without those conditions is noise. Published studies of literary interpretation and AI-assisted art illustrate this relational account, while the article reports no new experiment. A preregistrable comparison of matched base and instruction-tuned checkpoints, decoding settings, and creative, interpretive, and factual tasks is therefore specified as a future test. Finally, the article treats “desire,” “unconscious,” “paranoiac,” and “line of flight” as functional metaphors for an input → learned causal-functional organization → output sequence, not as attributions of consciousness, psychiatric states, intention, or autonomous authorship. The result is a plural account that preserves strict factual regimes where truth matters while identifying a bounded role for generative deviation in creative and exploratory practice.

title: Media frames of China’s poverty alleviation: the case of The New York Times
abstract: International media coverage of China’s poverty alleviation efforts represents a significant phenomenon in contemporary global development discourse. This study investigates how The New York Times constructs representations of the Chinese government’s poverty alleviation through corpus-based Critical Discourse Analysis of 254 articles spanning 2013-2023. Employing keyword analysis, collocation examination, and modal verb investigation, the research examines consistent linguistic patterns in NYT’s coverage strategies. The findings reveal discourse construction patterns in which simultaneous factual reporting coexists with evaluative positioning, contributing to a nuanced understanding of media representation beyond binary evaluative frameworks. The analysis demonstrates how lexical choices, grammatical structures, and headline framing patterns function coherently to shape interpretive possibilities for international audiences. These results contribute to understanding media discourse power in cross-cultural contexts and provide insights for international communication practice.

title: Does market-based environmental regulation enhance enterprises’ digital transformation? Evidence from carbon emission trading system
abstract: Digital transformation is a key path for enterprises to enhance their competitiveness. As a market-based environmental regulation instrument aimed at reducing carbon emissions and achieving the dual-carbon goals, the carbon emissions trading system (CETS) plays an important role in enterprises’ digital transformation (EDT). To fill the research gap on the role of CETS in EDT, this study utilizes panel data of Chinese listed firms from 2007 to 2022, treating CETS as a “quasi-natural experiment”, and employs a multi-period difference-in-difference (DID) model to explore the impact of CETS on EDT. The results indicate that, firstly, CETS significantly enhances EDT, and this finding remains robust across a series of tests, including the Goodman-Bacon decomposition and PSM-DID. Secondly, the promotional effect of CETS on EDT is associated with firm characteristics, region and industry. Its promotional role is more prominent in non-SOEs enterprises, small-scale enterprises, enterprises located in east areas, and enterprises operating in low-carbon and high-tech industry. Thirdly, CETS can facilitate EDT through R&D investment and resource allocation efficiency, and government participation positively moderates the positive impact of CETS on EDT. This study provides policy implications for promoting sustainable development and facilitating EDT.

title: Silencing dissent: military co-optation and authoritarian consolidation in Nigeria’s Fourth Republic
abstract: Literature has shown a resurgence of authoritarianism across Africa since the early 2000s, both hybrid and fully consolidated forms, whether through democratically elected leaders consolidating power or via military coups, as recently observed in Niger, Burkina Faso, Sudan, Mali, and Guinea. This article argues that Nigeria, under the APC government, has transitioned toward authoritarianism, consolidating control through the systematic co-optation of military and security institutions and the strategic suppression of dissent. Adopting a qualitative research design based on document and content analysis, this study draws on media reports, official statements, legal frameworks, and observer reports to examine patterns of state behaviour. It focuses on the militarisation of elections, the imposition of a state of emergency in opposition strongholds such as Rivers State, and the coerced defection of key opposition figures as mechanisms of political control. The findings reveal a systematic use of institutional power, intimidation, and military co-optation to capture political space and weaken opposition mobilisation, demonstrating how formally democratic processes are subordinated to authoritarian objectives. The article identifies a shift in the operational logic of authoritarian consolidation from primarily electoral manipulation to an institutionalised reliance on coercive state power, in which military co-optation serves not only to suppress opposition but also to manage elite cohesion within the ruling coalition.

title: School violence and convivencia escolar in Chilean public policy in the post-pandemic context
abstract: The return to in-person schooling after the pandemic heightened public concern about school violence and convivencia escolar in Chile. This study examines how the Chilean Ministry of Education constructs these phenomena. Using critical discourse analysis, we analyzed 34 official documents published between 2022 and 2024. The analysis involved coding excerpts referring to violence, convivencia escolar , and mental health, examining recurring discursive strategies, and grouping the excerpts into interpretive repertoires according to shared semantic and pragmatic patterns: (a) From conflict to violence: an institutional reading; (b) School violence and convivencia as objects of institutional regulation and control; and (c) Convivencia escolar as formative learning. The findings are discussed in relation to tensions among punitive, regulatory, and formative approaches, as well as school management. Limitations include the exclusive use of Ministry documents and the inability to generalize the results.

title: Urban low-carbon transition and tourism competitiveness: a quasi-natural experiment
abstract: Despite global low-carbon transitions, the causal effect of Urban Low-carbon Transition (ULCT) on Urban Tourism Competitiveness (UTC) remains unexplored. This study investigates this relationship by treating China’s low-carbon city pilot policy as a quasi-natural experiment. Using a time-varying Difference-in-Differences (DID) model on panel data from 272 Chinese cities (2005-2019), we find that ULCT significantly enhances overall UTC. Decomposing UTC into four dimensions reveals that this positive effect extends to tourist attraction, tourism industry, ecological, and socio-economic competitiveness. Mechanism analyses indicate that industrial structure rationalization acts as a negative mediator for attraction and industry competitiveness but a positive one for socio-economic competitiveness. In contrast, industrial structure advancement is a positive mediator for industry competitiveness. Furthermore, innovation input and environmental regulation serve as positive mediators for improving ecological and socio-economic competitiveness. The effects are more pronounced in eastern and central China, lower-tier cities, and resource-dependent cities. As the first to integrate ULCT and UTC into a unified framework, this study elucidates the underlying mechanisms, offering crucial insights for policymakers to synergize low-carbon goals with tourism development.

title: Mapping ESG leadership education in higher education: a systematic review and conceptual synthesis of governance-informed learning pathways
abstract: The growing institutional emphasis on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles has created new expectations for higher education institutions to prepare graduates who can engage with governance accountability, stakeholder responsibility, and sustainability-oriented decision-making. However, ESG is often conflated with broader sustainability education, and less is known about how ESG leadership education is conceptualized in higher education research. This study presents a systematic literature review and bibliometric synthesis of 72 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025 and indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. Supported by thematic coding, descriptive statistics, and limited exploratory co-occurrence analysis, the review examines how ESG leadership education is represented, organized, and conceptually linked to governance-informed learning within the indexed literature. The study does not provide primary empirical evidence of student-level competency gains, institutional transformation, or societal impact. Instead, its core contribution is to synthesize the conceptual, methodological, and thematic structure of the field and to propose a literature-derived ESG leadership pathway framework. The findings indicate a marked increase in ESG-related leadership education research after 2020. Experiential learning, curriculum integration, governance literacy, and ESG integration frequently appeared alongside leadership competency themes; however, these patterns reflect associations within published studies rather than causal evidence of educational effectiveness. This review contributes by reframing ESG leadership education as a governance-informed extension of broader sustainability competency models rather than as an entirely separate educational framework. Because the dataset was restricted to Scopus- and Web of Science-indexed articles, the findings may underrepresent gray literature, local journals, institutional reports, and practice-based innovations from developing regions. The proposed framework should therefore be understood as a conceptual synthesis rather than a validated empirical model.

title: Mapping the InsurTech landscape: a taxonomy of successful business models
abstract: Abstract The rapid evolution of digital technologies has given rise to new business models and value creation pathways in the insurance sector, commonly grouped under the umbrella of InsurTech. While existing literature has acknowledged this trend, a comprehensive, empirically-grounded classification of these models remains underdeveloped. This study addresses this gap by developing a robust taxonomy of InsurTech business models and empirically deriving a set of business model archetypes. By synthesizing insights from academic literature, industry reports, and a hand-collected dataset of 100 leading firms from the 2023 InsurTech100 list, we identify five key dimensions of InsurTech innovation: target market, revenue model, value proposition, technology, and emerging business model innovations. Critically, this research moves beyond descriptive classification by applying a multi-method clustering framework suited for categorical data, employing K-means, K-modes, and Gower’s distance with hierarchical clustering and K-medoids, to uncover four distinct and stable business model archetypes: Technology-Focused Enablers, Customer-Centric Disruptors, Embedded Ecosystem Integrators, and Specialized Niche Providers. Cross-method validation using the Adjusted Rand Index demonstrates strong convergence across methods (ARI = 0.86–1.00), with silhouette scores ranging from 0.51 (K-means, Euclidean) to 0.68 (Gower’s distance), confirming moderately strong cluster separation. These archetypes reveal the dominant strategic configurations in the InsurTech landscape, highlighting how firms either enable incumbents with advanced data analytics, disrupt the sector with user-friendly platforms, integrate into broader digital ecosystems, or specialize in underserved risk segments. The findings provide a clear and structured understanding of the competitive landscape, offering insights for insurers, technology vendors, and regulators. The paper concludes by discussing the theoretical and practical implications of these archetypes, acknowledging the study’s limitations, and outlining specific avenues for future research.

title: Investigating the relationships among instructional practices, reading motivation and engagement in an EFL context
abstract: Despite extensive research on second language (L2) reading pedagogy, the relationships among instructional practices, reading motivation, and engagement remain underexplored in the English as a foreign language (EFL) context. This study investigated these linkages through a survey of 470 Chinese EFL undergraduates. Findings revealed predominantly positive associations between instructional practices and reading motivation, except for the negative relationship between strategy-based instruction and intrinsic motivation. While all motivation factors (self-efficacy, intrinsic/extrinsic motivation) were positively associated with reading dedication, only extrinsic motivation demonstrated a negative relationship with reading avoidance. Strategy-based teaching enhanced dedication, whereas evaluative feedback unexpectedly increased avoidance. Implications for enhancing EFL learners’ reading motivation and engagement in Chinese higher education are discussed.

title: Mapping the barriers: an exploratory case study of research engagement among teaching-focused academic staff in higher education
abstract: Abstract The increasing presence of teaching-focused roles in higher education has prompted growing concern about how such academics are supported to engage in research. Despite being expected to engage in research activities, many staff in these roles face significant barriers, ranging from high teaching workloads and limited access to funding, to institutional frameworks that prioritise research-led models of academic success. This study examines a key gap in the literature by exploring the lived experiences of teaching-focused staff and evaluating the interconnected nature of these barriers. This qualitative study drew on semi-structured interviews with 16 teaching-focused academics at a post-1992 United Kingdom (UK) university. Thematic analysis was employed to identify key challenges, which were then mapped using causal loop diagramming to visualise how organisational, structural, personal, and external-level factors interact systemically. The resulting model was validated through a workshop with participants. Findings highlight complex feedback loops that compound the difficulties faced by staff. A lack of clarity around research expectations, limited mentorship opportunities, and performance metrics misaligned with teaching-focused roles also emerged as critical issues. This study offers both conceptual and practical contributions and provides a holistic view of the dynamics at play and identifies leverage points for institutional intervention. The study calls for targeted support structures, including ring-fenced research time, formal mentoring schemes, and recognition of alternative scholarly outputs, to better integrate teaching-focused academics into research cultures. Moreover, the study reimagines what inclusive research engagement could look like in an increasingly diverse academic workforce, and how institutions might respond more equitably to the needs of all academic staff.

title: Can E-commerce development improve the nutrition-environment synergy of food consumption? Evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China
abstract: Abstract With the rapid advancement of digitalization and informatization globally, the effect of e-commerce on human behavior has been widely examined. However, it remains unclear whether and to what extent e-commerce promotes sustainable consumption practices, particularly regarding the nutrition-environment synergy of food consumption. Using data from the China Urban Household Survey, this study examines the causal effect of e-commerce development on the synergy between these two dimensions and sheds light on the underlying mechanisms. Employing a difference-in-differences approach based on a quasi-natural experiment of the National E-commerce Demonstration Cities Policy (NEDCP), our study finds that the NEDCP significantly enhances the nutrition-environment synergy of food consumption in urban China. The positive effect is especially pronounced among low-income households and those with female, older, or more highly educated household heads. Mechanism analysis suggests that the NEDCP achieves this by raising household disposable income, increasing the proportion of plant-based foods in household food consumption, and reducing the proportion of animal-based foods. Given the positive effect of e-commerce development, policymakers are advised to continue advancing e-commerce initiatives as a means of raising household income and fostering a transition toward more plant-based diets, thereby enhancing nutritional health and environmental sustainability.

title: A polycentric vision of social-emotional skills across 15 sites in the OECD SSES 2023
abstract: Abstract Social-emotional (SE) skills are fundamental to adolescent development, yet how these skills interconnect as systems across cultural contexts remains underexplored. Drawing on data from 45,908 15-year-olds across 15 culturally diverse sites participating in the OECD 2023 Survey on Social and Emotional Skills (SSES), this study employed network analysis to examine the structure of 15 skills mapped to the Big Five personality framework. Two main findings emerged. First, optimism, persistence, and achievement motivation formed a universal motivational core, consistently exhibiting the highest expected influence across all sites, with the achievement motivation–persistence link showing the greatest cross-context stability. Second, cross-cultural comparisons revealed polycentric patterns: South American sites (Bogotá, Chile, Peru, Sobral) cohered around achievement motivation; European sites clustered with optimism as a central node; and Asian sites exhibited marked heterogeneity, with empathy central in Gunma (Japan) but peripheral in Jinan (China). These findings advance understanding of SE skills as culturally mediated systems rather than isolated traits, demonstrating that skill levels and network influence are distinct dimensions of social-emotional functioning. The study provides an empirical foundation for designing culturally responsive social and emotional learning (SEL) interventions that balance universal priorities with context-sensitive adaptation.

title: Recursive cognitive warfare and domestic legitimation: official and platform discourse during Pelosi’s 2022 Taiwan visit
abstract: This study examines China's response to then Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives Nancy Pelosi's August 2022 visit to Taiwan through a qualitative frame analysis. It advances a framework of recursive cognitive warfare, in which official narratives are operationalised through specific frames, amplified as public affect within a state-managed platform ecology, and selectively reabsorbed into official discourse as evidence of popular consensus. Across the complete verifiable official-statement corpus, framing recurs along three dimensions: subject, action, and solution. Official statements construct U.S. and Taiwan-related actors through sovereignty, legality, and non-interference claims; define the visit as a violation; and present countermeasures as justified, necessary, or historically warranted. Both registers perform a “double movement” that appropriates liberal-legal vocabulary while delegitimising liberal actors, sustaining a domestic legitimacy infrastructure for coercion. Convergence across registers is patterned, though its causal direction remains suggestive rather than conclusive.

title: Contesting the commons: managing Darjeeling’s springs in a changing Eastern Himalaya
abstract: Darjeeling, a city in the Eastern Himalaya, has faced chronic water shortages for decades. Its water supply is fragmented across three spring-dependent systems: a colonial-era municipal network, private delivery services, and neighborhood springs managed by community organizations called samaj . Existing research frames these systems’ water delivery failures as a supply-demand problem: urbanization intensifies demand, governments fail to build adequate infrastructure, and climate change reduces spring availability. Drawing on a decade of fieldwork informed by environmental history and political ecology, we argue that this supply-demand framing obscures more than it reveals, and that the tension between commons and enclosure offers a more productive analytical lens. Through this lens, the samaj -managed springs emerge as the most socially and ecologically embedded of the three systems, constituting what we term a cosmopolitical commons , in which human obligation, ecological process, and embodied knowledge are not merely linked but mutually constitutive. The samaj -managed springs are, however, also a contested commons : the other two systems, driven by statist and commodifying logics of enclosure and extraction, are eroding the samaj ’s capacity for collective stewardship even as the springs themselves deteriorate under intensifying urbanization and climatic stress. Addressing Darjeeling’s water crisis thus requires more than supply-side investment: it demands recognizing commoning as the city’s most resilient water management system, supporting it institutionally, and actively resisting the enclosures that undermine it.

title: Dynamic network DEA efficiency of Chinese higher education institutions: insights from the teaching, research, and grant application subprocesses
abstract: In the education community, there is widespread concern over the technical efficiency of higher education institutions (HEIs). To consider the internal structure of the efficiency measurement, network data envelopment analysis (NDEA) models have gradually been used in HEIs since 2010. In practice, there are input and output conversion processes in which, for example, shared inputs and dynamically changing shared inputs are converted into carry-over items in the education production process. However, existing NDEA studies rarely account for shared inputs and carry-overs for internally linked activities and the dynamic period efficiency evaluation of HEI. This study adopts a multistage dynamic network DEA (DNDEA) in the multiplier form, analyzing teaching, research, and grant application subprocesses for 64 “985 Project” and “non-985 Project” universities in China from 2018 to 2020. Unlike predetermined weights of subprocesses, our proposed DNDEA model utilizes endogenous weight determination and carry-overs embedded across periods, allowing HEIs to determine the relative contribution of each subprocess. On average, the evaluated 64 HEIs achieved overall efficiency of 0.6985, with research and teaching performing relatively well at 0.8373 and 0.9618, respectively, while the grant application stage lags significantly at 0.0218. Teaching performs consistently well across all HEIs. Most HEIs show improvements in teaching and research, while nearly half exhibit a declining trend in grant application efficiency. The results also indicate disparities in the efficiency scores for the research and grant application subprocesses. The “985 Project” universities outperform “non-985 Project” universities especially in research, whereas more “non-985 Project” universities prioritize teaching. Additionally, different weights are endogenously assigned to the three observed subprocesses, reflecting each HEI’s unique strengths and varying priorities for improving efficiency. Research emerges as the dominant stage driving overall efficiency, while grant application represents a critical area for improvement for all HEIs. To enhance overall technical efficiency, expanding collaborative networks, strengthening research records, and targeted training are required, particularly in the grant application.

title: Shadow fleets under sanctions: the regulations of the IMO framework
abstract: The emergence of “shadow fleets”, clandestine maritime networks designed to circumvent sanctions, poses a critical challenge to global maritime governance, safety, and environmental protection. This paper examines the regulatory response of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) to this phenomenon. It argues that, despite establishing a comprehensive framework through conventions such as the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) and the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL), the IMO’s approach remains reactive and fragmented. The Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) is also considered in light of its relevance to seafarers’ rights. The study demonstrates that shadow fleets engage in systematic violations, including AIS manipulation, illicit ship-to-ship transfers, and the operation of aging and poorly maintained vessels, thereby increasing risks to maritime safety, environmental protection, and labor welfare. The analysis demonstrates that these patterns persist due to structural constraints, including the non-binding nature of key instruments, uneven flag state enforcement, and the technical limitations of the IMO’s mandate. In response, the paper proposes a more integrated governance model, including a precautionary exercise of the IMO’s mandate, strengthened enforcement through targeted audits and transparency measures, enhanced coordination with other regimes such as the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and the International Labour Organization (ILO), and clarification of the role of coastal states within the exclusive economic zone (EEZ). This research contributes to the field of maritime governance by bridging policy-oriented analyses of shadow fleet operations with legal scholarship, offering a political economy explanation for persistent non-compliance and providing policy-relevant insights for mitigating associated risks.

title: Tech-savvy but different: a comparative study on generational adoption of Fintech-enabled mobile payments
abstract: Mobile payment technology has emerged as a disruptive force, revolutionizing traditional financial systems and accelerating the shift toward a cashless economy. The objective of this study is to examine the determinants of mobile payment adoption among Generation Z and Millennials, two generational cohorts that are tech-savvy and important for the growth of fintech. The study employs an extended UTAUT model, which integrates Government Initiatives, and 912 valid responses were collected, analyzed using partial least squares structural equational modeling and multi-group analysis through SmartPLS 4. The results stated that Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, Price Value, Personal Innovativeness, and Government Initiatives significantly impact mobile payment adoption among both cohorts. However, the results of MGA revealed that Facilitating Conditions had a statistically different impact between generations; it mainly impacts millennials. These findings offer important theoretical and practical insights for policymakers and service providers in understanding generational patterns in the recent scenario of mobile payment adoption.

title: Marital formation and childbirth during the COVID-19 pandemic: survey-based evidence from Iran
abstract: Abstract With a representative survey of 1214 participants conducted in early 2022, this study investigates the relationship between the COVID-19 pandemic and marital formation and childbirth dynamics in Iran. The results of the empirical investigation using logit models suggest that the experience of unemployment due to the pandemic is positively associated with getting married during the pandemic, and the experience of losing a close relative or family member is negatively associated with getting married. In addition, concerns about the persistence of the pandemic and the vaccination status show negative associations with childbirth during the pandemic. We found heterogeneous results depending on gender, location, and social class; for example, the negative associations of concern about a prolonged pandemic and vaccination status with childbirth are statistically significant in the female subsample but not in the male subsample. Overall, the results have implications for the development of the fertility rate and population in post-pandemic Iran.

title: Digital technology innovation and ecological product supply: empirical evidence from Chinese cities
abstract: Improving the level of urban ecological products supply (UEPS) is of great significance to ecological benefits and sustainable urban development. Based on the Solow model, this paper constructs an ecological product production function incorporating digital technology elements, reveals the direct impact mechanism of digital technology innovation (DTI) on UEPS through mathematical derivation, and theoretically explains its indirect transmission path. Based on the panel data of 284 prefecture-level cities and above in China from 2011 to 2023, the empirical test shows that: (1) the regional imbalance of UEPS is significant, and the average UEPS of 284 cities is only 0.274; (2) DTI has a positive driving effect on UEPS, and this conclusion remains valid in robustness examinations like generalized method of moments and the instrumental variable method, which supports the theoretical derivation based on the Solow model, that is, DTI directly promotes supply growth by improving the allocation efficiency of ecological factors; (3) The regression outcomes regarding the mechanism effect indicate that DTI exerts an indirect promoting influence on the enhancement of UEPS by stimulating green consumption demand, Facilitating industrial structure transformation, and enhancing the accessibility of green finance, revealing the multi-channel transmission mechanism of DTI empowering UEPS; (4) DTI exhibits significant heterogeneity in the UEPS, which is verified in resource-based and non-resource-based cities and different regional divisions. Among them, in resource-based cities and central and eastern cities, the marginal effect of DTI on the UEPS is relatively stronger. This study provides a theoretical and practical reference for the government to implement effective macro-control in the UEPS.

title: Intergenerational transmission of substance-related health-risk behaviors in later life: a focus on childhood physical abuse and emotional neglect
abstract: While studies have documented associations between parental and offspring substance-related health-risk behaviors during childhood and adolescence, it remains unclear whether childhood parental substance-related health-risk behaviors are associated with offspring substance-related health-risk behaviors assessed in later life. In the present study, substance-related health-risk behaviors refer specifically to smoking and drinking. Moreover, the potential mediating and moderating pathways underlying this long-term association have not been fully explored. This study examined the association between childhood parental smoking and drinking behaviors and offspring smoking and drinking behaviors assessed in later life, while also investigating the potential mediating roles of childhood physical abuse and emotional neglect and the moderating role of offspring gender. The analytic sample included 14,164 respondents (mean age = 61.41 years) from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. The results indicated that childhood parental substance-related health-risk behaviors were positively associated with offspring substance-related health-risk behaviors assessed in later life. Childhood physical abuse and emotional neglect emerged as significant indirect pathways linking parental and offspring substance-related health-risk behaviors. In addition, offspring gender significantly moderated this association, with stronger associations observed among male offspring than among female offspring. This study provides evidence of a long-term association between childhood parental and offspring substance-related health-risk behaviors assessed in later life and identifies potential mediating and moderating pathways underlying this relationship. The findings highlight the importance of adopting a life-course perspective when addressing substance-related health-risk behaviors among middle-aged and older adults and suggest that childhood physical abuse and emotional neglect may represent important targets for prevention and intervention efforts.
