title: Silent struggles: a qualitative inquiry into stigma experienced by caregivers of substance use disorder (SUD) patients
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of stigma among caregivers of individuals with substance use disorder (SUD) in the context of Indian society, specifically in Odisha. A qualitative phenomenological design was employed to understand caregivers' personal narratives and perceptions of stigma in caregiving for individuals with SUD. Methods In-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 primary caregivers of SUD patients receiving treatment at a mental health and de-addiction center in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Participants were selected using purposive sampling. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-step thematic analysis. The study adhered to COREQ reporting guidelines. Results Five overarching themes were identified: (1) Discordant family relationships, including strained marital dynamics and caregiver health decline; (2) Financial meltdown resulting from treatment costs and loss of income; (3) Psychological abuse experienced by caregivers in the form of verbal or physical aggression; (4) Assigning blame, including scapegoating by family and society; and (5) Social fragmentation and shame due to societal judgment and isolation. The stigma experienced was multifaceted, encompassing emotional, financial, relational, and social dimensions. Conclusion Caregivers of individuals with SUD in India face significant stigma, often compounded by gender roles, community perceptions, and lack of systemic support. These challenges impact caregiver well-being and highlight the need for nurse-led, community-based, and culturally sensitive interventions aimed at caregiver support and stigma reduction.

title: Citywide echoes of the energy revolution: How new energy policies enhance urban green development resilience?
abstract: In the face of mounting global climate change challenges, integrating urban resilience with green development has become a crucial pathway to achieving sustainable development. This study constructs an indicator system for urban green development resilience (UGDR) based on panel data from 262 prefecture-level cities in China from 2008 to 2022, and applies the VHSD-EM model for comprehensive measurement. By further employing a difference-in-differences model combined with machine learning methods, the study systematically evaluates the impact and underlying mechanisms of the New Energy Demonstration Area (NEDA) policy. The results reveal that the NEDA policy significantly enhances UGDR. In the mechanism analysis, this paper innovatively incorporates the perspective of “coopetition relationship” into the institutional and technological framework of ecological modernization theory, enriching the theoretical understanding of policy effects. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that NEDA exerts stronger effects in old industrial base cities and in economically developed and developing regions. This research provides both theoretical and practical insights for the optimization and expansion of renewable energy policies, emphasizing the importance of institutional reform, technological innovation, and intercity coopetition in improving energy efficiency and environmental governance, and ultimately advancing green, low-carbon transformation and the realization of sustainable development goals.

title: Social capital and digital competence as predictors of curriculum internationalization
abstract: Abstract This study analyzes the factors that foster faculty participation in internationalization processes at a private university in Mexico, highlighting the role of digital competences and institutional support. Using a mixed-methods design, 303 faculty members responded to a questionnaire combining Likert-scale and open-ended questions. Quantitative analysis included ANOVA, regression, and decision tree modeling, while qualitative data were thematically coded. Findings reveal that access to academic networks, professional motivation, and perceived benefits are key drivers of international engagement. While digital competences are present, their impact is amplified when combined with institutional strategies for training, guidance, and recognition. The study underscores the value of creating environments that strengthen international academic collaboration through inclusive approaches. It recommends expanding opportunities for faculty across all contract types, incorporating flexible training and recognition mechanisms that contribute to building a global-minded institutional culture.

title: Reconstructing perished vernacular architecture: a digital humanities perspective on methods for digitally reconstituting lost rural built heritage
abstract: With accelerating globalization and urbanization, vernacular architecture, as an important carrier of regional culture, is increasingly confronted with the dual fragmentation of its spatial environment and historical information. Conventional reconstruction research remains constrained by incomplete historical records and the lack of a systematic methodological framework. This study integrates a multiple-evidence analytical approach with digital humanities technologies to develop a comprehensive reconstruction method for perished vernacular architecture. The method proceeds through three stages: AI-assisted historical textual criticism, digital translation and inference of spatial information, and parametric modeling with visual representation, thereby enabling both spatial reconstruction and cultural-semantic interpretation. To enhance the reliability and transparency of the digital reconstruction process, this study proposes an Execution-Feedback-Revision (EFR) cognitive recursive model as a theoretical framework for human-AI collaborative reasoning and further reveals an evidence-constrained mechanism for the convergence of uncertain historical spatial cognition. Large language models expand the scope of spatial interpretation by integrating multi-source historical information and conducting semantic reasoning. Expert knowledge and multi-dimensional evidence systems jointly establish constraint boundaries for hypothesis evaluation and refinement. Through iterative recursive feedback, spatial hypotheses inconsistent with historical evidence are continuously identified and revised, progressively narrowing the interpretation space and transforming uncertain initial understandings of historical spatial knowledge into reliable spatial interpretations supported by evidence. Using the Maoshan Academy in Ningbo, Zhejiang, as a case study, the research systematically demonstrates the interactive negotiation among multi-source historical materials, AI-generated feedback, and human verification across key tasks such as site confirmation, spatial-sequence analysis, and roof-type identification. It further employs parametric techniques to generate adjustable digital models capable of expressing uncertainty, thereby reconstructing and analyzing the academy’s architectural form, spatial configuration, and cultural significance. The digital reconstruction methodology proposed in this study provides a systematic technical framework for research on extinct vernacular architectural heritage reconstruction and validates the evidence-constrained convergence mechanism of uncertain historical spatial cognition. It further offers a transferable methodological reference for the digital regeneration of extinct vernacular architectural heritage and vernacular knowledge spaces across diverse regional and cultural contexts.

title: Building a Saudi Waqf Index: public data, Sharia governance, and policy design for a resilient endowment ecosystem
abstract: Abstract The concept of Waqf (Islamic endowment) has re-emerged as a key pillar in the institutional structure of social development and financial sustainability as part of Vision 2030 in Saudi Arabia. Empirical studies of the waqf sector, however, continue to face a measurement deficit: no single, publicly verifiable framework exists to systematically track its size, governance quality, and socioeconomic impact over time. This study addresses that gap by constructing a Saudi Waqf Index (SWI) for the 2018–2024 period, drawing exclusively on official annual reports published by the General Authority for Awqaf (GAA). The index operationalises four Sharia governance principles as quantifiable measurement constructs: Ḥifẓ al-māl (protection of wealth), amānah (fiduciary stewardship), bayān (transparency), and sharṭ al-wāqif (founder-stipulation compliance). These constructs are embedded within four analytical pillars: financial sustainability, ecosystem readiness, governance architecture, and social alignment. Using longitudinal, sector-level data from official government sources, the study traces indicative patterns of institutional consolidation across resource structure, regulatory convergence, sectoral allocation, and benefit distribution. Findings indicate steady institutionalisation and financial growth post-2018, alongside a persistent lag in outcome-based social impact measurement. The paper offers a reproducible, policy-relevant diagnostic framework for waqf assessment grounded in public data and Sharia-informed governance principles.

title: Asymmetric volatility spillovers and dynamic connectedness under uncertainty: evidence from BRICS exchange rates, the US Dollar, the Japanese Yen, and oil markets
abstract: This paper examines asymmetric volatility spillovers and dynamic connectedness among BRICS exchange rates, the US Dollar Index (USDX), the Japanese Yen (JPY), Brent crude oil, and the Geopolitical Risk Index (GPRD), employing a Time-Varying Parameter Vector Autoregression (TVP-VAR) framework combined with a GJR-GARCH specification. By decomposing volatility into positive (good) and negative (bad) components, the analysis offers a detailed perspective on risk transmission under extreme market conditions. The findings indicate that the Russian Ruble and oil-market volatility function as persistent net transmitters of shocks, particularly during major crises such as the 2014–2015 oil price collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the 2022 Russia–Ukraine conflict. By contrast, the Chinese Yuan and Indian Rupee consistently behave as net receivers, reflecting their exposure to global macroeconomic uncertainty. Portfolio results show that USDX, JPY, and Brent crude oil contribute to greater portfolio resilience and risk reduction during periods of uncertainty, while asymmetric portfolio dynamics reveal that adverse oil shocks intensify systemic risk, especially for the Russian Ruble and South African Rand. Overall, the results highlight the relevance of asymmetry-aware approaches for managing currency and commodity risks and provide practical insights for investors and policymakers in emerging markets.

title: Path dependence or path creation? Evolution and influencing factors of future industry investment networks in China from 2012 to 2024
abstract: Abstract Future industries represent a strategic commanding height in the new round of global scientific and technological revolution. The spatial evolutionary patterns of their investment networks have emerged as a frontier topic in economic geography. Based on investment data from future industry enterprises in China during 2012–2024, this study constructs an inter-city future industry investment network (FIIN) covering six sub-sectors, namely future manufacturing (FMF), future energy (FE), future information (FI), future materials (FM), future space (FS), and future health (FH). The evolution and influencing factors of FIIN in China are analyzed through methods including dominant flow analysis, social network analysis, and geographically weighted random forest. The results show that the major nodes of FIIN have undergone a transition involving agglomeration from resource-based cities toward innovation-oriented core cities. New first-tier cities have gradually grown into secondary core nodes. The node patterns of the six sub-sectors exhibit differentiated features jointly associated with technological attributes, factor endowments, and policy orientations. The dominant flows of FIIN have evolved from spatial dispersion toward core concentration and from unipolar dominance toward multipolar coordination. Long-distance backbone linkages across city clusters and regions have become increasingly dense. FIIN has evolved from an early-stage form characterized by dispersion and isolation into a mature network featuring close connectivity, efficient transmission, and local coordination. The influencing factors of FIIN have undergone a fundamental shift in the spatial importance structure from demand-side predictors toward technology supply-side predictors. The predictive importance of technological supply capacity has continuously strengthened, policy support has risen to rank among the top predictors, and natural geographical factors have systematically receded to the bottom of the ranking. These insights provide evidence consistent with path creation in FIIN and provide a reference for formulating strategies to develop frontier industries.

title: Visibility without protection: gendered barriers to artistic practices and science communication through art in academia
abstract: Artistic practices offer researchers alternative modes of expression and, in some cases, of science communication, yet they remain institutionally marginal within academia. This study first develops a theoretical framework to explain the symbolic and structural exclusions that women face in artistic practices and science communication through art and then illustrates it with empirical evidence. Drawing on a national survey of 6276 researchers and an expert workshop in Spain, we show that gender, ideology, and caregiving responsibilities intersect to limit women’s participation in science communication through art—an emergent but under-recognised form of academic labour—particularly among more conservative researchers. We conceptualise this condition as visibility without protection, whereby science communication through art exposes researchers to increased public visibility without corresponding institutional support. The study clarifies how structural and cultural dynamics combine to produce gendered vulnerability in science communication through art and calls for academic norms that better recognise diverse forms of knowledge expression.

title: The impact of natural disasters on corporate performance: large sample evidence from China
abstract: We examine the causal impact of major natural disasters on corporate performance and innovation activities. Using the EM-DAT disaster database, we analyze three types of natural disasters with the most significant impact on China: earthquakes, floods, and storms. By matching disaster data with the China Industrial Enterprise Database, we find that major natural disasters exert immediate negative shocks on corporate operations, though the specific impacts on financial returns and productivity vary by disaster type. However, in the long run, major natural disasters drive heterogeneous recovery trajectories, though the ultimate improvements in corporate performance and efficiency are highly contingent upon disaster-specific attributes. Using data on patent applications, we discover that natural disasters initially decrease innovation activities in affected areas. Yet, over time, firms in disaster-affected regions innovate more than those in unaffected areas. Mechanism analysis reveals that different types of disasters trigger distinctly divergent recovery paths. Specifically, Floods facilitate firms’ capital upgrading through government financial subsidies and credit support, thereby enhancing long-term efficiency. In contrast, while Storms do not bring external financial support, they compel firms to climb the value chain through technological innovation. Earthquakes, however, result in high costs of restorative reconstruction that crowd out productive resources, leading to a long-term reduction in production efficiency, with only labor-intensive and small- and micro-sized enterprises demonstrating strong survival resilience. This study provides a pragmatic framework for policymakers and business leaders in responding to natural disasters, demonstrating that the strategic alignment of intervention measures with disaster-specific attributes is essential for transforming catastrophic shocks into opportunities for long-term economic resilience and growth.

title: Resolving conflicting findings on low-carbon city pilots: stage-specific impacts and the role of voluntary vs. mandatory policies in emissions reduction
abstract: Although China’s Low-Carbon City Pilot (LCCP) policy has been extensively studied, its precise impact on carbon emissions remains contested. Some studies report substantial reductions in emissions and intensity, while others find limited or no effects. A key reason for these discrepancies is the failure to distinguish between the policy’s three distinct implementation phases. Launched in 2010, 2013, and 2017, each batch of pilot cities adopted increasingly stringent regulatory approaches, shifting from voluntary initiatives to mandatory enforcement. The failure to account for these differences in policy design leads aggregate analyses to obscure critical variations in outcomes, thereby limiting the ability to determine the effectiveness of specific measures across varying contexts. Addressing this gap helps clarify ongoing theoretical debates in climate governance and can inform more effective, locally tailored policy design in China and other emerging economies. This study addresses that gap by separately evaluating the three LCCP batches (2010–2013, 2014–2016, 2017–2021) using a multi-period Difference-in-Differences (DID) framework. Key findings indicate that: (1) Mandatory measures in the third batch significantly reduced CO₂ intensity by 0.168 tons/10,000 CNY in pilot cities, contrasting with earlier voluntary phases showing statistically insignificant effects; (2) Emission reductions from mandatory measures appear to stem primarily from government supervision and technological innovation, with limited impact on individual green travel behavior; (3) Voluntary measures reduced per capita CO₂ emissions by 5.669 tons in high-income regions but increased emissions in low-income areas, highlighting context-dependent efficacy. Based on city-level data from China, these findings offer lessons for emerging economies: mandatory policies are crucial for rapid industrial emission reductions, while voluntary measures are more effective in high-income, tech-intensive regions. Long-term success depends on integrated strategies that align top-down regulation with grassroots participation. By showing that stage-specific evaluation and the strategic sequencing of voluntary and mandatory measures can significantly enhance decarbonization outcomes, this study contributes to ongoing theoretical discussions and provides empirical insights for policy practice.

title: Digital Oasis: How does digital-real integration improve corporate green governance?
abstract: The deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy at the technological level has not only reshaped the production organization modes and resource allocation logic of traditional manufacturing enterprises, but also provided new pathways for enhancing corporate green governance capability. Based on the time-based view and organizational adaptation theory, this study takes Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2024 as the research sample to systematically examine the impact of digital-real integration on corporate green governance performance and its underlying mechanisms. The findings indicate that: (1) digital-real integration significantly improves corporate green governance performance, suggesting that the deep coupling between digital technologies and real industrial technological systems helps optimize corporate green governance systems and enhance governance capability; (2) mechanism analysis reveals that digital-real integration promotes green governance performance by improving firms’ response agility and enhancing knowledge orchestration capability, thereby strengthening firms’ dynamic adaptability to environmental changes; and (3) heterogeneity analysis shows that the promoting effect of digital-real integration on corporate green governance is more pronounced among firms with high media attention, firms in heavily polluting industries, and non-state-owned enterprises. This study extends the research framework of corporate green governance from a dynamic perspective, broadens the explanatory boundaries of the time-based view and organizational adaptation theory, and provides empirical evidence and practical implications for improving corporate green governance capability in emerging digital contexts.

title: The Relationship Between Digital Literacy Skills and WhatsApp Group Use in Internal Communication Among Nurses
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the internal communication methods used by nurses, examine their WhatsApp group usage habits, and explore the relationship between these habits and their digital literacy skills. A descriptive and correlational design was adopted to examine associations between variables at a single point in time. Data were collected from 326 nurses working at a university hospital between March and December 2024 via both online and paper-based questionnaires and were analyzed using SPSS 25 software. Findings revealed that WhatsApp was among the most frequently used internal communication tools, ranking after face-to-face communication and mobile phone calls. While all participants reported using WhatsApp in general, 98.8% were members of a department-specific WhatsApp group used for internal communication. Among the participants, 80.4% reported being satisfied with WhatsApp-based communication, and 79.8% believed it had a positive effect on departmental communication. The use of WhatsApp groups varied significantly according to nurses’ positions, work patterns, departments, and length of employment. Ordinal logistic regression analysis demonstrated that higher digital literacy scores were significantly associated with greater odds of reporting satisfaction with WhatsApp group use and a positive perceived effect on communication. These findings underscore the potential value of digital literacy training and clear institutional guidelines for the appropriate use of WhatsApp groups in internal communication.

title: The synergistic role of stakeholders’ corporate social responsibility in the football business supply chain management framework: a systematic review
abstract: Although many industries have effectively integrated Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) to boost Supply Chain Management (SCM) performance, its vital link in sports, particularly football, remains underexplored in research, and it is essential to recognize and leverage the role of CSR in football SCM to enhance operational effectiveness and drive positive change in the industry. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to identify the synergistic role of stakeholders’ CSR in the football business SCM framework. The research involved a systematic review of 74 documents published between 2006 and 2025. The PRISMA 2020 guideline and the ATLAS. ti software was also used. Concepts related to the role of CSR activities in the football business and in SCM were identified. The improved role of CSR activities in the football business’s SCM encompasses managerial improvements, value creation, marketing enhancements, sustainable development, attracting and retaining fans, achieving social and cultural outcomes, enhancing stakeholder relations, and improving economic performance. Businesses can grow significantly by integrating stakeholders’ CSR initiatives within an SCM framework. Football academies, schools, producers of goods and services, and governing bodies must work closely with clubs that create football products. This collaboration fosters remarkable synergy, enhancing market positioning and strengthening connections with society, fans, media, and sponsors. As a result, clubs gain greater empowerment, benefiting stakeholders throughout the value chain. This study highlights the synergistic role of SCM in enhancing stakeholder commitment in the football industry, a crucial factor for business success.

title: The impact of eco-compensation policies on the ecological product value realization rate in compensated areas
abstract: Abstract The realization of ecological product value serves as a vital link between socioeconomic development and environmental resources. A high ecological product value realization rate effectively captures the synergy between economic growth and ecological conservation, ultimately promoting ecological sustainability. Nonetheless, few studies have systematically estimated the ecological product value realization rate, analyzed its evolutionary patterns, and assessed the impact of eco-policies on it from a policy evaluation perspective. To bridge this gap, this paper estimates the ecological product value realization rate for 37 cities from 2004 to 2023. It includes both the compensated area under the Xin’an River Basin eco-compensation policies and its surrounding cities. Based on this panel dataset, a difference-in-differences model and a synthetic control model are constructed to explore the impact of these eco-policies on the ecological product value realization rate. It is observed that the ecological product value realization rate has improved across all cities, with an average value of 0.5952, and is particularly high in cities northeast of Huangshan. Moreover, the results demonstrate that eco-compensation policies exert significant and long-term positive effects on the ecological product value realization rate, contributing to an increase of approximately 6.06%. This effect is primarily attributed to mechanisms such as industrial structure change and green technology development. Robustness tests confirm the reliability of these results. These conclusions offer empirical evidence to assist administrations in designing equitable ecological benefit-sharing mechanisms that effectively integrate eco-compensation policies with ecological product value realization.

title: Policy synergy in green transition: a tripartite evolutionary game analysis of pollution and carbon mitigation through command, market, and voluntary interventions
abstract: Promoting the synergy of pollution reduction and carbon mitigation is a crucial strategy for China’s current climate and environmental governance. This requires active policy measures from both the production and consumption sides. This study constructs a tripartite evolutionary game model of the government, enterprises, and consumers, while considering the effects of green transformation on pollution reduction and carbon mitigation. It explores the impact of the coordinated implementation of command-control, market-incentive, and voluntary policies on promoting green production and consumption. The key findings are as follows: 1) The decisions of the government, enterprises, and consumers are interrelated. To drive the system toward the optimal equilibrium state of green production and consumption, breaking the initial path dependence is crucial. The government must enhance regulatory intensity in the early stages and strengthen publicity and education for enterprises and the public, thereby effectively elevating the initial participation willingness of all three parties. 2) Policy implementation should be tailored to industrial heterogeneity. For industries with substantial abatement potential and high emission intensity, market policies are most effective; these sectors should be prioritized for inclusion in the carbon trading market with differentiated quota schemes. Conversely, for industries with lower emission bases and limited abatement potential, low-cost administrative controls or direct environmental taxes are more suitable. 3) The substitution relationship among policies requires dynamic alignment with market and technological maturity, yet a diversified policy mix remains indispensable. When abatement efficiency and carbon prices are sufficiently high, market-based tools can lower compliance costs through streamlined processes, such as replacing environmental taxes with a single carbon trading mechanism. However, voluntary interventions on the consumption side cannot be substituted by market regulation or mandatory supervision.

title: The instability of the two cultural attractors found within the Renaissance
abstract: Cultural attractor theory proposes that recurrent psychological biases shape the persistence and transformation of cultural traditions. Portraiture offers a unique test case, embedding perceptual cues that reflect both individual choices and collective conventions. Using automated facial analysis (OpenFace), we examined over 2,000 digitized portraits from Renaissance and post-Renaissance Europe, religious artworks, and Japanese ukiyo-e. Results replicated Morin’s (2013) finding of a Renaissance shift toward direct gaze, but this trend reversed after 1600, suggesting the attractor was not stable. Religious works diverged, becoming more averted, while secular portraits engaged viewers. The left cheek bias was strong in the Renaissance, weakened in later Europe, and remained stable in ukiyo-e. Across analyses, sitter fame—but not gaze—predicted cultural visibility. Our study demonstrates how computational analyses of artworks can recover long-term dynamics of human psychology, offering “cognitive fossils” that illuminate the coevolution of visual culture and social behavior.

title: The impact of digital service experience on customer loyalty in traditional agricultural enterprises: evidence from SEM and fsQCA
abstract: Although prior studies link digital service experience to customer loyalty, limited attention has been paid to how this relationship operates in traditional agricultural enterprises undergoing digital transformation. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, this study examines how digital service experience translates into customer loyalty through customer engagement and customer satisfaction, and whether brand image strengthens this process. Based on 504 responses from consumers in China’s dairy industry, PLS-SEM was used to test net effects, mediation, moderation, and moderated mediation, while fsQCA identified configurations leading to high and non-high customer loyalty. The SEM results show that digital service experience positively affects customer loyalty through engagement and satisfaction, including a sequential mediation path. Brand image strengthens the direct effect on loyalty, the effect on engagement, and the sequential mediation process, but not satisfaction-related paths. The fsQCA results reveal multiple equifinal loyalty configurations. This study extends the SOR framework to agricultural digital service contexts, clarifies the mediating mechanisms of customer loyalty formation, and reveals multiple pathways through which loyalty is achieved.

title: The role of swift guanxi and empathy in co-creation behavior: a cultural analysis of influencer marketing in China
abstract: Value co-creation between influencers and users requires closer attention to market and cultural factors. This study explores the co-creation process between influencers and consumers through swift guanxi and empathy, using PLS-SEM and ANN methods. It examines differences associated with regional cultural tightness in value co-creation behaviour. Based on guanxi theory and social capital theory, the study examines the relationships among wishful identification, presence, interactivity, swift guanxi and empathy, and further assesses how swift guanxi and empathy relate to value co-creation behaviour. The results indicate that consumers in regions with lower cultural tightness are more significantly influenced by empathy in value co-creation behaviour compared to those in regions with higher cultural tightness, and that the association between wishful identification and swift guanxi was stronger among male than female respondents in our sample. This study adds empirical evidence on how regional cultural tightness may condition the relationship between empathy and value co-creation in Chinese influencer marketing. The findings offer context-specific insights into consumer behaviour in short-video commerce and should be interpreted within the limits of the cross-sectional, self-report design.

title: Beyond static responses: multi-agent LLM systems as a new paradigm for social science research
abstract: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) transition from static tools to fully agentic systems, their potential for transforming social science research is well recognized. This paper introduces a structured framework for understanding the diverse applications of agentic LLM systems, ranging from simple data processors to complex, multi-agent systems capable of simulating emergent social dynamics. By mapping this developmental continuum across six levels, the paper clarifies the technical and methodological boundaries between different agentic architectures, surveying current capabilities and future potential. It highlights how lower-tier systems streamline conventional tasks like text classification and data annotation, while higher-tier systems enable new forms of inquiry, including the study of group dynamics, norm formation, and large-scale social processes. However, these advancements also raise challenges around reproducibility, ethical oversight, and emergent biases. The paper critically examines these concerns, arguing for sound validation methods, interdisciplinary collaboration, and standardized evaluation metrics. It argues that while agentic LLM systems offer considerable potential for the social sciences, using them responsibly will require careful, context-sensitive deployment and ongoing methodological refinement. The paper concludes with a call for future research that balances technical innovation with ethical responsibility, working toward agentic systems that not only replicate but also extend social science methodology.

title: Psychosocial predictors and justification patterns of traditional and alternative medicine in Peru
abstract: Abstract This mixed-methods study investigates the prevalence, attitudes, psychological predictors, and reasons for perceived effectiveness of traditional and alternative medicine in Peru. A representative national sample ( N = 805) reported their experiences with 16 unconventional medical techniques, alongside psychometric measures of pseudoscientific beliefs, ideological traditionalism, and trust in the medical profession. Traditional medicine was more widely used, while alternative medicine elicited more favorable attitudinal responses. Pseudoscientific beliefs predicted greater endorsement of both modalities, with traditionalism specifically linked to traditional medicine. To enrich the psychometric findings, we applied natural language processing techniques to 2716 reasons for perceived effectiveness extracted from spontaneous open-ended responses, revealing distinct rhetorical patterns: alternative medicine was more often justified through pseudoscientific and biomedical-sounding arguments, whereas traditional medicine drew on cultural, spiritual, and experiential narratives. Network and co-occurrence analyses confirmed that both modalities follow distinctive general combinatory logics of justification. However, subgroups mixing traditional and alternative medicine also emerged, such as spiritually oriented practices and techniques pivoting traditionalist conceptions. These findings reflect the interplay between global health discourses and local belief systems. Overall, this study highlights the value of integrating cultural and linguistic analyses to understand public engagement with unconventional health practices.

title: Rewriting modernity: body, lepers, and the exoticizing gaze in Ma Yuan’s fiction
abstract: Abstract Ma Yuan’s fabrication (1986), widely regarded as one of the most challenging works of contemporary Chinese fiction, has been extensively analyzed as a quintessential example of metafictional writing. Departing from previous critics’ use of the term “meta-narrative,” this paper examines Ma Yuan’s experimental narrative as an exoticizing gaze that represents the bodies of lepers. Drawing on postcolonial theory and affect studies, I argue that this gaze marginalizes lepers as a minority Other within a Han-majority cultural context. Simultaneously, Ma Yuan idealizes Tibetans as embodiments of purity and benevolence while portraying them as traditional and pre-modern from a mainstream cultural lens. This dual representation, I propose, reflects Ma Yuan’s ambivalent stance toward socialist national discourses and the modernization process in post-Mao China. While attempting to rebel against authoritative ideologies, his narrative inadvertently reinforces dominant cultural paradigm. This tension highlights the broader challenges faced by Chinese avant-garde writers in the 1980s, who sought to redefine personal identity amidst the legacy of historical trauma while navigating the demands of sharing indigenous narratives within a globalizing cultural market during the reform era.

title: Language, gender and news media: a corpus-assisted critical discourse study of binary gender representations in China Daily
abstract: This study gives a corpus-assisted critical discourse study of the binary gender representations in Chinese most influential English-language newspaper China Daily (hereinafter CD) during the first two decades of the 21st century. By integrating text mining with FCDS, the research explores the particular ways of binary gender representations in CD synchronically and diachronically and reveals how they are shaped by the competing forces of the state, the market and feminism in China. The findings suggest that while significant progress is evident, such as the shift toward individualized representations of women, increased focus on their rights, health and professional achievements, and broader depictions of diverse life experiences, traditional gender ideologies persist. Media representations continue to emphasize women’s marital status, reproductive roles, and domestic responsibilities, reflecting deep-rooted societal norms and highlighting the tension between feminist progress and conventional expectations. The complex patterns in the newspaper’s binary gender representations further confirm the dynamic influences of the competing forces of the state, the market, and feminism during the examined period.

title: Complex systems frameworks are crucial in responding to the climate, poverty, and health nexus
abstract: The relationship between climate change, poverty, and health is increasingly understood as requiring a complex systems lens in the design of effective and sustainable responses. Climate change exacerbates poverty and health inequities in ways that are non-linear, multidimensional, and deeply interconnected, making traditional intervention approaches insufficient. In this comment, four types of complexity are examined—compositional, experiential, dynamic, and governance—each of which provides a distinct lens for understanding the multilayered interactions at the climate-poverty-health nexus. Building on these dimensions of complexity, complex systems frameworks that provide structured ways to examine and intervene in the climate-poverty-health nexus are explored. Through multiple examples, we illustrate how such approaches can be practically applied. Complex systems-informed analyses can lead to better-designed policies and strategies that are not only more likely to be effective but also more equitable and sustainable in mitigating the impacts of climate change on the health of those living in poverty.

title: “Not just language conversion but cultural transmission”: comparing human-first and AI-first workflows for translation quality, efficiency, and speed in the Anthropocene
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped translation workflows, moving from manual, sentence-level crafting to integrated pipelines using translation memories, neural machine translation, and large language models, yet education struggles to prepare translators for these shifts, risking deskilling and ethical challenges. This study aimed to optimize training by comparing two AI-assisted workflows in a food-related menu translation task, evaluating quality, time, edits, and trainee perceptions to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and self-efficacy. Class 1 ( n = 29) used an AI-first workflow, where AI generated initial drafts followed by human post-editing to correct errors and refine outputs. Class 2 ( n = 27) employed a human-first workflow, with translators drafting texts and AI polishing to enhance style and coherence. Quality (fluency, adequacy), time, edit behaviors (total, necessary, harmful), and perceptions were assessed via quantitative metrics and qualitative feedback. Class 2 outperformed Class 1 in adequacy ( M = 43.02 vs. 39.22, p = 0.002, d = −0.85) and total score ( M = 89.93 vs. 86.67, p = 0.012, d = −0.68), with no fluency difference. Class 1 was faster ( M = 2763.69 s vs. 3494.11 s, p < 0.001, d = −2.40) but made more harmful edits ( d = 1.07). Class 1’s time-quality correlation ( r = 0.905, p < 0.001) showed effort-intensive post-editing, unlike Class 2’s efficiency. Human-first workflows improve quality and confidence, while AI-first prioritize speed. Training should emphasize human-first workflows, prompt design, and selective post-editing to align with workplace curation roles, countering deskilling.

title: Disaster, diaspora, and the construction of post-Kobe subjectivity: a cultural trauma narrative study of Murakami Haruki’s after the quake
abstract: Abstract How natural disasters are transformed into collective meaning crises through cultural mediation remains an underexplored question in cultural trauma studies. Although cultural trauma theory has generated significant conceptual advances since its foundational articulation, its empirical base remains predominantly anchored in Western contexts, and East Asian disaster experiences, particularly the mechanisms through which literary narrative participates in trauma construction, have been insufficiently theorised. This study introduces two analytical dimensions to Alexander’s cultural trauma claim-making model. The first is indirectness, which demonstrates that absence and silence can function as effective claim-making strategies. The second is embodiment, which establishes that bodily practice constitutes a pre-discursive pathway of meaning reconstruction operating prior to the formation of discursive claims. The concept of the “post-Kobe subject” is proposed to theorise a dynamic mode of identity that neither reverts to pre-trauma stability nor remains permanently fragmented. Employing Riessman’s narrative analysis framework in conjunction with Alexander’s cultural trauma theory, this study conducts a systematic analysis of Murakami Haruki’s short story collection After the Quake (2000/2002), examining the social construction functions performed by literary narrative in the cultural traumatisation of the 1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake. The analysis yields three interrelated findings. Indirect narrative, defined here as the systematic avoidance of direct disaster representation, itself constitutes a form of cultural trauma claim-making. The earthquake triggers a threefold diaspora encompassing spatial, relational, and meaning dimensions of social bond dissolution. Characters construct a dynamic form of identity, the post-Kobe subject, through embodied practice and narrative action within traumatic rupture. This study provides an empirical supplement to cultural trauma theory grounded in East Asian disaster experience and demonstrates the methodological potential of narrative analysis in cultural trauma research.

title: Volcanic hazards, uncertainty and destination reputation: media narratives of the El Hierro eruption
abstract: In this study, the role of mass media in the social construction of a natural hazard and its impact on a tourist destination are analysed, using the 2011 submarine volcanic eruption on the island of El Hierro (Spain) as a case study. Drawing on a content analysis of 2073 press articles and face-to-face interviews with stakeholders, the paper examines how journalistic narratives may shape hazard perception. The results indicate that media coverage, focused on scientific uncertainty and political controversy, generated an image of insecurity that increased the impact on tourism arrivals and exacerbated local economic consequences. We conclude that communication management is a critical factor in shaping tourism destination image and in promoting trust in the face of a hazard. This study highlights the need for ethical information strategies that balance public safety with the protection of territorial reputation.

title: The macroeconomic impact of Chinese economic uncertainty in East Asia: evidence from a large multi-economy TVP-VAR model
abstract: This paper examines the spillover effects of Chinese economic uncertainty on Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan, set against the backdrop of China’s structural transition and rising geopolitical tensions. Using a large multi-economy time-varying parameter vector autoregressive model estimated with quarterly data from 2000 to 2024, we document that transmission dynamics are highly state-dependent, amplifying during global turbulence, notably the Global Financial Crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. However, while uncertainty itself transmits rapidly across the region, the resulting macroeconomic outcomes diverge from conventional theoretical predictions. Specifically, although Chinese uncertainty shocks can depress East Asian exports to China, they induce sustained real GDP gains in Japan and negligible output responses in South Korea and Taiwan. Moreover, East Asian inflation and interest rates remain largely insulated from China’s uncertainty shocks. These findings align with the downstream uncertainty mechanism proposed by Grigoris and Segal (2025). We attribute this regional resilience to effective trade diversification, potential safe-haven effects, prudent domestic stabilization policies, and, crucially, the downstream expansionary effect.

title: Why do consumers continue to use online-to-offline delivery services? Moderating roles of social anxiety
abstract: The proliferation of mobile Internet has accelerated the uptake of online-to-offline delivery (O2OD) operations. Although existing literature has extensively investigated the food (meal) delivery—a traditional O2OD concept, it remains unclear why consumers continue to use O2OD in a multi-service scenario—a broader O2OD context where consumers utilize multiple delivery services. Additionally, consumers with social anxiety may rely more on O2OD, as using these services reduces offline interpersonal interactions. Drawing upon the extended unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT2), this study developed a framework applicable to a general O2OD context, with a particular interest in incorporating social anxiety as a moderator. Data were derived from a two-stage online survey completed in China and subsequently analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Results emphasize that individual beliefs (i.e., convenience expectancy, network size influence, and delivery price value), facilitating conditions, and habit positively predict continuance intention, which, alongside habit and facilitating conditions, in turn predicts actual use. Social anxiety weakens the effects of convenience expectancy and delivery price value on continuance intention while strengthening the influence of network size. The study contextually adapts and extends the UTAUT2 baseline model to a generalized O2OD context, identifies social anxiety as a boundary condition, and provides practical insights for O2OD platforms as well as for consumer well-being.

title: Offshore gambling as a social practice: socio-material dynamics in online gambling communities
abstract: Abstract Offshore gambling remains a challenge despite regulatory tightening; yet limited attention has been given to the socio-material environments that make unlicensed play accessible and routinely practiced. This study employs a mixed-methods design, combining BERTopic modelling of 7,901 posts from Flashback.org with qualitative analysis of 392 user narratives, guided by Social Practice Theory. Topic modelling maps dominant discursive patterns, while theory-informed qualitative coding examines how users navigate payment pathways, interpret regulatory environments, and sustain everyday participation. Findings show that offshore gambling persists through the interplay of material infrastructures—digital payment providers, verification systems, and licensing regimes—and evolving user competences, including folk-legal reasoning and peer-based troubleshooting. In addition, shared cultural meanings render the practice meaningful to participants, legitimizing engagement through narratives of rationality, fairness, and adaptation. These dynamics are synthesized in a conceptual model that explains offshore gambling as a self-stabilizing social practice shaped by ongoing interactions between infrastructures, user competencies, and shared meanings under regulatory, market, and technological pressure. This perspective underscores the need for harm-reduction approaches that move beyond individual or policy shortcomings and address the broader socio-material conditions sustaining offshore gambling.

title: Does digital governance reduce corruption? Comparative evidence from emerging and developed economies
abstract: Abstract Digital governance remains underutilized despite its potential, especially in emerging market economies (EMEs) where structural and technological barriers persist. While digital technologies are increasingly used to combat corruption, they pose significant risks of digital control and create more opportunities for corruption. There is, however, a dearth of studies examining these mixed or heterogeneous effects across both developed and EMEs. To fill this gap, the present study investigates the relationship between digital governance and corruption control using the Feasible Generalized Least Squares model across a panel of 43 developed countries and EMEs from 2002 to 2022. By constructing a multidimensional Digital Governance Index and its sub-components using Principal Component Analysis, the research offers a comprehensive assessment of how digital governance, including data regulations, internet governance, social media governance, data integrity, and digital democracy, influences corruption control. The findings indicate that improvements in digital governance enhance corruption control. However, the effect is more pronounced in developed economies. The effectiveness of various dimensions of digital governance largely depends on institutional capacity and quality, and other contextual dynamics across countries.

title: Perceived safety and social inclusion are more strongly associated with quality of life in older age: repeated moderated mediation analyses
abstract: Abstract Person-environment (P-E) fit and ageing theories suggest that perceived safety and social inclusion are associated with health outcomes. However, no study has utilised time-separated unique samples to investigate whether age moderates the association of perceived safety with quality of life (QoL) through social inclusion. This study used three distinct, time-separated samples to ascertain whether the indirect association between perceived safety and QoL through social inclusion is moderated by age. This study employed a moderated mediation analysis repeated at three waves [wave 1 (2007/2008); wave 2 (2014/2015), and wave 3 (2018/2019)] from the World Health Organization’s Study on Global AGEing and adult health Ghana (WHO-SAGE Ghana). It included a weighted sample of 14,172 adults aged 50 to 112 years. The unique sample for each wave was 4724 nationally representative adults, and the Hayes’ Process Macros (Model 59) was utilised to assess moderated mediation. Perceived safety was not directly associated with QoL but was indirectly associated with QoL through social inclusion. The association of perceived safety with QoL was fully mediated by social inclusion, and the mediation was stronger in older age. There was a direct positive association of social inclusion with QoL, which was stronger in older age. The foregoing results were consistent across the three time points and samples. Social inclusion may be more strongly associated with QoL in older age. The results support positive ageing theories, including the Socioemotional Selectivity Theory, and reinforce the importance of enhancing neighbourhood safety and social inclusion.

title: Does intergenerational income upward mobility increase the subjective well-being of middle-aged and older people in China?—Evidence from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS)
abstract: Intergenerational income mobility is widely regarded as a key indicator of social vitality and opportunity, yet its consequences may extend beyond the mobile individuals themselves. Using 3956 parent–child pairs from the China Family Panel Studies, this study examines whether adult children’s intergenerational income upward mobility (IIUM) is associated with the subjective well-being (SWB) of middle-aged and older parents, and through which forms of intergenerational support such associations operate. Using a structural equation model, we find that IIUM is significantly associated with higher SWB. This association is partially mediated through two opposing support channels: IIUM is linked to increased financial transfers from children, which enhances parental SWB, but also to reduced emotional support, which modestly offsets these gains. The magnitude of these pathways varies across key social and institutional groups (e.g., employment/retirement status, hukou, and medical insurance coverage). These findings extend research on intergenerational mobility beyond the outcomes of the mobile individuals themselves by showing that adult children’s upward income mobility has measurable spillover effects on parents’ subjective well-being, and by identifying the material–emotional support trade-off through which these effects operate.

title: How much is too much? Carbon tax thresholds for climate mitigation and social equity
abstract: This study investigates how carbon taxation simultaneously affects climate change mitigation and income inequality through potential nonlinear threshold effects. Using a dynamic panel threshold approach and data from 70 countries over the period 2000–2022, the analysis identifies two critical turning points in the effectiveness of carbon taxation. The results show that a carbon tax below $31 per tonne of CO₂ fails to generate sufficient incentives to reduce emissions. Furthermore, while a tax exceeding this level becomes environmentally effective, it also introduces a significant social trade-off: once the tax surpasses $84 per ton of CO₂, it tends to worsen income inequality by disproportionately affecting low-income households. This highlights a narrow policy window where carbon pricing is both environmentally effective and socially neutral. To achieve both objectives, policymakers should adopt a dual strategy — setting carbon taxes above the environmental threshold while simultaneously redistributing revenues to offset regressive effects. Robustness tests using an alternative carbon tax proxy and multiple climate indicators (CO₂ emissions, precipitation, humidity, and temperature) confirm the consistency of the results. Overall, the study provides new empirical evidence on how the precise calibration of carbon taxation can balance sustainability and equity goals in climate policy.

title: Multidimensional factors influencing young farmers’ willingness to attend agricultural training in rural China
abstract: In agricultural modernization, improving the skills of young farmers is crucial, but the willingness to participate in training in underdeveloped areas is still low. To this end, based on 1467 survey data from a rural area, this study used a binary Logistic model to analyze the determinants of training participation from four dimensions: personal, economic, social and psychological. The results showed that gender and education level significantly affected the willingness to participate in training ( p < 0.05); farmers with high family income had low willingness to participate in training ( p < 0.05), while being willing to pay higher training fees significantly enhanced the willingness to participate in training ( p < 0.01); social support had a positive effect on the willingness to participate in training ( p < 0.05); motivation to participate in training and confidence in future development significantly affected the willingness to participate in training ( p < 0.01). Heterogeneous analysis shows that low-income groups are more dependent on training costs and social support, while high-income groups are more influenced by personal planning and expectations. The study reveals the multidimensional mechanism of young farmers ‘training decision-making, emphasizing the pertinence and effectiveness of training policies by lowering economic threshold and strengthening support system.

title: Evaluating culture-led growth strategies in Asian economies: A multi-regional input-output analysis
abstract: Culture-led development strategies have been widely adopted across Asian economies to stimulate territorial growth through diverse policies and initiatives aimed at promoting cultural and creative industries (CCIs). This paper attempts to evaluate the economic impact of cultural and creative industries in the Asian region using a Global Multi-Regional Input-Output (GMRIO) model. Results show that, according to the GMRIO multipliers, an additional $1 million of final demand in CCIs corresponds to $1.59 million in value-added, $0.70 million in income, and 80 jobs. However, the effects vary regionally and depend on development paths: Eastern Asia shows strong value-added and income multipliers but weaker employment effects, while Southern and South-Eastern Asia display the opposite trend. Mainland China stands out with high multipliers across all dimensions, reflecting the combination of large market and structural characteristics of its economy. These findings highlight how the observed structural differences in multiplier effects suggest potential trade-offs: more developed economies show higher value-added and income multipliers, while lower-income economies tend to have higher employment multipliers. These patterns can inform discussions and strategic planning on how CCIs may be leveraged according to regional characteristics.

title: Risk perception of disinformation in Sweden: exploring the influence of trust, social position, and previous experience of risk
abstract: Abstract Disinformation has become an increasingly researched and debated phenomenon in recent years. While the dissemination of disinformation is not a new phenomenon, the digitalized and globalized information flows have transformed the communication environment. Consequently, there has been a significant rise in scholarly studies on disinformation. However, most studies on disinformation focus on North America, and empirical data from countries such as Sweden is lacking. This study consequently examines perceptions of disinformation in Sweden considering social position, trust, and previous experiences with risk and crises. Analysing data from a national representative survey conducted in Sweden 2023 ( n = 2480), we use multiple regression analysis to explore individual risk perception of disinformation as well as its classification as a societal threat. This study demonstrates that disinformation is a risk that is perceived differently compared to other risks, particularly in relation to social position. We thus advance current knowledge on disinformation by expanding available empirical data in the field, and in so doing, offer insights on risk perception and disinformation in a Swedish context.

title: The hermeneutic journey of Shangdi: cross-cultural dialogue and semantic evolution
abstract: Abstract The concept Shangdi 上帝 in Chinese has undergone significant semantic evolution, from its association with the supreme deity in ancient Chinese cosmology to its increasing connection with the Christian God in specific historical and discursive contexts. This paper explores the historical trajectory of Shangdi , examining its interpretation through three key dimensions: the understanding of Shangdi in ancient Chinese culture, the interpretation by missionaries such as Matteo Ricci and James Legge, and the reception, reinforcement and contestation of Shangdi ’s Christian meaning within specific Chinese discursive communities. Drawing on Hans-Georg Gadamer’s hermeneutics, the study frames the evolution of Shangdi as a dynamic process, where linguistic, cultural, and theological frameworks intersect and contest one another. The analysis shows how Shangdi has become a super-sign—a term simultaneously rooted in Chinese traditions and recontextualized within Christian theological paradigms. By examining historical texts, missionary translations, and contemporary reinterpretations, the paper reveals the complexities of the integration of Shangdi into global religious discourse. This study contributes to understanding how semantic shifts reflect broader cultural negotiations, offering insights into the interplay of faith, language, and identity in the context of globalization.

title: Compulsory citizenship behavior effects on work withdrawal of transcultural individual by sequential motivation mediation
abstract: Multicultural human resources are essential for organizational globalization, yet effectively managing cross-cultural motivation while reducing work withdrawal behavior remains challenging. Drawing on the Job Demands–Resources model and Self-Determination Theory, this study investigates how compulsory citizenship behavior influences work withdrawal behavior through the sequential mediation of extrinsic and intrinsic work motivation among 1658 cross-strait employees from Mainland China and Taiwan. Results indicate that the mediation pathway operates consistently across groups, although its strength varies: the negative effect is strongest for Mainlanders ( β = −0.16), followed by Taiwanese in Mainland ( β = −0.13), and remains statistically significant, though weaker, for Taiwanese ( β = −0.10), whereas it is not statistically significant for Mainlanders in Taiwan ( β = 0.002). This observed variability suggests a potential “culture–institution activation effect,” defined as the relatively stronger transformation from extrinsic to intrinsic motivation when cultural norms and institutional factors are aligned. Under these aligned conditions, motivational transformation appears more pronounced, which may influence employees’ behavioral responses to organizational pressures. By highlighting both universal and context-dependent aspects of motivational processes, this study contributes to the integration of JD-R and SDT frameworks and provides practical guidance for managing transcultural talent and improving work engagement in Chinese cultural settings.

title: Decoding the urban energy transition of the Yangtze River Economic Belt: spatio-temporal trends and predictor contributions via interpretable machine learning
abstract: This study constructs a proxy-based, multidimensional composite urban energy transition (ET) index from energy-consumption pressure, industrial-structure upgrading and energy-efficiency improvement for 108 cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB) from 2006 to 2022. Global Moran’s I, LISA time paths and spatio-temporal transitions are combined with chronologically validated tree-based ensemble models, and SHAP is used to interpret relative predictive contributions, non-linear associations and pairwise interactions. The index generally increased, displaying a pattern of downstream leadership, midstream improvement and upstream differentiation. Annual Moran’s I values were positive and statistically significant, with a mean of 0.4141. Type I represented the largest LISA transition category, while the spatio-temporal variability rate (46.30%) exceeded spatio-temporal cohesion (39.81%), indicating more pronounced stage-specific adjustment than cohesive movement under the adopted classification. GBDT achieved the best overall validation and test performance and was selected for interpretation. SHAP ranked social development (x2), land use (x9), economic development (x1), renewable-energy resource endowment (x6) and scientific research (x3) as the five leading predictors. Their contributions were non-linear and spatially heterogeneous, with more stable positive contributions downstream and greater variation in the middle and upper reaches. The strongest pairwise interactions were x1–x9, x2–x9, and x1–x2, showing that predictive contributions varied with the combination of economic development, social development, and spatial allocation. These findings provide a reference for formulating differentiated green development policies and improving composite urban ET performance in the YREB.

title: Investigating the spatial distribution of China’s Dong ethnic drum towers: influencing factors and synergistic dynamics with human activity patterns
abstract: China is a quintessential multi-ethnic integrated nation, where extensive cultural heritages have emerged through the process of ethnic convergence. The Dong ethnic drum tower stands as a highly regarded example. Although numerous studies have thoroughly examined the spatial features, construction techniques, and the relationship between drum towers and Dong settlements, the role of drum towers as cultural heritage in supporting the social organizational functions of these settlements remains insufficiently understood from a scientific perspective. This study therefore investigates the spatial distribution characteristics of Dong drum towers within settlements in Guizhou Province, China, employing space syntax and correlation analysis. The findings reveal that: (1) Dong drum towers are consistently situated at the core of Dong villages, exhibiting low spatial depth and high integration; (2) the areas surrounding drum towers serve critical roles in transportation connectivity and community social interaction; and (3) this research not only contributes actionable insights for the scientific preservation of Dong drum tower heritage, but also offers inspiration for the protection of similar point-like cultural heritage sites, thereby advancing the sustainable development of cultural heritage on a global scale.

title: From “DeepSeek Moment” to “Sputnik AI Moment”: Appraising the discursive construction of technological legitimacy in Sino-American Media
abstract: Integrating Appraisal Theory with Critical Discourse Analysis, this study examines how mainstream Chinese and U.S. media construct distinct evaluative stances towards DeepSeek AI. Drawing on a corpus of 40 reports, the research scrutinizes three primary types of targets (product/technology, organization/actor, and impact/consequence) following the paradigm of statistical description, semantic interpretation, and critical explanation. Findings indicate divergent evaluative patterns: Chinese outlets explicitly legitimize DeepSeek’s rise through positive Valuation and Capacity resources, combining moral evaluation with rationalization to cast it as a “DeepSeek Moment”. The U.S. media, despite a journalistically balanced tendency, implicitly lean toward de-legitimation through negative Propriety and Veracity (moral evaluation) and evocation of Insecurity (mythopoesis), constructing a “Sputnik AI Moment” framework. Anchored by recontextualization and intertextuality within narratives of human welfare versus zero-sum competition, this contrast highlights deeper ideological struggles for the discursive power to construe the semiotic reality and define the global technological landscape. Ultimately, this study demonstrates how technological news discourse functions as a constitutive medium in the geopolitical landscape in the digital age.

title: Emotional and behavioral problems in children of parents with severe mental illness in Wuhan, China: the roles of child maltreatment and exposure to parental victimization
abstract: Guided by a developmental-ecological and trauma-informed framework, children of parents with severe mental illness (SMI) may develop emotional and behavioral problems (EBPs) through inherited vulnerability, disrupted caregiving, socioeconomic adversity, stigma, and trauma-related exposures. However, the roles of direct trauma (child maltreatment, operationalized here as emotional and physical abuse) and indirect trauma (exposure to parental victimization) remain poorly understood. This study investigated the prevalence of child maltreatment and exposure to parental victimization and their associations with EBPs among Chinese children of parents with SMI. Trained staff conducted interviews during home visits with 369 children aged 8–17 years (mean age: 12.6 years; 52.8% boys) living with a parent with SMI, along with the child’s primary caregiver or guardian. Child maltreatment and parental victimization were assessed via standardized questions, with child maltreatment referring specifically to emotional and physical abuse, and EBPs were measured using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire. Logistic regression and classification tree analysis (CTA) were used to examine associations and interaction pathways, respectively. Among the participants, 15.7% of children reported at least one type of child maltreatment (emotional: 14.9%; physical: 7.3%), and 19.8% witnessed at least one type of parental victimization (emotional: 16.3%; physical: 13.6%). Child maltreatment and parental victimization, as well as their subtypes, were independently associated with EBPs (adjusted ORs: 2.05–4.72, P ≤ 0.025). CTA revealed interaction patterns between parental physical victimization and physical abuse of the child, and between parental emotional victimization and emotional abuse of the child, in relation to EBPs. Within the broader ecological risks faced by families affected by SMI, direct and indirect trauma were prevalent and were significantly associated with EBPs in children. These findings suggest that trauma-related exposures may represent salient proximal pathways linking parental SMI to child mental health difficulties and support trauma-informed assessment and care.

title: Correction: Elucidating university students’ intentions to seek automated writing feedback from Grammarly: toward perceptual and systemic predictors
abstract: Correction to: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-024-03861-1 , published online 18 August 2025

title: Festivities at the edge of data: an interdisciplinary study of Andean festivals in wikidata
abstract: This article examines how two Andean ritual traditions, Qoyllur Rit’i and the Virgen del Carmen of Paucartambo, are structurally represented within Wikidata. Using a compact knowledge graph extracted from Wikidata through ritual, geographic, heritage, and classificatory relations, we combine Louvain community detection, k-core coreness, and complementary network measures to analyze their relational embedding. The results show a tension between two forms of computational visibility. Qoyllur Rit’i is associated with a broader national-regional cluster but remains outside the innermost structural core, while the Virgen del Carmen of Paucartambo appears in a small ritual-specific community and occupies an outer core level. Institutional and geopolitical entities, together with heritage-classification entities, occupy the structural core of the graph. We interpret these patterns not as direct measures of cultural significance, but as evidence of how Wikidata’s semantic model, classification properties, linking practices, and editorial accumulation make some cultural relations more visible than others. The paper contributes to digital humanities and critical heritage studies by showing how graph analysis can serve as a diagnostic tool for examining the limits of linked open data in representing ritual practices, collective memory, and embodied forms of cultural knowledge.

title: From family to school and society: a sustainable model of intergenerational learning developed in China
abstract: Abstract Intergenerational learning provides support for resolving intergenerational conflicts brought about by differentiated life courses. Existing research has primarily concentrated on examining the motivations for and impacts of intergenerational learning, while the process through which it is sustainably created has not yet been systematically documented. Intergenerational learning, as observed across familial, educational, and societal contexts in Eastern China, serves as a significant source of novel insights. We developed a comprehensive theoretical framework with family-school-society cooperation and intergenerational learning models. Fourteen participants, including principals, teachers, parents, grandparents, older adult learners, and grandchildren, were recruited as interviewees guided by the qualitative research paradigm. The study found that theorists and practitioners collaborate to promote the process of intergenerational learning from family to school and society. Guided by theoretical insights, the principal led a ‘family intergenerational learning’ project which aims to employ the blood relations to address intergenerational conflicts. Driven by family-school cooperation and an age-friendly school, the primary school has established a ‘school intergenerational learning’ model by encouraging grandparents and grandchildren to participate in classroom learning together. Capitalizing on the growing connectivity among educational institutions, the primary school forged a collaborative partnership with an older adult school and a community school to develop an institutionalized model of ‘social intergenerational learning’. Overall, this study proposes a new theoretical framework from the perspective of home-school-community collaboration to reveal the practical logic of intergenerational learning. Furthermore, this study offers practical implications and policy insights for addressing challenges associated with population aging through the facilitation of intergenerational learning.

title: Gender differences in indirect associations between mental health symptoms and academic performance: the role of perceived school climate in rural Chinese boarding high schools
abstract: Adolescents in rural Chinese boarding schools spend most of their time on campus, making perceived school climate (PSC) a central context for learning and well-being. However, evidence remains limited on whether PSC is cross-sectionally associated with both mental health symptoms (MHS) and academic performance (AP), and whether these associations differ by gender in boarding settings. Guided by ecological systems theory, this cross-sectional study used multi-group structural equation modeling (SEM) with 322 students from four rural boarding high schools to examine associations among MHS, PSC, and AP. MHS were assessed with the Chinese-adapted DASS-21 (depression, anxiety, stress); PSC with an adapted EDSCLS (relationships, safety, engagement); and AP with a composite of standardized exam scores and teacher ratings. After establishing measurement invariance across gender, we specified hypothesized associational paths and tested whether the indirect association varied by gender. Results indicate higher MHS related to less favorable PSC, and less favorable PSC related to lower AP, yielding a negative indirect association for both girls and boys; its magnitude did not differ reliably by gender. Sensitivity analyses produced similar overall fit. Given the cross-sectional design, findings are interpreted as associations, underscoring the need for longitudinal and intervention studies.

title: Institutional design, game dilemmas and rule restructuring: the evolution and optimization of China’s multi-level protection scheme of cybersecurity
abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s digital transformation, the Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) has evolved into the core institutional pillar of the nation’s cybersecurity governance, yet its implementation confronts severe market dysfunctions, including cut-throat price competition and degradation of evaluation quality. This study undertakes a systematic examination of the three-decade evolution of China’s MLPS, delineating it into foundational, legalization, and strengthening stages, thereby revealing its core institutional logic centered on the “balancing cybersecurity and digital development.” Drawing on an interdisciplinary framework integrating institutional economics, administrative law, and game theory, this study unpacks the deep-rooted strategic dilemmas driving market distortions in the MLPS evaluation ecosystem. These dilemmas encompass the Prisoner’s Dilemma among evaluation institutions, information asymmetry between regulators and institutions, misalignment of interests within multi-layer principal-agent relationships, and the absence of repeated game mechanisms. Leveraging empirical data on MLPS evaluation institutions and regulatory penalties spanning from 2017 to 2025, the study identifies the institutional roots of market distortions, attributing it primarily to deficient incentive and constraint mechanisms. Consequently, it proposes a systematic optimization path anchored in the principles of proportionality, reliance protection, and the accountability, involving substantive rule restructuring and complementary implementation mechanisms. This study addresses a notable gap in the literature by systematically theorizing the interplay between MLPS institutional design and market outcomes. Furthermore, it offers an empirically grounded Chinese perspective on the evolution of cybersecurity governance, with actionable implications for jurisdictions seeking to balance security mandates with market efficiency in digital transformation.

title: Trauma healing through music in McEwan’s The Children Act
abstract: Abstract Previous scholarly inquiries into Ian McEwan’s The Children Act have predominantly been conducted through the prism of psychology, illuminating various facets of his exploration of the pains and dilemmas people face. However, few have addressed the close connection between music and healing from trauma in the novel.
