The main findings are as follows: (1) Northeast China exhibits a widespread trend of population shrinkage, with Heilongjiang and Jilin provinces being the most significantly affected. As the central city of Jilin, Changchun demonstrates a pronounced siphoning effect, intensifying population loss in surrounding regions. The economic resilience index across the region displays an overall decline yet exhibits considerable spatial heterogeneity: Heilongjiang shows marked internal disparities, whereas Jilin and Liaoning provinces demonstrate convergent downward trajectories. (2) The spatial linkage structures of the population shrinkage network and the economic resilience network demonstrate substantial dissimilarities. In the population shrinkage network, provincial capitals and regional hub cities function as core nodes, exhibiting high network centrality. Conversely, the economic resilience network is predominantly sustained by resource-based cities as pivotal nodes. Owing to industrial path dependence, these cities have developed distinctive regional mutual-support mechanisms, which contribute to maintaining high network centrality. (3) The relationship between the population shrinkage network and the economic resilience network exhibits a clear spatial scale effect. QAP analysis at the full-network level reveals a weak and statistically insignificant correlation, indicating that the two networks have evolved through relatively independent pathways. However, at the node level, nine cities display statistically significant correlations, five exhibiting positive associations and four demonstrating negative relationships, reflecting differentiated urban resilience mechanisms in responding to population shrinkage. The policy implications indicate that enhancing economic resilience and mitigating population shrinkage necessitate regionally differentiated strategies. Core cities should reinforce coordinated development mechanisms to harness agglomeration advantages, while resource-based cities must overcome path dependency and foster new drivers of resilience through industrial diversification and innovation. This study offers a novel analytical framework and a robust decision-making foundation for deciphering the complex interactions within population-economy systems and advancing sustainable regional development.

title: An improved interval fuzzy GRA-TOPSIS model for sustainable investment decision-making of oil and gas blocks
abstract: Abstract Facing volatile oil prices, strict ecological regulations and complex geological conditions, traditional multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) methods for oilfield investment overemphasize economic benefits while ignoring non-economic indicators and attribute uncertainty. To solve these deficiencies, this paper proposes an improved MADM framework for oil and gas development investment decision-making. Firstly, a five-dimensional evaluation index system covering economic, technological, geological, ecological and social attributes is established. Secondly, interval-valued fuzzy numbers (IVFNs) and interval fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (IF-AHP) are adopted to quantify index weights and address decision uncertainty. Furthermore, grey relational analysis (GRA) and technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) are combined to rank development schemes. A case study of six oilfield blocks in China verifies the reliability of the proposed framework. The results indicate that this method can effectively reduce decision bias and comprehensively characterize multidimensional attributes. This study provides a systematic decision-making tool for oilfield investment optimization and offers references for the sustainable development of oil and gas resources.

title: Ambidextrous leadership and enterprises’ sustainable innovation capabilities: the chain mediating role of organizational innovation climate and employee innovative behavior
abstract: Sustainable innovation serves as an inexhaustible driving force for enterprise development, yet few studies have explored the impact of ambidextrous leadership on an enterprise’s sustainable innovation capability. This study adopts ambidextrous leadership as its starting point, introducing organizational innovation climate and employee innovation behavior as two mediating variables. It constructs a chained mediation model to examine the relationship mechanism of ambidextrous leadership on enterprise sustainable innovation capability, thereby enriching research on the factors affecting sustainable innovation capability. Empirical analysis was conducted on 311 valid questionnaire responses using SPSS 27.0 and PROCESS, employing multiple regression and the Bootstrap method to test the proposed research hypotheses. The results show that: ambidextrous leadership is positively associated with enterprise sustainable innovation capability, and ambidextrous leadership style shows a stronger positive association with enterprise sustainable innovation capability is better than that of a single leadership style, organizational innovation climate and employee innovative behavior play a partial mediating role in the above relationships, and the mediation chain formed by both of them plays a chain mediating role. The research findings not only reveal the “black box” mechanism through which ambidextrous leadership influences sustainable innovation capability but also provide new insights for enterprises seeking to improve their sustainable innovation capability.

title: Digital Innovation Ecosystems in Agriculture: A Systematic Review–Based Framework
abstract: Abstract The agriculture sector has witnessed a significant digital transformation in recent years. Large companies, governments, and entities have invested efforts to create and orchestrate innovation ecosystems in the field. Such ecosystems may not only stimulate productivity and economic gains but also support agricultural sustainability. This article contributes to the topic by proposing a theoretical model to guide the development and implementation of digital innovation ecosystems in agriculture. We adopted a systematic approach to review the extant literature and organize the findings into a coherent framework and research propositions. Our study summarizes the (1) contextual factors, (2) processes, (3) members, (4) goals, (5) features, (6) services, (7) outcomes, and (8) challenges innovation ecosystems may face to consolidate. Despite the growing interest in digital innovation ecosystems in agriculture, knowledge on the subject remains sparse and fragmented. Our study organizes the literature and provides a set of propositions that guide future research.

title: Catalyst or constraint? Academic independent directors and corporate consciousness of climate change under ESG practice
abstract: This study investigates the role of academically experienced independent directors (AIDs) in shaping firms’ climate risk consciousness in Chinese listed companies. Using a panel dataset from 2008 to 2023 and fixed effects regression models, we find that a higher proportion of AIDs significantly enhances firms’ climate risk consciousness. The effect operates through two mechanisms: improving the quality of corporate information disclosure and shaping executives’ environmental cognition. The influence of AIDs is stronger in firms with low managerial ownership, weaker internal ESG performance, higher analyst coverage, and in regions with stricter environmental regulations. The study contributes to the literature by examining the previously underexplored impact of AIDs on corporate environmental awareness, identifying key moderating factors, and highlighting the role of China’s Confucian cultural context in shaping board effectiveness. These findings provide practical implications for policymakers and corporate practitioners regarding board composition and the integration of academic expertise to promote corporate sustainability.

title: Leadership for sustainable innovation: understanding the role of visionary leadership in digital transformation
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the role of visionary leadership in fostering sustainable innovation amid digital transformation, focusing specifically on the city of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. As the Kingdom undergoes a profound socio-economic shift under Vision 2030, leadership has emerged as a critical driver in aligning organizational practices with national sustainability and digitalization goals. Employing an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, the research first conducted qualitative interviews with public and private sector leaders, identifying four major themes: Vision as a Strategic Compass, Culture of Empowerment and Experimentation, Digital Transformation as a Sustainability Enabler, and Barriers Rooted in Institutional and Cultural Structures. A subsequent quantitative phase, involving 175 survey participants, validated these findings through descriptive and inferential statistics, including regression and exploratory path analysis. Results indicated that visionary leadership was significantly and positively associated with sustainable innovation outcomes, both directly and indirectly through empowerment culture and digital technology integration. Conversely, institutional and cultural barriers were shown to inhibit innovation potential. The study proposes a region-specific conceptual model capturing the complex interrelations between leadership, sustainability, and digital capability, moderated by institutional context. This research contributes theoretically by contextualizing global leadership frameworks within the Arab Gulf and practically by offering actionable insights for leaders, policymakers, and digital transformation strategists. It highlights the need for adaptive leadership strategies that are both technologically progressive and culturally sensitive in driving sustainable futures.

title: Institutional legitimacy and voluntary environmental certification: diffusion mechanisms of green factory standards in China
abstract: Abstract In the context of global sustainable development and the “dual carbon” goals, environmental protection has become a crucial issue that cannot be ignored in the economic development of various countries. In particular, the Pearl River Delta region, as an important base for China’s manufacturing industry, is facing huge pressures and challenges in accelerating transformation and promoting green development. This paper selects the data of A-share manufacturing listed companies in the Pearl River Delta region from 2014 to 2021 as the research sample and uses methods such as the multi-period difference-in-differences model to examine the non-binding impact of green factory certification on non-certified enterprises. Furthermore, through channels such as resource acquisition, market competition, and information disclosure, the study analyzes how green factory certification influences the environmental protection investment behavior of non-certified enterprises. The research finds that green factory certification has a significant positive effect on the environmental investment of non-certified companies. It also reveals an inverted U-shaped relationship between the number of green factories and the environmental investment of non-certified companies. Additionally, the article points out that in regions with weaker mandatory environmental regulations, the non-binding impact of voluntary environmental regulations is more significant.

title: From divine curse to technological salvation: the human quest for liberation from toil
abstract: Historically, within Western frameworks, the burden of labor has been contextualized through a theological narrative: labor as a form of ontological toil rooted in the biblical curse of Genesis 3:17. This paradigm established work as a divinely ordained existential endurance demanding moral submission. However, successive scientific revolutions disrupted this narrative, giving rise to modern technology as an ideological means of seeking mastery over nature. This paper analyzes the dialectical tension between the existential parameters of biblical labor and the mechanistic assertions of contemporary technological systems—a phenomenon Neil Postman conceptualizes as Technopoly. I argue that contemporary technological systems have transcended mere utility, operating as a surrogate technical deity that renders the biblical curse of labor obsolete. By offering a secularized salvation predicated on efficiency and automation, Technopoly repositions itself as the ultimate agent of material redemption. This promise culminates in the vision of the “End of Work,” reframing liberation not as a deferred spiritual afterlife, but as an immanent technological reality—the realization of a modern, earthly heaven. Engaging critically with thinkers from John Paul II and Bulgakov to Postman, Francis, and Stiegler, this paper maps the positive virtues of this post-work heaven, its existential boundaries, and the enduring ontological question of whether an automated paradise can truly satisfy humanity’s historic longing for the Transcendent or render it entirely obsolete.

title: Evaluating the affordance and intellectual structures of 3D virtual world language learning: a co-citation analysis
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the affordance of 3D virtual world language learning (3DVWLL) by using the co-citation approach. Previous studies report the effective implementation affordance regarding immersive learning experiences, communicative language strategies, and a versatile integration of digital learning materials (Lin & Lan, 2015; Reisoğlu et al., Avgousti, 2018; AUTHOR & COLLEAGUE, 2020). However, a unified account is still required to explain the diverse and incoherent achievements the reviews demonstrate. The objectives of the current study are two-fold. The first one serves to depict the intellectual structure among the core studies of this field and to recognize the theoretical roots in comparison to SLA’s intellectual structure (Zheng, 2019). The second one is to provide pedagogical norms for language education as a resource for evaluating teaching plans when practitioners integrate 3DVWs into course designs. The methods of co-citation analysis include (i) document co-citation analysis (DCA) to identify the associations among studies within a discipline and (ii) social network analysis (SNA) to represent the complex relationships among research streams. The results revealed a well-established intellectual structure of the 3DVWLL research field, comprising highly co-cited pairs and research streams from 2000 to 2024. Such findings indicate high scholarly collaboration among researchers, based on the cascaded linkage among issues revealed through document co-citation analysis and the primary and isolated components identified through social network analysis. The results of the co-citation analysis substantiated the philosophical roots of learning cognition, pedagogical ecology, and their relation to SLA theories. The study further proposes three implementing principles for task design, learning activities, and learning cognition. To conclude, 3DVWs not only represent a practical technological resource in language pedagogy but also contribute to the theoretical development of SLA.

title: Effects of emotions on concentration and usage intention to short video viewing among older adults
abstract: Abstract Concentration and usage intention levels in elderly short video viewers are investigated in relation to emotional influences. The experiment included three short video groups corresponding to positive, neutral, and negative emotional categories. Eye-tracking technology was used to capture real-time changes in the elderly's concentration, and an OpenCV-based facial emotion recognition system recorded their facial expressions. Additionally, a scale assessed four indicators: information acceptance, valence, concentration, and usage intention. Results showed that high-intensity emotions like “happy,” “anger,” and “surprised” significantly enhance concentration. However, while valence and addiction do not have a straightforward positive correlation, the bipolarity of valence levels (very high or very low) notably impacts usage intention. This indicates that strong emotions can enhance the concentration of elderly viewers and also increase their intention to use.

title: Understanding the relationship between socioeconomic status and mathematical literacy through computational thinking
abstract: Abstract In the 21st century, students have much easier access to information. Therefore, in this era, students are expected to do more than simply access information; they must also interpret and structure it and use it effectively to solve problems. The development of students’ ability to produce solutions to real-life problems is considered to depend not only on individual effort but also on interaction with socioeconomic conditions and cognitive structures. This study examines the statistical indirect association of self-reported computational thinking in the relationship between socioeconomic status and mathematical literacy. The sample of this study consisted of 520 eighth-grade students selected from eight public schools in five districts in Turkey. Analyses conducted using structural equation modelling indicated that socioeconomic status was positively associated with self-reported computational thinking and mathematical literacy. Additionally, self-reported computational thinking showed a significant indirect association between these two variables. These findings should be interpreted as evidence of statistical associations rather than causal mechanisms, given the cross-sectional design of the study and the self-reported nature of the computational thinking measure. The results suggest that students’ self-reported computational thinking tendencies may be associated with differences in mathematical literacy across socioeconomic backgrounds, while future longitudinal and performance-based studies could further clarify these relationships.

title: From familial obligations toward individual choice? Embodied cultural capital and fertility beliefs in contemporary China
abstract: Abstract In contemporary Chinese society, embodied cultural capital plays a crucial role in the detraditionalization of fertility beliefs. However, empirical evidence on this association remains limited, and the attitudinal pathways linking cultural resources to fertility beliefs have not been sufficiently clarified. This study examines how embodied cultural capital relates to traditional fertility beliefs among Chinese adults, with particular attention to gender role attitudes and pursuit of marriage as two related attitudinal pathways. Using data from the nationally representative 2021 China General Social Survey, this study applies linear regression models to assess the association between embodied cultural capital and traditional fertility beliefs. Interaction models are used to explore group heterogeneity, and stepwise regression is applied to examine the two attitudinal pathways. The findings reveal that embodied cultural capital significantly reduces adherence to traditional fertility beliefs among the Chinese people, and significant differences in this effect were observed across groups. Specifically, this weakening effect was less pronounced among married and male individuals. Furthermore, embodied cultural capital indirectly weakens adherence to traditional fertility beliefs through two primary mechanisms: enhancing egalitarian gender role attitudes and strengthening a personal-happiness-oriented pursuit of marriage. These results suggest that embodied cultural capital impacts fertility beliefs through both direct and indirect pathways, with the latter primarily mediated by gender role attitudes and the pursuit of marriage as key subjective mechanisms.

title: A multilevel analysis of factors influencing quality of cultivating innovative practice ability in Chinese professional degree programs
abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s growing demand for high-level applied talents, this study adopts Bandura’s Social Learning Theory to explore multilevel factors influencing the quality of cultivating innovative and practical ability among professional degree postgraduates. It constructs an analytical framework encompassing three core dimensions: students’ internal motivation and practical competence, the guidance capacity of dual-supervisors, and the supportive role of practical teaching environments. Using structural equation modeling (SEM) with data from 196 valid survey responses, the research empirically examines both direct and indirect impacts of these factors on the depth and breadth of capability development. Key findings reveal that students’ intrinsic motivation and practical literacy, dual-supervisors’ ethical standards and instructional expertise, and well-equipped, policy-supported, innovation-oriented practice bases significantly enhance cultivation outcomes. These results not only provide theoretical insights into the mechanisms of capability formation but also offer practical guidance for universities and policymakers to optimize talent cultivation strategies. By bridging the gap between academic theory and industrial practice, the study contributes to advancing China’s high-quality, practice-oriented postgraduate education system and addressing industry demands for skilled professionals.

title: Validating the Psychological Entitlement Scale (PES) in older adults and testing its cross-age measurement invariance
abstract: Abstract Psychological entitlement is often associated with maladaptive traits and negative behaviors and leads to interpersonal problems. This study examined the validity of the Psychological Entitlement Scale (PES) in the older adult population and its equivalence across age groups. In Study 1, we surveyed 1826 older adults. and conducted item analysis, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), Cronbach’s alpha, and McDonald’s omega. Building on Study 1, we surveyed an additional sample of 3730 adults and 2374 emerging adults in Study 2 to examine the measurement invariance of the PES across the adult lifespan. EFA extracted a single factor explaining 70.91% of the variance, with factor loadings ranging from 0.75 to 0.88 and communalities from 0.56 to 0.78. CFA showed that the single-factor model fit well (χ²/df = 4.821, RMSEA = 0.067, SRMR = 0.018, CFI = 0.988, IFI = 0.988, TLI = 0.978). In Study 2, we found that the PES exhibits measurement equivalence across different age groups. Moreover, the psychological privilege of older adults is significantly higher than that of adults and emerging adults. The PES has good reliability and validity and can be used as a valid tool to assess the psychological privilege of Chinese older adults.

title: Data scraping for AI model training and data privacy: a comparative analysis of United States and European Union Data Privacy Laws
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has made data not only the choicest but also a very susceptible commodity. Even before the recent boom in AI, data was regarded as the new oil of the digital era. However, AI has amplified this due to its dependence on data for training AI models. In sourcing data for AI training, the internet is a rich resource with abundant data. Consequently, companies engage in massive data scraping to provide sufficient data for effective AI model training. Meanwhile, scraping often involves unauthorized access to information on websites or internet platforms, thereby raising legal concerns, including privacy-related issues. In this note, the authors explore the intersection between AI model training and data scraping using a doctrinal research method, further interrogating the lawfulness of scraping under extant data privacy laws in the United States (U.S.) and the European Union (EU). Findings show that in the U.S., scraping data for AI may be permissible as long as the scraped data is publicly accessible. On the other hand, data scraping of publicly available personal data violates the EU data protection laws, unless it satisfies the lawful basis requirements of Article 6 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Whilst data scraping is not per se illegal under EU law, it is almost unjustifiable in light of the stringent requirements of Article 6 of the GDPR. Despite these stringent requirements, it is worth noting that in practice, the enforcement of the provisions of GDPR by the Data Protection Authority (DPA) has not been uniform across member states, considering the lenient approach in some jurisdictions. Regardless of the differences in the U.S. and EU jurisdictions, further analysis shows that data scraping generally undermines data privacy, as it operates against the very principles that underpin privacy protection. Underscoring the importance of data scraping to AI and innovation more broadly, the authors suggest reconciling data scraping with data privacy by rethinking and reforming extant privacy laws.

title: Audit quality and ESG-corporate sustainability performance: evidence on the mediating role of internal control system
abstract: Abstract With increasing pressure on companies to enhance their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reputation, auditing has become a critical tool for ESG compliance and accountability. Although the significance of audit quality in the promotion of corporate sustainability has been outlined by previous researchers, little has been said about the role of internal control system. This study fills this gap by examining the relationship between the audit quality and the ESG-corporate sustainability performance, with a particular emphasis on the mediating role of internal control system. A quantitative approach was applied by focusing on the top 100 largest companies listed in the Saudi Stock Exchange (TADAWUL). The results indicate that auditor expertise, compliance, and responsiveness play significantly affect ESG-corporate sustainability performance, without the same effect being detected for the auditor skepticism. Furthermore, auditor skills as well as responsiveness is positively associated with the internal control system that is also found to have a significant positive relationship with ESG-corporate sustainability performance. Notably, the internal control system was found to significantly mediate the relationship between auditor expertise, compliance, and responsiveness and ESG-corporate sustainability performance, but no mediating effect was found for auditor skepticism. This study contributes to the literature by revealing the mediating effect of internal control system, thereby enhancing the literature base in the field of study. Empirically, the study provides practical insights for stakeholders and policymakers on how audit quality through the internal control system can enhance ESG sustainability performance in the Saudi context.

title: Dancing with AI: how human-AI interaction affects employee task performance
abstract: The rapid increase in generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) products has revolutionised the interaction between humans and artificial intelligence. However, the conceptualisation, measurement, and performance implications of human-AI interaction in the workplace remain underexplored. This study utilised a grounded theory approach to explore the multidimensional construct of human-AI interaction. We then developed a measurement scale for human-AI interaction in the workplace using inductive and deductive methods. Finally, based on self-concept theory, we explored the mechanisms through which human-AI interaction is associated with task performance in the workplace. The results show that (1) human-AI interaction consists of three dimensions: anthropomorphic tool, adaptive trust, and unidirectional emotional connection. (2) The developed scale contained 19 items with good reliability and validity. (3) Human-AI interaction is positively associated with employees’ task performance, and role identity and self-efficacy partially mediate the relationship between human-AI interaction and task performance.

title: Empirical analysis of the impact of climate change on food and water security in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Abstract Even though climate change poses significant risks to food and water security, little attention has been paid to the dynamics of short- and long-term interactions between these two dimensions, especially in the context of Saudi Arabia. This paper aims to assess the influence of variations in climate parameters such as temperature, precipitation, and drought on food security (defined as agricultural output and food imports) and water security (measured by water consumption and groundwater levels) using annual data for 1990–2023. A vector error correction model (VECM) used to explore short-run dynamics and long-run relationships between the selected variables. Moreover, the Granger causality test applied to identify causalities within the food-water-climate nexus. According to the empirical findings, a one-degree centigrade increase in temperature decreases agricultural output by 0.28%, while a one-millimeter increase in precipitation contributes to a 0.31% growth in agricultural production. Additionally, the increase in drought frequency by one unit causes a rise in food imports by 0.41%, while an increase in water use by one unit contributes to a 0.39% fall in the underground water level. These results underscore the sensitivity of the Saudi Arabian food and water systems to climate change. It is therefore necessary for policymakers to embrace climate-resilient agriculture, enhance irrigation techniques, and diversify sources of food imports.

title: The influence of generative artificial intelligence on STEM education: a systematic review of recent empirical studies
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has emerged as a transformative force in STEM education, offering opportunities to enhance teaching and learning while presenting significant challenges. This systematic review employs the Activity Theory framework to analyze the influence of GenAI on STEM education systems, synthesizing findings from 61 empirical studies published between December 2022 and May 2025. The reviewed studies are predominantly situated in higher education contexts, and the conclusions drawn should be interpreted with this scope in mind. Guided by three research questions, the review first summarizes prior systematic reviews using a SWOT framework, identifying GenAI’s strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. Our review then examines the characteristics of the six components of the GenAI-integrated STEM education activity system—subject, object, community, tools, rules, and division of labour. Finally, we explore how GenAI, as a mediating tool, reshapes system dynamics, demonstrating its potential to foster personalized learning, support pedagogical innovation, and expand access to learning resources, while highlighting challenges such as over-dependence, reliability concerns, and ethical dilemmas. These findings underscore the necessity of responsible and thoughtful application of GenAI to maximize its benefits in STEM education while mitigating potential adverse effects. Our review demonstrates Activity Theory’s efficacy in providing a holistic understanding of GenAI’s role in STEM education and offers evidence-based recommendations for educators, policymakers, and researchers.

title: China certified emission reductions: legal nature, transactions and regulation
abstract: China’s carbon trading system centers on the carbon allowance market and the China Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) market. As a tradable carbon credit, CCER plays a crucial role in achieving low-cost emission reductions. The precise legal nature of CCER remains contested, and this lack of consensus introduces uncertainty into CCER transactions. Moreover, regulatory loopholes such as double counting, and greenwashing continue to undermine the integrity of the market. This article makes four arguements. First, it defines CCER as a “thing” under Chinese real right law, capable of being registered as a real right. Second, it explores the legal effects of CCER registration. Third, based on specific circumstances that may give rise to defective transactions, it proposes applying the doctrine of bona fide purchase to CCER transactions to enhance transaction reliability. Fourth, it identifies ways to strengthen CCER supervision and ensure the efficient execution of CCER trades.

title: Behavioral intentions for social drought protection: insights from the extended parallel process model
abstract: The impact of climate change-induced droughts necessitates comprehensive mitigation strategies. This study employed the Extended Parallel Process Model to analyze the factors influencing individuals’ behavioral intentions for social drought protection in South Korea. Using survey data from 1000 participants, this study explored the interplay among perceived threat levels, perceived efficacy, fear arousal, and fear control. The key findings revealed that (1) higher levels of perceived threat, perceived efficacy, and fear arousal were associated with greater intention to protect against drought, whereas higher fear control was associated with lower protection intention; (2) the discriminating value between perceived efficacy and threat level (DV) was negatively associated with fear arousal and positively associated with fear control; (3) fear control was negatively associated with fear arousal; (4) fear arousal and fear control mediate the relationship between DV and protection behavioral intention. By integrating psychological perspectives, this study provides insights into the development of targeted interventions for climate change adaptation, emphasizing a multidimensional approach beyond traditional paradigms.

title: Direct and moderating effects of generative AI on new user retention in social Q&A platforms: evidence from Stack Overflow
abstract: Social question-and-answer (Q&A) platforms such as Stack Overflow have experienced a significant decline in user engagement, following the rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including ChatGPT. Grounded in self-determination and motivational affordance theories, this study examines five motivational features—upvotes, downvotes, collaborative edits, user profile completion, and comments—that influence new user retention. Generative AI is introduced as a novel external factor exerting both direct and moderating effects. Hierarchical logistic regression was applied to a dataset of 10,000 newly registered Stack Overflow users to compare the user retention mechanisms before and after ChatGPT’s introduction. The results indicate that receiving upvotes or comments and user profile completion significantly promote continued participation, whereas downvotes and the emergence of generative AI reduce it. Following the advent of generative AI, the positive influence of user profile completion weakened, suggesting that autonomy-related needs may now be fulfilled through AI tools external to the platform. By contrast, the effects of votes and comments remained stable, likely because generative AI cannot replicate these social interactions. This study extends the motivational affordance framework by integrating the influence of emerging external technologies and offers practical insights for enhancing new user retention on social Q&A platforms in the generative AI era.

title: When nationalism meets environmentalism: an inverted U-curve linking national sentiment to carbon emission intensity through an institutional lens
abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of rising corporate carbon emissions, managerial attributes are garnering increasing scholarly scrutiny. Utilizing a panel dataset from China’s A-share market between 2010 and 2023, this paper employs an institutional theory perspective to examine the relationship between national sentiment and carbon emission intensity. We reveal a significant inverted U-shaped relationship between national sentiment and carbon emission intensity. Meanwhile, we also find that market competition negatively moderates the relationship between national sentiment and carbon emission intensity, whereas emission reduction target constrains and environmental penalties positively moderate it. Moreover, corporate social responsibility and green investment act as significant mediating channels in this relationship. Furthermore, national sentiment significantly influences enterprises characterized by high pollution, low subsidies, or low R&D intensity, and its impact on green patent, encompassing both green invention and green utility models still exhibits a significant inverted U-shaped relationship.

title: Breaking the barrier: exercise preferences and motivational factors in stressed Chinese secondary school students
abstract: This study explores the motivations, barriers, and exercise preferences among Chinese secondary school students experiencing psychological stress. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 29 adolescent students, and a deductive analysis was employed to identify key themes related to their exercise behaviors. To ensure objectivity and minimize bias, data were triangulated. The findings revealed seven motivational themes driving exercise participation, health benefits, external encouragement and supervision, body shaping, personal inspiration, academic performance, enjoyment, and prior exercise experiences. Conversely, five key barriers were identified: academic pressure, negative exercise experiences, lack of motivation, illness, and adverse weather conditions. Participants generally preferred moderate to vigorous group-based exercises lasting 30 to 60 min, 3–5 times per week. Gender differences emerged in both barriers and motivations: girls were more likely to forgo exercise due to academic demands, while boys cited illness as a primary obstacle. Additionally, girls reported needing more external encouragement to engage in exercise, whereas boys required greater personal inspiration. These insights can inform the design of targeted exercise programs to effectively reduce stress in this population.

title: Management accounting in the digital age: investigating the impact of big data analytics on decision-making processes
abstract: Abstract The study intended to examine the role of Big Data Analytics (BDA) affects on decision making practices in banking industry in Kingdom of Bahrain. The sampling method is used and relies on a descriptive analytical approach through a questionnaire to collect data from selected employees of a selected bank. To obtain the results, the study collected 90 respondents with multiple designations and profiles in banking sector who are dealing with big data in their routine working activities. The study revealed that there is a statistically significant positive correlation between BDA and decision-making timeliness, accuracy, and organizational performance enhancement. Furthermore, the research established a definite influence on improving risk management. To gain a sustained competitive edge, the study recommends implementing BDA in company strategy development, digital infrastructure improvement, and the development of human capital. This will strengthen the overall banking performance in Bahrain as well as reinforce the competitive advantage of banks. The implication of this study helps the policy makers, and leadership in the banking sector to deeply understand their decision outcome and have comprehensive plan before their key decision-making process.

title: How do characteristic elements of public spaces affect spatial vitality? An analysis of influence effects and response thresholds from the Hangzhou section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal
abstract: Spatial vitality is theoretically grounded in classic urban planning and human settlement theories, including Jane Jacobs’ Urban Diversity, Jan Gehl’s Social Space, and Kevin Lynch’s Image of the City . It is explicitly defined as a public space’s capacity to attract sustained recreational engagement and foster diverse social interaction, and it serves as a core metric for evaluating urban public space quality and human settlements development amid global stock-based urban renewal. This study addresses a well-documented critical gap: while macro- and meso-scale urban vitality research is oversaturated, prevailing analytical models are predominantly limited to linear correlation analysis. These models lack quantitative threshold-based causal inference for nonlinear vitality-generating mechanisms in micro-scale waterfront contexts. This study takes 56 micro-scale waterfront public spaces along the UNESCO World Heritage Hangzhou Section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal as its research samples. It develops a “built environment-functional activity-spatial vitality” analytical framework, first identifies core vitality drivers via correlation analysis, and finally quantifies nonlinear response thresholds for national Grade I vitality standards through Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) and Spatial Lag Model (SLM)-corrected regression that controls for spatial spillover effects. Results reveal locational centrality, public transport station accessibility, water surface ratio, cultural and sports facility density, and functional integration degree as core vitality drivers. These drivers present heterogeneous thresholds across ecological conservation, commercial-business, and residential living functional typologies, a difference that is interpreted as driven by divergent user demands and context-specific vitality generation pathways. This study advances prevailing linear correlation-focused models by establishing typology-specific, quantifiable thresholds for vitality enhancement. It explicates the core “built environment optimization-functional activity catalysis-sustained vitality generation” mechanism, and further provides empirically grounded, threshold-informed planning guidance and a replicable analytical framework for micro-scale urban public space vitality research.

title: A comparative study of history of science, philosophy of science, and combined instruction on students’ understanding of the nature of science in a Chinese high school context
abstract: Despite the empirical evidence for the role of the history and philosophy of science in science education, the independent effects of history and philosophy of science courses have not been comparatively studied. Hence, this study implemented three elective courses—philosophy of science, history of science, and history and philosophy of science—in Chinese high schools to explore their impact on students’ understanding of the nature of science, as conceptualized in the Family Resemblance Approach. It addresses the following question: to what extent do these courses influence students’ scientific perceptions in both cognitive-epistemic and social-institutional systems? Pre- and post-course questionnaires were used to assess changes in students’ views and compare the effects across the three instructional approaches. The results of this study showed that the philosophy of science course helped students improve their cognitive-epistemic systems. Meanwhile, students who took the other two courses improved their understanding of the nature of science in terms of both cognitive-epistemic and social-institutional systems. The results of this study provide valuable insights into the connection between the history and philosophy of science in the teaching process and offer practical implications for science education. However, given the small sample size and the non-random assignment of instructional groups, the findings should be interpreted with caution and warrant further investigation in more diverse and representative contexts.

title: Digital technology application and corporate green innovation: digital financial inclusion as an institutional turning point in China
abstract: Digital transformation is widely expected to support corporate green innovation, yet existing studies offer limited insight into when and under what conditions digitalization reshapes firms’ innovation behavior. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms during 2014–2023, this study examines whether digital financial inclusion conditions the relationship between digital technology application and green innovation. A panel threshold regression approach is used to identify whether changes in the institutional financial environment alter firms’ innovation decision-making logic. The results show that digital technology application is positively associated with green innovation, but this effect exhibits a clear threshold pattern. When digital financial inclusion remains below a critical level, the effect is limited. Once the threshold is crossed, the effect increases substantially, indicating a shift from resource substitution to strategic complementarity. Further analysis shows that green invention innovation responds to digitalization only at higher levels of digital financial inclusion, whereas utility-model green innovation benefits at lower levels. The threshold effect is more pronounced for non-state-owned enterprises, pollution-intensive firms, firms with limited internal cash flow and firms operating in less competitive markets. These findings demonstrate that the impact of digital technology application on green innovation depends on institutional financial maturity rather than following a uniform pattern.

title: Applying Natural Language Processing to Address Healthcare Bias: Using CARE-SD to Evaluate the Distribution of Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Notes
abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) are a critical medium through which patient stigmatization is perpetuated among healthcare teams. We identified doubt markers and stigmatizing labels in MIMIC-III, a de-identified EHR, via expanded lexicon matching and machine learning classifiers. Predictors of rates of linguistic features were assessed using Poisson models. We found higher rates of stigmatizing labels per chart among patients who were Black or African American (RR: 1.16), patients with Medicare/Medicaid or government-run insurance (RR: 2.46), self-pay (RR: 2.12), and patients with a variety of stigmatizing disease and mental health conditions (RR: 1.50–4.90). Patterns among doubt markers were similar, though male patients had higher rates of doubt markers (RR: 1.25). We found increased stigmatizing labels used by nurses (RR: 1.40), and social workers (RR: 2.25), with similar patterns of doubt markers. Stigmatizing language occurred at higher rates among historically stigmatized patients, perpetuated by multiple provider types.

title: Exploring the role of the body in learning: a mixed-method study of embodied learning in secondary education
abstract: The Flemish traditional educational system faces challenges concerning adolescents’ academic performance and overall well-being, as well as an increase in sedentary behaviour. To address these challenges, previous research advocates for a stronger emphasis on the development of student-centred and innovative didactic approaches that prioritise mental and physical well-being, while simultaneously enhancing academic achievement for all learners. One such approach is called embodied learning (EL), referring to the simultaneous acquisition of knowledge through physical activity. Although previous research in pre- and primary education has demonstrated positive associations, EL intervention studies in secondary education remain scarce, reveal inconclusive results and opt for future research focussing on longer interventions using mixed-method designs. In order to address some of these gaps, the current study pursued three main objectives adopting an explorative design: (1) To what extent does EL improve secondary school students’ academic performance (learning outcomes) compared to traditional seated learning? (2) To what extent does EL enhance secondary school students’ school-related well-being (emotions, feelings, and stress) compared to traditional seated learning? (3) To what extent does EL increase secondary school students’ physical activity levels (activity levels) compared to traditional seated learning? Both qualitative (focus groups) and quantitative (questionnaires, activity trackers and EL intervention) methods were employed in four Flemish secondary schools. Research questions 1 and 2 were addressed in a total sample of 348 students, while research question 3 was examined in a smaller subsample ( n = 40) from this cohort to assess physical activity levels. The findings of the current study point to preliminary positive associations between EL, learning outcomes, and specific aspects of school-related well-being. These associations appear to be influenced by contextual factors such as the physical learning environment and the habituation period required to adapt to simultaneously executing physical activity while learning. When the association between these contextual factors within the field of EL is further examined, a more movement-driven approach may hold potential to contribute to the Flemish educational landscape.

title: Enlightening the Anthropocene: reconsidering anthropocentrism for environmental education
abstract: Abstract This paper argues that the Anthropocene must be understood not primarily as a geological epoch but as an epistemic and ethical condition in which human action becomes inseparably entangled with natural and technological processes. In this hybrid world of “third nature,” the most urgent challenge is a pervasive misrecognition of humanity’s own role in shaping planetary systems. Against the objection that appeals to an undifferentiated humanity conceal specific interests, this misrecognition is reconstructed as unequally distributed and in part deliberately produced, which makes recognition a political rather than merely cognitive achievement. The paper develops the concept of Anthropocene enlightenment as a form of collective self-understanding that exceeds the individually addressed notion of Enlightenment. Because responsibility presupposes recognition, the primary educational task is argued to be hermeneutic before it is moral. Education emerges as the infrastructure of collective recognition, and is specified here in a worked pedagogical sequence.

title: Same event, different stories: a corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis of the 20th CPC National Congress in Chinese and US mainstream media
abstract: As China’s first major national congress in the post-pandemic era, the 20th CPC National Congress has considerable domestic and international influence. This study employs a corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis to investigate the divergent discursive constructions of the Congress across six mainstream Chinese and American media outlets. The findings reveal a clear dichotomy of representations. Chinese media predominantly reproduce official discourses and construct a positive narrative of the Congress by framing it as a pivotal event guiding China’s future trajectory. In contrast, American media tend to adopt a more critical perspective, presenting it as an occasion of political power transition and consolidation by amplifying expert and dissident interpretations. These disparities reflect the clash of underlying political ideologies and the intensifying narrative competition between the two countries. This study offers valuable insights into how mainstream media outlets function as ideological apparatuses that (re)construct political narratives and (re)shape global public perceptions.

title: Validating an instrument to assess realization of substantive and production well-being needs among native and migrant older adults in the Netherlands
abstract: Abstract Older adults’ well-being depends on fulfilling substantive needs (e.g., affection, comfort, stimulation) and production needs (e.g., control, avoidance of a loss frame). Validated instruments capturing both need types across culturally diverse populations are scarce. This study aimed to validate a combined instrument assessing substantive and production needs among Dutch, Surinamese-Dutch, Turkish-Dutch, and Moroccan-Dutch older adults and to examine group differences in need fulfilment and in life satisfaction as a global indicator of subjective well-being. Data were drawn from a representative sample of 862 older adults (65–98 years) in Rotterdam, stratified by migration background. Substantive needs were measured using the SPF-ILs, and production needs with the control and loss avoidance dimensions of the SPF-Q. Life satisfaction was assessed with Cantril’s ladder. Psychometric evaluation included confirmatory factor analysis, measurement invariance testing, internal consistency, and construct validity. Associations with migration background and life satisfaction were examined using regression analyses. Confirmatory factor analysis supported factorial validity (RMSEA = 0.032, CFI = 0.972, SRMR = 0.035), with good internal consistency across subscales ( α = 0.69–0.84). Measurement invariance held across gender and migration background. Native Dutch participants reported higher affection, comfort, stimulation and loss avoidance than Turkish- and Moroccan-Dutch older adults, higher control than Moroccan-Dutch older adults, and lower status than Turkish-Dutch older adults. Production needs, particularly loss avoidance, independently predicted life satisfaction and attenuated the effects of the five substantive needs. The combined SPF-ILs and SPF-Q is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing both substantive and production needs among culturally diverse older adults. Fulfilment of production needs, especially loss avoidance, plays a key role in sustaining life satisfaction, emphasizing the importance of capturing both the “what” and the “how” of well-being. This instrument offers a comprehensive framework for research and interventions supporting well-being in diverse aging populations.

title: Financial distress and ESG integration: a systematic review
abstract: The prediction of financial distress remains a critical concern for businesses, investors, and policymakers, as it enables proactive measures and informed decision-making to support sustainable growth. In the contemporary discourse on corporate finance, the relationship between financial distress and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) goals has assumed increasing significance. Despite the global emphasis on transparency and the disclosure of non-financial information, a consensus regarding the interpretation and impact of ESG disclosure remains lacking. This study aims to identify the major ESG indicators highlighted in the literature and to examine their relationship with financial distress. A systematic literature review was undertaken in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, focusing on studies published between 2015 and 2025 in the Scopus and Web of Science databases. A total of 50 articles were identified and assessed based on methodological rigor, thematic scope, and relevance. The findings suggest that, while traditional distress models rely primarily on financial ratios, recent research increasingly incorporates ESG metrics in predicting corporate vulnerability. However, such integration is inconsistent across sectors and regions, with outcomes depending on measurement consistency, methodological rigor, and contextual alignment. The study underscores the need for comprehensive, interdisciplinary approaches that connect corporate finance with sustainable development practices, advancing both theoretical and practical understanding.

title: Interpretation of Łukasiewicz’s Ł3 system with the hidden variable
abstract: Abstract It is generally believed that the law of excluded middle and the law of (non-)contradiction do not apply to Jan Łukasiewicz’s Ł 3 , and many attempts have been made to resolve the issue. Based on the “Interpretation with Hidden Variables” within the framework of the STRF (Special Theory of Relativity of Function), this paper, while fully accepting the syntax and maintaining the truth-value semantics of Ł 3 , demonstrates that the third value in Ł 3 1/2, is actually a combination of “true” and “not true”. Furthermore, this combination can exhibit different arrangements, meaning that there are distinct truth-value distributions corresponding to a single degree of truth. Consequently, it becomes evident that the law of excluded middle and the law of (non-)contradiction remain valid as theorems within Ł 3 . Thus, Ł 3 is simply a classical propositional logic system that has yet to be fully and correctly understood.

title: Barriers, motivations, and the path to gender parity in the maker communities
abstract: Abstract The maker movement, characterized by do-it-yourself (DIY) innovation and collaborative production, has emerged as a potential driver of skill development, sustainability, and community engagement. However, despite its potential to foster inclusive and circular economies, gender disparities persist in participation within makerspaces. This study investigates the motivations, barriers, and gender differences influencing engagement in European makerspaces, drawing on a comprehensive survey of over 6000 respondents across 28 European countries, including Turkey. Using principal component analysis (PCA), we identify distinct dimensions of motivations and barriers, revealing that women are more motivated by skill enhancement, community engagement, and sustainability but express greater challenges related to access to information, time constraints, and technical skills. Men, on the other hand, are more concerned with externalities such as environmental and health impacts. The study also highlights minor concerns about inclusivity, with both men and women expressing dissatisfaction with the representation of age, gender, and ethnic diversity in makerspaces. Despite these barriers, women demonstrate a greater willingness to visit maker communities and to use makerspace facilities compared to men, yet do not actually use them more, even not when they have first-hand experience with them, suggesting persistent gendered barriers within the maker spaces. The findings underscore the need for targeted interventions, such as accessible training programs, mentorship opportunities, and financial support, to bridge the gap between motivation and participation. We discuss the findings in terms of how equitable design and support of makerspaces can foster circular economy practices while enhancing access to community-based skill development.

title: Exploring the underlying roles of perceived social inequality in the relationship between internet use and fertility expectations in China
abstract: Abstract China’s declining fertility rate has attracted growing public concern. Understanding the determinants of individuals’ fertility intentions is crucial for optimizing fertility-related policies and promoting long-term population equilibrium. Drawing on data from the 2018 and 2022 waves of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), this study systematically examines the impact of Internet use on fertility intentions among people of reproductive age. The results indicate that Internet use significantly reduces fertility intentions (α = −0.1587, p < 0.01); the longer individuals use the Internet per day, the fewer children they intend to have (α = −0.0190, p < 0.01). This negative effect is more pronounced among females, individuals under 30, and residents in both eastern and western regions. The mediation analysis reveals that perceived social inequality serves as a key intermediary mechanism: Internet use amplifies individuals’ perceptions of income disparity, which lowers their subjective social status and, consequently, suppresses fertility intentions. Moreover, the moderating analysis shows that Confucian culture can partially buffer this adverse effect. Based on these findings, this paper recommends improving the credibility and dissemination quality of fertility-related public information to enhance individuals’ ability to evaluate and trust information sources; optimizing fertility support services for key demographic groups to reduce real-life pressures; strengthening the responsiveness of social policies to mitigate class-based anxiety; and fostering balanced interpretations of traditional cultural values to promote gender equity and sustain fertility intentions.

title: Unraveling how subsidy policies shape farmers’ fertilizer applications: implications for organic-chemical substitution
abstract: Organic fertilizers offer agronomic and ecological advantages over chemical fertilizers, making them critical for curbing chemical fertilizer overuse without threatening food security. While subsidies are commonly used to encourage organic-chemical substitution, less is known about how farmers respond to different subsidy levels and how such responses reshape economic and environmental trade-offs. Using survey data from 983 vegetable farmers in China, this study applies a farm-level positive mathematical programming model to simulate short-run input allocation under alternative organic fertilizer subsidy scenarios. The results show that higher subsidies increase organic fertilizer use and reduce chemical fertilizer use, but do not generate uniformly positive outcomes across policy dimensions. Subsidy-induced substitution is associated with lower operating profit excluding subsidy transfers, although the magnitude of this effect varies across crops. Environmental performance improves as substitution intensifies, but the marginal return to additional subsidy weakens at higher subsidy levels. The findings reveal trade-offs across target attainment, production-side profitability, and environmental improvement. Under the present short-run scenario design with fixed land endowments, a moderate subsidy range around 250–300 CNY/ton appears most policy-relevant, because it achieves or nearly achieves the stated substitution targets while avoiding the sharper economic deterioration observed at higher subsidy levels. The results suggest that effective policy design should calibrate subsidy intensity to policy objectives, crop heterogeneity, and complementary support measures.

title: Material minds: mapping care and learning across everyday objects
abstract: What can mapping care and learning across everyday material objects tell us about the human mind? Traditional perspectives have often treated objects as passive tools valued mainly for their utility or market worth. In contrast, psychological and cultural research has emphasized the psychological and identity-related significance of material objects. Building on prior human-object interaction (HOI) research, this study examines care and learning as two previously identified psychological dimensions characterizing meaningful engagement with material artefacts. Using a large-scale online survey of 3441 Japanese adults, we examined how object-related characteristics—such as ownership, shared memories, subjective irreplaceability, mental concentration, instrumentality, perceived monetary value, and difficulty of use—were associated with care and learning. Cluster analysis of 39 object types identified six distinct profiles of care and learning, indicating systematic variation across object types. Ownership, irreplaceability, and mental concentration showed positive adjusted associations with both care and learning, while shared memories were more strongly associated with learning. In contrast, usage duration and frequency were largely unrelated to either dimension, indicating that temporal exposure alone was not closely associated with care or learning. By mapping patterns of care and learning across diverse everyday objects, this study extends the HOI framework and provides an empirical basis for connecting it with research on the extended self. Because the study was cross-sectional, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. Overall, the results highlight the psychological significance of everyday material artefacts beyond their utility or market value and support closer attention to how people experience and relate to objects in contemporary material culture.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Restructuring of Saudi Labor Markets: A Statistical Analysis of Job Displacement and Skill Transformation
abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence into state-led rentier economies presents unique structural challenges, particularly within Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 framework. Utilizing a balanced panel dataset of 120 sector-year observations across 10 economic sectors over a 12-year period, this study examines the structural association between AI adoption and the employment share of Saudi nationals. To address prevalent limitations in composite index construction and prevent methodological overfitting, the analysis employs a parsimonious econometric strategy. The AI Adoption Index is rigorously validated through internal consistency testing (Cronbach’s α = 0.87) and PCA-based sensitivity analysis, ensuring robustness beyond arbitrary weighting conventions. The empirical framework relies on fixed-effects panel regression supplemented by an instrumental variable (IV) approach to mitigate potential endogeneity, alongside a comprehensive battery of diagnostic tests (Hausman, Modified Wald, and Wooldridge). The findings reveal a statistically significant negative association between AI adoption and national employment in routine-intensive sectors (β = −0.41, p < 0.05), contrasted by a positive correlation with high-skill digital competencies (β = +0.67, p < 0.01). Theoretically, these structural shifts are interpreted through a macro-sociological lens of digital labor segmentation, explicitly distinguishing between observable macro-level reconfigurations and micro-level subjective experiences without claiming to measure individual worker consciousness. The study concludes with targeted policy recommendations for inclusive AI governance and sector-specific upskilling, ensuring digital transition strategies align with the social equity objectives of the state.

title: Economic integration and carbon rebalancing in China’s grain functional zones
abstract: Achieving regionally coordinated and sustainable development has become an urgent global priority amid accelerating globalization and intensifying environmental challenges. In China, balancing agricultural carbon emission equity with regional economic integration is essential for addressing environmental justice and promoting low-carbon transformation. This study employs the coupling coordination degree (CCD), space–time geographically weighted regression model (GTWR), and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to reveal the multi-stage interactive response mechanisms between agricultural carbon emission equity and regional economic integration across China’s three major grain functional zones, from the perspectives of spatial heterogeneity and temporal non-stationarity. The results indicate that the major grain-producing zones (MGPZs) exhibit high ecological support but low production efficiency, while the major grain-consuming zones (MGCZs) maintain strong economic performance under ecological constraints, and the production-consumption balanced zones (PCBZs) have been fluctuating. There are significant differences in economic integration, with higher integration in MGPZs and MGCZs compared to lagging PCBZs. The coordination between equity and integration shows significant spatial and temporal variations, with only Jiangsu Province achieving high coordination. Moreover, key factors, including agricultural industrial structure, investment intensity, and pesticide application intensity, exert heterogeneous and sometimes conflicting effects on the carbon-economy coordination at different dimensions. These findings suggest that one-size-fits-all policies are inadequate. Instead, region-specific strategies that focus on ecological compensation, efficient input management, and interregional cooperation are essential. The study provides a theoretical basis for environmental impact assessments and the formulation of targeted policies that harmonize agricultural carbon mitigation with sustainable regional economic development.

title: The impact of vertical shareholding on platform’s information sharing decisions in virtual product supply chains
abstract: Information sharing between downstream distribution platforms and upstream virtual product developers is a key coordination mechanism in the virtual product supply chain (VPSC). While previous studies have examined how vertical shareholding affects stakeholders’ decision-making, demand information sharing among VPSC members within a vertical-shareholding structure remains underexplored, which raises the question of how a distribution platform shares the demand information in a vertical-shareholding VPSC. To address this gap, this study investigates the impact of vertical shareholding on information sharing in a VPSC. We develop a two-tier VPSC model with a developer and a distribution platform (holding superior demand information), and examine the demand information sharing strategies under different shareholding structures: (i) no shareholding ( \({NS}\) ), (ii) platform shareholding ( \({PS}\) ) and (iii) developer shareholding ( \({DS}\) ). Our analyses reveal that, first, under no shareholding and \({DS}\) , the platform voluntarily shares demand information when the price sensitivity of demand is low, regardless of the developer’s shareholding ratio. However, under \({PS}\) scenario, the incentive to share demand information depends on both the price sensitivity of demand and the platform’s shareholding ratio. Specifically, when demand is relatively price-sensitive, the platform is more willing to share information when its shareholding ratio is sufficiently high and less willing to share when it is low. Second, both \({PS}\) and \({DS}\) enhance product quality and platform effort levels regardless of the information-sharing strategy. Third, irrespective of the information sharing strategy, shareholding consistently benefits the platform, whereas the developer gains only when the shareholding ratio remains below a threshold under both \({PS}\) and \({DS}\) . Finally, we confirm the robustness of our analysis through two extensions that incorporate risk aversion and the Nash game framework.

title: Impact of green technology innovation on the value of manufacturing enterprises
abstract: In the context of the national innovation-driven strategy, green technology innovation in manufacturing enterprises is not only an effective way to address current environmental challenges but also an important strategy for achieving long-term stable development. Focusing on publicly listed manufacturing enterprises, this study explores the nonlinear and lagged effects of green technology innovation and the mediating roles of ESG performance and financing constraints based on observations from 2010 to 2024. The results indicate a positive U-shaped relationship between green technology innovation and enterprise value, along with a lagged effect. Furthermore, green technology innovation can indirectly influence enterprise value creation by enhancing ESG performance and reducing financing constraints. The conclusions are validated through endogeneity and robustness tests. Further heterogeneity analysis shows that the impact of green technology innovation on value creation is more significant in enterprises located in eastern regions and non-state-owned enterprises. This study provides a theoretical basis for enhancing corporate green technology innovation and promoting high-quality technological and economic development in the country.

title: Socio-demographic and online behavioural drivers of misinformation engagement in Hungary: evidence from linked survey and social media data
abstract: Abstract This study examines how socio-demographic and online behavioural characteristics are associated with misinformation engagement by combining survey data with donated Facebook trace data from a representative sample of the Hungarian Internet user population. Hungary provides a particularly interesting case for this research given its democratic backsliding and changing media landscape, which make understanding individual-level engagement with misinformation especially salient. The results show that from the socio-demographic factors only age was consistently associated with misinformation engagement, but membership in specific interest clusters on Facebook strongly shapes misinformation engagement, suggesting that online communities serve as powerful filters of information exposure: some ecosystems amplify engagement with misinformation, while others are associated with lower levels of such engagement. The study also illustrates that structural socio-demographic factors should be studied together with online behaviour to provide a more complete understanding of the drivers of misinformation engagement.

title: Teacher cognition and practices of feedback intervention: perspectives from Chinese university EFL teachers
abstract: While existing research has documented a variety of feedback intervention activities, few studies have systematically examined teacher cognition and practices regarding these activities. Defining feedback intervention as teachers’ deliberate integration of pedagogical activities to enhance students’ feedback literacy, this study explored how eight Chinese university EFL teachers perceived and implemented such activities using semi-structured interviews, classroom observations and the analysis of relevant artifacts. The results revealed that although participants unanimously acknowledged the necessity and potential benefits of feedback intervention, they readily endorsed activities aimed at sharpening students’ evaluative judgement and stimulating further action while dismissing cognitive guidance intended to help students appreciate feedback. Their classroom implementations were characterized by a prevalent reliance on intuitive, loosely structured approaches and sometimes a deliberate avoidance of intervention activities they themselves considered effective, exhibiting a salient cognition-practice disparity. This mismatch was largely shaped by a complex interplay of personal, student-related and contextual influences. A framework was developed to elucidate the complex interdependence between teacher cognition, practices and these multi-directional influences. The findings advocate for a fundamental reconceptualization of feedback intervention from incidental practice to intentionally designed instruction with collaborative efforts from teachers, students and institutions.

title: Trade frictions and corporate social responsibility (CSR): evidence from the risk mitigation perspective
abstract: This paper applies resource-based theory and stakeholder theory to examine trade frictions as a motive for corporate social responsibility (CSR). Using trade remedy investigations as a proxy for trade friction, we find that trade frictions increase CSR engagement, and this effect is stronger for firms in highly competitive industries, SOE firms, and those located in provinces with low levels of social trust. A motivation-based mechanism analysis shows that trade frictions increase firms’ business risk, which strengthens incentives to engage in CSR as a risk-management response. The positive effect of trade frictions on CSR is stronger among high-risk firms, and CSR engagement subsequently reduces future business risk. Moreover, this effect is weakened for firms with higher levels of digital transformation or innovation investment, suggesting that CSR operates as one of several alternative strategies for managing trade-friction risks. Additional tests show that trade frictions reduce corporate value, while proactive CSR engagement can offset this negative effect. Overall, the findings indicate that trade frictions stimulate CSR engagement and provide new insights into the literature on the determinants of CSR.

title: Fan comments, emotions, and imagination in Chinese online soccer novels from a digital humanities perspective
abstract: In the era of global digitalisation, soccer fan communities within the niche domain of online literary fandoms, alongside their concomitant nationalist discourses, have emerged as pivotal subjects of scholarly inquiry. However, extant research has largely overlooked the cultural dimensions and subjective articulations of these fan groups. Moreover, as research paradigms increasingly shift towards digital media, methodological frameworks rooted in digital humanities warrant further refinement. This study examines 297,290 reader comments on soccer-themed online novels authored by Lin Hai Ting Tao on Qidian Chinese Literature, analysing the affective expressions and virtual imaginaries of Chinese digital soccer fans. Utilising computational tools such as Python, Nvivo and ROST CM, alongside hermeneutic interpretation, the findings reveal that readers: (1) employ a ‘plot borrowing’ narrative strategy to articulate real-world perspectives; (2) pursue vicarious competitive experiences within the author’s constructed the “Second Soccer World “, transposing unrealised championship aspirations onto fictional narratives; and (3) exhibit radical romanticism within the dialectical tension between virtual and real spaces, manifesting a form of digital nationalism. Practically, this study provides actionable insights for national institutions and sports organisations engaged in fan management tasks related to competitive sports such as soccer. Theoretically, it advances the digital representation of online fan communities and contributes a robust digital humanities methodology for textual analysis.

title: The green dividend of the digital economy: how information consumption reduces urban carbon emission intensity
abstract: This paper investigates the environmental impact of the National Information Consumption Pilot Policy (NICPP), a key Chinese initiative promoting digital economic activities. Using the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we examine its effect on urban carbon emission intensity (CEI) with a difference-in-differences (DID) model based on a panel dataset of 268 prefecture-level cities in China from 2008 to 2023. The empirical findings indicate that the NICPP significantly lowers urban CEI, and this conclusion is supported by a series of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis suggests that service sector upgrading and green technological innovation are two channels through which information consumption reduces urban CEI, while logistics efficiency strengthens the policy effect by reducing the additional distribution-related emissions generated by the expansion of online consumption. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the CEI-reducing effect is more pronounced in cities with more advanced digital infrastructure, higher levels of financial development, and cleaner energy consumption structures.
