This study provides quasi-experimental evidence on the green dividend of information consumption policies and offers policy implications for aligning digital development with urban low-carbon transition.

title: Associations of marital status and social participation with frailty among adults aged 50 and older in 19 countries: evidence from five prospective cohort studies
abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid global population aging, frailty has emerged as a major challenge affecting the physical and mental health, quality of life, and the sustainability of healthcare and social systems for middle-aged and older adults. Existing research suggests that marital status and social participation may be important social determinants of health related to frailty, but the evidence remains inconsistent. This study aimed to use a harmonized methodological approach to examine the associations of marital status and social participation with frailty among adults aged 50 years and older, using data from five large-scale databases covering 19 countries/regions. This study also explored potential moderators and interaction effects within these associations. Data were drawn from five large, multinational, population-based longitudinal cohort studies: HRS, ELSA, SHARE, CHARLS, and MHAS. Logistic regression models were used to examine the associations of marital status and social participation with frailty, and subgroup analyses were conducted to assess potential moderating effects. Random-effects models were then used to pool the results. In addition, additive and multiplicative interaction effects between marital status and social participation were tested, and participants were classified into eight groups based on marital status and social participation to estimate their joint associations with frailty. The analyses showed that, except in CHARLS and MHAS, individuals with non-married statuses had significantly higher odds of frailty than married individuals (pooled OR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.11–1.51), with the association being particularly pronounced among those who were divorced/separated or widowed. The association between marital status and frailty was significantly moderated by national development level and age. The study also found that lack of social participation was significantly associated with higher odds of frailty (pooled OR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.12–1.50). However, the pooled additive and multiplicative interaction effects between marital status and social participation were not statistically significant. Nevertheless, compared with individuals who were married and socially active, those who were unmarried, particularly widowed, and lacked social participation had substantially higher odds of frailty (pooled OR: 1.86, 95% CI: 1.35–2.57). These findings suggest that social connectedness and targeted support for potentially vulnerable groups may be important for informing healthy aging strategies and frailty prevention efforts across different countries and populations.

title: The role of intelligent environmental supervision on corporate pollution emissions
abstract: Abstract With the increasing emphasis on environmental protection, the Chinese government has substantially expanded its investment in intelligent environmental supervision. However, its effectiveness in reducing corporate pollution emissions remains unclear. Using panel data of Chinese listed firms from 2011 to 2019, this study examines the impact and underlying mechanisms of intelligent environmental supervision on corporate emission reduction. The results reveal that intelligent environmental supervision significantly curbs corporate pollution emissions via two channels: stimulating green innovation and raising investment in pollution treatment. We further identify a substitution effect between government environmental information disclosure and intelligent environmental supervision. This substitution effect is more pronounced in regions with low public environmental concern and among heavily polluting firms. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the emission reduction effect is stronger for non-state-owned enterprises, heavily polluting firms, and firms with lower financial constraints, as well as those located in regions with weaker regulatory intensity and in eastern China. These findings provide robust empirical evidence to support the advancement of intelligent environmental governance.

title: Societal pathways to sustainability: unpacking the roles of humanities, sports, and social consciousness in environmental stewardship across nordic economies
abstract: Nordic countries are also reputed to be at the world forefront in environmental management, but with increasing urbanization, cultural consumption, and lifestyle emissions, the emerging conflicts between social development and environmental sustainability are becoming noticeable. The paper answers five fundamental research questions: Do urban development, cultural investment in the humanities, social consciousness, the sports economy, and economic expansion affect the pressure of sustainability in the Nordic economies? The sustainability pressure (SP) represents per capita CO2 emissions, measuring sustainability pressure, and the societal and economic drivers representing the humanities (HM), social consciousness (SC), sports economy index (SEI), urban growth (UG), and economic expansion (EE) using 2017Q1- 2023Q4 quarterly panel data. To reflect both the distributional heterogeneity and the robustness of the model, the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) is utilized in combination with Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS). The findings show that UG, HM, and SC have significant effects on increasing SP, whereby their effects are more prominent at the high emission quantiles. Conversely, SEI minimizes SP at every quantile, as well, indicating a positive contribution of the sports sector to a reduction in emissions. EE does not have any significant effect on SP, and relying on this, it can be stated that environmental pressure is not significantly influenced by short-term economic growth in this case. These results highlight the need to incorporate dimensions of society like culture, trust, lifestyle, and urbanization into policy on sustainability. The paper has added novel evidence concerning the effect of socially rooted factors on the environment in well-developed welfare states and provided practical implications to integrate social investment with climate goals in accordance with SDGs.

title: Family parenting styles and their associations with student academic performance and social adaptability: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Family parenting style has a profound impact on students’ growth. Existing research focuses on the direct impact of parenting style on students’ growth, and lacks attention to the mediation and regulation mechanism between psychological variables and environmental variables between parenting style and individual growth. Taking into account the representativeness of the sample and its relationship with student development, this paper focuses on the path mechanism of authoritative, despotic, and neglectful family education styles on academic self-efficacy and individual growth and development. Based on social cognitive theory (SCT), ecological system theory (EST), and socioeconomic status (SES) model, a structural equation model (SEM) is constructed and combined with mediation effect and moderation effect analysis. The influence mechanism of the three family education styles on academic achievement and social adaptability is systematically explored, and family SES is included as a potential moderator variable, aiming to deepen the understanding of the impact on student growth. The results show that authoritative parenting style can significantly improve students’ self-efficacy, thereby promoting academic achievement ( \({{PAQ}}_{{auth}}\to {SE}\to A\) estimate is 0.154, p < 0.001, and confidence interval 95% CI is [0.109, 0.203]). Authoritarian and neglectful parenting styles negatively affect self-efficacy ( \({{PAQ}}_{{authcratic}}\to {SE}\to A\) and \({{PAQ}}_{{neglectful}}\to {SE}\to A\) estimates are −0.152 and −0.137, respectively, p < 0.001). Self-efficacy has a significant positive predictive effect on social adaptability ( \({\theta }_{1}=0.452\) , p < 0.001). Social adaptability includes three dimensions: interpersonal adaptability, emotional regulation ability and environmental adaptability. And family SES has a significant moderating effect ( p < 0.001). Based on this, this study suggests advocating authoritative parenting, providing support for families with low SES, and improving the quality of family communication to enhance students’ self-efficacy, thereby promoting their comprehensive personal development and healthy growth.

title: Ethnic narratives in Dunhuang Bianwen: a digital humanities approach to pluralistic integration
abstract: As a representative form of folk storytelling and singing literature in the Tang Dynasty, Dunhuang Bianwen emerged in the multi-ethnic borderland of northwest China. It directly reflects the perceptions of ethnic interactions in folk society and possesses significant research value. Guided by the ethnic boundary theory, this study takes the 78 Bianwen texts recorded in the Collected Works of Dunhuang Bianwen (Wang et al., 1957). It constructs a quantitative model integrating three core indicators—Interaction Density, Emotional Orientation, and Interaction Impact intensity—and Standard History Narrative Distance Coefficient, analyzing the interactions between the Han ethnic group and surrounding ethnic minorities including the Turks and Tibetans. This research reveals the narrative essence of “differences exist in interactions while connections are sustained through differences” within the pluralistic integration pattern of the Chinese nation, and offers an interdisciplinary analytical paradigm for relevant studies.

title: Lighting the way: how women political participation shapes energy efficiency
abstract: The pursuit of sustainable energy solutions has become a global priority, with energy efficiency (EE) recognised as a crucial strategy for reducing energy consumption and addressing environmental challenges. Despite growing awareness of the importance of women’s political participation (WPP) for sustainability, its role in shaping EE outcomes remains underexplored. This study examines the association between WPP and EE in G20 nations over the period 1990–2021. Using two-way fixed effects model, the findings indicate that WPP significantly enhances EE. Mediation analysis further demonstrates that WPP fosters EE by promoting industrial upgrading. Additionally, the threshold effect analysis suggests that beyond a certain Human Development Index threshold, the link between WPP and EE becomes even stronger. These findings highlight the crucial role of inclusive political representation in achieving energy efficiency goals and provide evidence-based insights for policymakers seeking to advance sustainable energy transitions.

title: Secondary school biology teachers’ planned topic-specific pedagogical content knowledge for teaching respiration
abstract: Topic-specific pedagogical content knowledge (TSPCK) allows teachers to transform content into forms that learners can easily understand. This study examined secondary school teachers’ planned TSPCK in respiration using 28 teachers’ content representations (CoRes). The teachers were selected from two districts of Zambia. The CoRes ( n = 28) were scored using a rubric and analysed descriptively in SPSS, while CoRe texts were analysed thematically. The mean TSPCK score indicated an overall basic TSPCK level ( M = 1.59, SD = 0.65). Teachers’ knowledge of conceptual teaching strategies ( M = 1.96, SD = 0.74), representations and analogies ( M = 1.96, SD = 0.84) received the highest scores. However, teachers’ knowledge of students’ prior knowledge—including misconceptions—( M = 1.25, SD = 1.14), what makes the topic easy or difficult to teach or learn ( M = 1.32, SD = 1.19), and curricular saliency ( M = 1.43, SD = 0.63) received the lowest scores. The qualitative findings further revealed fragmented integration of TSPCK components, with pedagogical decisions often disconnected from learners’ prior knowledge—including misconceptions—and conceptual difficulties. Furthermore, teachers mentioned typical misconceptions and learning difficulties related to respiration. The findings suggest the potential value of targeted professional development and strengthened emphasis on topic-specific PCK in teacher education. The study recommends integrating structured tools, such as CoRes, into teacher education to improve teachers’ ability to address misconceptions, identify curricular saliency, and foster the coherent integration of TSPCK components. Future research may extend to larger samples and triangulate CoRe data with classroom observation and learner data across different contexts.

title: How does school organizational democracy influence school development: a moderated mediation model of organizational citizenship behavior and job satisfaction
abstract: Abstract Democracy is a core feature of modern governance, yet the mechanisms through which organizational democracy drives school development within school settings remain under-explored. This study aims to examine the relationship between school organizational democracy and school development, with organizational citizenship behavior as a mediator and job satisfaction as a moderator. A cross-sectional study was conducted, and SPSS 27.0 was used to analyze survey data from 583 teachers in Beijing, China. The results showed that school organizational democracy is positively related to school development, organizational citizenship behavior plays a mediating role in this relationship, and job satisfaction acts as a moderating role. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding how school organizational democracy shapes school development through teachers’ behavioral and attitudinal factors. Practically, the study offers targeted implications for school managers and teachers. School managers should foster a supportive democratic climate and promote teachers’ active participation. Teachers are encouraged to actively participate in school governance, collaborate with colleagues, and contribute to cultivating a more democratic school environment.

title: Research on the pathways of intangible cultural heritage in enhancing urban cultural soft power—taking Quanzhou City, Fujian Province as an example
abstract: As the only Chinese city inscribed on all three major UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) lists, Quanzhou boasts 7 world-class and 36 national-level ICH projects. This rich heritage provides a robust foundation for advancing the city’s cultural soft power. However, field investigations reveal prominent challenges in integrating ICH preservation with the development of urban cultural soft power. These bottlenecks include stagnant living transmission, insufficient synergy with urban development, limited dissemination impact, and a severe imbalance between conservation and commercial exploitation. Grounded in systems engineering principles, this study employs a mixed-methods approach encompassing field surveys (yielding 17 in-depth interviews conducted in March 2026), official dataset analysis(2015–2024), ArcGIS kernel density estimation, and comparative horizontal benchmarking against Suzhou and Chengdu—two national-level historical and cultural cities. We propose a five-dimensional enhancement framework—encompassing structural design, element optimization, conflict resolution, multi-stakeholder collaboration, and quality upgrading—to leverage ICH for soft power augmentation. Furthermore, the study delineates phased implementation mechanisms, quantifiable evaluation metrics, and monitoring tools, offering a theoretical reference and practical paradigm for historical cities aiming to elevate their cultural soft power through heritage resources.

title: Social media news use and political expression among young adults: evidence from China
abstract: Political expression is an important component of democratic politics, and social media has become the main way for young adults to access political information. Nevertheless, it still remains unknown that how social media news use (SMNU) affects political expression among young adults. This study relies on data from “2018 Internet User Social Attitude Survey” to examine the effect of the SMNU on political expression among Chinese young adults and explore its inner mechanism from a socio-psychological perspective. Results indicate that after controlling for demographic variables and internal political efficacy, the SMNU has not only direct effects on online and offline political expression positively, but also indirect effects on them mediated via social media trust. Moreover, political interest positively moderates the mediation effect of the SMNU on online political expression, further enlarging the gap between those with higher political interest and those with lower political interest in online political expression. It has no significant impact, however, on the mediation effect of the SMNU on offline political expression. These findings attempt to advance our understanding of the multiple mechanisms affecting political expression from socio-psychological attitudes.

title: Navigating AI in EFL academic writing: examining perceptions, frequency of use and ethical orientations
abstract: With widespread leveraging of artificial intelligence tools in English as a foreign language (EFL) classes, there is a need to examine their potential influence on the academic writing of EFL learners. While AI use in language learning has been examined extensively in the past few years, EFL students’ perceptions, frequency of use, and the ethical orientations concerning AI use in academic writing remain insufficiently investigated. To fill this lacuna, our mixed-methods study looked at the perceptions of EFL learners toward the potential and frequency of AI use for academic writing. Additionally, it explored their ethical orientations toward AI adoption in academic writing. Employing a convenience sampling strategy, we collected quantitative data from 351 first-year university students using an online survey. We also gathered qualitative data from seven participants through semi-structured interviews. The findings revealed that the surveyed learners perceived AI as a useful resource for academic writing and had positive attitudes toward the potential benefits of AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, Grammarly, Wordtune, and Quillbot) for developing essential writing skills and fostering confidence in writing. Approximately half of the respondents were aware of some of the most common ethical concerns regarding AI use for academic writing. The study presents valuable implications for EFL teachers and policymakers on how to ethically and responsibly use AI for academic writing.

title: An intersectional approach to the literary universe of contemporary Turkish author Menekşe Toprak
abstract: Contemporary Turkish writer Menekşe Toprak is primarily known for her short stories; her first collection, Letter in the Suitcase (Valizdeki Mektup), was published in 2007. Following her second collection, Which Language is Love (Hangi Dildedir Aşk), she shifted to novel writing with The Children of July (Temmuz Çocukları, 2011), followed by The End of Lament (Ağıtın Sonu), The Whisper of Bees (Arı Fısıltıları), and Déjàvu. From her early stories onward, Toprak has created introspective characters and focused on themes such as gender, identity, and the experiences of migrant women. This article analyzes the female protagonists in Menekşe Toprak’s fiction through the lens of intersectionality. Intersectionality provides a framework for exploring how intersecting structures of power—such as gender, migration status, and cultural affiliation—simultaneously influence her characters’ inner lives and social positions. By employing thematic close reading, the analysis explores how these overlapping axes of identity are narratively constructed, emotionally expressed, and structurally encoded in Toprak’s work. As a migrant woman writer herself, Toprak not only reflects transnational experiences in her protagonists but also offers nuanced literary insights into the interplay between personal and collective forms of displacement, belonging, and agency. This interdisciplinary approach thus illuminates the emotional, political, and psychological dimensions of migration in Toprak’s fiction, thereby positioning her as a significant voice in contemporary migration literature.

title: Could corporate ESG performance impacts controlling shareholders tunneling: evidence from China
abstract: Using a sample of Chinese listed firms, this study investigates how corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance affects tunneling by controlling shareholders. We find that higher ESG performance significantly reduces tunneling, with this effect being stronger in state-owned enterprises and in firms operating in more developed legal environments. Mechanism analyses indicate that internal control enhancement, information promotion, investor protection, and market attention serve as four key channels through which ESG curbs tunneling. Cross-sectional tests reveal that the disciplining effect of ESG is more pronounced when monitoring by non-controlling large shareholders is weaker, when the divergence between control and cash-flow rights is larger, and when listed firms are subject to stricter regulatory oversight (e.g., A + H share listings). We also document significant spillover effects, whereby a firm’s ESG disclosure reduces tunneling among industry-region peers. Overall, this study provides new evidence on how ESG disclosure mitigates agency conflicts between controlling and minority shareholders in settings with weaker institutional safeguards. The findings underscore the value of integrating ESG practices into corporate governance to protect minority investors and promote sustainable business development.

title: Large Language Model-driven knowledge graph construction for Qing Yongzheng imperial artifact production
abstract: This study constructs a knowledge graph for Qing imperial artifacts during the Yongzheng period, utilizing the Huoji Dang archives to systematize fragmented historical records and establish a robust methodological framework for Qing material culture research. Employing Large Language Models (LLMs) integrated with a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework and carefully optimized prompts, we successfully automate the extraction of unstructured data and store the resulting structured entities within Neo4j. Experimental results demonstrate DeepSeek-V3’s superior performance under RAG augmentation, achieving a Micro F1 score of 86.75% (Precision:80.54%/Recall:94.00%) and a Macro F1 score of 84.70% (Precision:83.29%/Recall:88.39%). The generated knowledge graph visually reveals the underlying organizational hierarchies, intricate production workflows, and prevailing imperial esthetic preferences embedded within these archival records. The primary contribution of this work lies in enabling the systematic structuring of historical texts via graph technology, thus providing a unified platform for the study of Qing imperial material culture. This approach significantly enhances traditional research paradigms by integrating advanced artificial intelligence with digital humanities methodologies.

title: The numismatic reflection of Abbasid-Turkish traditions in Bengal Sultanate coinage
abstract: This study examines how the Bengal Sultanate’s coinage reflected political authority, Islamic religious identity, and cultural change. It argues that coinage was a tool for asserting legitimacy and connecting Bengal to Abbasid-Turkish legacies. The analysis shows how rulers used a mix of Bengali symbols and Islamic motifs on coins to signal sovereignty and local identity. Arabic inscriptions, especially the Kalima and the names of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, were deliberately used to express religious legitimacy and authority. By adopting Abbasid and Turkish titles, Bengal’s rulers aligned themselves with the wider Islamic world, enhancing their stature. The use of Islamic symbols was more than ceremonial; it reinforced the Sultanate’s Islamic character and social cohesion. Overall, Bengal’s coinage illustrates how local and Islamic influences merged to express regional sovereignty within the larger Islamic context.

title: How teacher–student relationships are associated with adolescent suicide risk: a three-wave longitudinal study of perceived burdensomeness and psychological capital
abstract: Adolescent suicide represents a critical global public health concern, underscoring the urgent need to identify its underlying psychological mechanisms and protective factors. The present study employed a three-wave longitudinal design over one year with a sample of 1428 secondary school students to examine whether teacher–student relationships are associated with subsequent suicide risk through parallel mediating pathways involving interpersonal needs and psychological capital. Results from path analyses indicated that perceived burdensomeness, resilience, and optimism significantly mediated the association between teacher–student relationships and adolescent suicide risk. Among the significant mediators, optimism showed the largest estimated indirect effect among the significant mediators. The findings suggest that supportive teacher–student relationships are prospectively associated with lower adolescent suicide risk primarily via lower perceived burdensomeness and higher resilience and optimism, highlighting the critical role of positive psychological resources in adolescent suicide prevention.

title: Parents’ hedonic, eudaimonic, and extrinsic motives for happiness: associations with parenting behaviors
abstract: Although happiness motives are known to influence personal well-being, their relevance to parenting behaviors, which are crucial for child well-being, remains understudied. This study examined how parents’ hedonic (e.g., seeking fun), eudaimonic (e.g., seeking meaning), and extrinsic motives (e.g., seeking wealth) relate to parenting behaviors in a cross-sectional study involving parents from China (Study 1) and in a two-wave longitudinal study with parents from the United States (Study 2). The findings show that eudaimonic motives relate to higher levels of autonomy support/behavioral control and lower levels of psychological control/inconsistent parenting, whereas extrinsic motives relate to lower levels of autonomy support and higher levels of psychological control. Furthermore, we observed inconsistent findings regarding the relationship between hedonic motives and parenting behaviors across the two studies. These findings highlight the importance of extending happiness motive research beyond intrapersonal domains into interpersonal contexts, thereby helping identify the relevance of different happiness motives to others’ well-being.

title: Reframing sacredness: ritual reconfiguration in Xiangxi Miao Drum Dance and Balinese Legong Dance
abstract: This article examines the reconfiguration of ritual within traditional dance practices in the Global South through a comparative ethnographic study of the Xiangxi Miao Drum Dance in China and the Balinese Legong Dance in Indonesia. Drawing on multi-sited fieldwork conducted in Dehang and Pinglang Miao villages and in Ubud, Bali, the study analyzes how these sacred forms respond to the pressures of secularization, tourism development, and heritage institutionalization. Both dances are rooted in cosmological belief systems and embodied ritual practices, yet their contemporary trajectories diverge as they encounter distinct political, religious, and cultural infrastructures. Using the conceptual frameworks of restored behavior proposed by Schechner, the repertoire articulated by Taylor, and the discourse of intangible heritage, the analysis examines how ritual elements are preserved, reframed, or aestheticized through embodied gesture, choreographic adaptation, and institutional mediation. Rather than interpreting these transformations as cultural decline, the article argues that they represent ongoing processes of ritual translation and embodied negotiation. The study demonstrates that ritual transformation should be understood not as cultural decline but as a process of reconfiguration, sustained through embodied memory, performer agency, and context-specific negotiation. Through these processes, traditional dances continue to function as living sites of memory, affect, and agency, mediating between devotion and display within contemporary performance ecologies. Specifically, the Xiangxi Miao Drum Dance reconfigures sacredness through semiotic embedding within state-led heritage narratives, while the Balinese Legong does so through kinesthetic internalization that cultivates taksu.

title: What factors influence evidence use in policy? An updated systematic map
abstract: Abstract In 2014, a large systematic map found that relational factors were amongst the most frequently reported facilitators of evidence use in policy. Since then, there has been a growth in evidence-use initiatives and research, many of which have attempted to address relational factors. In this timely updated map, we describe the current state of research about which factors influence evidence use in policy. A search strategy combining ‘evidence’, ‘barriers and facilitators’ and ‘policy/policymakers’ was used to identify studies across 15 electronic databases between 2012 and 2022. Studies were screened for those that include empirical data about evidence use in policy. Data extraction enabled descriptive analyses characterising studies in terms of focus, topic area, setting, and types of factors influencing use. Two thousand, one hundred and ninety-nine studies were included, a 20-fold increase over 10 years. The most commonly reported factors influencing use were the relevance of evidence, and then organisational (resources, skills, personnel and managerial support). A large number of studies reported on evidence-use interventions ( n = 877) of which 379 were evaluations. Findings may indicate a shift towards relational and systemic thinking about evidence use. There appears to be a growing recognition of the resourcing, work, time, and workforce required to embed evidence use within and between organisations. With this huge growth in the literature, particularly in new evidence use interventions being tested across policy sectors, continued review and mobilisation is necessary to effectively inform the design and implementation of evidence use interventions and research.

title: The paradox of financial process reengineering: efficiency gained vs. financial flexibility reduced
abstract: Digital transformation has increased pressure on firms to redesign finance processes, yet evidence on the flexibility consequences of such redesign remains limited. This study examines whether financial process reengineering in the finance function, proxied by financial shared service center (FSSC) adoption, is associated with lower financial flexibility. Using a panel of Chinese A-share non-financial listed firms from 2013 to 2022, the analysis combines fixed-effects regressions with a staggered event-study difference-in-differences design based on first-adoption timing inferred from the Management Discussion and Analysis section of annual reports. The baseline estimates show a negative association between FSSC adoption and overall financial flexibility, and the reduction is more pronounced for cash flexibility than for debt flexibility. The timing-based evidence shows jointly insignificant lead coefficients within the plotted pre-adoption window and negative post-adoption dynamics, with the strongest declines emerging one to two years after first adoption. Additional mechanism evidence indicates that investment becomes less sensitive to internally generated cash after adoption, while indirect proxies show higher selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) intensity and lower external financing constraints. Overall, the findings are consistent with weaker internal liquidity redeployment after adoption. They suggest that firms should evaluate shared-service reforms not only by cost savings and process standardization, but also by their implications for liquidity responsiveness and internal capital allocation.

title: Gender inclusion and governance: the role of productive capacity
abstract: Abstract The purpose of this study is twofold. First, it examines the unconditional impact of gender inclusion on governance in Africa. Second, it investigates the moderating role of productive capacity in shaping the effect of gender inclusion on governance. The study focuses on 51 African countries over the period 2010 to 2022. The empirical strategy is based on two approaches. First, an estimated baseline regression model with the pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) technique. Second, dynamic model estimation through the adoption of the interactive System Generalized Method of Moments (SGMM) estimator to address unobserved heterogeneity and simultaneity-driven endogeneity. For robust policy outcomes, governance quality is assessed using an aggregation of six governance indicators, which are further disaggregated into political, economic, and institutional governance. Similarly, gender inclusion is assessed through female labor force participation, female self-employment, female political representation, and female employment. The findings indicate that enhanced productive capacity mitigates the unconditional negative effect of gender inclusion, thereby fostering improved governance outcomes. Moreover, the study identifies the threshold levels at which this reversal occurs. Other findings and policy implications are discussed in alignment with the African Union’s 2063 agenda and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: Design and evaluation of an AR-integrated STEM-BCG learning kit to foster creative problem solving in secondary chemistry education
abstract: Chemistry education faces significant challenges in helping students visualize abstract molecular concepts, creating cognitive barriers that hinder understanding and application of theoretical knowledge to real-world sustainability problems. This study aimed to design an AR-integrated STEM-BCG Learning Kit based on constructivist principles to support creative problem-solving in acid-base chemistry, examine students’ creative problem-solving abilities and academic achievement, and evaluate user experience. Using a quasi-experimental design with 79 eleventh-grade students divided into experimental ( n = 40) and control ( n = 39) groups, the study developed a learning kit with seven components grounded in a comprehensive theoretical framework. Because intact classes were assigned to conditions, the groups differed at pre-test; normalized gain, ANCOVA, and non-parametric tests were used to address this non-equivalence. Results showed that the experimental group achieved larger gains in creative problem-solving skills (pre-test M = 8.82, SD = 1.41; post-test M = 15.94, SD = 1.92; normalized gain=0.63) compared to the control group (pre-test M = 10.54, SD = 1.37; post-test M = 12.28, SD = 1.57; normalized gain = 0.17), with a very large but imprecisely estimated effect size ( d = 2.08, 95% CI [1.53, 2.63]) and larger academic achievement gains (Cohen’s d = 0.87, 95% CI [0.40, 1.33]; normalized gain=0.70 versus 0.50). The two outcomes were correlated ( r = 0.64). Experimental-group students reported positive experiences (M = 4.49, SD = 0.64) and good perceived usability (SUS = 83.25); these self-reports had no comparison condition. This preliminary study suggests that integrating AR technology with BCG principles within a constructivist framework shows promise for supporting students’ creative problem-solving skills and academic achievement in chemistry education in this context. Because the study involved one school, one teacher, one topic, and a five-week implementation of a multi-component package, the findings are preliminary and cannot be attributed to augmented reality alone; replication with an activity-matched comparison condition, blinded scoring, and delayed post-tests is needed.

title: Assessing digital economy indicators in the context of the Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: The digital economy’s role in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has attracted significant attention, with many countries proposing digital development strategies. However, differences in objectives and indicators hinder international comparability. This paper establishes a conceptual framework for the digital economy based on the SDGs and the Global Digital Compact. Using this framework, 20 existing indicator systems are analyzed in terms of coverage. Findings show that existing systems mainly focus on “Decent Work and Economic Growth” (SDG 8) and “Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions” (SDG 16), but underrepresent SDGs 1, 5, 6, 7, 14, 15, and 17. Regarding digitalization and inequality, indicators emphasize connectivity, governance, shared access, and security, while neglecting digital cooperation, human rights, data protection, and global collaboration. The proposed framework serves as a comprehensive tool for assessing the digital economy and guiding policies. This study supports refining measurement systems to better evaluate digital development and its impact on sustainability.

title: How research experience moderates doctoral students’ career aspiration-choice relationship
abstract: Doctoral career entry is often understood as a process of sorting by labour-market competition and accumulated academic capital, making resource-rich training a presumed ‘safe harbour’ for aspiring academics. Yet graduates with strong institutional advantages also leave academia, while students who begin doctoral study with similar academic aspirations reach different career destinations. Existing research generally treats aspirations, accumulated capital and research conditions as separate predictors, leaving unclear whether students’ experience of doctoral research conditions the correspondence between initial aspirations and eventual employment. Using data from 10,428 doctoral graduates across 359 Chinese institutions, this study estimates robust logistic regression models for humanities, social sciences, natural sciences and engineering. Academic aspiration at enrolment strongly predicted academic career entry (OR = 12.85), but this association was conditional: a more favourable subjective research experience, encompassing supervisory support, intellectual alignment and protected scholarly time, strengthened the aspiration–choice relationship (interaction OR = 1.12). The interaction was positive across all four disciplines and statistically significant in social sciences, natural sciences and engineering; the positive estimate for the smaller humanities subgroup remained uncertain. These findings reposition subjective research experience from an additional predictor of career choice to a statistical boundary condition on the aspiration–choice relationship, thereby connecting the cognitive and affective dimensions of doctoral socialisation in explaining career differentiation.

title: Socioeconomic and spatial impacts of short-term rentals: a systematic review of Airbnb’s shared accommodation
abstract: Short-term rentals (STRs) have transformed the global housing and tourism landscape, reshaping urban economies, residential communities, and neighborhood dynamics. Within this broader market, shared accommodation, exemplified by Airbnb, has expanded rapidly through peer-to-peer platforms and is linked to housing affordability issues, long-term resident displacement, and gentrification in major cities across the globe. The study aims to conduct a systematic literature review that synthesizes spatial distribution patterns of short-term rentals (STRs) and their socioeconomic impacts on urban neighborhoods, using Airbnb as a primary empirical case. This systematic review synthesizes 53 empirical peer-reviewed studies published between 2017 and 2024, following the PRISMA-P guidelines. Using descriptive statistics, content analysis, and co-word analysis, the review identifies three principal findings. First, shared accommodation listings are spatially clustered in affluent areas with high tourist demand and proximity to cultural landmarks, business districts, and well-connected transport networks. Second, quantitative evidence consistently links STR proliferation to declining long-term housing supply and accelerated gentrification, particularly in tourism-intensive districts. Third, qualitative findings point to subtler yet equally significant social consequences, including the erosion of community cohesion, heightened residential dissatisfaction, and growing security concerns among long-term inhabitants. The expansion of shared accommodation has generated significant yet uneven consequences for housing markets, social cohesion, and urban planning, particularly in tourism-concentrated and heritage districts, manifesting in rental price escalation, intensified gentrification, and infrastructural strain. The review concludes that context-sensitive regulation is essential to balance the economic opportunities. STRs must address the imperatives of social equity, cultural preservation, and urban sustainability. This study provides a systematic evidence base to inform land-use planning, housing policy, and regulatory frameworks.

title: Exploring flourishing, personal best goals, engagement, and teacher support in adolescent English learning: a goal-setting theory perspective
abstract: Abstract Grounded in Goal-setting Theory, this study examined the relationships among flourishing, personal best goals, and engagement in English learning among Chinese senior high school students and further explored whether teacher support moderated the association between personal best goals and engagement. A total of 661 students participated in a questionnaire survey and structural equation modeling was used to test the hypothesized model. The results showed that flourishing positively predicted both personal best goals and engagement. Personal best goals also positively predicted engagement. In addition, the relationship between personal best goals and engagement was stronger among students who perceived higher levels of teacher support. This study contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of goal-setting processes in adolescent English learning by highlighting the role of flourishing and the contextual significance of teacher support.

title: Teachers’ perceptions of female principals’ leadership styles in basic education schools: an Omani perspective
abstract: Despite extensive research on educational leadership, studies examining female leadership in basic education schools within Oman remain limited particularly regarding its impact on teachers and school climate. Addressing this gap is crucial to inform leadership development and policy strategies in the context of Oman’s Vision 2040. This quantitative study seeks to identify the predominant leadership style of principals in basic education schools in the Sultanate of Oman from the teachers’ perspective. It aims to examine its impact on teachers and assess the magnitude of its effect on educational performance and teacher outcomes. A questionnaire was administered to 202 female teachers using the convenience sampling method. The study applied the Multi-Factor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ), which consisted of four main dimensions: transformational leadership, transactional leadership, passive/avoidant leadership, and leadership outcomes. Cronbach’s alpha showed good reliability, and Pearson correlations coefficients fell within acceptable limits. SPSS was used to compute means, standard deviations, one-way ANOVA, and Eta analyses. The results revealed that transformational leadership is the prevailing style, with high scores in expected leadership outcomes. Additionally, the findings indicated a significant effect of leadership styles on teachers, highlighting the central role of school principals in enhancing teacher performance and fostering a positive learning environment. Based on these findings, the study recommends strengthening the adoption of transformational leadership among female school leaders and supporting training programs to develop leadership skills effectively.

title: Integrating ESG into remanufacturing: third-party model selection aligned with consumer eco-consciousness under the carbon cap-and-trade policy
abstract: As global efforts to reduce carbon emissions intensify, manufacturers face increasing pressure to integrate environmental sustainability into their supply chain strategies. Carbon cap-and-trade policies have become an important market-based mechanism for reducing emissions while creating economic incentives for sustainable production. Unlike existing studies that primarily examine remanufacturing operations or carbon policies separately, this study develops an ESG-oriented closed-loop supply chain model to investigate how manufacturers choose between outsourcing and authorization third-party remanufacturing (3PR) models under carbon cap-and-trade regulation and heterogeneous consumer green preferences. The model jointly captures the strategic interactions among manufacturers, third-party remanufacturers, consumers, and the government, providing a comprehensive framework for sustainable remanufacturing decisions. The results generate several important insights. First, the authorization model leads to higher remanufactured product prices and recycling rates but lower demand for remanufactured products than the outsourcing model. Second, stronger consumer green preferences increase the profitability of both manufacturers and 3PRs, but they affect the two parties’ preferred remanufacturing models differently: manufacturers increasingly favor authorization, whereas 3PRs prefer outsourcing. Third, carbon cap-and-trade policies significantly reshape model selection. Preference alignment between manufacturers and 3PRs occurs only under sufficiently asymmetric carbon quotas, while intermediate quota allocations create strategic conflicts, highlighting the importance of policy design. Finally, although manufacturers may benefit more from authorization under strong consumer green preferences, the outsourcing model consistently generates higher social welfare, suggesting a potential divergence between private incentives and societal objectives. These findings provide actionable insights for firms seeking to integrate ESG strategies into remanufacturing decisions and for policymakers designing carbon-quota trading schemes that balance corporate incentives, environmental sustainability, and social welfare.

title: Contract and digital chains: the effect of dual-chain coupling on farmers’ credit access
abstract: This study investigates how the integration of contract and digital chains is associated with farmers’ access to formal credit under conditions of information asymmetry and collateral scarcity. Using microdata from the China Rural Revitalization Survey (CRRS), multidimensional indices are constructed to measure participation depth in both chains, and a Conditional Mixed Process (CMP) model is applied to estimate the relationship between dual-chain coupling and farmers’ credit outcomes, together with supplementary channel analyses. The results show that dual-chain coupling significantly increases both the amount of credit received and the likelihood of obtaining credit. The contract-chain and digital-chain indices are also positively and significantly associated with credit amounts when examined separately, indicating that both dimensions provide important foundations for the credit-enhancing role of dual-chain coupling. The channel analyses provide evidence consistent with the view that dual-chain coupling is associated with higher income and improved information efficiency, which may strengthen repayment capacity and reduce lenders’ screening costs. The association is significantly stronger among better-educated farmers, while the results also provide suggestive evidence of a stronger association outside major grain-producing regions. A supplementary nonlinear analysis indicates that the positive association between dual-chain coupling and credit amount becomes statistically detectable only after CCI enters the moderate-to-high range, suggesting that organizational and digital participation need to reach a sufficient degree of coordination before their joint credit benefits become empirically evident. The findings imply that coordinating cooperatives and e-commerce platforms can support a rural credit system based on organizational participation and traceable data.

title: Environmental Education Across the Curriculum: Challenges of Integration in the Turkish Educational System
abstract: Sustainable environmental education (SEE) is a foundational element in aligning national curricula with global sustainability goals. This study examines the extent to which both SEE concepts—such as environmental awareness, energy conservation, recycling, and eco-friendly practices—and broader sustainable environment (SE) concepts—such as green finance, renewable energy, and carbon emission reduction—are integrated into the Turkish National Curriculum from preschool through high school. Through a systematic curriculum analysis supported by an extensive literature review, this study identifies significant variation in the distribution of sustainability-related themes across grades and subjects. Our findings highlight a notable concentration of SEE content in upper-secondary science-based subjects, while early childhood education and humanities disciplines show limited integration. This uneven distribution suggests differences in the curricular emphasis placed on sustainability-related themes across educational stages and disciplines. The findings support the value of a more holistic and interdisciplinary curriculum approach, beginning in early education, to strengthen the curricular integration of sustainability-related themes and better align educational content with sustainable development goals.

title: Trajectory of life satisfaction during the COVID-19 pandemic mitigation period: the effects of personality and changes in optimism
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly impacted individuals’ life circumstances. In this unique context, people with different personality traits may experience varying trajectories of life satisfaction. However, there is limited research examining the role of personality in shaping these trajectories or investigating the underlying mechanisms. This study aims to explore the potential relationship between personality and the trajectory of life satisfaction, and to examine the mediating role of optimism in this relationship. The sample consisted of 2935 participants ( M age = 52.92, SD = 15.96, range: 15–75, 47.09% male) from the Longitudinal Internet studies for the Social Sciences (LISS) panel. The findings revealed that life satisfaction increased during the COVID-19 pandemic mitigation period from 2020 to 2022. Individuals with high levels of extraversion ( β = 0.09, p < 0.001), conscientiousness ( β = 0.09, p < 0.01), and emotional stability ( β = 0.42, p < 0.001) exhibited a high level of life satisfaction at the onset. Emotional stability exhibited the most influential effect on life satisfaction. Nevertheless, only emotional stability predicted a slower increase in life satisfaction ( β = −0.11, p < 0.05). Furthermore, this study identified several mediation pathways. The initial level of optimism served as a mediator in the links between personality (except for emotional stability) and the initial level and change in life satisfaction. The changes in optimism mediated the effects of agreeableness and emotional stability on the subsequent change in the slope of life satisfaction, as well as the association between emotional stability and the intercept of life satisfaction. These findings contribute to our understanding of the factors influencing individuals’ subjective well-being and provide implications for interventions to enhance life satisfaction.

title: Self-efficacy as a shield: moderating the impact of enterprise social media on team collaborative performance
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the impact of enterprise social media (ESM) on employees’ collaborative performance. The purpose is to clarify conflicting results by examining both the positive and negative factors of ESM consumption. We gathered survey data from 200 employees at technology companies. PLS-SEM (SmartPLS-4) was used for analysis, with the PROCESS macro and bootstrapping. Measurement tests were highly reliable, with strong convergent and discriminant validity. Central results are uncomplicated. The use of ESM enhances employees’ access to social support, while also elevating perceptions of information overload. The relationship that exists between collaborative performance and ESM use is positively mediated by social support. In comparison, the information overload yields a negative mediating effect. The total impact of ESM on collaboration is non-linear: ESM promotes collaboration at low and moderate levels of use, but its effects decrease with higher use and may be detrimental at overload levels. Employee self-efficacy moderates the mediation channels. Higher levels of employee self-efficacy enhance the positive social support channel and undermine the negative overload channel. Some practical implications are implied. To begin with, managers should promote ESM behaviors that foster supportive relationships and knowledge sharing. Second, information flow should be regulated by organizational governance, filtering, and clear norms to avoid information overload. Third, specific training to raise employees’ self-efficacy will enable them to reap the benefits of collaboration and reduce cognitive strain. The present paper presents a synthesized empirical model that balances the contradictory ESM impacts and offers practical recommendations for organizations that must balance digital collaboration and employee well-being.

title: Teachers’ views on the use of first-person pronouns in academic writing
abstract: Abstract Although there is a growing body of research on first-person pronouns (e.g. I, me, we) in academic prose, English for Academic Purposes (EAP) teachers’ views on their use in academic writing have received little attention. Our study addresses this gap by investigating EAP teachers’ views on the use of first-person pronouns in academic writing, according to discourse functions (e.g. expressing self-benefit, stating a purpose). Data were collected from an online survey and semi-structured interviews. All the interviewees are currently teaching at the tertiary level in the Asia-Pacific region. Our study shows that teachers’ views on the use of first-person pronouns are fairly positive, particularly for low-risk functions (e.g. stating a purpose), but they feel less comfortable using them in high-risk functions (e.g. stating a claim). Our analysis shows that teachers’ views are guided by a consideration for risk-taking and genre. The three most common sources that influenced teachers’ views are published research articles, university writing experience and academic writing textbooks. Our statistical analysis shows that teachers with publication experience tend to have a positive view of pronoun use.

title: Comparing public and private R&D: implications for environmental sustainability in G7 economies
abstract: Abstract Economic activity has contributed to a wide range of environmental challenges, increasing the importance of research and development (R&D) as a means of supporting sustainable development. Although the environmental implications of R&D have been widely examined, relatively little attention has been paid to the potentially different roles of public and private R&D. Given that these two forms of R&D differ in their objectives, funding structures, and innovation processes, distinguishing between them may provide a more nuanced understanding of their environmental effects. Against this background, this study examines the environmental impacts of public and private R&D expenditures in the G7 countries over the period 1985-2021 using panel data techniques. The findings from the Driscoll and Kraay (1998) estimator and the Beck and Katz PCSE estimator indicate that both public and private R&D expenditures contribute positively to environmental sustainability. The estimated coefficients are larger for private-sector R&D, suggesting a relatively greater contribution compared with public-sector R&D. Furthermore, the Dumitrescu and Hurlin (2012) panel causality test indicates a unidirectional causal relationship running from private R&D expenditures to environmental quality, whereas a bidirectional causal relationship is identified between public R&D expenditures and environmental quality. Overall, the findings suggest that strengthening private-sector innovation, while maintaining support for public R&D, may enhance environmental sustainability in advanced economies.

title: Analyzing consumer switching intentions toward low-altitude flying vehicles in Shenzhen: A Push, Pull, Mooring, and SEM ANN Approach
abstract: Low-altitude flying vehicles are a new form of urban transportation that can help reduce traffic congestion and improve travel efficiency. Understanding consumer switching intentions toward this new transport mode is important for supporting the growth of low-altitude mobility in Shenzhen. The purpose of this study is to examine how push, pull, and mooring effects influence consumers’ switching intentions toward low-altitude flying vehicles. This study uses a hybrid structural equation modeling (SEM) and artificial neural network (ANN) approach to analyze the proposed relationships. Survey data were collected from 1063 respondents in Shenzhen, China. The results show that push and pull effects have a positive effect on switching intention, while mooring effects have a negative effect and also weaken the influence of push and pull effects. These findings help explain consumer switching behavior and provide useful guidance for policymakers and industry stakeholders to promote the adoption of low-altitude flying vehicles.

title: The influence of corporate social responsibility in shaping corporate reputation: examining the mediating effects of corporate image and knowledge creation in the construction industry
abstract: Abstract Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has become a strategic imperative in the construction industry, shaping corporate reputation and fostering sustainable growth. This study investigates the influence of CSR on corporate reputation in the Pakistani construction industry, emphasizing the mediating roles of corporate image and knowledge creation. Grounded in stakeholder theory, the study employs a quantitative research design and collects data from 302 respondents using a structured questionnaire. The data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) via Smart-PLS to examine the direct and indirect effects of CSR on corporate reputation. The results reveal that CSR significantly enhances corporate reputation, with this relationship strongly mediated by corporate image and knowledge creation, highlighting the importance of strategic CSR practices for knowledge development and stakeholder engagement. The study is significant because it provides both theoretical and practical contributions: theoretically, it extends stakeholder theory by integrating CSR, corporate image, and knowledge creation in the construction sector; practically, it guides industry leaders on leveraging CSR initiatives to strengthen corporate image, foster knowledge creation, and enhance stakeholder trust. Additionally, policymakers can use these insights to design incentives and frameworks that promote CSR adoption, supporting a socially responsible, knowledge-driven, and competitive construction industry.

title: Linguistic analysis of Chinese language usage in face-to-face versus virtual communication: insights from non-native and native Chinese speakers
abstract: Abstract In the contemporary educational landscape, the prevalence of online and face-to-face (F2F) teaching, along with the advancement of blended teaching as a pivotal force in educational reform, has transformed the learning environment. However, the nuances between these two instructional modes remain insufficiently explored. This study employs an experimental task, leveraging certain linguistic parameters from narrative analysis, to quantitatively assess the oral expression abilities of 40 learners of Chinese as a second language and 40 native Chinese speakers, both in online settings and in F2F settings. The study compares oral performance in online versus F2F interactions and investigates how varying linguistic backgrounds influence language parameters. Findings indicate that different communication styles have varying impacts on diverse language parameters, and the influence of communication mode on performance is more pronounced among native speakers. F2F interviews exhibit superior oral performance compared to online interviews, as evidenced by fewer repetitions and hesitations, a lower total number of characters and sentences, and greater communicative efficiency. The implications of this study are far-reaching, including the optimization of teaching by effectively integrating online and F2F methods, emphasizing practical and contextually relevant instruction for non-native learners, and incorporating communication efficiency as a crucial metric in teaching evaluation frameworks.

title: The effects of degree centrality and process innovation in the relationship of supplier participation and innovation performance of SMEs
abstract: This study examines the influence of supplier participation (SP), process innovation, and degree centrality on product innovation performance of small and medium-sized firms (SMEs) in China. There is an increasing awareness that the supplier is a key external information source for driving innovation in SMEs. However, existing studies on the impact of SP are inconsistent. This research quantifies the mediating effects of SMEs’ degree centrality and process innovation between SP and innovation performance. Drawing on a sample of 1989 SMEs in China, the study reveals that degree centrality partially mediates the impact of SP on innovation performance, highlighting the importance of a central position within supply chain networks. Additionally, both degree centrality and process innovation exert direct positive effects on product innovation performance. Moreover, technology commercialization moderates the relationship between degree centrality and product innovation performance. These insights advance the understanding of open innovation in SMEs and provide practical implications for managers seeking to optimize their innovation strategies.

title: Burnout among Chinese healthcare professionals as affected by artificial intelligence
abstract: With burnout becoming an “epidemic” among healthcare professionals, previous research has explored various factors influencing burnout, such as gender, age, marital status, working hours, and social support. However, the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on burnout in frontline medical practice remains underexplored. This study utilizes an online survey (n = 416) to investigate whether specific AI-assisted healthcare applications amplify or alleviate three dimensions of burnout in Chinese healthcare professionals: emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced accomplishment. The results indicate that Chinese healthcare professionals perceived the risk of AI as positively associated with overall burnout. In contrast, their perceived ease of use and usefulness of AI are negatively correlated with personal accomplishment. Moreover, those utilizing AI-assisted surgery and treatment report lower accomplishment levels. This study provides insights into redefining professional value for healthcare professionals in the AI era, contributing to the broader discussion on technology’s role in reshaping human work and identity.

title: Managerial climate change attention and supply chain innovation effect: evidence from China
abstract: Abstract This study examines the impact of customers’ managerial climate change attention on suppliers’ green innovation. The findings indicate a positive relationship between customers’ managerial climate change attention and suppliers’ green innovation. This relationship is further reinforced when customers possess comparatively stronger bargaining power. Customers’ managerial climate change attention promotes suppliers’ green innovation by redirecting suppliers’ managerial attention toward climate issues and by inducing greater R&D investment in response to anticipated demand. Further, the attention paid to climate change-related opportunity and physical shock have superior supply chain spillover effects over the attention paid to regulatory shock. Customers’ managerial climate change attention has positive effects on both the application and grant of green patents. This paper suggests a new green innovation effect rooted in managerial climate change attention.

title: From institutional support to pedagogical innovation: AI literacy as a mediator and boundary conditions in pre-service teacher education
abstract: Educational institutions worldwide are investing heavily in AI training, yet the extent to which this support is associated with pedagogical innovation among pre-service teachers remains unclear. Drawing on Organizational Support Theory, Human Capital Theory, Social Cognitive Theory, and Diffusion of Innovations theory, this study examines whether AI literacy statistically mediates the association between institutional support and pedagogical innovation, and whether school culture and technology self-efficacy condition different stages of this association. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 350 pre-service teachers from five universities across eastern, central, and western China (all urban settings). Data were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling with robust maximum likelihood estimation and conditional-process analysis with 5000 bootstrap resamples. AI literacy accounted for 53.4% of the total association between institutional support and pedagogical innovation. The association between institutional support and AI literacy was stronger in more supportive school cultures (simple slope: 0.65 vs 0.41), and the association between AI literacy and pedagogical innovation was stronger among pre-service teachers with higher technology self-efficacy (simple slope: 0.67 vs 0.37). The study contributes a conditional-process account that connects institutional support, capability development, and contextual and individual conditions. The practical implications are presented as evidence-informed possibilities rather than causal prescriptions.

title: Examining the macroeconomic drivers of self-employment in Nigeria
abstract: Nigeria’s formal job market has failed to keep up with the country’s growing population, causing a staggering number of citizens to work for themselves out of necessity rather than opportunity. This phenomenon is usually referred to as a survival, entrepreneurship boom. To this end, this study analyzes the impact of economic growth, poverty, the rule of law, and agriculture on self-employment in Nigeria between 1990 and 2023. Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) and other advanced econometric techniques were used. The findings from the ARDL long run form and bounds test and ARDL error correction regression reveal that (i) Gross domestic product positively influences self-employment in the short and long run, (ii) stringent rule of law consistently reduces self-employment in the long run, (iii) poverty is found to lower self-employment only in the long term, and (iv) agriculture shows no significant long-run effect. The robustness of these results is confirmed through multiple stability and diagnostic tests. These insights underscore the complex drivers of self-employment in Nigeria and provide critical guidance for policymakers seeking to design strategies that foster sustainable self-employment. To promote self-employment in Nigeria, the government could focus on economic growth, moderate regulatory standards, and strengthening poverty-reduction efforts.

title: Integrating biofeedback technologies into postural education: improving back posture, health literacy, and sustainable health habits
abstract: Low back pain (LBP) is a prevalent condition across all ages, and inadequate back posture is a key contributing factor. Educational settings offer an opportunity to promote postural awareness as a preventive measure. Biofeedback tools, such as the EduBack system, which uses Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) to monitor lumbar curvature, have shown potential for enhancing body awareness and supporting posture correction. However, their impact within school-based postural education remains underexplored. This study evaluated the immediate effects of the EduBack biofeedback system on postural awareness and back posture habits among secondary school students. An experimental pre-post design was implemented with 47 students in their fourth year of secondary education, randomly assigned to an experimental group using the biofeedback tool or a control group. Across eight sessions, several postural parameters were assessed during sitting, standing, and functional lifting tasks. The experimental group showed significant improvements in most measured postural variables. Lumbar lordosis in sitting increased from –5.9° to –10.1° ( \({\eta }_{p}^{2}\) = 0.18), maximum active pelvic tilt range of motion in standing improved from 20.4° to 30.7° ( \({\eta }_{p}^{2}\) = 0.63), and excessive lumbar flexion-extension during the rising-from-a-chair task decreased from 82.7% to 41.1% ( \({\eta }_{p}^{2}\) = 0.27). Significant Group × Time interactions ( p < 0.05) confirmed that the biofeedback tool produced greater improvements than the control group. These findings indicate that the EduBack biofeedback system enhances immediate postural awareness and supports healthier back posture behaviours in adolescents. The results highlight the potential of integrating biofeedback technologies into school-based postural education programmes and underscore the need for further research examining long-term effects and broader implementation.

title: Effects of GenAI-assisted reading activities on EFL learner’s reading comprehension, reading motivation and reading anxiety
abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of Generative AI (GenAI)-assisted reading activities in enhancing English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners’ reading comprehension, motivation, and anxiety over a 16-week semester. A mixed-methods approach compared an experimental group ( n = 65) using GenAI-generated texts and feedback with a control group ( n = 65) engaged in traditional reading tasks. Pre- and post-tests, questionnaires, and interviews revealed that the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in reading comprehension, exhibited higher intrinsic motivation and reading efficacy, and reported lower comprehension and vocabulary anxiety. These findings suggest that GenAI’s tailored content and interactive feedback foster cognitive and affective gains in EFL reading. The study underscores GenAI’s potential to innovate EFL pedagogy by supporting personalized learning, though further research is needed to optimize its cognitive impact.

title: How to improve the market-based allocation mechanism of water rights for irrigation water users in China: a four-party game perspective
abstract: Promoting market-based trading in irrigation water rights and improving allocation mechanisms are critical for strengthening water governance and advancing sustainable agricultural development. This study develops a four-party evolutionary game model involving local government (LCG), irrigation district management unit (IMU), social capital (SCP), and irrigation water users (IWU) to examine the evolutionary dynamics and key determinants of the market-based allocation of irrigation water rights. The results show that: (1) The system admits 11 pure-strategy equilibria that are locally asymptotically stable under specific parameter conditions, and $$\left(\mathrm{1,1,1,1}\right)$$ is the primary locally stable outcome under the baseline scenario. (2) System evolution is jointly shaped by the four actors’ initial strategy probabilities, which mainly affect convergence speed and evolutionary trajectories rather than the long-run direction or final equilibrium. (3) Single-factor sensitivity analysis shows that higher service fee, expected return, reward-penalty intensity, repurchase price multiplier, subsidy rates for IMU and SCP, and reputational benefits, together with lower water resources taxes and a moderate reduction in reserved water volume, promote the market-based development of irrigation water-rights trading. (4) Two-factor sensitivity analysis identifies synergies between subsidy rates and reputational benefits, water resources taxes and reward-penalty intensity, expected return and management-technical factors, service fee and irrigation water-use benefits, and repurchase price multiplier and irrigation water-use benefits, with coordinated adjustments improving stability and accelerating convergence. This study provides theoretical and policy insights for improving market-based allocation of water resources and encouraging multi-actor participation in irrigation water-rights trading.

title: Taming the volatility curse: the critical moderating role of governance and efficiency in achieving energy security in MENA
abstract: Abstract The impact of natural resources on energy security has recently gained prominence in resource research, with mixed empirical findings. A concurrent academic interest, fueled by ongoing global instability, is based on increasing evidence that it is the volatility of resources, rather than their abundance per se, that drives the resource curse, yet no prior study has directly tested this proposition in the context of energy security. This study addresses this gap by providing one of the first empirical test of the hypothesis that volatility, not abundance, is the primary channel through which natural resources affect energy security, and by exploring the nonlinear, threshold-dependent roles of governance and energy efficiency as moderators of this relationship. Using a System Generalized Methods of Moments estimator to data from 13 Middle East and North African countries—major global energy consumers—this study confirms that resource abundance positively affects energy security, whereas volatility significantly undermines it. The moderating effects reveal complex dynamics: governance and energy efficiency substantially alter the volatility–energy security nexus, with sign reversals indicating threshold-dependent relationships. Specifically, this study identifies a governance policy threshold (2.03, on a scale of −4.85 to 3.61) beyond which complementary policies are essential to mitigate volatility. An avoidable energy inefficiency threshold (1.53, on a scale of 1.07 to 2.78) is also identified, beyond which volatility’s negative impact intensifies. These findings underscore the need for integrated policy responses, including governance reforms, enhanced energy efficiency, economic diversification, renewable energy partnerships, and fiscal stabilization mechanisms to enhance energy security in resource-dependent economies.

title: From crisis to catalyst: unveiling the impact of information literacy on operational efficiency and organizational performance of SMEs in the digital post-pandemic era
abstract: Abstract The pandemic accelerated the digital transformation of SMEs. The purpose of this paper is to develop a theoretical model that explains the impact of Information Literacy (IL) and Digital Literacy (DL) on the Operational Efficiency (OE) and Organizational Performance (OP) of SMEs. Moreover, the relationships between Information capabilities (IC) and Digital capabilities (DC) with IL, DL, OE, and OP were examined. The study used a quantitative research approach. The survey responses of 1288 SME representatives formed the basis for the analysis. This study adopted Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to examine the validity and reliability of the measurement and structural models. According to the results, IC and DC were positively associated with OP and OE. Significant relationships were also found between IL and DL, and between IC and DC. This points to the often-overlooked fact that IC and DC usually result from deeper aspects of digital transformation. Finally, the study highlights the role of IL as a critical factor for successful digital transformation. Many studies on SMEs consider IC and DC to be the primary sources of successful digital transformation. However, these capabilities are often the result of deeper factors - IL and DL. Our study contributes to uncovering these underlying sources.

title: Analysing ambivalent attitudes through narratives: a transdisciplinary approach
abstract: Abstract Ambivalence toward treatment is a defining feature of anorexia nervosa (AN), yet the role of illness-related beliefs in maintaining the disorder remains underexplored. While current models of AN maintenance foreground cognitive-emotional traits, coping styles, and interpersonal dynamics, illness-related beliefs are often reduced to binary “pro” versus “anti” positions, overlooking the ways language itself conveys ambivalence. This paper proposes a transdisciplinary approach, drawing on psychosomatic medicine, psychology, psychiatry, literary studies, and rhetoric, to examine how ambiguity in patient narratives reflects and sustains ambivalence. Close analysis of diverse genres–including memoirs, poetry, and social media posts–reveals nuanced articulations that defy conventional coding schemes. Ambiguity, far from obscuring meaning, provides insight into the simultaneity of attraction and repulsion patients experience toward both AN and its treatment. By treating narratives as constitutive rather than merely descriptive of belief, this approach expands the evidentiary base of AN research and offers clinicians new tools for recognizing and engaging ambivalence in practice. Integrating narrative and literary methods with psychological frameworks can deepen understanding of illness-related beliefs and support more holistic approaches to treatment.

title: “We see ourselves on screen”: Queer film reception and tomboy identity formation in contemporary China
abstract: Abstract This article examines how tomboy-identifying individuals from second-tier Chinese cities negotiate identity, family pressure, queer film reception, and coping practices.
