It combines semi-structured interviews with 11 participants and contextual semiotic analysis of frequently referenced queer films, drawing on queer theory, gender performativity, symbolic interactionism, and resilience. In this sample, tomboy identity was a context-specific position rather than a synonym for lesbian identity. It was shaped by masculine gender expression, same-sex desire, T/P role expectations, family obligation, and social legibility. The study identifies three overlapping coping orientations: strategic compliance, parallel adaptation, and protective resistance. Participants used films including Yes or No (Saratswadee Wongsompetch, 2010), The Handmaiden (Park Chan-wook, 2016), Blue Is the Warmest Colour (Abdellatif Kechiche, 2013), and Portrait of a Lady on Fire (Céline Sciamma, 2019) as symbolic and emotional resources. These films helped them process family pressure and imagine alternative relationships, even as they criticised stereotyped and commercialised queer representation. Derived inductively from participants’ reception narratives, the Tomboy Identity Negotiation and Coping Narrative Model conceptualises identity negotiation as a cyclical process linking family pressure, coping practices, film reception, audience interpretation, and resilient meaning-making.

title: Clan culture weakens organ donation willingness—based on empirical evidence from China
abstract: The persistent global shortage of human organs underscores the urgent need to increase organ donation rates, making the identification of effective strategies a critical area of academic and policy enquiry. This study examines how clan culture—characterised by strong collective norms and hierarchical kinship structures—influences individual decisions to donate organs in China. Using the density of ancestral halls as a proxy for clan culture, we analyse data from 2226 participants across 276 prefecture-level cities in China. The results reveal that clan culture, as an informal institution, significantly weakens individuals’ willingness to donate organs. This association varies with the surrounding informal institutional environment: it is weaker where public discourse on organ donation is more active and where higher education is more prevalent, and stronger where religious activity is more widespread. These patterns point to a substitutive/complementary structure among informal institutions, in which some provide alternative sources of legitimacy while others reinforce the same bodily-integrity norms. By integrating clan-based cultural dynamics into the discourse on organ donation, this study contributes to a deeper understanding of how sociocultural contexts shape health-related behaviours and offers theoretical insights for designing culturally responsive organ donation campaigns.

title: Synergistic configurations of livelihood capital drive pastoralist well-being: evidence from Tibetan Plateau, China
abstract: Grassland governance has shifted from a primary focus on ecological restoration toward greater attention to pastoralists’ well-being. Against this background, subjective well-being (SWB) has become a core indicator for assessing livelihood outcomes in pastoral regions. Using survey data from 163 pastoral households in Sunan Yugur Autonomous County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau, this study applies fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to identify multiple pathways through which livelihood capital configurations generate high SWB. It further examines how these configurations vary across three community types exposed to distinct grazing management intensities. Results show a mean SWB score of 0.659, with 55.21% of households reporting moderate to high SWB. The grazing community records the highest SWB (0.721), while the stall-feeding community reports the lowest (0.608). Three equivalent pathways to high SWB are identified at the full sample level, in which natural and social capital serve as core conditions. In grazing communities, natural and social capital form the dominant synergistic configuration, reflecting strong ecological dependence and cohesive social ties. Under stricter grazing controls, mixed-feeding and stall-feeding households rely more on human and physical capital. Financial capital plays a limited role in all configurations, suggesting systemic constraints including low financial literacy and inadequate institutional access. These findings offer empirical evidence for context-specific pathways to improving household well-being and provide a flexible, place-based framework for sustainable rural development in ecologically fragile regions.

title: Associations between physical fitness and academic achievement among Chinese school-aged children: the role of sociodemographic moderators
abstract: The current state of evidence concerning the associations between physical fitness (PF) and academic achievement (AA) among children is mixed, suggesting that specific moderators may influence those relationships. Thus, this study aimed to examine (i) the associations between PF and AA among Chinese school-aged children and (ii) whether sex, grade, and parental education moderated those associations. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, we examined PF and AA in 7142 children from the Beijing area (mean age = 8.24 ± 1.33 years; 54.3% boys). PF was assessed using the Chinese National Student Physical Fitness Standard (CNSPFS) battery, demographic information was collected via standardized questionnaires, and AA in reading, mathematics, and English was evaluated using standardized school tests. Because timed sit-ups were administered only in Grades 3–6 and the 50 m × 8 shuttle run only in Grades 5–6, the hierarchical regressions were interpreted as staged models matched to test availability, and moderation results were further probed using conditional-effects analyses. Results: In the fully adjusted models, lower BMI was associated with better reading scores ( β = −0.060, p = 0.005); higher rope-skipping performance was associated with better reading (β = 0.095, p < 0.001), mathematics ( β = 0.113, p < 0.001), and English scores ( β = 0.106, p < 0.001); better sit-up performance was associated with better reading (β = 0.052, p = 0.015), mathematics ( β = 0.230, p < 0.001), and English scores ( β = 0.122, p < 0.001); higher vital capacity was associated with mathematics ( β = 0.360–0.373 across adjusted models, p < 0.001) and English ( β = 0.109–0.111, p < 0.001); and shorter 50 m sprint and 50 m × 8 shuttle-run times were associated with better mathematics performance ( β = −0.246 and −0.206, respectively; both p < 0.001). Sex, grade, and parental education moderated several of these associations, with the clearest patterns observed for VC and sprint performance. Conclusion: This study provides evidence for positive associations between selected PF indicators and AA in Chinese school-aged children and shows that these associations vary according to sex, grade, and parental education. Future longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to clarify directionality and mechanisms.

title: High lexical construal levels decrease negativity bias in online reading: evidence from recognition and eye-tracking experiments
abstract: Negativity bias in online reading widely occurs and leads to harmful results at the individual and social levels, but few studies have examined how to reduce this bias from the perspective of lexical processing. This study examined whether and how high lexical construal levels decrease negativity bias through a recognition memory experiment (Study 1) and an eye-tracking experiment (Study 2). In Study 1 ( N = 70), results showed a negativity bias in recognition memory, which was attenuated under high construal levels, primarily through a reduction in the discrimination sensitivity ( A ’) advantage for negative words. In Study 2 ( N = 53), eye-tracking revealed that at low construal levels, negative words were processed more quickly than positive words, indicating automated processing. Critically, at high construal levels, this pattern reversed, with positive words being processed more efficiently. These findings demonstrate that high lexical construal levels reduce negativity bias not by equalizing processing, but by attenuating the automatic advantage for negative words and shifting efficiency toward positive information.

title: Time or money? The effect of karma beliefs on consumer donation form preference
abstract: Charitable giving is commonly studied in terms of whether and how much individuals donate. However, this focus implicitly assumes that different resources are morally interchangeable, overlooking a more fundamental question: in what form people choose to give. Drawing on social exchange theory and cultural psychology, this research examines how belief in karma shapes individuals’ preferences for donating time versus money. We argue that, within karmic belief systems, moral actions are evaluated based on their qualitative moral enactment rather than quantitative magnitude. Because donating time more directly embodies personal sacrifice, experiential involvement, and sustained moral effort, it is perceived as more spiritually efficacious and morally weighty than donating money. Across a series of experiments, we find that stronger karmic beliefs increase individuals’ preference for time donations over monetary donations. This effect is mediated by karmic reciprocity motivation, reflecting a generalized moral exchange with a cosmic order, and is contingent on transcendent gratitude. Specifically, karmic reciprocity motivation translates karmic beliefs into time-donation preferences only when individuals experience high levels of transcendent gratitude. By demonstrating how cultural belief systems render resources morally non-equivalent, this research extends social exchange theory beyond interpersonal reciprocity and offers actionable insights for designing culturally resonant charitable appeals.

title: The effect of ESG assurance on ESG reporting consistency: evidence from textual similarity
abstract: This study explores the impact of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) assurance on the similarity of ESG reporting among peer companies. By analysing data from paired listed firms in China, our findings reveal a significant increase in ESG similarity for those pairs that have received ESG assurance. Further investigation reveals that this positive relationship is even stronger when the ESG assurors are nonauditor firms or have greater experience. Additionally, we assess the style of the assurance providers and find that ESG similarity is notably greater for firm pairs that share the same ESG assuror. Finally, while ESG assurance neither enhances within-firm ESG reporting similarity compared with the previous year (i.e., repetitiveness) nor induces artificial homogeneity across unrelated industries (i.e., homogenization), it does strengthen the connection between ESG reporting similarity and analyst forecast accuracy. Overall, these results suggest that ESG assurance plays a key role in improving and standardizing ESG reporting practices, leading to increased ESG reporting similarity that is valuable to its users.

title: The identification of systemically important financial institutions from the aspect of “Too Connected to Fail”
abstract: This paper investigates the identification of Systemically Important Financial Institutions (SIFIs) from a “Too Connected to Fail” perspective by applying the K-shell algorithm to a dynamic tail-risk contagion network. The network is constructed for China’s financial system using the FARM-Selection method and CoVaR measure across the COVID-19 pandemic. We find that the pandemic elevated systemic risk and increased the number of SIFIs, which were securities companies, fintech firms, and city commercial banks during the crisis. This reflects the critical role of market-making, digital payment channels, and regional credit intermediation under conditions of heightened volatility and policy support. In the post-pandemic period, SIFIs are investment institutions, insurance companies, trust firms, and fintech firms, indicating a structural reorientation of the financial system toward long-term capital allocation, risk transfer, and embedded digital finance. This shift underscores the tail-risk contagion networks adapting from crisis-driven liquidity reliance to longer-term strategic intermediation. Furthermore, SIFIs show a negative relationship with market values, suggesting that highly tail-risk connected institutions are not necessarily the largest in market capitalization. Robustness is confirmed using the PageRank algorithm. The paper provides a network-based monitoring framework and policy insights for mitigating systemic risk in China, highlighting regulating connectivity-driven systemic importance.

title: Reframing vaccine safety: recognizing mass psychogenic illness as an adverse event following immunization
abstract: Abstract Diagnoses of mass psychogenic illness (MPI) following vaccination usually occur after the failure of all efforts to find a plausible biological mechanism for the collective reaction to the vaccine in question. They are experienced as waste-basket diagnoses that leave sufferers feeling dissatisfied and neglected, without appropriate treatment or sympathy and without a “real” diagnosis. In this article, we examine reports of MPI following vaccination, focusing on vaccination programs against human papillomavirus (HPV), which usually target adolescent and preadolescent girls, as well as social science research that tries to explain the social factors involved. In particular, we interrogate social science research that aligns with participants’ feelings that they are being dismissed because MPIs are not perceived to be real illnesses. Our analysis of the scholarly literature finds that relying on debunking strategies contributes to limitations in social science responses to instances of MPI following vaccination. Recognizing MPI reactions as plausible adverse reactions to vaccination, we argue, could lead to successful treatments and changes to vaccination programs, both of which could bolster trust in vaccination, as long as the diagnosis is not used to dismiss or diminish psychogenic adverse reactions. As part of this process, the informational and communicative context is crucial to addressing vaccinee suffering and improving public trust.

title: The characteristics of financial asset price fluctuations in China- based on GARCH model
abstract: This study investigates the volatility dynamics across five major financial markets—money, stock, bond, foreign exchange, and gold—using monthly data from 2004 to 2023. Employing GARCH-type models, including TGARCH and DCC-GARCH. Our findings reveal three significant insights. First, market prices exhibit pronounced clustering behavior. Second, both the stock and gold markets demonstrate significant leverage effects, with negative shocks having a substantially greater impact than positive ones. Third, there are significant volatility spillover effects between financial markets. Notably, there are particularly robust correlations between the stock and bond markets, as well as the stock and gold markets. These findings enhance the understanding of cross-market volatility transmission and provide implications for strengthening risk monitoring, optimizing leverage management, and designing diversified financial instruments to improve market stability.

title: Exploring the financial burden of health care for undocumented immigrants
abstract: Access to healthcare for undocumented immigrants remains a persistent challenge globally. In Turkey, the increasing number of undocumented immigrants has brought new complexities to the healthcare system, particularly in terms of uncompensated care. This study aims to explore the hospital visits, admissions, and uncompensated health care costs of undocumented immigrants in two city hospitals in Ankara province, Turkey. This descriptive study analyzed hospital records from 1 January 2023 to 30 June 2024. The study population consisted of foreign nationals whose hospital episodes were charged to the patient as self-paying, an administrative category used here as a proxy for undocumented status; the Ministry of Health released its utilization and cost data under official authorization, and the research team categorized and analyzed them. We used logistic regression to predict the likelihood that inpatient service costs were covered, controlling for nationality, emergency visit, intensive care admission, and average length of stay. The findings revealed that 81.4% of the total healthcare costs related to undocumented immigrants remained uncompensated. The majority of patients were from Syria, Afghanistan, Iraq, and Somalia. Emergency department visits accounted for 42.1% of total visits, while outpatient clinic visits represented 35.7%. The average unreimbursed cost per patient was calculated at $583. The provision of healthcare services to undocumented immigrants has become an increasing economic burden on the Turkish healthcare system. To facilitate access to healthcare for vulnerable groups within the undocumented migrant population, new financial mechanisms must be developed by both national and international stakeholders. In addition to financial solutions, legal and humanitarian strategies are also needed to ensure equitable access to healthcare for undocumented immigrants.

title: How government digital governance enhances supply chain efficiency: the mediating role of resource misallocation
abstract: This study examines the impact of government digital governance on corporate supply chain efficiency using a difference-in-differences approach and panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms. The results show that government digital governance significantly enhances corporate supply chain efficiency by alleviating internal financial and external market resource misallocation. The effect is particularly pronounced among firms located southeast of the Hu Huanyong Line, those closer to suppliers, non-state-owned enterprises, and firms with lower supply chain concentration. This study offers empirical evidence on the economic effects of government digital governance and provides insights into promoting resilient, efficient supply chain systems in transitional economies.

title: The financial benefits of sustainability: analyzing the impact of sustainable finance on capital costs for London stock exchange firms
abstract: Abstract Corporations that implement sustainable financial strategies experience a reduction in borrowing costs. A broader range of investors, particularly those prioritizing ESG considerations, is typically attracted to these firms. Investors view a high cost of capital as an indicator of high risk, requiring a higher return to mitigate that risk. This study utilized the resource-based view (RBV) theory to examine the impact of investments in sustainable finance on the cost of capital. The selection of companies was guided by rigorous inclusion criteria, and a purposive sampling strategy was employed to collect 18 years of data from 227 companies listed on the London Stock Exchange between 2006 and 2023, using Thomson Reuters Eikon DataStream. The study employed the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG) and two-step Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimation methods to analyze the relationships between the variables. The findings indicate that green bonds issued, CSR expenditures, and investments in renewable energy positively and significantly impact the cost of debt, equity, and weighted average cost of capital (WACC). Conversely, sustainable-linked loans negatively and significantly affect the cost of debt. Additionally, the moderating relationship between a firm's age and the issuance of green bonds positively and significantly impacts the cost of debt, cost of equity, and WACC. To enhance their appeal to socially conscious investors, companies should demonstrate transparency regarding their environmental benefits, thereby boosting investor confidence in the organization.

title: Policy-text assessment of data minimisation compliance in mobile banking: lessons from China
abstract: The spread of mobile payments has made mobile banking apps integral to day-to-day financial transactions in China. These applications access and process a wide range of personal information stored on users’ devices, giving rise to significant privacy concerns, most notably with respect to the principle of data minimisation. While prior studies on Chinese banks’ privacy policies exist, the extent to which joint-stock commercial banks’ policies align with the Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL)’s data minimisation principle remains underexplored. This study presents a policy-text assessment of twelve leading Chinese joint-stock commercial banks’ privacy policy employing a structured 0–2 scoring rubric across necessity, purpose limitation, and storage limitation dimensions. The findings indicate that, although the overall textual alignment with PIPL is generally high, moderate scores often reflect linguistic ambiguity in legal storage and deletion provisions, which may undermine consumers’ trust. It is essential to emphasise that these findings pertain to declared policy commitments rather than actual data-handling practices. Our analysis informs sectoral guidance and underscores the need for greater language precision to bolster consumer trust.

title: The structure and resilience of traditional energy trade networks in countries along the belt and road
abstract: Energy security, as a cornerstone of national strategic frameworks, plays a pivotal role in advancing the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). This study investigates the structure and resilience of energy trade networks across 154 BRI countries (regions) from 2001 to 2023, utilizing coal, oil, and natural gas trade data and constructing a dynamic weighted directed network model. The results demonstrate that the evolving BRI energy trade network showcases improved connectivity and a sophisticated, multi-tiered brokerage system; however, nodal influence remains highly uneven. Core nodes, including South Africa, Russia, and China, continue to exert disproportionate influence, maintaining a core-periphery structure with degree distribution Gini coefficients consistently above 0.4. This hierarchical pattern coexists with multicentric restructuring in the backbone network, where strengthened connectivity between core layers accompanies reduced betweenness centrality disparities and increasing topological complexity. Notably, improvements in resilience vary significantly by sector: coal trade networks achieve 4% higher recovery efficiency than their oil and gas counterparts, even as the network overall shows enhanced robustness against both random and targeted attacks. Most importantly, the declining coefficient of variation in nodal resilience, from 10.84% to 8.76%, provides empirical evidence of a progression toward equilibrium in regional energy cooperation. This study underscores the need for dynamic core-node monitoring systems, decentralized trade frameworks, and collaborative innovation platforms to optimize BRI energy governance. These insights provide actionable pathways for building adaptive, multicentric energy systems that align with sustainable development goals.

title: Developing environmental performance in the Bangladesh banking sector: role of fintech, climate finance and environmental awareness
abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between climate banking and the environmental performance of banks in Bangladesh, focusing on climate finance, environmental awareness, and the role of FinTech. The study used the partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) technique to analyse data from 312 bank practitioners. The results revealed that climate banking practices (CBP) are positively associated with climate finance (CF), environmental awareness (EA), and FinTech adoption (FA). CF and FA are positively related to the bank’s environmental performance (BEP), while EA determines both direct and indirect associations with BEP. FA and CF play a mediating role in the relationship between CBP and BEP. This research contributes to the first empirical understanding of how digital transformation and climate-aligned financing mechanisms can promptly promote sustainability in the Global South banking sector context. This builds the groundwork for understanding how increased climate change resilience can contribute to the sustainability and global competitiveness of banks in emerging economies. This also aids policymakers and banks in developing convergence strategies with global frameworks for sustainable development.

title: How does corporate ESG performance affect the return resilience of infrastructure REITs? An empirical analysis based on spatiotemporal perspective and Chinese data
abstract: This study examines the impact of corporate ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) performance on the return resilience of infrastructure real estate investment trusts (Infra-REITs). Based on transaction data from 66 Chinese Infra-REITs between June 2021 and May 2025, and referencing the GRESB ESG benchmark and reporting framework, corporate ESG performance is categorized into three dimensions: Environmental Performance (E), social performance (S), and governance performance (G), encompassing 17 indicators. The optimal parameter geodetector model was employed to conduct factor detection and interaction analysis, systematically evaluating the impact mechanisms of ESG factors on Infra-REITs’ return resilience. Subsequently, ArcGIS software was used to identify differences in key factors influencing return resilience across eastern, central, and western China. The findings reveal: (1) Labor responsibility, Regional project development, and fund management capabilities are core determinants of return resilience. Project environmental and social performance exhibit significant positive correlations with Infra-REITs return resilience, whereas management performance shows weaker associations—challenging the conventional assumption of universal positive ESG effects; (2) The interactions among ESG dimensions significantly enhance the explanatory power for return resilience, particularly in the impact of Regional project development and labor responsibility on the Resistance index, as well as the influence of carbon footprint and social responsibility on the recovery index. (3) The spatial characteristics of ESG factors lead to differing emphases among Infra-REITs across regions. Infra-REIT projects in eastern regions prioritize social and governance performance, while central region projects emphasize enhancing social performance. Western region projects focus on environmental performance and fund pricing premiums driven by resource scarcity. Based on these findings, policy formulation and operational practices should adopt differentiated strategies tailored to Infra-REIT types and regional characteristics to optimize ESG performance, so as to enhance overall return resilience.

title: Emission strategies of conglomerates: pollution emission and transfer mechanisms under energy regulation
abstract: Abstract Conglomerates constitute a core component of modern economies and play a pivotal role in resource allocation. Using China’s “Top 1,000” energy conservation program as an exogenous policy shock, this paper employs a difference-in-differences design based on manufacturing firm panel data to investigate how energy regulation affects intra-conglomerate pollution strategies. We find that stringent energy regulation significantly reduces pollution emissions at targeted firms, yet leads to substantial pollution being shifted to their unregulated affiliates. Internal pollution relocation is more prevalent among larger, capital-intensive, high-tech, and state-owned enterprises. Mechanistically, energy regulation improves energy efficiency and end-of-pipe treatment at regulated firms, while also enhancing abatement at their affiliates. Moreover, energy regulation generates significant spillover effects on both pollution abatement and employment in affiliated firms. This study provides novel empirical evidence on the efficacy of energy-saving policies and illuminates how conglomerates adjust production decisions in response to regulatory pressure.

title: Between myth and power: global players and the politics of reception of Black Myth: Wukong on Reddit
abstract: Once peripheral to the global gaming industry, Chinese studios have increasingly sought to reposition themselves as global creative leaders. Black Myth: Wukong (Game Science, 2024) marks a pivotal moment in this shift toward culturally distinctive, mechanically complex, and narratively rich high-budget game production. While the game has been widely celebrated within China for its adaptation of classical mythology and its impressive audiovisual and technical design, its international reception reveals more ambivalent dynamics. This study examines how non-China-based gamers interpret and debate Wukong on Reddit, a major platform for transnational gaming discourse. Using Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), supported by automated data scraping and sentiment analysis, the article identifies three key discursive nodes shaping the game’s global circulation. First, players express strong fascination with the game’s mythological aesthetics, though their interpretations are often shaped by cultural discount. Second, discussions reflect ambivalence toward China’s soft power ambitions, combining aesthetic admiration with political skepticism. Third, frictions emerge around cultural translation, geopolitical distrust, and contested gender representations. The article argues that Wukong ’s “Chineseness” functions simultaneously as a cultural resource and a site of ideological tension within the platformed geopolitics of contemporary gaming.

title: Exploring the impact of generative AI-facilitated personalized learning on EFL students’ speaking and writing skills
abstract: The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in education has created opportunities for individualized learning. However, its effects on the speaking and writing skills of EFL students are still insufficiently examined. Current research predominantly emphasizes AI-assisted writing support, with limited empirical data on its efficacy in enhancing speaking proficiency. Seventy-eight EFL undergraduate students from a private university in North Cyprus were recruited for this study. The participants included 53 males and 25 females ( N = 78). The participants were between 18 and 25 years old. They were assigned to control and experimental groups. Pretests and posttests were used to assess fluency, accuracy, coherence, and lexical resources in both speaking and writing. The experimental group completed the same sequence of GenAI-supported tasks using standardized prompts, while the control group completed equivalent tasks using traditional instructional methods. This strategy facilitates the evaluation of the intervention’s efficacy by comparing performance variations between the two groups. Results from paired t-tests, independent t-tests, and ANCOVA showed that the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group, with large effect sizes, in both skills. Within the scope of this study, GenAI-facilitated personalized learning was associated with measurable gains in speaking and writing proficiency when implemented as a structured pedagogical co-assistant rather than a substitute for instruction; broader generalization beyond this sample and institutional context awaits further research. The study discusses implications for classroom practice, educational policy, and responsible GenAI integration in English language teaching.

title: Impact of number of children and childrearing values on recognition of homemakers’ value in China: age-period-cohort analysis with data of the World Values Survey (1995–2018)
abstract: Utilizing data from the World Values Survey spanning five waves (1995–2018) in China and employing a Hierarchical Age-Period-Cohort (HAPC) model, this study examines how the number of children and the childrearing values affect the recognition of homemakers’ value across genders, with attention to period and cohort dynamics in China. Results show that the number of children had no significant effect on the recognition of homemaker value among women and men, while the childrearing values had a positive impact, although this influence diminished among men who highly valued childrearing. Further period–cohort analyses show that the effect of the number of children on recognition of homemakers’ value has become increasingly positive, while the influence of childrearing values remains stable. This reveals that stronger childrearing values remain associated with greater recognition of homemakers’ value among women under the enduring influence of Confucian ethics. It also suggests that women with a greater number of children have increasingly sought broader societal recognition of homemakers’ value as China’s pronatalist policies have expanded. Conversely, although men had consistently higher recognition of homemakers’ value, largely render context-dependent judgments shaped by family childcare needs and personal benefits. These findings refine Becker’s quantity-quality trade-off model and advance the gendered political implications of Yan’s neo-familism thesis, providing empirically grounded insights for the construction of fertility support systems in the post-three-child era.

title: Quantile analysis of green innovation and renewable energy effects on G20 ecological footprint
abstract: Abstract This study examines the effects of green technologies (GT) and renewable energy (RE) on the ecological footprint (EFP) at different distribution levels across G20 countries over the period 1992–2021. Utilizing Panel Quantile-on-Quantile Regression (PQQR) and Panel Conditional Quantile (PCQ) models, the results show that GT significantly reduces EFP across most quantiles, with its impact intensifying at higher levels. However, a modest decline in efficacy at the highest quantile suggests possible transitional or scale effects that may temporarily offset environmental benefits. These findings underscore the long-term potential of GT to improve environmental quality, provided that implementation strategies minimize early-stage inefficiencies. Conversely, RE demonstrates a consistent mitigating effect on EFP in the lower and middle quantiles, though its influence weakens and becomes statistically insignificant in the upper quantile. This pattern indicates that RE is more effective under conditions of low to moderate environmental pressure, whereas its standalone capacity to curb ecological degradation diminishes in high-EFP settings. In such contexts, RE should be complemented by broader policy frameworks, including industrial decarbonization and improved energy efficiency measures. Overall, these results highlight the need for differentiated environmental strategies tailored to a country’s ecological footprint, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of GT and RE in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

title: Confucian institutional ethics: an informal constraint on corporate greenwashing
abstract: Amidst global efforts towards low-carbon transition and the increasing focus on corporate environmental responsibility, understanding the role of informal institutions becomes crucial. Positioning Confucian culture as an informal institutional factor, this study examines its impact on corporate greenwashing mitigation using panel data from Chinese listed firms between 2010 and 2024. Empirical results demonstrate that Confucian culture significantly inhibits corporate greenwashing, a conclusion supported by robustness and endogeneity tests. Furthermore, we identify the underlying mechanisms, including corporate social responsibility, managerial self-interest, and accounting information disclosure. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that this inhibitory effect is particularly pronounced in regions with relatively weak Western cultural influence and formal rules. This study enriches upper echelons theory, imprinting theory, and social responsibility theory, providing empirical evidence for understanding how Confucian culture shapes corporate environmental decision-making. Collectively, it provides robust empirical evidence on the pivotal role of informal cultural institutions in guiding corporate environmental conduct and facilitating low-carbon transition.

title: The promise and peril of digital technology: evidence from digital skill polarization in Indonesia
abstract: Abstract The expansion of the digital economy presents new economic opportunities, particularly for geographically challenged populations, yet its benefits hinge on individuals’ ability to leverage digital tools productively. This paper proposes a conceptual framework to measure digital skills in developing economies, demonstrating its application with novel and nationally representative survey data from Indonesia. Despite the massive rollout of internet connectivity, there is a lack of systematic frameworks to assess and monitor digital skills, particularly in developing economies. This gap limits policymakers’ ability to design effective interventions that address the challenges of skill-biased technological change. Focusing on Indonesia, this paper introduces a novel framework to assess adults’ digital skills and its application using survey data. The paper reveals several important insights. First, digital skills remain very low among adult population in Indonesia, potentially undermining the impact of improved internet connectivity in the last few decades. Second, among internet-users, most have skills for general use, such as communications, whilst only a small share has specialized skills (e.g., work-related, productivity software, or programming language). There is also heterogeneity in digital skills across different demographic groups. Digital-skills proficiency is driven by the interplay of both technical and cognitive abilities (critical thinking and growth mindset), along with certain demography factors such as connectivity, age, and education level. Advanced skills are concentrated among those with better connectivity, higher education, and prime working age. The paper highlights the need for systematic tracking of digital literacy and skill development, the integration of skill-building strategies into national digital transformations to mitigate impacts from skill-biased technological change. The paper concludes with insights and policy implications relevant to broader emerging economies.

title: Before the data arrive: a pre-entry transferability framework for alternative credit scoring in emerging economies
abstract: Abstract Despite rapid digital adoption, approximately 51% of Indonesian adults remain unbanked, and access to formal credit is further constrained by limited credit bureau coverage—a gap that alternative credit scoring can help close, but only if the behavioral signals developed in more advanced markets can be reliably transferred to the local context. This study addresses the fundamental challenge facing financial institutions that seek to extend credit access in emerging economies: how to evaluate the deployability of alternative credit scoring variables across national markets before any local performance data are collected. We propose the Cross-Market Variable Transferability Score (CMVTS), a composite index that combines Jensen-Shannon divergence over variable distributions, Spearman rank correlation over macro-economic indicators, and cosine similarity over a comparative statistics vector. Their weighted combination yields a single score bounded in [0, 1] that maps directly to a three-tier decision rule—HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW—prescribing whether direct transfer, partial adjustment, or local redevelopment is warranted. Applied to the Korea–Indonesia market pair using a synthetic credit bureau dataset of 3,129,036 records and 34 macro-economic indicators, the CMVTS yields 0.9225–0.9338 across all 47 tested specifications (0.9338 under the baseline specification; 0.9225 under the refined empirical-prior specification), placing the verdict firmly in the HIGH tier. This verdict rests on a single, structurally comparable market pair; whether it reflects genuine market similarity as opposed to favourable pair selection can only be settled by cross-pair empirical validation, which we identify as the principal direction for future work. Nine transferred variables yield projected portfolio figures of a lift of 262.8 and an approved-population bad rate of 0.024% at the 550-point threshold, illustrating the expected risk differentiation achievable through direct variable transfer prior to local recalibration. To our knowledge, CMVTS is the first framework to operationalize a pre-transfer quantitative transferability assessment for credit scoring variables as a composite of information-theoretic, rank-order, and structural similarity measures, applied prior to any target-market data collection. By enabling financial institutions to screen variable transferability prior to market entry, the CMVTS framework can accelerate the deployment of alternative credit scoring in underserved markets—advancing the goals of financial inclusion aligned with SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)—two of the United Nations’ 2030 Sustainable Development Goals targeting equitable economic inclusion.

title: I am also a candidate for president in the upcoming elections: simulating an election campaign with gifted students
abstract: Abstract The aim of this research is to reveal the political tendencies and interests of gifted students at high school level and to enable them to explore political election processes and leadership aspects through an applied election campaign simulation. The study group of the research, in which the qualitative research method was adopted, consisted of 14 students, 6 female students and 8 male students, aged 15–16, who were diagnosed with giftedness (130 IQ and above) and who were studying at high school level in a Science and Art Center in Türkiye. In this direction, an election simulation was prepared by the researchers and applied for 12 weeks. The study employed basic qualitative research design. The data was collected through semi-structured interviews and student-produced documents and analyzed using descriptive analysis. To summarize the results of the study in general, it is possible to say that the gifted students in the study group achieved the gains expected from them at the end of the election campaign simulation, that conducting the political election process by doing and experiencing it, and moreover, by being the planner of this process at the beginning of this process, contributed positively to the students, and that the election simulation was associated with gifted students’ exploration of the political election process and their leadership aspects.

title: Unlocking informal social support to empower empty-nest families’ tourism consumption in the digital age
abstract: The aging of the population is becoming more and more severe, and the continuous growth of empty-nest families cannot be ignored. With improvements in the quality of life for older people and increased leisure time, their tourism consumption potential is gradually emerging. However, it is unclear which factors more influence the tourism consumption of empty-nest families. Based on the China Family Panel Survey (CFPS) data, this study identifies the impact of informal social support on the tourism consumption of empty-nest older adults and examines the underlying mechanisms. This study finds that informational and emotional support show more significant effects on the tourism consumption of empty-nest families, while instrumental and economic support have a relatively limited effect. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that the effects are more pronounced among older-aged empty-nesters, retired households, and urban households. Mechanism analyses show that the effect on empty-nest families operates primarily through improving health status and digital literacy. This study provides insights into promoting tourist consumption among empty-nest elders and encouraging the tourism sector’s sustainable growth in the digital age.

title: Energy security risk and the global energy transition under external uncertainty: evidence from 74 countries
abstract: As climate change intensifies and the global energy crisis deepens, the energy transition has become a central policy priority for both developed and developing nations. However, rising concerns over energy security, coupled with increasing economic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions, complicate the transition process. This study investigates the effect of energy security risk (ESR) on energy transition (ET), while considering the moderating roles of economic policy uncertainty (EPU) and geopolitical risk (GPR). A panel dataset covering 74 countries from 1980 to 2022 is analyzed using a two-way fixed effects model, which controls for both country-specific and time-specific heterogeneity. To ensure the robustness of the findings, several checks are performed, including the use of alternative energy transition measures, subsample periods, and endogeneity tests. The empirical results reveal that higher ESR significantly promotes global ET. However, this effect is conditional on external uncertainty. Specifically, EPU weakens the positive effect of ESR on ET, whereas GPR, geopolitical actions, and war strengthen this effect. Heterogeneity analysis further demonstrates that the effect is stronger in countries with higher shares of renewable energy production and in upper-middle-income economies, while it turns negative in energy-exporting countries, likely due to the resource curse, where heavy reliance on fossil fuel exports hampers the adoption of renewable energy. These findings highlight the complex interplay between energy security and external uncertainty in shaping energy transition dynamics. Policy implications include the need for enhanced energy diversification, the stabilization of policy environments to reduce uncertainty-induced distortions, the integration of geopolitical risks into energy planning, and the adoption of differentiated transition strategies for energy-exporting economies.

title: Moving towards the pathway to net-zero carbon emissions through nuclear energy in OECD countries: the moderating role of artificial intelligence
abstract: Abstract Existing research highlights that artificial intelligence can enhance energy security and support the pursuit of net-zero carbon emission goals. Yet, scholarly attention to its role in shaping the relationship between nuclear energy use and carbon dioxide emissions remains limited. This study addresses that gap by offering one of the earliest empirical investigations linking artificial intelligence, nuclear energy consumption, and CO₂ emissions across 17 Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries from 1994 to 2020. This study also examines whether artificial intelligence can help to form an environmental Kuznets curve (EKC) in OECD countries. To achieve this objective, we design a novel analytical framework that examines the influence of artificial intelligence and nuclear energy on the dynamics of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC). Empirical analysis indicates that nuclear energy contributes to reduced carbon emissions. Additionally, artificial intelligence has a negligible impact on CO 2 emissions. Furthermore, there is unidirectional causality between artificial intelligence and CO 2 emissions, as well as between nuclear energy and CO 2 emissions. To summarize, nuclear energy consumption contributes to the formation of EKC, whereas artificial intelligence does not appear to have a similar effect. Based on these results, some economic policy implications are discussed.

title: Uncertainty And Performance of Firms in Vietnam
abstract: This study develops a sustainable approach to construct uncertainty indices at national and provincial levels in Vietnam, leveraging Google Trends data to assess economic, social, and environmental uncertainties. Using a robust selection process (Delphi method), the paper identifies a benchmark keyword and 12 related terms to build these indices, reflecting search frequency trends. The analysis, based on panel data from 2016 to 2020, employs the system Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) to evaluate the impact of uncertainty on firm performance. At the national level, uncertainty peaked in 2011 and 2013 but has since declined. At the provincial level, Quang Tri, Quang Binh, Kon Tum, and Phu Yen exhibited the highest uncertainty in 2020, while Thanh Hoa, Dong Nai, Hanoi, and Ho Chi Minh City were the most stable. Findings reveal that both national and provincial uncertainty reduce firm performance, with economic uncertainty boosting Total Factor Productivity (TFP), whereas social and environmental uncertainties hinder it. Provincially, institutional quality mediates this impact in a U-shaped pattern, suggesting targeted policy interventions to enhance firm resilience. These insights inform strategies to mitigate uncertainty’s adverse effects, supporting sustainable economic development in Vietnam.

title: Supplier concentration and supply chain resilience: unpacking the dual role of digitalization and information transparency
abstract: Supply chain resilience (SCR) has long been recognized as crucial to survival in today’s turbulent environment. Despite extensive discussions on supplier concentration, the insights into its role in achieving SCR remain limited and inconsistent. To provide a more balanced view, the complex influence of supplier concentration on SCR is examined through the perspective of resource dependence theory (RDT). This research hypothesizes an inverted U-shaped relationship between supplier concentration and SCR, with digitalization and information transparency acting as moderating factors. This relationship is supported by our empirical evidence based on a sample of 2278 Chinese listed firms during 2008–2022. Interestingly, our findings indicate that the inverted U-shaped relationship is flattened by digitalization, but steepened by information transparency of the focal firm. Both moderators shift the turning point of the curve to the right. Notably, the curvilinear relationship is stronger in firms with high market share, non-state-owned enterprises, firms operating in highly competitive industries, and those located in regions with strong institutional development. Additionally, our further analysis shows that digitalization and information transparency independently influence how supplier concentration affects SCR, but their effects do not reinforce each other when considered jointly. The curvilinear relationship operates through the supply chain governance efficiency mechanism and the opportunism–uncertainty mechanism. This work contributes to the understanding of SCR determinants and the literature on optimal supplier concentration. It also provides practical implications for business practitioners and policymakers, offering valuable insights into how to manage supplier concentration to enhance overall resilience.

title: The relationship between cognitive appraisal, achievement emotions, and motor skills in a physical education classroom context: a longitudinal study
abstract: The purpose of this study, based on Control-Value Theory of Achievement Emotions, was to examine the correlations and longitudinal associations between cognitive appraisal, two achievement emotions, and two motor skills in a physical education classroom context. The study employed a two-year longitudinal follow-up design, with follow-ups spaced one year apart, and included a total of 698 middle school students aged 12–15 years ( M = 13.43; SD = 0.68), comprising 382 males and 316 females. Correlation analysis revealed moderate to strong positive correlations among academic sense of control, subjective task value, enjoyment, and badminton skill, and moderate negative correlations between these variables and boredom as well as basketball time (indicating better basketball skill), both within and across time points (all ps < 0.01). In the cross-lagged model, T1 academic sense of control significantly predicted T2 enjoyment and T2 basketball skills; T1 subjective task value significantly predicted T2 enjoyment and T2 basketball skills; enjoyment and basketball skills showed reciprocal predictive relationships; T1 boredom mood significantly predicted a slower T2 basketball time (indicating poorer basketball skill); and T1 badminton skills significantly predicted T2 enjoyment mood. In the semi-longitudinal mediation model, enjoyment mediated between feelings of academic control and basketball skills; enjoyment mediated between subjective task value and basketball skills. Overall, the findings suggest that enjoyment can influence adolescents’ motor skills and that feelings of academic control and subjective task value are important antecedents of enjoyment. This study provides a basis and direction for improving physical education teaching, and provides an in-depth understanding of the actual situation of emotion, motor skills and related factors in the current physical education classroom to help educators better grasp the current situation in the classroom, and then optimize the teaching process in a targeted manner to improve the quality of physical education teaching.

title: ESG performance and financial performance in banks: a comparative analysis of China and the USA under environmental uncertainty and COVID-19
abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and financial performance of banks in the two world’s largest economies, with the moderating impact of environmental uncertainty (e.g., “operational revenue volatility”) and COVID-19. Using unbalanced secondary data of 315 banks spanning from 2011 to 2022, we examine both the direct and non-linear effects of ESG performance on financial performance, employing advanced econometric estimation techniques such as two-step system GMM (2sGMM) and two-stage least squares (2SLS). The analysis finds that: (i) ESG performance positively influences financial performance in both Chinese and US banks, with China showing a stronger effect due to its evolving regulatory landscape, while the relationship in the US is more nuanced, given the mature ESG framework. (ii) The results also confirm that ESG performance non-linearly influences financial performance across the samples, with an inverted U-shape relationship; (iii) Additionally, we further investigate the moderating impacts of environmental uncertainty and COVID-19, uncovering that environmental uncertainty dampens the nexus between ESG performance and bank financial performance, while COVID-19 further amplifies it. This study contributes to the existing literature by offering a comparative perspective on the effect of ESG performance on financial outcomes across different economic contexts and presents valuable insights for policymakers, regulators, and financial institutions aiming to navigate the emerging landscape of ESG performance amidst global uncertainties.

title: Scaffolding agency in cultural policy: a capabilities framework for evaluating cultural interventions
abstract: Abstract The role of culture in promoting social and behavioral change has gained increasing attention in cultural policy, yet mechanisms of intervention, which we situate on a spectrum ranging from nudges to cultural interventions, remain insufficiently conceptualized. This lack of clarity obscures how different interventions relate to one another and complicates their evaluation, contributing to the well-known limitations of “toolkit” approaches. This paper develops a unifying framework that understands interventions as ways of scaffolding agency across multiple dimensions. Drawing on the capabilities approach, philosophy, and situated cognition, we argue that nudges and cultural interventions are best conceived as points on a spectrum defined by the degree of agency they afford. This perspective provides principled criteria for both intervention design and impact assessment, offering an alternative to reductive evaluation models while accommodating the complexity of cultural engagement.

title: Reading Fear in Ancient Sculpture: A FACS Based Psycho-Iconographic Approach
abstract: Ancient sculpture communicates cultural, ideological, and emotional meanings, yet emotional expression has often been interpreted primarily through descriptive evaluation. This study proposes a three-layered model combining FACS based morphological observation with iconographic and psycho-iconographic interpretation to examine representations of fear in ancient sculpture. Since FACS was developed for facial behaviour in motion, the sculptures are treated not as behavioural records but as static, artistically stylised facial forms. Visible features of the brow, eyes, mouth, and jaw are first described and then compared with FACS Action Unit appearances. Focusing on Classical and Hellenistic works and their Roman copies and adaptations, the analysis shows that facial forms associated with fear frequently overlap with pain, surprise, physical tension, shock, and defensive reactions, while narrative contexts of threat, defeat, and impending death strengthen their interpretation as fear-related. The proposed model does not aim to identify the inner emotions of the figures or to establish a universal emotional code, but rather to make the visual, iconographic, and psycho-iconographic stages of emotional interpretation clearer and more comparable.

title: The impact of inward foreign direct investment on ASEAN countries’ participation in global value chains
abstract: This paper empirically examines the structural impact of inward foreign direct investment (FDI) on global value chain (GVC) participation utilizing a panel dataset covering nine ASEAN economies over the period of 2000–2020. The analysis distinguishes between aggregate GVC participation and its forward and backward components. It investigates how the FDI-GVC relationship varies across countries at different stages of economic development and levels of industrial sophistication. The results reveal a clear asymmetry in the effects of FDI. Inward FDI is positively and significantly associated with aggregate GVC participation and backward linkages, while its effect on forward linkages is statistically insignificant. This pattern is more pronounced in middle- and low-income ASEAN economies, whereas FDI shows no significant association with GVC participation in high-income member states. Furthermore, the marginal effect of FDI on GVC participation declines as the level of industrial technological sophistication increases. These findings suggest that while FDI contributes to expanding ASEAN’s integration into global production networks, its role in facilitating upgrading toward upstream activities remains limited. Complementary policies aimed at strengthening domestic absorptive capacity and industrial capabilities are therefore important to translate FDI-driven integration into qualitative upgrading within GVCs.

title: Open government data as a driver for artificial intelligence innovation
abstract: Abstract As the digital economy era arrives, the data factor plays a crucial role in artificial intelligence innovation. Governments, as the principal custodians and generators of data, hold a vast repository of core data. It remains unclear whether open government data promote artificial intelligence innovation. Based on the data-driven innovation paradigm, this article constructs a theoretical model to explain how open government data improve artificial intelligence innovation and then empirically explores the impacts of open government data on artificial intelligence innovation. Specifically, with data on 281 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2023, this research adopts staggered difference-in-differences (DID) and spatial DID approaches to explore the direct and spatial spillover effects of open government data on artificial intelligence innovation. The main findings can be summarised as follows: Open government data not only positively influence artificial intelligence innovation in a certain city but also foster artificial intelligence innovation in neighbouring cities. Enterprises play a dominant role in driving innovation within the artificial intelligence industry compared both to universities and colleges and to research institutes. These conclusions provide theoretical insights and practical suggestions for improving artificial intelligence innovation from a data-driven perspective.

title: Integrating ERP, MES, and PLM for condition-based maintenance: a digital transformation framework for medical device manufacturing
abstract: This study presents a practical framework for digitalized asset management in a multinational medical device manufacturer transitioning toward continuous manufacturing. Using an exploratory case study supported by Weibull reliability modeling, we evaluate the shift from manual, schedule-based maintenance to condition-based, data-driven strategies. The proposed system integrates Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) within an ISA-95–aligned architecture, enabling real-time monitoring, optimized maintenance scheduling, and improved resource allocation. Results show a 9.3% reduction in conditional failure probability and a cumulative production increase of over 600,000 parts within 450 days. In addition, the framework eliminates paper-based records, enhances cost transparency, and improves resource efficiency, contributing to both economic and environmental sustainability.

title: Adaptation to climate change in agricultural production: habitus, field, and capital from a Bourdieu perspective
abstract: Climate change has significantly affected agricultural production and farmers’ livelihoods, requiring continuous adaptation to changing environmental conditions. Drawing on Bourdieu’s concepts of field, habitus, and capital, this study examines how farmers adapt to climate change and how different forms of capital shape their adaptive capacity. A qualitative phenomenological design was employed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 farmers in the Çatalca district of Istanbul, Türkiye. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis with the support of MAXQDA 24, generating five themes and 23 subthemes. The findings indicate that farmers combine inherited local knowledge with modern agricultural practices, while adaptation is influenced by unequal access to economic, cultural, and social capital. Farmers with stronger economic resources, broader social networks, greater access to scientific knowledge, and higher symbolic status demonstrate greater adaptive capacity. The findings further show that climate change is gradually transforming farmers’ habitus as traditional agricultural practices become increasingly misaligned with changing environmental conditions. From a Bourdieusian perspective, the agricultural field both shapes and is shaped by farmers’ forms of capital, while habitus mediates adaptation strategies and is continuously reconstructed through this process. By extending Bourdieu’s theoretical framework to climate change adaptation, this study demonstrates that adaptation is not merely a technical or environmental response but a socially structured process shaped by power relations, unequal capital, and the transformation of habitus. The findings contribute to the growing literature on the social dimensions of climate change adaptation and provide implications for socially inclusive and culturally sensitive adaptation policies.

title: How does the digitalization of global value chains affect China’s carbon welfare performance?
abstract: Enhancing carbon welfare performance (WPCE) is an important driving force to promote economic and social development in the direction of green and low-carbon. Based on the panel data of 30 provinces in China from 2007 to 2020, the article systematically examines the effects and mechanisms of Global Value Chain (GVC) digitization on China’s WPCE. The study finds that the digitalization of GVCs significantly contributes to the improvement of WPCE, and the mechanism analysis shows that the digitalization of GVCs contributes to the improvement of China’s WPCE through the fourfold pathways of optimizing industrial structure, promoting technological innovation, accumulating human capital, and mitigating resource misallocation. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect of GVC digitization on China’s WPCE is more prominent in the southern region, the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB), and regions with better economic development. The findings of the study provide policy references and a theoretical basis for how China can move towards green and low-carbon transformation and realize high-quality development.

title: Revisiting the fiscal deficit and infrastructure nexus: insights from Nigeria’s economic development
abstract: Fiscal deficits remain a persistent challenge in Nigeria, primarily driven by weak revenue mobilisation, over-dependence on oil, and high recurrent expenditure, which limits investment in critical infrastructure. This research revisits the fiscal deficits and infrastructure nexus in Nigeria, utilising annual data from 1990 to 2022. The analysis employs the ARDL bounds testing approach, complemented by FMOLS, CCR, and Granger Causality tests. The results reveal that, in the short term, physical infrastructure exerts a delayed negative and significant effect on fiscal deficits (−0.36, p < 0.01, lagged), inflation with mixed impacts (0.03 contemporaneous, + 0.03 lagged, both significant), and oil revenue strongly reduces fiscal deficits (-1.46, p < 0.01), a reflection of Nigeria’s fiscal vulnerability to commodity cycles. In the long run, physical infrastructure increases fiscal deficits (+0.36, p < 0.05, lagged), social infrastructure (health and education) has a positive but insignificant effect (+0.15), while inflation reduces deficit (−0.03, p < 0.01). GDP growth remains positive but insignificant. Granger causality tests indicate that inflation unidirectionally causes fiscal deficits, emphasising the central role of macroeconomic stability. These findings resonate with Keynesian, endogenous growth, and Hirschman’s unbalanced growth theories, which support the idea that targeted infrastructure spending, though initially deficit-inducing, may catalyse growth in the long term. The study recommends stabilising inflation through fiscal-monetary coordination, diversifying revenue beyond oil, and prioritising borrowing for high-return projects. Policymakers should strengthen human capital and expand public-private partnerships (PPPs) to bridge the infrastructure gap while mitigating fiscal vulnerability, thereby ensuring that Nigeria’s infrastructural needs are met through sustainable fiscal management.

title: Key predictors of subjective well-being among Chinese people: a multi-wave national cross-sectional analysis using machine learning, 2015–2023
abstract: Subjective well-being (SWB) refers to individuals’ subjective appraisal of their own well-being and provides invaluable insights for public policy. However, the relative importance of its numerous predictors remains poorly understood. This study employed a machine learning approach with multi-wave national data to identify the key predictors of SWB among Chinese people. Data were drawn from the 2015 ( N = 10,968), 2021 ( N = 5458), and 2023 ( N = 11,326) three-wave repeated cross-sectional surveys of the Chinese General Social Survey. Using the XGBoost algorithm, we modeled SWB scores based on 31 predictors. Analysis of feature importance consistently identified six factors as the most robust predictors across all three waves: perception of social equity, family economic status, depression, current social class, age, and self-reported physical health. The six-feature model achieved R 2 = 0.21–0.26 in development and 0.23 in external validation, recovering 84.0–86.7% of the variance explained by the full 31-feature model, demonstrating stable predictive performance across independent cohorts. These findings identify a parsimonious set of core predictors for the Chinese population and offer an evidence-based foundation for targeted policymaking. The simplified model also holds potential for practical application in policy simulation and decision support.

title: The role of psychological factors in shaping online tourism platforms customer’s purchase intention: a fuzzy Delphi and FCM approach
abstract: The growing digitalization of tourism services has reshaped consumer behavior, yet many users, particularly in developing markets, still hesitate to make online purchases due to perceived risks and low technological trust. This study investigates the determinants of customers’ purchase intention on online tourism platforms by integrating the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and Ecosystem Theory within a hybrid Fuzzy Delphi–Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) framework. Drawing on data from both experts and users, the research identifies 27 interrelated factors influencing behavioral intention. Findings show that technological trust, perceived usefulness, and perceived risk have the greatest effects, while social reassurance and usability act as key mediators. Theoretically, the study extends TPB through dynamic trust–risk interactions modeled via FCM, advancing understanding of online decision-making. It contributes new knowledge by linking psychological and technological perspectives, and offers practical and managerial insights for enhancing user trust, design usability, and policy support for reliable digital tourism ecosystems.

title: Evaluating the role of governance structure in enhancing technological innovation efficiency in strategic alliances
abstract: This study examines how alliance governance structure affects firms’ technological innovation efficiency. Technological innovation efficiency is measured using a stochastic frontier approach that captures how effectively firms transform innovation inputs into outputs. Using a sample of 377 Chinese listed firms engaged in strategic alliances from 2009 to 2019, the results suggest that firms participating in equity alliances exhibit significantly higher technological innovation efficiency than those involved in non-equity alliances. Within equity alliances, joint ventures are associated with lower technological innovation efficiency than equity participation alliances. Mediation analyses suggest that the association between equity alliances and technological innovation efficiency operates partly through greater intangible assets accumulation, lower financing constraints, and stronger executive incentives. Additional analyses indicate that these associations are more pronounced in repeated alliances and weaker in discontinued alliances, highlighting the role of alliance continuity in realizing governance-related efficiency gains. The findings suggest that alliance governance is relevant not only to whether firms innovate but also to how efficiently they convert collaborative resources into technological outcomes.

title: Associations of structured and unstructured physical activity time in kindergarten with physical fitness in preschoolers: an isotemporal substitution and time threshold analysis
abstract: This cross-sectional study aimed to examine how reallocating time across different types of activities is associated with preschoolers’ physical fitness and to identify potential time thresholds that could inform kindergarten activity planning. A total of 337 Chinese preschoolers (168 boys, 169 girls; mean age 4.41 ± 0.89 years) from nine kindergartens participated. Time allocation among sedentary behavior (SB), structured physical activity (PA), and unstructured PA was quantified using accelerometer data and video observation, and physical fitness was assessed with standardized tests from the Chinese National Physical Fitness Measurement for Preschool. Isotemporal substitution models and compositional time-allocation change point analyses were conducted using R software. Reallocating 10 min of SB to either structured PA or unstructured PA was associated with higher physical fitness scores, with structured PA showing a stronger association. These associations followed a linear dose-response pattern. Model-derived threshold estimates were identified at 53 min for structured PA and 40 min for unstructured PA; however, only the structured PA threshold showed a statistically significant difference in composite fitness scores. Structured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) also demonstrated positive associations with fitness outcomes when replacing other activities, with an estimated threshold of 23 min. These findings suggest that replacing sedentary time with structured or unstructured PA, particularly structured MVPA, is positively associated with improved physical fitness in preschoolers. The estimated time thresholds provide preliminary evidence-based targets for optimizing kindergarten activity curricula and inform the design of future longitudinal interventions.

title: A study of analysing characteristics of students’ informal learning between peers within different environments—Taking British architecture schools as examples
abstract: Abstract Alongside the development of architectural education, especially the engagement of virtual and distance platforms, traditional design studio pedagogy has been challenged in this discipline. This paper makes a thematic analysis to compare architecture students’ informal learning experiences between peers in physical and virtual environments. The relative data are collected by both quantitative and qualitative measures, divided into two phases. The first phase was processed within three British architectural institutions, whose students were taken surveys to collect their preferences on learning within the conventional design studio and remotely; the second source was collected from observations and interviews conducted explicitly in one British architectural institution. Those data were analysed to summarise the main factors which affect architecture students’ learning experiences within the design studio and virtual environment, respectively. The study identified four main factors, which are face-to-face and distance contacts, studio atmosphere and its alternatives, peer-to-peer bonds, and the form of a community and/or a group. Additionally, research has shown that the majority of architecture students have a preference for studying in a studio environment that is created within a traditional design studio atmosphere. This suggests that the virtual platforms are unable to fully replace the physical design studio.

title: Favorite and most difficult school subjects among STEM and non-STEM university students in Serbia and the USA
abstract: Attitudes toward school subjects are shaped by individual preferences, teaching practices, and broader sociocultural factors. However, cross-national research on how students interpret their favorite and most difficult subjects remains limited. This study employs a cross-sectional mixed-methods design to examine how undergraduate students from Serbia and the United States retrospectively evaluate their high school experiences. The sample consisted of 255 students (53.7% from Serbia, 46.3% from the United States; 59.2% female, 40.8% male), who provided open-ended responses regarding their favorite and most difficult subjects and the reasons underlying these choices. Responses were analyzed using an inductive coding procedure and subsequently examined through quantitative statistical analyses. The identified reasons were grouped into four dimensions: personal (interests and perceived abilities), content-related (subject characteristics), teacher-related (teacher’s role and support), and instructional (teaching methods and quality of instruction). In addition, both students and subjects were categorized as STEM or non-STEM to enable cross-disciplinary comparisons. The findings reveal systematic cross-cultural differences in explanatory patterns. Students from the United States more frequently selected STEM subjects as their favorites and tended to interpret their experiences through internal factors such as interest, self-confidence, and perceived competence. In contrast, students from Serbia more often attributed both enjoyment and difficulty to external, school-related factors, including teaching practices and curriculum structure. Mathematics emerged as a subject with a dual status, frequently identified as both favorite and difficult, highlighting the role of interpretive frameworks in shaping students’ responses to academic challenge. Overall, the results suggest that students’ perceptions of school subjects are not determined solely by subject characteristics but are constructed through context-dependent interpretations shaped by educational and cultural environments. These findings contribute to a more nuanced understanding of cross-cultural differences in students’ academic attitudes and have implications for designing educational practices that support both motivation and engagement, particularly in STEM domains.

title: The facial emotional characteristics of figures in the Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes murals
abstract: The murals of the Dunhuang Mogao Caves, as a global artistic treasure, demonstrate how facial emotional characteristics in their depictions not only epitomize the evolution of art history but also reflect sociocultural interactions. This paper synthesizes existing research to systematically analyze emotional representations of figures across historical periods in these murals, emphasizing the persistent challenge of precisely defining period-specific facial emotions due to the subjective nature of emotion recognition. The study reveals a phased evolution in emotional expressions corresponding to sociocultural transformations. Through a taxonomic analysis of emotional features, this research establishes a novel framework for investigating how facial expressions in the murals convey both affective states and social hierarchies. It further interprets the symbolic functions of emotional motifs in artistic creation, uncovering profound intertextual relationships between the murals’ visual language, social structures, and cultural environments. These findings provide interdisciplinary methodological implications for art anthropology and historical iconography, bridging formal artistic analysis with sociocultural interpretation.

title: An analysis of the dynamic structure and evolution of international rock phosphate trade
