abstract: The significant increase in global demand for agricultural products and the shift in the global geopolitical balances have underscored the importance of access to reliable fertilizer markets to ensure global food security. In this paper the dynamic structure and evolutionary mechanisms of the global rock phosphate trade network (GRPTN) are explored using time discrete dynamic network models with time-across dependences in the pre-pandemic period 2015–2020. The coefficient estimates reveal the driving forces behind the establishment of trade links in the GRPTN. The main features identified include low density and reciprocity, small world and scale free character, decentralized structure, slight disassortativity, and moderate geographic heterophily. In addition, the results of fitting a Temporal Exponential Random Graph Model (TERGM) confirm the expected effects of the structural variables as well as those of different economic, geographic, and time-dependence covariates, including the Agriculture Value Added and the Cultivated area of the exporting country, the total trade value of both the importing and exporting countries, the specific region to which the importing or exporting country belongs and geographical contiguity. Moreover, the time-dependence effects are significant and indicate a high level of stability of the GRPTN both in terms of the persistence of existing links and in the infrequent appearance of new ties. The results confirm the geostrategic importance of this non-renewable component essential for ensuring adequate yields in agricultural production.

title: Translating Tourist Landscape in Jordan Cities: Application and Implication
abstract: This study examines the process of Arabic to English bilingual tourist sign translation in the Jordanian context, and specifically in the area of Jerash, Umm Qais and the Dead Sea. It discusses the nature of the translation errors; the translation strategies used and offers suggested solutions to the translation errors. The analysis of a corpus of 150 bilingual tourist signs employed Zhang & Xu, (2015)‘s taxonomy of translation errors and Baker (1992) theory of equivalence. Analysis is done both quantitatively and qualitatively. The result shows that lexical error is the most common error type, followed by pragmatic and syntactic errors. The study also uncovers the dominant translation strategies in use and offers alternatives to them on the basis of the different levels of equivalence. The study makes practical suggestions for both translators and tourism authorities to facilitate bilingual tourist signage in Jordan and boost tourists’ linguistic and cultural experience.

title: An evidence-based mixed-methods randomized controlled trial of a WeChat sexual health intervention for older chinese women
abstract: This mixed-methods randomized controlled trial evaluated a culturally adapted WeChat sexual health interventionfor older Chinese women. A total of 205 women aged ≥60 years were randomized to a 21-day sexual healthintervention or healthy-aging control, with assessments at baseline, post-intervention, and 2-month follow-up.Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), quality of life using the WHOQOL-OLD,and qualitative interviews were conducted with 36 participants. No signifi cant between-group diff erences were foundin FSFI scores. In contrast, WHOQOL-OLD scores were signifi cantly higher in the intervention group at post-intervention and remained modestly higher at follow-up. Qualitative fi ndings indicated improvements in emotional comfort, .relational intimacy, self-acceptance, and confi dence in discussing sexual health. The fi ndings suggest thatculturally adapted digital sexual health interventions may enhance broader quality of life among older Chinesewomen even when measurable sexual function remains unchanged, supporting greater attention to relational andpsychosocial dimensions of later-life sexual health.

title: Born in the wrong era: rethinking human-AI relations through the lens of anemoia
abstract: Abstract As large language models [LLMs] become increasingly integrated into everyday communication, they not only transform how users access information but also reshape emotional and social dynamics. This study explores how individuals emotionally respond to the growing presence of AI, with a particular focus on anemoia – a nostalgic longing for a past barely or never personally experienced. Drawing on a qualitative content analysis of 1.625 Reddit comments, this research reveals that user discourse frequently reflects discomfort, emotional fatigue, and yearning for simpler, more human-centered eras. Using a Grounded Theory [GT] approach, the study identifies core emotional themes, including alienation, perceived loss of authenticity, and digitally mediated loneliness, and demonstrates how these are expressed on a spectrum of anemoia. The findings position anemoia as a useful interpretive lens for understanding emotional ambivalence toward AI, revealing how imagined pasts influence user attitudes. By introducing the concept of AI-triggered anemoia , the study contributes to emerging debates on affective responses to AI and calls for more psychologically sensitive approaches to AI development.

title: The impact of Trump 2.0 tariff policy on international trade: evidence from Chinese firms
abstract: Abstract The tariff policies implemented by Trump during his second term have caused systemic disruptions to the global trade system, exacerbating uncertainties in the global economic order. First, we estimate the key parameters of the model using the simulated method of moments based on export data from Chinese firms. Then, we embed the model within a general equilibrium framework. Utilizing the estimated key parameters, we simulate two tariff scenarios: one reflecting the actual scenario of increased tariffs imposed by Trump on countries worldwide during his second term, and another where tariffs between countries are reduced by 5%. Under Trump's tariffs: 1.The EU's export share to the US drops by 65.77%, and China's by 44.44%. 2.Denmark's price index rises by 5.62%, while China's increases by 0.21% and the US's decreases by 1.2%. 3.Real wages in Africa increase by 16.37%, while Asia sees a 3.49% rise. Global trade welfare slightly declines. With a 5% tariff reduction: 1.Domestic sales shares fall, with Slovenia's dropping by 15.27%, China's by 0.57%, and the US's by 1.74%. 2.Global trade welfare improves, with Belgium experiencing a 1.81% increase.

title: Ethics in natural language processing: a systematic meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the ethical considerations of Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies, which are increasingly utilized in decision-making, content moderation, and creative fields. While significant research examines ethical issues in specific NLP applications, there is a lack of comprehensive frameworks covering ethics across the full range of NLP applications. To address this gap, we conducted a meta-analysis of the academic literature on NLP ethics. Our findings reveal a rapid expansion of research in this area, driven largely by the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs). The literature is especially concentrated in healthcare and is primarly focused on identifying ethical challenges and defining ethical standards, whereas comparatively less attention is given to the design and implementation of practical ethical tools and standards. The most frequently discussed ethical values include accuracy, privacy, transparency and traceability, and bias mitigation. In contrast, environmental sustainability and explainability remain relatively underexplored areas. The analysis also suggests that geographic concentrations of research fundings, particularly in Western countries, may influence the ethical priorities reflected in the literature. By providing a systematic cross-domain synthesis of research trends, ethical concerns, and emerging gaps, this study contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of NLP ethics and highlights the need for broader ethical frameworks and stronger efforts to translate ethical principles into practice.

title: School principals’ leadership behaviors and teachers’ quiet quitting: the mediating role of trust in the principal and the moderating role of surface acting
abstract: Teachers’ quiet quitting has emerged as an important challenge for educational organizations, particularly in centralized systems where teacher and school principal autonomy may be limited. In such contexts, teachers’ perceptions of their school principals and their trust in them may be especially relevant for understanding quiet quitting behaviors. Surface acting may also shape the extent to which teachers display quiet quitting. Against this background, we examined the mediating role of trust in the school principals and the moderating role of surface acting in the relationships between school principals’ supportive and directive leadership behaviors and teachers’ quiet quitting. The final sample comprised 421 teachers working in primary, middle, and high schools across 27 schools in Türkiye. The hypothesized relationships were tested using mediation and moderation analyses with bootstrapping techniques to assess direct and indirect effects. The results indicated that trust in the school principal mediated the relationship between supportive leadership and teachers’ quiet quitting, whereas both direct and indirect relationships were observed for directive leadership. Furthermore, teachers’ surface acting significantly moderated the relationship between trust in the principal and quiet quitting. A moderated mediation analysis showed that the indirect effect of leadership behaviors on quiet quitting through trust was conditional on surface acting, such that this effect was stronger among teachers reporting higher levels of surface acting. The findings indicate that supportive leadership may be associated with lower quiet quitting through trust-building processes, whereas directive leadership may be associated with higher quiet quitting. They further indicate that trust may be especially important for teachers reporting high levels of surface acting. These results imply that educational policymakers and school principals should prioritize trust-building strategies to reduce quiet quitting, rather than depending primarily on controlling directive leadership behaviors.

title: Debt mismatch, equity mismatch and total factor productivity of listed enterprises in China
abstract: In the analysis of financial mismatch, the focus is typically on the efficiency of debt allocation, while the efficiency of equity allocation is often neglected. Based on the financial data of Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed companies from 2012 to 2022, this study comprehensively reflects the status of financial mismatch by utilizing the allocation efficiency of both debt and equity. An empirical analysis is conducted through the construction of a two-way fixed effects model and a mediation effect model. The results show that financial mismatch will significantly inhibit the total factor productivity of enterprises, and this conclusion is still valid after robustness test and endogenous test. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the inhibitory effect of debt mismatch on total factor productivity is more obvious in state-owned enterprises, large-scale enterprises, and enterprises in the eastern region, while the inhibitory effect of equity mismatch is stronger in non-state-owned enterprises and enterprises in the central region, with no clear scale heterogeneity. The mechanism test shows that financial mismatch will inhibit the improvement of total factor productivity by inhibiting the R&D innovation ability of enterprises and exacerbating financing difficulties.

title: Interoperability is new: investor relations management and corporate green innovation
abstract: Whether investors can become an effective market-oriented force is the key to cracking many difficulties in the process of green innovation. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2013 to 2022, this paper examines the relationship between investor relations management (IRM) and corporate green innovation. The results show that the level of IRM is positively associated with corporate green innovation. Among the different dimensions of IRM, web communication and communication feedback exhibit the most consistent positive associations, whereas the results for the other communication channels vary across model specifications. Further analysis reveals that IRM improves firms’ green innovation performance through information governance and supervision and management effects. In addition, the intensity of environmental regulation and the level of green finance can increase the linkage between IRM and green innovation; as complementary stakeholders, customer and supplier characteristics encroach on the space for IRM to exert green innovation effects. Finally, IRM enhances both green and non-green innovation performance as well as firm value and market returns. This paper discusses the green innovation effect of IRM in depth and provides empirical data and relevant insights for firms to promote green innovation and strengthen investor protection from the perspective of internal governance mechanisms.

title: How deepfake plausibility, media literacy, and personal attitudes shape detection, liking, and intentions to share political deepfakes on social media
abstract: The increasing realism and accessibility of political deepfakes pose serious risks to democratic discourse by blurring the line between authentic and manipulated media. The present study examined how deepfake quality, media literacy, and attitudes toward the person depicted in the video shape individuals’ ability to detect political deepfakes, their emotional responses (liking), and behavioral intentions (social media sharing). A total of 1,124 participants from the United Kingdom, Slovenia, and Italy viewed manipulated videos about climate change and immigration that varied in quality. The results showed that high-quality deepfakes were less likely to be detected and received more positive evaluations than low-quality ones. In contrast, quality did not significantly influence sharing intention. Media literacy and attitudes toward the person in the video emerged as strong predictors across outcomes; higher media literacy improved detection and reduced liking and sharing, while more positive attitudes decreased detection and increased both liking and sharing. Mediation analyses demonstrated that liking partially mediated the link between detection and sharing intention. Furthermore, moderated mediation models revealed that this indirect effect was stronger among individuals with high media literacy (for climate change videos) and favorable attitudes toward the video’s subject (for both topics). Overall, the study highlights the need for interventions that address not only detection skills but also emotional and motivational susceptibility to persuasive synthetic media. Enhancing media literacy and implementing platform-level friction mechanisms may help curb the spread of political deepfakes online.

title: Navigating pragmatic and humanistic discourses: Chinese preservice teachers’ agency in the pursuit of professional goals
abstract: Student teachers’ agency related to their judgment and capacity in professional goal pursuit has garnered attention in teacher education programs and academia. Their agency is governed by the discourses in the educational and social fields in which student teachers are situated. This case study employs semi-structured interviews, informal discussions, and field immersive observations to explore how pragmatic and humanistic discourses across multiple fields have impacted the economic and moral agency development of 15 preservice master’s students in professional goal pursuit throughout their professional journeys. The findings confirm that pragmatic and humanistic discourses intertwined to affect participants’ acquisition of two different forms of agency. Pragmatic discourse, which emphasizes capital accumulation, competitiveness, and performative accountability, nurtured and continuously strengthened participants’ economic agency. However, this influence sometimes diminished their moral agency in advocating for changes in educational practices grounded in humanistic values. Participants’ moral agency was initiated and reinforced through the humanistic care in their situated educational fields, as well as collective and self-critical reflections on pragmatic rationales and transformative changes. Hence, this study advocates for the synergistic contributions of all relevant stakeholders to recognize the entanglement of pragmatic and humanistic discourses, critically reflect on, negotiate and mediate their interplay, and work collaboratively to support student teachers’ moral agency in ways that go beyond thin pragmatic aims.

title: Spatial network structure analysis of urban tourism flows in Nanchang based on crowdsourced data
abstract: Urban tourism is a vital driver of economic and cultural development in modern cities. This study investigates the spatial network structure and dynamics of urban tourism flows, using Nanchang City as a case study. By integrating crowdsourced data, the DBSCAN clustering algorithm, and social network analysis, we identify tourist Areas of Interest (AOIs) and evaluate their aggregation across five key dimensions. Subsequently, centrality analysis and structural hole measurement are applied to decipher the spatial pattern of tourism flows. The key findings are: (1) The spatial distribution of scenic spots in Nanchang exhibits a distinct cluster centered on the August 1st Memorial Hall area, highlighting the city’s strong potential to cultivate a unique red tourism brand. (2) The tourism flows network reveals a significant structural imbalance, characterized by an over-concentration of visitors at a few core nodes (e.g., Tengwang Pavilion and Bayi Square) and the presence of pronounced structural holes. This pattern indicates intense inter-destination competition and an uneven distribution of tourism benefits. These insights provide an evidence-based foundation for optimizing tourism route planning, mitigating congestion at core scenic spots, and promoting balanced regional development through targeted marketing and product differentiation.

title: Ontological evaluation system of memes in traditional settlement cultural landscape based on knowledge mapping
abstract: The cultural landscapes of traditional Chinese settlements stand as tangible witnesses to historical transformations. They embed a variety of distinctive genes that have shaped regional development, together forming a unique body of knowledge known as Traditional Chinese Settlement Cultural Landscape Genes (TCSCLG). With the acceleration of urbanization, traditional settlements are encountering developmental crises, creating an urgent need for systematic identification of their cultural landscapes and the exploration of digital conservation pathways. From the perspective of ontological information theory, this study conceptualizes the diverse information attributes embedded within TCSCLG as specialized knowledge. It conducts cultural mining, structuring, and digital representation through the lens of knowledge management and organizational theory. By integrating the Object-Oriented Cultural Landscape Genes (OOCPLG) classification model into genes, this study establishes a dual-strand “ecological–social” TCSCLG structure to identify the cultural landscape characteristics of traditional settlements. Accordingly, a comprehensive TCSCLG ontological framework is developed, comprising 2 primary categories, 5 secondary categories, 11 tertiary categories, and 26 quaternary categories, accompanied by a visualized TCSCLG knowledge graph. Furthermore, by applying the Analytic Hierarchy Process and Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation (AHP–FCE), a multi-stakeholder assessment framework is constructed to evaluate inheritance outcomes and identify key cultural genes for targeted conservation. This approach not only enables full-element recognition of TCSCLG and accurately captures cultural gene transmission patterns but also supports the digital conservation and management of meme-based knowledge, as demonstrated through a case study of the Huayuan settlement in Fujian Province. The findings offer valuable guidance for cultural landscape development in other traditional settlements and provide a scientifically grounded, digitized methodology to support culturally distinctive and sustainable development.

title: Exploring the potential of large language models for public participation in urban redevelopment planning
abstract: Public participation is essential to human-centered urban planning, yet existing approaches often struggle to translate dispersed public opinions into clear and discussable preference expressions. This limits substantive deliberation between public preferences and expert knowledge, making it difficult to effectively incorporate public needs and experiences into planning decision-making. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to support participatory planning by helping organize diverse public preferences and facilitating deliberation between public perspectives and expert knowledge. This study explores this potential in the context of urban redevelopment in Chinese cities, where divergences between public and expert preferences are common. We develop a reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)-based LLM framework for learning expert- and public-oriented preferences and apply it to 226 urban redevelopment cases. The results show that, under controlled conditions, fine-tuned LLMs can generate planning proposal texts that reflect distinguishable expert- and public-oriented preference emphases, demonstrating their potential to support preference diagnosis and deliberation preparation in urban planning. At the same time, the findings reveal limitations in technical stability, highlighting the need for cautious and transparent integration of LLMs into participatory planning processes.

title: Irrigation rationality: a behavioral account of rural settlement hierarchy
abstract: What encourages people to settle together in a hierarchical pattern in rural societies? Traditional accounts of settlement hierarchy, including central place theory and rank-size laws, are insufficient, as they overlook the productive rationality required for agricultural irrigation. In this study, we examine whether irrigation is associated with the hierarchical structure of rural settlements. We quantify their hierarchical structure using the rank-size distribution of over 2600 agrarian settlements that crop rice or wheat across rural China. Our findings indicate that rice-cropping settlements exhibit a less hierarchical structure than wheat-cropping settlements, consistent with differences in the spatial morphologies of their irrigation networks and housing distributions. Besides, the degree of irrigation dependence is systematically associated with variation in settlement hierarchy. Historical analyses over the past century further suggest that irrigation networks and settlements co-evolved in a coordinated but differentiated way: stable backbone canals supported the expansion of central settlements, while newly extended terminal canals were associated with the emergence of small peripheral settlements. These findings provide new evidence for the behavioral explanation of how agricultural irrigation affects the agricultural settlement hierarchy and effectively extend the productive principle to settlement theories.

title: Algorithmic stratification in social media narrative framing: an agent-based testing of sex and educational disparities in career information access
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how social media algorithms create information accessibility gaps through an Agent-based Testing (ABT) approach. Using 640 controlled virtual accounts on REDnote (RED) varying by sex and educational levels, 96,000 career-related search results were analyzed. Findings reveal significant algorithmic stratification patterns: lower-educated and women users receive more positively emotional and gender-stereotyped content, and the inter-sectional influence between the assigned sex and educational level of those accounts collectively shapes the narrative perspective and framing of the content, creating complex stratified recommendation patterns. This study makes several contributions: it empirically demonstrates gender discrimination in social media algorithmic recommendation systems, quantifies the differential career information delivery across sex groups, and identifies specific mechanisms through which algorithmic systems perpetuate gender inequality in career development opportunities. These findings provide empirical evidence for mitigating algorithmic gender discrimination in the occupational domain.

title: How does China promote balanced regional development through the ATA system? Institutional compensation mechanism of the tourism industry
abstract: This study focuses on China’s institutional innovation with distinctive national characteristics, the A-grade Tourist Attraction (ATA) system. It reveals that the ATA system essentially serves as a balanced governance tool integrating landscape recreation services with cross-regional and urban-rural policy regulation. However, current research has overlooked fundamental explanations of ATA’s intrinsic nature as a political-economic instrument. By analysing the evolutionary process and diffusion patterns of China’s ATA network, this study demonstrates how the Chinese government employs ATA brand authorization to implement differentiated policy incentives for tourism economy, thereby addressing optimization challenges of China’s uneven economic landscape. This study reveals that China’s ATA system has evolved through three distinct phases: growth pole cultivation, core-periphery diffusion, and comprehensive coordinated development. Its evolutionary mechanisms manifest through spatial compensation and graded compensation. The spatial evolution of the ATA system demonstrates policy-driven hotspot emergence and multi-tier differentiation, exhibiting strong alignment with national strategic zones and revealing a hierarchical development pattern that reflects vertical interventions across central government-strategic development areas-local governance levels. This hierarchical intervention, alongside variables like population agglomeration, transportation infrastructure, and topographical conditions, embodies China’s strategy to unleash resource value in tourism zones through transport network construction and population policy regulation. This mechanism uses policy leverage to transcend market limitations, creating opportunities for underdeveloped regions. The study innovatively proposes a cross-scale framework for certification systems, expanding understanding of policy tourism instruments and providing a reference framework for developing nations to resolve the growth-equity paradox.

title: Farmers’ adaptation and mitigation choices under climate change: evidence from a mixed-methods survey in the Western Himalayas
abstract: Abstract Agriculture in the Western Himalayas faces a “dual climate stress”: the compounding impact of slow-onset temperature rise and acute extreme events like cloudbursts. While farmers tend to rely on both customary knowledge and contemporary innovations, evidence on how climate perceptions translate into concrete behavioural change in high-risk hill regions remains limited. This study fills that void by analysing the perceptions, adaptation practices, and mitigation measures of farmers from the Mandi district of Himachal Pradesh, a region exposed to climate-related hazards such as cloudbursts, landslides and flash floods. Drawing on a concurrent mixed-methods design combining a structured survey of 100 farmers with coded open-ended responses, results show that 90.5% reported changes in rainfall patterns, 83.3% perceived deterioration in soil quality, and 87.7% perceived deterioration in air quality over the past 10–15 years. However, a pronounced “awareness-action gap” emerged: despite high awareness, 96% of farmers did not grow drought-resistant crops or plants and 80% did not grow cover crops, although agroforestry was reported by 55%. Taken together, these patterns indicate an awareness–action gap and are consistent with ‘survival-first’ decision-making under financial and institutional constraints, rather than a simple lack of knowledge. To address this gap, the findings suggest policy options including hyper-local advisories linked to micro-climate data, small-scale varietal trials, and timely insurance-claim settlements. These findings provide context-specific implications for strengthening smallholder resilience in climate-fragile mountain ecosystems.

title: The role of online reviews in improving public health: evidence from restaurant hygiene inspections
abstract: Foodborne illnesses present a significant public health challenge, as traditional restaurant inspection systems are often constrained by limited resources, infrequent monitoring cycles, and difficulties in ensuring sustained compliance with hygiene standards. This study examines the potential of online consumer reviews as a decentralized, real-time complement to conventional inspections in enhancing restaurant hygiene. Using a unique dataset of Yelp reviews and official inspection records from Arizona restaurants (2015–2020), we apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques to identify that 4.6% of all reviews contain hygiene-related complaints, and we assess their associations with subsequent inspection outcomes. Our findings show that hygiene-related complaints are strongly associated with future hygiene violations. For non-claimed restaurants, a single hygiene-related complaint is associated with a 75.4% increase in the expected number of violations at the next inspection. In contrast, for claimed restaurants, this relationship is associated with a 3.3% decrease. Furthermore, some chain restaurants—although they did not publicly respond to complaints—appear to adopt more proactive internal strategies: each additional complaint is associated with a 6.3% reduction in priority violations, after controlling for relevant covariates. These results suggest that online reviews may help reduce information asymmetries and may create incentives for improvements in hygiene practices. By illustrating how consumer-generated feedback can supplement traditional regulatory mechanisms, this study contributes to both the public health and online review literature. It also offers actionable implications for consumers, restaurant managers, platform operators, and policymakers. Incorporating online review signals into public health surveillance systems may enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of food safety monitoring, ultimately helping to reduce the risk of foodborne illnesses.

title: Insider trading surveillance and enforcement in emerging markets: a comparative analysis of Vietnam’s surveillance regime
abstract: In the context of emerging economies increasingly integrating with the global economy, ensuring the integrity and transparency of the stock market has become a pressing requirement. This article examines the enforcement of insider trading regulations in Vietnam, with particular attention to challenges in inspecting, detecting, and supervising increasingly sophisticated insider trading practices. Employing doctrinal legal analysis, structured institutional comparison, and descriptive analysis of a census of 705 administrative sanctioning decisions issued between 2022 and 2025, the study evaluates Vietnam’s current supervisory framework under the Securities Law 2019 and its implementing regulations. The institutional arrangements of the United States and the United Kingdom are used as contrasting benchmarks to identify alternative mechanisms to reduce the distance between surveillance detection and enforceable proof. The analysis identifies several structural weaknesses, including a clear separation between detection and enforcement functions, limited enforcement authority at the exchange level, and technological bottlenecks stemming from fragmented data systems that hinder timely detection and handling of illegal transactions. These factors contribute to delays and reduced effectiveness in law enforcement, despite Vietnam’s official prohibition of insider trading. Drawing on the domestic enforcement record, practical assessments of administrative enforcement activities, and selectively on these institutional benchmarks, the paper proposes specific recommendations to strengthen market inspection and supervision, improve data-sharing and coordination mechanisms among regulatory agencies, and modernize the transaction-monitoring system. These reforms are necessary to strengthen control over insider trading in Vietnam amid rapid technological change and increasing market complexity.

title: Digital technologies in music pedagogy: fostering aesthetic perception and philosophical reflection among undergraduate music education students
abstract: The aim of this study was to explore the role of aesthetic and philosophical appreciation of modern music among students in the context of digitalization. In total, 650 students from 6 Chinese educational institutions participated in the study. The study is grounded in two theoretical frameworks: the praxial philosophy of music education, which links musical understanding to the practice of music-making, and aesthetic experience theory, which conceptualizes the perception of art. Using random sampling, students were divided into 6 control and 6 experimental groups. Learning effectiveness was assessed through a t-test and questionnaire analysis. The experiment showed that the long-term and regular use of digital technologies led to increased levels of academic achievement in the experimental groups (by more than 30 points compared to the initial results). Additionally, 78% of students acknowledged that interaction with digital platforms broadened their musical horizons, allowing them to explore new styles, genres, and techniques (compared to 39% in the control group). Overall, students in the experimental groups who used the VRhythm and Soundtrap platforms demonstrated higher success rates and more positive attitudes toward digital technologies.

title: Relationship anarchy and free love: a Deleuzian-anarchist critique of marriage
abstract: This article argues that marriage functions as a regulatory dispositif that overcodes desire and normalises intimacy so as to reproduce patriarchal and capitalist hierarchies. Replacing repression models with a Foucauldian account of productive power, and mobilising Deleuze and Guattari’s concepts of capture and rhizomatic assembly, I show how the marital couple operates as an arborescent template that monopolises recognition and channels care. Against this, I reconstruct relationship anarchy as a political ethics of non-proprietary attachment that pluralises legitimacy, secures care through design rather than status, and resists hierarchies without evacuating commitment. The contribution is threefold: a genealogy of monogamy as normalisation; an ontological and normative defence of rhizomatic forms of association; and a sketch of prefigurative infrastructures that enable reliable, accountable networks of care. The upshot is to reorient debates on kinship and intimacy toward forms-of-life that can be exited without forfeiting recognition.

title: Network structure of depressive symptoms in father–mother–adolescent triads: Do networks differ by age?
abstract: Adolescents’ and their parents’ depression influence each other reciprocally. However, the specific mechanisms that contribute to the shared occurrence of depression at the symptom level within families remain unclear. Additionally, these relationships may vary across different stages of adolescent development as depressive symptoms change over time. This study uses network analysis to examine father‒mother‒adolescent triads, aiming to explore the interconnectedness of depressive symptoms within families and how these connections may differ across various developmental stages. This cross-sectional study included 2,647 father‒mother‒adolescent triads from the China Family Panel Studies in 2016. Network analysis was utilized to identify central and bridge symptoms that connect different communities (i.e., family members) in depressive networks across the early (10–12 years), middle (13–15 years), and late (16–18 years) stages of adolescence. Parental report of “feeling sad” was central to the network across most stages. Specific symptoms in parents such as “feeling sad” and “inability to get going” bridged different communities. Variations in node strength and connectivity were observed across different stages. These findings highlight the transactional processes that contribute to the persistence of depression among families across different stages of adolescence. Parental symptoms such as “feeling sad” and “inability to get going” were key symptoms, suggesting potential targets for family-based interventions. Interventions involving both parents and those tailored to adolescents’ developmental stages may enhance treatment effectiveness, although bridge-related findings are exploratory because of limited stability.

title: Cultural rituals and regional economies: an input–output analysis of religious pilgrimage activities in Taiwan
abstract: This study employs an input–output framework to evaluate the economic impact of the major religious procession events in Taoyuan, Taiwan. By integrating detailed expenditure data with regionally adjusted Leontief models, we quantify the direct, indirect, and total output effects across local industries. Our results indicate that, within the input–output framework, these cultural rituals generate measurable short-run production effects, with total output multipliers ranging from 2.08 to 3.02. Sectors such as apparel, food services, and cultural performance exhibit relatively strong propagation effects. The findings suggest that spending composition—rather than total budget alone—is closely associated with multiplier strength. The study provides policy-relevant evidence for considering how cultural-event expenditures may be allocated across locally embedded sectors, while recognizing the limitations of a static input–output framework.

title: Pathways to inclusion: a comparative analysis of Turkish municipalities
abstract: Abstract Even after Syria’s December 2024 ceasefire, Turkish municipalities remain confronted with the governance challenges that Syrian displacement has produced over more than a decade. This study examines 81 municipalities through text mining of strategic plans (2006–2022), combined with Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA) of 16 selected cases. The analysis identifies two distinct pathways to inclusive migration governance. Municipalities aligned with the ruling AKP developed more extensive governance repertoires where high refugee presence converged with international NGO partnerships. Opposition-led cities, in particular those governed by CHP and HDP, faced systematic resource constraints and recourse to alternative networks, including EU funding and civil society engagement. Political alignment thus shapes not only resource access, but the opportunity structures within which migration governance capacity can be developed at all. Against this backdrop, Turkey’s authoritarian centralization produces uneven geographies of inclusion, in which local responses depend as much on political positioning as on refugee numbers or economic capacity.

title: Knowledge transfer in open innovation: a scientometrics analysis
abstract: Abstract Over the past decade or so, the relationship between open innovation and knowledge transfer has continued to receive widespread academic attention. Although a substantial body of literature has reviewed each domain separately, there remains a lack of quantitative and systematic examination of their interconnection. Thus, this study employs a bibliometric analysis based on 1508 publications from the Web of Science Core Collection and conducts visualization analyses using CiteSpace and VOSviewer to systematically reveal the intellectual structure and evolutionary trajectory of research linking open innovation and knowledge transfer. The results indicate that the intellectual landscape of this field consists of seven major research themes, reflecting its core knowledge structure and primary research hotspots. The temporal evolution analysis further identifies three key stages: the conceptual emergence stage (2003–2007), the theoretical development stage (2008–2014), and the diversified expansion stage (2015–present). Building on these findings, this study develops a multi-level analytical framework encompassing the macro-level (institutional and ecosystem contexts), meso-level (organizational capabilities and structures), and micro-level (individual motivations and behaviors) to elucidate the multi-layered pathways through which knowledge transfer operates within open innovation. The findings contribute to a more systematic understanding of the relationship between knowledge flows and collaborative innovation, offering practical implications for firms and policymakers seeking to optimize collaboration mechanisms and institutional design across different stages of innovation.

title: Balanced time perspective and time-oriented well-being dimensions: patterns and relationship across adulthood
abstract: The study investigates the relationships among Balanced Time Perspective (BTP) and both life satisfaction and flourishing in emerging, middle, and advanced adults while validating the Italian version of the Balanced Time Perspective Scale (BTPS). By integrating satisfaction with life, a reflective evaluation rooted in past and present experiences, and flourishing, a future-oriented process of growth and purpose, this study adopts a time-oriented perspective on wellbeing. A total of 681 Italian participants aged 18–65, categorized into emerging, middle, and advanced adulthood, completed the BTPS, the Satisfaction with Life Scale, and the Flourishing Scale. Psychometric validation of the BTPS included exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. Variations in BTP profiles and their relationships with time-oriented well-being dimensions were analyzed using ANOVA and MANOVA, focusing on age-specific patterns and interactions. The BTPS demonstrated strong validity and reliability. Time-oriented well-being dimensions revealed complex, non-linear age-related variations. Emerging adults exhibited the highest future orientation and total BTP scores, which declined with age. Individuals characterized as Time-expansive consistently scored the highest across well-being dimensions. Conversely, Time-restrictive and Reminiscers scored low on the well-being dimensions. Significant interactions between age and BTP profiles in well-being scores suggested that well-being outcomes are related to both life stage and temporal orientation, offering a nuanced understanding of adult development. This study underscores BTP as a critical factor in understanding the patterns of time-oriented well-being across adulthood and the dynamic interplay among age, temporal balance, and well-being, providing a foundation for targeted interventions and longitudinal studies to explore adaptive functioning across the life course further.

title: The modern gut: a surface to conquer
abstract: Abstract Science, medicine, and technology have historically had a profound influence on our conception of the gut. In this paper, I examine the transformation of the human gut into a surface—a territory that is increasingly accessible and manipulable through technological advancements. Driven by imaging, sampling, and sequencing innovations, the gut has transitioned from an “obscure and undisclosed” internal organ to a site of intense scientific, medical, and commercial interest. How does our understanding of the interaction between current technology and the digestive system inform our perspective on the modern human gut? How has the gut become a surface to conquer? While the discovery of the microbiota has captured a significant part of the narrative on the human–gut interaction, it is not the only element to consider. Weaving scientific, humanities, and biogeographical perspectives, I argue that the gut has become a surface, a territory open to access. By analyzing the gut as a surface, this work sheds light on the evolving landscape of human-technology interactions and their impact on our embodied experience.

title: Can smart cities boost new quality productive forces? Evidence from a DID approach across 270 Chinese cities
abstract: This study employs a time-varying difference-in-differences (DID) approach to investigate the causal effect of smart city construction on the new quality productive forces (NQPF), along with regional heterogeneity and moderating mechanisms. The results indicate that smart city construction significantly enhances the NQPF, a conclusion supported by various robustness tests. Compared to non-pilot cities, pilot smart cities exhibit an average increase of approximately 0.38% in the NQPF, with this effect growing over time. The positive impact of smart city construction on the NQPF is statistically significant only in western cities, resource-based cities, and cities with higher administrative ranks. Besides, economic development and innovation levels amplify the marginal enhancement effect of smart city construction on the NQPF, whereas industrialization levels suppress this marginal effect. The findings not only provide empirical support for synergizing urban digital and intelligent transformation with the advancement of the NQPF but also deepen theoretical understanding of their evaluation while fostering integrated research on urban development and the NQPF.

title: Corporate social responsibility and organizational performance: practices and future research agenda from a twenty-year review
abstract: Abstract Corporate social responsibility (CSR) and organizational performance (OP) have been closely intertwined concepts, attracting sustainable interest from businesses and academics over the past two decades. However, prior reviews often lacked insight into the evolving research trends in the literature on CSR-OP, as well as the systematic integration of their intricate relationships. Addressing this gap, this study employs a systematic review to examine current research focuses, hotspots, and future directions in the CSR-OP nexus over the last two decades (2004–2023). The findings reveal that: (i) there has been an exponential increase in CSR-OP publications and citations since 2017; (ii) the United States is the dominant contributor to the CSR-OP scholarship, with China standing out as a developing country among the top ten contributors; and (iii) four major research clusters identified via co-occurrence network analysis, namely “moderating or mediating factors affecting the CSR-OP relationship,” “CSR and financial performance,” “CSR non-financial performance, and environmental performance,” and “CSR, firm performance, and corporate governance.” Emerging trends such as gender diversity, eco-innovation, and political connections further expand the field’s scope. This study advances CSR scholarship by mapping its knowledge landscape and identifying promising avenues for future inquiry in relation to OP. The findings provide valuable insights for corporate managers seeking to enhance CSR practices and for policymakers addressing gaps in sustainability and governance frameworks.

title: Predicting work–life balance insights: A data-driven approach using unsupervised learning
abstract: The evolving nature of work has altered how individuals manage the boundaries between their professional and personal lives, raising significant concerns about work–life balance and overall wellbeing. While work–life balance has been the subject of extensive research, contemporary methodologies often rely on predefined categories or self-reported metrics, limiting their ability to capture the intricate and diverse patterns that define daily work experiences. This study employs a data-driven approach to reveal hidden work–life balance profiles by applying unsupervised learning to comprehensive datasets on lifestyle and wellbeing. Using UMAP for dimensionality reduction alongside DBSCAN clustering enabled the identification of distinct groups characterized by different levels of productivity, stress, health behaviors, financial stability, and personal achievements. These profiles, derived from empirical data, are then evaluated using supervised learning models, including XGBoost, LightGBM, KNN, and other classification methods, to assess their stability and distinguishability. The findings indicate that the recognized work–life balance states are consistently distinguishable across various modeling techniques, suggesting a robust underlying structure. These results offer valuable insights for policymakers and organizations aiming to foster sustainable work practices and enhance wellbeing.

title: Climate change exposure and firm value in China: evidence consistent with a discount-rate interpretation
abstract: This paper examines the relationship between firm-level climate change exposure and firm value in China. Using A-share listed firms from 2002 to 2020 and a disclosure-based measure of perceived climate change exposure, we find a significant negative association between climate change exposure and firm value. Our measure provides incremental explanatory power beyond conventional proxies, including ESG indicators and climate change news risk measures. Channel tests provide evidence consistent with a discount-rate interpretation. Both transition and physical-risk exposures are negatively associated with firm value. However, for firms in carbon-neutral industries, transition exposure is positively associated with firm value, consistent with transition-related growth opportunities. The negative associations are more pronounced for firms in high-pollution industries and coastal regions. Further results indicate that the negative valuation association is weaker among firms with stronger green innovation and ESG ratings. Overall, our findings highlight the pricing of climate risk and the role of transition opportunities in firm valuation.

title: Chinese-style intergenerational support: reciprocity or exploitation?
abstract: As China faces accelerating population aging, intergenerational support and reciprocity within families have drawn increasing scholarly attention. Using panel data from the China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (CLASS) between 2018 and 2023, this study empirically examines the effects of parental downward intergenerational support on children’s upward reciprocity and the mechanisms underlying this relationship. The findings indicate that parental downward support significantly promotes children’s upward reciprocity, primarily by enhancing elderly support expectations and the frequency of intergenerational contact. Different forms of downward support exhibit distinct effects: economic support more effectively elicits economic reciprocity from children, whereas parental household assistance and grandchild care primarily drive children’s upward household assistance. Heterogeneity analyses show that these positive effects are significant across all groups, with larger estimated effects in rural households and lower-income groups. Confucian cultural intensity further amplifies the positive association between intergenerational support and reciprocity. Moreover, greater parental support may coincide with lower perceived care from children, suggesting a potential mismatch between instrumental support and emotional response. This study advances the understanding of intergenerational resource flows within families and offers theoretical and practical insights for promoting intergenerational harmony and informing relevant policy interventions.

title: Multi-agent behavioral decision analysis for social public resources digital sharing considering government subsidies and penalties
abstract: Digitalization is reshaping the allocation and sharing of social public resources, yet sustained social public resource digital sharing (SPRDS) remains hindered by strategic interaction among stakeholders and governance frictions. A tripartite evolutionary game model involving the government, resource suppliers, and demanders is developed, integrating limited regulatory capacity and a dynamic subsidy–penalty mechanism. The stability conditions and evolutionary trajectories of the participants’ strategies are examined through evolutionary stable strategy analysis, and numerical simulations based on healthcare resource digital sharing in Sichuan. Results show that SPRDS exhibits strong path dependence and bi-stability, with higher initial sharing efforts promoting the adoption of positive sharing strategies. Policy tools have a nonlinear threshold effect, with high-intensity subsidies and penalties leading to an S-shaped shift towards positive sharing. Greater reputational loss under passive regulation accelerates the shift of government to active regulation, while excessively high regulatory costs reduce regulatory effectiveness. Synergistic benefits, the distribution ratio, and sharing investment cost jointly determine the stability of positive equilibrium strategies. This study clarifies the effective boundaries of regulatory intervention and provides actionable guidance for designing cost-effective regulation and fair benefit-distribution mechanisms to promote sustainable and high-quality allocation of social public resources.

title: Institutional dynamics of digital transformation in environmental governance: a socio-technical analysis of OECD Countries
abstract: This study examines the complex interrelationships between digital infrastructure and environmental policy through an institutional theory lens. Using panel data from 35 OECD countries and the Augmented Mean Group methodology to address cross-sectional dependence, we investigate how institutional arrangements mediate the interaction between digital capabilities and environmental governance outcomes. Results reveal that digital infrastructure is associated with improved environmental performance ( β = 0.0267, p < 0.01), but this relationship is contingent upon regulatory quality and institutional capacity. Environmental policy frameworks ( β = 0.0353, p < 0.05) operate through complementary institutional mechanisms, while digital government services ( β = 0.0859, p < 0.10) function as critical institutional interfaces. Our findings challenge technological determinism, demonstrating instead that institutional arrangements significantly moderate the effectiveness of digital solutions in environmental governance. This research contributes to socio-technical systems theory by revealing how institutional contexts shape the translation of digital capabilities into environmental outcomes in developed economies.

title: Systematic review of green finance and the green economy towards SDG 7: a TCCM and bibliometric analysis
abstract: This study provides a bibliometric analysis of green finance and green economy in relation to Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7) for the time span 2015–2024, using a combined bibliometric and Theory-Context-Characteristics-Methodology (TCCM) framework. The results show a rapid increase in studies, especially after 2020, consistent with a global rise in attention to clean energy transitions. The output of researchers’ work and its citation impact are highly concentrated in a few nations, mainly China, with significant regional inequities, especially in Africa and Latin America. The report indicates a strong focus on sustainable finance tools, renewable energy solutions, and carbon-reduction measures. However, the equity-oriented features of SDG 7, such as gender inclusion, decentralized energy systems, and energy access for marginalized populations, are not sufficiently integrated theoretically or empirically into the research. Dominant theoretical perspectives privilege environmental efficiency at the cost of social justice, suggesting a structural disconnection between research focus and the inclusive mandate of SDG 7. Drawing on these results, the study makes three overarching policy recommendations: (i) the formulation of tiered, context-specific green finance taxonomies with SDG 7 covenants embedded in green bond structures, supported by blended finance instruments to de-risk investment in energy-deficient markets; (ii) the enhancement of performance-based governance through SDG 7 equity sub-indicators, hybrid ESG disclosure standards and a global harmonized green taxonomy to prevent greenwashing; and (iii) the advancement of green fintech corridors, microfinance windows and decentralized finance mechanisms, such as blockchain-enabled credit scoring and mobile micro-investment platforms, to democratize capital access for marginalized communities. Together, these conclusions imply that finance is a systemic and inclusive engine of the global green economy in achieving SDG 7.

title: How strong is Chinese nationalism: evidence from a nationwide survey
abstract: Chinese nationalism has been increasingly evident and influential in China’s foreign policymaking. Based on a nationwide survey conducted in June–July 2024, this article revisits the fundamental but important question, namely, how strong Chinese nationalism is. Survey results show that respondents are generally proud of being Chinese, but only moderately believe that China is superior to other countries and that China should defend its national interests, even though doing so may hurt other countries’ interests or violate international norms. Heterogeneous effects were observed across demographic groups. Moreover, our analysis reveals a notable verbal–action gap: many respondents who score high on assertive nationalism are unwilling to bear personal economic costs, such as higher taxes, to support increased military spending. This article also discusses the implications of these findings.

title: Work well-being as a key factor for better performance among young employees
abstract: The present study examines the relationship between work well-being and job performance among young employees (Gen Z and Millennials) in Spain. A PLS-SEM analysis of survey data from 412 workers was conducted to ascertain how four dimensions of well-being (job satisfaction, supervisor emotional accessibility, organisational respect, and impact on mental health/personal life) affect three performance facets (task, contextual and counterproductive behaviours). The findings of the study demonstrate that job satisfaction exerts a substantial influence on both task and contextual performance. Conversely, the detrimental effects on mental health and personal life are found to be associated with an escalation in counterproductive behaviours and a decline in contextual performance. It is interesting to note that supervisor emotional accessibility and organisational respect did not directly influence performance, suggesting that they may act as baseline expectations rather than motivators. The findings serve to refine social exchange theory and offer practical guidance, prioritising mental health protection and intrinsic job satisfaction to enhance young workers’ performance and well-being.

title: Bridging the credibility gap: sustainability assurance, corporate transparency and debt costs in China
abstract: Voluntary sustainability assurance may enhance disclosure credibility, yet its financing relevance in emerging markets remains uncertain. Drawing on signalling, agency, and legitimacy theories, this study examines whether corporate transparency helps explain the association between sustainability assurance and the cost of debt in China. Using 21,694 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share listed firms during 2019–2024, we find no significant total association between assurance adoption and the cost of debt. Assurance adoption is, however, positively associated with corporate transparency, while transparency is negatively associated with debt costs. A firm-level cluster-bootstrap analysis with 5000 replications estimates an indirect association of −0.0009, with a bias-corrected 95% confidence interval of [−0.0014, −0.0005]. One-year-ahead specifications, propensity score matching, and a randomization-based placebo test provide sensitivity evidence but do not eliminate endogeneity concerns. An alternative analysis using the Huazheng ESG rating yields a similar indirect pattern; this measure is interpreted as an external ESG rating rather than a direct measure of sustainability performance. The findings suggest that the financing relevance of sustainability assurance may operate through observable information-related outcomes accompanying adoption. Given the low rate of assurance adoption and the observational research design, the results should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects.

title: Digitalisation and energy transition in Africa: does government spending and the knowledge economy matter?
abstract: Energy transition in Africa aims to shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources, enhancing sustainable development. By fostering access to clean, affordable energy, it supports economic growth, climate action, and social equity across the continent, promoting a greener future. This study examines the interplay between digitalisation, the knowledge economy, and government spending in facilitating energy transition (ET). The paper employs the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) framework and data spanning 2000 to 2023 from 53 African countries. Our empirical approach utilises system GMM methods, then FE-2SLS and IV-2SLS for robustness checks. Results show that digitalisation initially impedes energy transition, but eventually improves it at higher digitalisation levels, lending credence to the EKC hypothesis. However, this effect is not uniform; it varies significantly by income group and geographical context (urban/rural). Interestingly, the government expenditure interacts with digitalisation to positively influence ET in Africa. However, the knowledge economy does not exert an immediate positive moderating effect. Instead, it must achieve a certain threshold level before it can effectively strengthen the relationship between digitalization and ET. The findings suggest that synergistic policies promoting digitalisation and strategic government investments can significantly enhance a sustainable energy future. Also improving the knowledge economy through education and research investments can accelerate technological innovation and adoption of renewable energy sources.

title: Examining the flow of cultural ecosystem services in Asia: insights from China’s meta-coupled relationships
abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of accelerating globalization and urbanization, cultural ecosystem service (CES) flows, despite being important in regional development and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), have yet to be systematically studied across spatial scales. Based on the meta-coupling framework, this study integrates the MaxEnt model and breakpoint model to quantitatively analyze the patterns and driving mechanisms of CES flows at three spatial scales: within China, between China and neighboring countries, and between China and distant countries. Drawing on 292,290 Asian points of interest (POI) and eight key environmental factors (with population density and potential evapotranspiration contributing the most), the research reveals the spatial differentiation and interaction characteristics of CES flows across multiple scales. The results indicate that CES flows exhibit significant differences among the three scales. At the domestic scale (internal coupling), high-value areas (≥0.61) for aesthetic and recreational CES are mainly concentrated in eastern and southern China, while high-value areas for spiritual and educational CES (≥0.61) are concentrated east of the Heihe-Tengchong Line. Moreover, interprovincial flows of aesthetic and recreational CES are more than 30% higher than those of other types, and the proportion of total CES flows falling in the medium-value range (0.25–0.75) increases significantly, suggesting strengthened interprovincial connections under multi-category weighting. At the neighboring scale (proximal coupling), CES exchanges are centered on historical-cultural ties and economic cooperation, with notably higher flows to Russia and Vietnam compared to Myanmar, and the proportion of total CES flows in the 0.50–0.75 range is the highest (17.6%). At the distant scale (distal coupling), flows of aesthetic and research-educational CES exceed those of spiritual and recreational CES, with high-value areas concentrated in West Asia and Eastern Europe, whereas the majority of total CES flows fall within the low-value range (0.00–0.25). These spatial patterns not only reflect the dynamics of cultural exchanges, but also hold important implications for regional environmental sustainability and management. The complex mechanisms underlying multi-scale CES exchanges underscore the need to fully consider the interactions and feedbacks among CES types, ensuring that environmental factors are consistently integrated into policy-making and cultural management, thereby providing robust quantitative support for decision-making.

title: Artificial Intelligence Boosts Rural Residents’ Income Growth: Empirical Evidence from China
abstract: In China, whether the application of artificial intelligence (AI) can release the digital dividend and boost the income growth of rural residents is directly relevant to the realization of the rural revitalization strategy. Based on panel data from 31 Chinese provinces covering 2003 to 2023, this study employs the two-way fixed effects model, panel mediating effect model, grouped regression, and Fisher’s combination test to empirically examine the impact, underlying mechanisms, and heterogeneity of AI application on rural residents’ income growth. The results indicate that AI application significantly and positively promotes rural residents’ income growth, and this conclusion remains robust after a series of robustness tests. Mechanism analysis demonstrates that AI boosts rural income by optimizing agricultural industrial structure and empowering agricultural economic development. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the income-enhancing effect of AI is stronger in western China, highly urbanized regions, non-major grain-producing areas, and regions with a higher level of agricultural modernization. This study provides empirical support for using AI to drive income growth among rural residents.

title: Does happiness at workplace matter? A study among employees from public and private sectors in Oman
abstract: This study aimed to assess the level of happiness at work among a sample of employees from the public and private sectors in Oman as well as determine the differences between male and female employees in terms of their level of happiness. It also aimed to assess the relationship between sociodemographic factors (educational level, income, job position, and type of employment) and happiness at work. The Happiness at Work Scale was administered to a convenience sample of (1003) employees from government and private sectors in Oman. The validity and reliability of the scale were also assessed. The results indicated above the average levels of happiness at work. There were significant differences between sociodemographic factors (educational level, income, job position, and type of employment) and happiness at work. However, gender and sector type were not associated with happiness at work. This study has specific implications for both research and practice.

title: Place names reflect the adaptation of human to environmental changes: taking the Erhai Lake Basin in China as an example
abstract: Under the global context of climate change, understanding the adaptation mechanisms of human societies to the environment has become a crucial issue for achieving sustainable development goals. The ecological wisdom embedded in traditional knowledge is increasingly valued for addressing environmental changes. This study takes the Erhai Lake Basin in China, as a case to explore the value of toponyms as carriers of local knowledge in revealing environmental changes and human adaptation strategies. Through a systematic analysis of the toponyms and their spatial distribution patterns related to settlement migration in the study area, the findings reveal three key patterns: 1) All of the geographical location fixed 1209 toponyms in the Erhai Lake Basin form three clusters located in low-altitude, flat, and expansive lakeside areas. Toponyms reflecting human life and production activities account for 55.1% of the total, while those reflecting natural environmental features account for 46.1%. 2) A total of 192 toponyms reflect human settlement migration, accounting for 10.01% of the total toponyms, with cluster areas consistent with the overall toponym distribution. These migration-related toponyms can be categorized into five types based on migration characteristics: Shang 上(upper) - Zhong 中(middle) - Xia 下(lower) prefixed toponyms (39.58%) exhibit a distinct vertical distribution from higher to lower elevations; Da 大(Big) - Xiao 小(small) prefixed toponyms (23.96%) are generally found at relatively higher altitudes; Nan 南(south) - Bei 北(north) (20.83%) and Dong 东(east) - Xi 西(west) (10.42%) prefixed toponyms with over half of these two categories being predominantly located on both sides of river valleys; Xin 新(new) - Jiu 旧(old) prefixed toponyms constitute the smallest proportion at 5.21%. 3) Four specific toponyms explicitly indicate past environmental features, with the highest altitude being ~140 m above the current water level of Erhai Lake, reflecting a period of higher water levels in Erhai Lake. The study confirms that the toponymic patterns in the basin reflect the state of human geography, and migration-related toponyms reflect environmental fluctuations and human adaptation processes. This inspires systematic research using toponyms to reveal strategies for human adaptation to environmental change, providing a new perspective for sustainable development practices under climate change.

title: Benefits and challenges of integrated care model for dementia in China: a scoping review
abstract: Dementia has become a growing public health challenge in China, while fragmented healthcare and elderly care systems limit the provision of continuous and coordinated care for people with dementia (PwD). Integrated care has been proposed as a potential approach to address these challenges. This scoping review aimed to map the current status, outcomes, and implementation barriers of integrated care models for PwD in China. Following the JBI methodology for scoping reviews, literature searches were conducted in seven databases, including PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Database. A total of 31 studies were included, comprising 26 empirical studies, 2 reviews, 2 theoretical studies, and 1 descriptive study. The Social Ecological Model was applied as a multilevel analytical framework to synthesize influencing factors. The findings showed that dementia integrated care in China has mainly developed through four models: collaboration between medical and elderly care institutions, medical units within elderly care facilities, establishing elderly care units within hospitals, family‑based integrated care. Existing evidence suggests that dementia integrated care may improve the quality of life of PwD and reduce caregiver burden. However, its implementation remains challenged by insufficient dementia awareness, limited family involvement, shortages of trained professionals, insufficient community-based services, and inadequate policy support. Future development should prioritize community-based dementia integrated care pathways, strengthen multidisciplinary workforce training, improve cross-sector coordination, and establish sustainable policy and evaluation mechanisms to support high-quality integrated care for PwD in China.

title: Impact of teaching business ethics on students’ attitudes. An experience of educational innovation
abstract: Questionable business practices highlight the growing interest in incorporating ethical content into curricula. However, there are gaps in research on the impact of teaching business ethics on university students’ attitudes. In particular, research on engineering students is scarce, despite the fact that many of these professionals will assume managerial roles. This paper compares two groups of engineering students through an innovative educational experience in which only one of the groups received business ethics content in the subject Business . To measure students’ attitudes, the widely validated Attitudes Toward Business Ethics Questionnaire was used. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to apply Rasch Measurement Theory to the ATBEQ in this research context, allowing a more rigorous psychometric assessment of the instrument and the derivation of a comparable interval-level measure, subject to model fit. The results show that there are no significant differences in the attitudes of the two groups after the teaching intervention. Finally, attitudes towards business ethics are more favourable when the scale items refer to one’s own behaviour than the behaviour of others. Likewise, a qualitative study using in-depth interviews delves into the explanation of the findings. The study provides practical implications and concrete recommendations for effective teaching methods and policies, while recommendations for future research are proposed.

title: Understanding pharmaceutical industry coalitions: a case study of Mallinckrodt
abstract: Abstract The opioid industry has used coalitions to lobby for policies beneficial to its interests and to influence public discourse. In this study, we reviewed the creation of Mallinckrodt’s Alliance for Balanced Pain Management (AfBPM) to better understand opioid industry coalitions. We searched the Opioid Industry Documents Archive (OIDA), an online, open-access collection of documents released in US litigation against opioid manufacturers, for materials on AfBPM. We conducted a retrospective qualitative review of 132 documents, including emails, press releases, and internal presentations, by coding them by themes drawn from the Policy Dystopia model. In the mid-2010s, Mallinckrodt created AfBPM to position itself as a responsible opioid manufacturer. It recruited independent organizations and held a 2014 summit to draw press attention. It sought to convey the message that opioid misuse was the responsibility of healthcare providers and patients, and used its website, news media campaigns, op-eds, and social media to spread these messages. Mallinckrodt used AfBPM as a tool to recruit other organizations and to claim that patients and prescribers were responsible for opioid misuse. Understanding industry use of coalitions like AfBPM can help develop policies that limit influence from coalitions advancing pharmaceutical manufacturer narratives.

title: Culturally responsive and equity-driven differentiated STEM pedagogy and assessment in diverse classrooms in Ghana
abstract: Persistent assessment inequities in linguistically and culturally diverse classrooms necessitate contextually grounded frameworks that advance both academic excellence and educational justice. The study developed, implemented, and evaluated a culturally responsive, equity-driven, and differentiated pedagogical-assessment framework for STEM learning in multilingual and socioeconomically diverse classrooms in Ghana. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design integrated qualitative data (interviews, observations, focus groups) with quantitative measures (pre-post-tests, subscale gains, ANCOVA, and Bayesian analyses). The study involved 210 participants 24 STEM teachers, 6 headteachers, and 180 Primary 4-6 pupils from six public basic schools in Ghana. Quantitative findings revealed statistically significant learning gains across schools and domains. Mean post-test scores increased by 13.96 points (29.12%), with a large overall effect size (Cohen’s d = 1.68; Hedges’ g = 1.89; η ² = 0.79; p < 0.001), indicating strong practical and educational significance. Subscale analyses showed consistent and convergent gains across all framework dimensions, including conceptual mastery (d = 1.72), application of skills (d = 1.67), inclusive strategy use (d = 1.62), opportunity-to-learn (d = 1.59), tiered instruction (d = 1.66), flexible grouping (d = 1.64), linguistic alignment (d = 1.70), and cultural asset integration ( d = 1.69), all demonstrating large effects (d > 1.5). ANCOVA results confirmed significant effects of the intervention across all domains while controlling for pre-test performance, including inquiry-based STEM practices (F = 26.03, p < .001, η²ₚ = 0.10), integrated STEM tasks (F = 19.38, p < .001, η²ₚ = .077), equity-driven instructional practices (η²ₚ = 0.05–0.07), differentiated pedagogical assessment (η²ₚ = 0.04–0.05), and culturally responsive assessment practices (η²ₚ = 0.05–0.06). The pre-test covariate remained significant ( F = 88.21, p < .001, η² = 0.328), indicating the importance of baseline achievement while confirming robust intervention effects Bayesian analyses indicated strong evidential support (posterior probabilities > 0.98; Bayes Factors = 28.1–36.4). Qualitative findings corroborated these results, highlighting increased teacher capacity for culturally relevant task design and improved student engagement and identity affirmation. The study offers empirically grounded guidance for decolonizing STEM assessment in multilingual and underserved contexts.

title: Interpreting tourist load: how does sports event tourism intensity impact tourist experience?
abstract: Abstract Sports event tourism has become an important driver of urban competitiveness, yet little is known about how tourists perceive the intensity of their participation and how this shapes their experiences. Existing research conceptualises tourism intensity mainly at the destination level, emphasising issues such as overcrowding and environmental pressure, while neglecting the individual-level loads tourists carry during event travel. This study develops an individual-level conceptualisation of sports event tourism intensity as a multidimensional, tourist-perceived load encompassing temporal, physical, cognitive, social, and sensory demands.
