Evidence of a structural transformation dilemma in development is confirmed: regions with greater employment concentration in the primary sector exhibit higher inequality, whereas expansion of secondary and tertiary employment facilitates more inclusive growth and equitable income distribution. Given that greater employment in secondary and tertiary activities is associated with lower inequality, South Africa should accelerate structural transformation by fostering value addition in agriculture and mining, investing in industry-relevant skills, and utilising Special Economic Zones to facilitate industrial development and inclusive growth

title: How digital detox influences purchase intention in social commerce: the mediating role of digital fatigue and the moderating role of mindfulness
abstract: The paper examines the mediating role of digital detox (DD) between purchase intention (PI)-digital fatigue (DF)-mindfulness (MF) as moderators in the context of social commerce. The research utilized a sample of 297 participants in the fashion and retail sector in the UAE to develop empirical data through self-administered questionnaire. The structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to test the connections between hypotheses and was strong enough to test for complicated mediation-moderation. The results show that DD has a significant positive effect on PI both in direct and indirect effect due to reduced DFs. In addition, MF strengthens the estimated positive connection between DD-PI and weakens the negative influence of DF on the formation of MF as a moderator. The article advances the digital consumption and social commerce literature because it has defined DD as a primary driver of consumer well-being and behavioral intention, particularly in terms of its application in emerging-market contexts. In a practical manner, the research offers meaningful perspective into managers and marketers to come up with consumer engagement policies that integrate digital balance and MF practises. Although the results produced are significant both in theoretical and managerial contributions, the data is tied to limited cultural and industry-specific generalizability boundaries, implying the need to employ cross-cultural and longitudinal studies in further investigations.

title: Teachers’ perspectives on ‘Double Reduction’ education policy: a survey of 12,524 educators in China
abstract: This study investigates the cognitive attitudes of primary and secondary school teachers in Sichuan Province, China, toward the implementation of the “Double Reduction” education policy (DREP), guided by policy diffusion theory. A descriptive survey design was employed, utilizing stratified random sampling to collect data from 12,524 teachers across four regions of varying socioeconomic development levels. A self-developed questionnaire (DREP Implementation Survey; Cronbach’s α = 0.757, KMO = 0.811, p < 0.001) was used to assess teachers’ evaluations of policy effectiveness, perceived impacts, and improvement intentions. Data analysis revealed three key findings: (1) Teachers generally held negative evaluations of policy implementation effectiveness; (2) exhibited dual attitudes toward policy impacts—acknowledging its role in promoting student development while expressing concerns about increased workload burdens; and (3) actively supported policy refinement, particularly advocating for differentiated strategies. Linear regression models demonstrated that effectiveness evaluations ( β = 0.081), impact perceptions ( β = 0.873), improvement intentions ( β = −0.077), teaching experience ( β = −0.138), and regional disparities ( β = −0.019) collectively explained 73.4% of the variance in teachers’ policy attitudes ( R ² = 0.734, p < 0.001). These findings are interpreted through the lens of policy diffusion theory, highlighting the critical role of implementers’ perceptions in shaping the adoption and diffusion of educational reforms. The study emphasizes the need for policymakers to implement tiered interventions, such as fully considering teachers’ workload, competency alignment, incentive mechanisms, subject-specific differences, and regional educational development levels, to reduce implementation disparities and enhance policy sustainability. By revealing the critical role of grassroots stakeholders in educational reform, this study deepens the application of policy diffusion theory in equity-oriented educational governance.

title: Examining the impact of ethnic diversity and income inequality on educational inequality from the SDG10 perspective
abstract: The main purpose of this study is to examine the effects of ethnic diversity and income inequality on educational attainment inequality in European Union countries. A spatial regression model was employed using annual data for the period 2010–2019. The results indicate that ethnic diversity, income inequality, higher education enrolment, sectarian diversity, and EU membership duration are positively associated with educational attainment inequality, whereas economic growth, education expenditure, and internet access reduce educational attainment inequality. The turning point analysis further confirms an inverted U-shaped relationship between ethnic diversity and educational attainment inequality. By contrast, although the estimated coefficients for EU membership duration suggest a concave functional form, the calculated turning point lies outside the observed data range, indicating that the positive association gradually weakens as membership duration increases rather than exhibiting a statistically supported inverted U-shaped relationship. The findings provide useful implications for policymakers seeking to reduce educational attainment inequality across European Union member states

title: Spatiotemporal evolution characteristics and obstacle factors of the coordinated development between the tourism industry and ecological security
abstract: Abstract Currently, the lack of a scientifically effective evaluation framework for measuring the interactive impact between the tourism industry and ecological security has hindered the policy understanding of green transformation in tourist destinations. Taking Zhejiang Province in China as an example, this study innovatively constructs an evaluation index system for the coordinated development of the tourism industry and ecological security. The findings are as follows: The TECE (Tourism - Ecological Coupling and Coordination) index, with the expansion of the tourism industry scale, initially exerts a coercive effect on ecological security. The TECE index exhibits significant spatial heterogeneity and is closely related to pressure indicators such as population and economic factors. The development of ecological industries is conducive to the promotion of the TECE index, while the expansion of the population and economic scale is not conducive to the stable development of TECE. The main obstacle factors mainly include per capital water resources, per capital forest land area, tourism foreign exchange income, inbound tourist reception, and improvement components such as star - rated hotels and travel agencies. This study enriches the theoretical understanding of the tourism - ecology coupling mechanism and provides a scientific reference for the development of regional green transformation.

title: Becoming reflective professionals: from performative anxiety to relational pedagogy through dialogic scaffolding
abstract: This study explores how pre-service teachers navigate the developmental continuum of reflective practice to construct their professional identities during microteaching. Drawing on reflection papers and peer/instructor feedback from 44 EFL pre-service teachers, as well as instructor feedback, the study employed qualitative analysis to trace the chronological trajectory from retrospective critique (reflection-on-action) to proactive pedagogical planning (reflection-for-action). The findings reveal a profound shift that moves beyond mere technical troubleshooting. First, participants transformed initial pedagogical friction and performative anxiety into vital opportunities for emotional regulation. Second, they evolved from executing rigid lesson plans to architecting responsive instructional dynamics. Finally, they rejected teacher-centered transmission, embracing a relational pedagogy designed to foster learner agency. Crucially, this evolution was catalyzed by dialogic scaffolding; peer and instructor feedback functioned not as summative evaluation, but as socially mediated intervention that bridged the gap between diagnosing limitations and envisioning their professional identity as an effective teacher. Ultimately, this study reconceptualizes reflection not as a solitary, post-lesson administrative task, but as a profound ontological bridge. The findings suggest that teacher education programs must embed socially mediated, forward-oriented reflective cycles to empower novices to evolve from anxious performers into adaptive, self-directed professionals capable of true reflective agency.

title: Psychosocial perspectives on suicidal thoughts: developmental trajectories and associated baseline factors among South Korean children
abstract: Abstract South Korea records the highest suicide mortality rate among OECD nations, with suicide constituting the primary cause of death for individuals aged 10–39 years. Despite extensive prevention efforts, limited research has examined the heterogeneous developmental patterns of suicidal thoughts during the critical elementary-to-middle school transition period. Understanding these developmental trajectories is essential for designing targeted, developmentally-informed intervention strategies. This prospective longitudinal study utilized data from the Korea Children and Youth Panel Survey 2018, following 2607 students from 4th grade through 9th grade (2018–2023). Suicidal thoughts were assessed annually using a single-item measure. Latent class growth analysis was employed to identify distinct developmental trajectories, with comprehensive assessment of individual (gender, sleep duration, self-esteem, problematic smartphone use, academic performance), family (income, parental warmth, rejection, inconsistency), and school factors (peer relationships, teacher-student relationships) as baseline correlates of trajectory class membership. Results revealed three distinct trajectory classes: low-stable (73.5%, n = 1915), moderate-increasing (19.2%, n = 501), and initially-high declining (7.3%, n = 191). The low-stable group maintained consistently minimal suicidal thoughts throughout the study period. The moderate-increasing group demonstrated persistently elevated levels with gradual increases over time. The initially-high declining group began with extremely high levels but showed significant improvement, followed by a modest rebound. Self-esteem emerged as the strongest baseline correlate of trajectory membership, with higher self-esteem associated with greater likelihood of low-stable membership (OR = 2.187, 95% CI: 1.422–3.363) and lower likelihood of initially-high declining membership (OR = 0.149, 95% CI: 0.084–0.264) compared to the moderate-increasing trajectory. Gender differences were significant, with males showing higher likelihood of low-stable trajectory membership. The identification of heterogeneous developmental patterns of suicidal thoughts provides important insights for suicide prevention among Korean children. The findings suggest that universal prevention approaches may be insufficient, highlighting the need for trajectory-specific interventions.

title: Regulatory penalties and ESG outcomes: a nonlinear governance mechanism
abstract: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between environmental penalty intensity and corporate ESG performance, as well as the contextual conditions under which this relationship changes. Using panel data for Chinese A-share listed companies from 2013 to 2023, we employ a fixed-effects model, supplemented by instrumental variable, propensity score matching, and Heckman two-step approaches, to address potential endogeneity and sample selection concerns. The results reveal a significant U-shaped relationship between environmental penalty intensity and ESG performance: at low levels of penalty intensity, increased penalties suppress ESG performance, whereas beyond a critical threshold, further penalties promote ESG improvement. Further analyses show that this nonlinear effect is shaped by three moderating conditions. Media attention strengthens the positive segment of the U-shaped relationship by increasing external scrutiny and reputational pressure. Political connections weaken the governance effect of environmental penalties by buffering firms from regulatory and market discipline. Green technological innovation positively moderates the U-shaped relationship by enhancing firms’ internal capability to convert regulatory pressure into substantive environmental upgrading and ESG improvement. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that the U-shaped relationship is more pronounced among firms with low goodwill, firms located in eastern regions, and firms facing lower financing constraints. This study contributes to the literature by moving beyond a linear perspective on environmental regulation and by identifying the external monitoring, institutional buffering, and internal capability conditions under which environmental penalties become effective governance mechanisms for improving ESG performance.

title: Constructing love: Relationship maintenance strategies of same-sex couples in China’s institutional void
abstract: This study explores how same-sex couples in China build and maintain intimate relationships despite the absence of institutional protection and established social templates. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we conducted in-depth interviews with 22 self-identified gay and lesbian individuals (11 men and 11 women) across 14 Chinese cities. We describe a relationship practice that is not templated, where couples create their own forms of relationships using a mix of partial and competing influences instead of relying on a predefined template. We term this ongoing process “constitutive negotiation.” Five recurring maintenance strategies emerged from the interviews: (1) establishing equality through economic negotiation, (2) creating private rituals in the absence of social scripts, (3) managing growth synchronicity, (4) navigating and redefining sexual intimacy, and (5) balancing a dual life across different social contexts. This work is both demanding and creative, requiring significant labor and vigilance to sustain relationships—efforts that legal recognition could alleviate. Despite these efforts, strain and separation are still common. The findings challenge relationship maintenance theories developed in more recognition-rich Western contexts, highlighting the agency of Chinese same-sex couples while providing a provisional rather than a universal understanding of how such relationships are sustained.

title: Investigating the complex dynamics of psychological stress and sociocultural influences on unhealthy meal frequency as a subclinical indicator of disordered eating behaviours
abstract: Unhealthy meal frequency (UMF), including meal skipping, irregular timing, and maladaptive eating patterns, is increasingly recognised as a major contributor to poor nutritional and mental health outcomes worldwide. In low- and middle-income countries such as Pakistan, rapid urbanisation, shifting gender roles, and strong sociocultural norms may uniquely shape eating behaviours, yet empirical evidence integrating psychological and sociocultural determinants remains limited. Previous research has largely focused on dietary quality or caloric intake, leaving the broader behavioural structure of meal frequency and its contextual drivers insufficiently understood. This study addresses the need for a comprehensive, culturally grounded examination of UMF in Pakistan by integrating demographic, psychological, and sociocultural factors within a single analytical framework. Using a cross-sectional sample of 412 Pakistani adults and a culturally adapted assessment of eating behaviours, we examined the prevalence, patterns, and predictors of UMF, with particular attention to gender and regional differences. Here we show that nearly half of participants (46.1%) met criteria for UMF, with markedly higher prevalence among females than males (52.2% vs 31.1%). Irregular meal timing and meal skipping were the most common patterns. Multivariate analyses revealed that sociocultural factors, especially cultural pressures, family food rules, and gender role expectations, were the strongest independent predictors of UMF, exceeding the influence of psychological factors such as emotional eating. Emotional eating partially mediated the relationship between cultural pressures and UMF, while gender significantly moderated this association, with substantially stronger effects observed in females. Regional disparities were evident, with the highest UMF prevalence in Punjab. These findings extend prior knowledge by demonstrating that UMF in Pakistan is driven less by individual psychological traits alone and more by embedded sociocultural structures that shape daily eating practices, particularly for women. More broadly, this work highlights UMF as a culturally patterned behaviour rather than a purely personal choice, underscoring the need for nutrition and public health interventions that move beyond individual-level education to address gender norms, family dynamics, and cultural expectations within rapidly changing societies.

title: Code-breaking spatial practices of Pokémon GO players in Shenzhen, China: Fubao industrial park as a laboratory for studying human behaviour in infrastructure space
abstract: Abstract This paper studies human spatial practices in an industrial park in Shenzhen, China and asks how people make space for themselves through ‘code-breaking’ behaviours even in strictly coded, programmed, and predetermined special economic zones (SEZs). The study draws upon Keller Easterling’s concept of ‘the zone’ and research into geographic aspects of hybrid reality game (HRG) play. Pokémon GO, the world’s most popular HRG, is inaccessible in most of the Chinese mainland due to internet regulatory restrictions. However, the game is accessible in a small portion (approximately 0.4 km) of the Fubao industrial park in the south of Shenzhen, bordering Hong Kong. We describe and analyse how HRG players navigate and claim mobility and publicness within this site that was designed to serve the extrastate capitalist and corporate logics of the special economic zone, as well as how other actors within this space respond to and engage with these HRG players. Many of these behaviours represent code-breaking that challenges top-down systems spatial governance, though without necessarily challenging wider social, economic, and political systems.

title: User evaluation of technology-enabled self-service kiosks: service assurance, environmental cues, and technology expertise
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how service assurance and environmental cues influence users’ post-adoption evaluation of self-service technologies (SSTs) and self-service kiosks (SSKs), incorporating the moderating role of technology expertise within the technology continuance theory (TCT) framework. Although prior research has examined initial technology acceptance, post-adoption evaluations in automated service environments remain underexplored. Data were collected from Korean consumers with prior experience using SSTs/SSKs, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was applied to test the proposed model. The results revealed that service assurance significantly affects both environmental cues and post-adoption evaluations, while environmental cues also exert a significant mediating effect between service assurance and post-adoption evaluation. Moreover, technology expertise moderates the relationship between environmental cues and post-adoption evaluation, indicating that users with higher technological proficiency perceive greater experiential value from well-designed SST environments. This study extends the TCT by integrating service quality and servicescape perspectives, offering a comprehensive understanding of how users’ cognitive and experiential factors interact in technology-mediated services. The findings also suggest practical strategies for managers to enhance customer experience by improving service reliability, optimizing physical and digital atmospherics, and tailoring user support based on technology expertise. Overall, this research provides both theoretical advancement and managerial insights into sustaining positive user engagement in the evolving landscape of smart service environments.

title: Developing an expert-informed framework for flipped lesson design in physical education: a European Delphi study
abstract: Contemporary education has increasingly emphasised student-centred approaches that encourage active participation, collaboration, and greater learner responsibility. Within this broader pedagogical shift, flipped learning has emerged as an approach that relocates selected instructional content to the pre-class phase so that face-to-face time can be used more extensively for application, interaction, feedback, and active learning. In physical education, this structure may be particularly valuable because lesson time is strongly oriented towards movement, practice, and interpersonal engagement. This research paper aims to develop a consensus-informed framework for the design and implementation of flipped lessons in physical education across European contexts. This European Delphi Study utilises the classic three-round Delphi approach. Invitation letters were sent to 50 European experts. Of the 50 invited experts, 20 agreed to participate in the Delphi study, resulting in a response rate of 40%. The findings informed the development of an expert-informed framework for flipped lesson design in physical education. The three-round iterative process achieved strong, statistically significant concordance for Knowledge and Skills, while the Attitudes & Values dimension demonstrated statistically significant but weak agreement. The resulting European Framework for Transformative Flipped Physical Education organises the Delphi-derived competencies into three interconnected pillars concerning professional knowledge, pedagogical and facilitation skills, and educational attitudes and values. The framework is intended as an expert-informed guide for interpreting flipped lesson design in PE and requires further empirical examination in practice.

title: Modelling and mechanism analysis of English vocabulary associative learning process of L2 learners
abstract: Although the associative learning strategy (ALS) is widely employed in vocabulary teaching, its mechanisms have rarely been quantified from a complex dynamic systems perspective. This study addresses this gap by constructing a word association corpus from Chinese university students and developing a stepwise diffusion modelling framework to simulate vocabulary network formation. Three computational diffusion strategies are proposed and compared through 750 computational simulations: RADS (random association diffusion strategy), MDDS (maximum degree diffusion strategy), and IDASDS (integration of degree and association strength diffusion strategy). Quantitative analysis reveals that IDASDS achieves the fastest network convergence and produces stronger semantic connectivity in terms of clustering coefficient and path length. The initial word count significantly affects the size of the first fully connected network but has minimal impact on ultimate convergence steps, confirming the emergent nature of associative learning. These findings provide quantifiable principles for vocabulary instruction: prioritising high-connectivity hub words and optimising initial vocabulary load can enhance learning efficiency by leveraging the small-world properties of lexical networks.

title: Do environmental regulation policies induce boundary effects: evidence from hog production in the Yangtze River Basin, China
abstract: Although environmental regulations are intended to improve ecological conditions, their implementation may also be accompanied by a relative concentration of polluting activities in boundary areas, thereby increasing pollution pressure in these locations. Hog production has long been a major contributor to water pollution in China. In response, the Chinese government has implemented the most stringent livestock and poultry environmental regulations (LERs) in its history. Using a staggered DDD model and a manually collected panel dataset covering 1028 counties across ten provinces, this study examines the effects of LERs on hog production and water pollution pressure in boundary counties. The findings show that LER implementation increased slaughter volume and slaughter density in boundary counties by 8.68% and 11.42%, respectively, with stronger effects in economically less-developed regions, consistent with the “pollution haven” hypothesis. The effects of LERs exhibit significant heterogeneity across different hog-farming functional areas, with notable increases in hog production in boundary counties located in potential growth and constrained development areas. The increase in hog-farming intensity in boundary areas is associated with modest increases in selected water-pollution indicators. Specifically, LERs weaken the positive relationship between hog production and water pollution to some extent, but the relative expansion of hog production in boundary areas following LER implementation remains associated with additional pollution pressure. After accounting for the mitigating effect of LERs, the marginal effects of slaughter volume on COD Mn are 0.0672, and the marginal effects of slaughter density on COD Mn and NH₃-N are 0.0916 and 0.0755, respectively. The findings offer policy-relevant insights for improving the effectiveness of environmental regulation and addressing boundary-pollution issues.

title: Beyond borders: understanding the determinants of global audience engagement with Chinese films
abstract: While Chinese cinema has enjoyed significant domestic success, its global audience engagement has been relatively low. Chinese film industry is significantly influenced by economic, cultural, and political factors. To improve the global market presence of Chinese films, there is a need to study these factors that influence the global audience engagement with Chinese films. In this study, ten significant determinants that influence global audience engagement with Chinese films were identified and evaluated using the mixed method (qualitative and quantitative) approach. The determinants were identified through comprehensive literature review which were confirmed by experts. The Total Interpretive Structural Modelling (TISM) was employed to present the identified determinants in a hierarchical structure exhibiting their significance level. While, Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) was used to categorize the determinants into the cause-effect cluster. The findings of the study highlighted that ‘cultural familiarity,’ ‘production values, and ‘cast appeal and star power ‘are top three causal determinants which influence other factors. The results support Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT) by demonstrating that audiences actively engage with films to satisfy cognitive, emotional, and social needs. Cultural familiarity, production quality, and cast appeal function as key gratification drivers shaping purposeful media consumption. Industry managers can enhance global audience engagement with Chinese films by adopting an integrated strategy that simultaneously addresses cultural familiarity, production quality, and cast appeal. This can be achieved by supporting culturally adaptive storytelling and international co-productions, alongside targeted investments in technical training and filmmaking infrastructure to meet global production standards.

title: Mistranslation, pseudotranslation, and wandering translation as modes of trans-translating: a translanguaging perspective
abstract: Drawing on translanguaging as a theoretical lens, this article reconceptualizes mistranslation, pseudotranslation, and wandering translation as distinct yet interrelated modes of trans-translating. Examining examples from colonial encounters, feminist writing, and digital culture, it shows how these practices enact epistemic resistance and cultural innovation, subverting linguistic hierarchies and amplifying marginalized voices. Trans-translating transcends source-target binaries to foster transcultural dialogue—yet this dialogue is not politically neutral. Its significance lies in what we theorize as situated accountability: a heuristic that assesses any translational act by asking who it serves, with what intention, under what conditions for reinterpretation, and through what counter-hegemonic spaces. By grounding ethical judgment in these concrete factors, the framework advances equitable exchange not by celebrating fluidity wholesale but by distinguishing emancipatory enactments from harmful ones.

title: Tourism, digital finance, and urban concentration in shaping regional economic growth in China
abstract: International tourism plays an important role in promoting economic growth in developing economies, particularly when supported by digital infrastructure and urban development. Following the rapid expansion of China’s tourism industry since 2000 and the parallel rise of digital finance, understanding the dynamics of tourism-led growth has become increasingly important for achieving balanced regional development. This study examines the relationships between international tourism, urban population, digital finance, and provincial economic growth in China from 2005 to 2024. To capture nonlinear dynamics, threshold regression analysis is applied, complemented by dynamic ordinary least squares and fully modified ordinary least squares to ensure robustness. The results show that international tourism has a significant positive impact on economic growth in linear models, while urbanization and digital finance also strengthen provincial economic performance. Threshold analysis reveals that tourism effects become stronger beyond specific thresholds. When international tourist arrivals exceed 1.419 (logged) and tourism receipts surpass 6.0504 (logged), the elasticity of tourism on provincial output increases by approximately 24–28%. Furthermore, digital finance and tourism exhibit asymmetric effects on tourist arrivals across provinces. These findings highlight the importance of nonlinear dynamics in assessing tourism-led growth and suggest that policymakers should promote digital tourism strategies to support sustainable regional development.

title: Gendered cultural representations of HIV/AIDS among HIV-negative Israelis: a narrative study
abstract: This study explored and compared the cultural representations of men and women living with HIV/AIDS among HIV-negative Israelis. A sample of 20 HIV-negative Israeli men and 23 women was recruited. The participants wrote a story about a 24-year-old man or woman with HIV/AIDS. Reflexive thematic analysis of the stories identified three themes in the narratives about a woman living with HIV/AIDS: (1) The deviant woman theme portrays women as morally transgressing and thus, blameworthy for acquiring HIV/AIDS; (2) The theme of turmoil deals with the women’s immediate reactions to their diagnosis as a tragedy or calamity; (3) The decline theme describes the long-term experience of women living with HIV/AIDS as one of isolation, accompanied by feelings of hopelessness, fear, depression, and other dire emotions. Two themes were identified in the narratives about men living with HIV/AIDS: (1) The women as vectors theme depicts women as temptresses “infecting” men with the virus; (2) The men living with HIV/AIDS theme describes men as attempting to forge a “normal” life despite their condition, while employing various mechanisms to manage potential or actual stigmatization. Overall, the findings suggest that culture does not portray people neutrally, but always through gendered assumptions and norms. Women living with HIV/AIDS are judged more harshly by society than men living with HIV/AIDS.

title: What behavioural science entails: the C-frame as a successor to the ‘personal responsibility’ policy paradigm
abstract: Behavioural science is much more than a set of techniques to influence behaviour. It represents a perspective on social reality – a perspective that is no less important than the economic or legal perspective. In this contribution, I will explain the profound consequences of taking the behavioural perspective seriously by focussing on two interrelated psychological concepts: self-control and perceived control. The research on self-control convincingly shows that there are serious limitations to people’s capacity to always act in accordance with their intentions and plans, expecially in times of setbacks and stress. The research on perceived control convincingly shows that if people lack sufficient resources and opportunities to achieve their life goals, the resulting feelings of powerlessness can be very harmful, both to themselves and to society in general. Policymakers should therefore abandon the ‘personal responsibility’ paradigm that has shaped so many public policies over the past decades, as it is based on unrealistic assumptions. This paradigm should be replaced by a new approach of ‘shared responsibility’ that is much more in line with the research findings. Given the central importance of the two related control-concepts to this new approach, one might also call it the ‘C-frame’.

title: Profiling university foreign language students in Singapore: motivations and perceptions of Spanish learners
abstract: 2024 marked the tenth anniversary of Spanish being offered at the Ministry of Education Language Centre (MOELC), while 2025 celebrated a decade of the Spanish Programme at the Centre for Language Studies (CLS) at the National University of Singapore (NUS). Despite these milestones, little research has examined Spanish as a Foreign Language (SFL) education in Singapore. This exploratory study addresses the gap by profiling university students learning Spanish, focusing on their linguistic background, their motivations and deterrents towards foreign language (FL) learning more broadly, and their perceptions of the Spanish language and its cultural context. Combining quantitative and qualitative methods, this research seeks to deepen the understanding of Singaporean learners, providing valuable socio-demographic and psychographic data for teaching Spanish FL in this particular multilingual and multicultural context.

title: AI Intervention for social exclusion: the emotional regulation function and basic need satisfaction mechanism of chatbots
abstract: This study investigates how chatbot interaction affects the basic needs of individuals experiencing social exclusion, the mediating role of positive emotions, and the optimal level of linguistic anthropomorphism in chatbots. This study was conducted through three progressive experiments. Study 1 employed the Cyberball paradigm to induce social exclusion, and the results showed that excluded individuals had a significantly higher willingness to use chatbots. Study 2 combined the O-Cam paradigm, physiological indicators, and scale measurements, confirming that chatbot use could significantly enhance basic needs such as belongingness and self-esteem, as well as positive emotions, while reducing negative emotions. Among these relationships, positive emotions played a full mediating role. Study 3 set up three groups with low, medium, and high levels of linguistic anthropomorphism. The results indicated that chatbots with a medium level of anthropomorphism achieved the optimal effects in improving basic needs, enhancing positive emotions, and reducing negative emotions. Collectively, these findings indicate that chatbots can serve as effective intervention tools for social exclusion, with their mechanisms of action related to the mediation of positive emotions and moderate anthropomorphism. This research provides theoretical and practical implications for relevant psychological interventions.

title: Spatial association network characteristics and influence mechanisms of urban land use efficiency from a complex network perspective: county-level evidence from the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei urban agglomeration
abstract: Urban agglomerations have emerged as critical platforms for optimising territorial spatial patterns and promoting regional coordination and high-quality development. These regions exhibit significantly structured characteristics, yet the cross-regional association mechanisms of urban land-use efficiency remain underexplored. This study employs the super-efficiency SBM model and complex network analysis to investigate the structural characteristics and driving mechanisms of the urban land-use efficiency (ULUE) spatial association network at the county level in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei urban agglomeration from 2005 to 2020. The findings are as follows: (1) Overall, ULUE in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei urban agglomeration exhibited an upward trend, although significant spatial disparities persist; (2) The spatial association network of ULUE exhibits stronger agglomeration than diffusion, with a hierarchical structure; (3) Inter-county linkages have become increasingly tight, with limited spatial spillover effects in core counties of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, while notable spatial interaction and synergy have emerged in boundary areas between municipalities, reflecting a weakening of administrative boundary barriers; (4) The network structure is evolving towards greater centralisation, with core county nodes exerting stronger influence on the stability of the overall structure, yet the overall pattern shows initial signs of transitioning from a “core-periphery” configuration to a “multi-centre, multi-layer” form; (5) Analysis of driving mechanisms reveals that changes in factors such as industrial structure, infrastructure, and government regulatory capacity reflect positive effects of regional integration policies, whereas disparities in economic development remain a key constraint on the spatial coordination of ULUE. Based on these findings, optimisation strategies are proposed, including constructing metropolitan and multi-centre systems, integrating multimodal infrastructure networks, strengthening cross-regional cooperation and governance models, and promoting deeper collaboration within industrial chains.

title: Career experiences of educated Syrian women in Türkiye
abstract: This study examines the career experiences of educated Syrian women under temporary protection in Türkiye, focusing on how forced migration has reshaped their professional trajectories and labor market participation. Adopting a qualitative research design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 24 Syrian women residing in a temporary accommodation centre in Kahramanmaraş, Türkiye. The study explores the effects of displacement on participants’ pre-existing occupational backgrounds, the barriers encountered in accessing or re-entering the labor market, and the strategies and support mechanisms that shaped their efforts to rebuild professional futures. The interview data were analyzed using descriptive thematic analysis. The findings indicate that forced migration disrupted women’s prior career trajectories and limited their access to qualified employment. Participants reported barriers related to legal insecurity, work permit restrictions, the non-recognition of qualifications, language difficulties, gendered family responsibilities, and discrimination. At the same time, social networks, NGO-supported activities, and vocational or educational opportunities provided partial support for adaptation and professional continuity. The women also articulated future-oriented aspirations related to teaching, public employment, language learning, technical skill development, and legal stability. Overall, the study suggests that the career experiences of educated Syrian women are shaped by the interaction of structural constraints and individual agency within the specific context of temporary protection in Türkiye. The findings highlight the importance of coordinated policies addressing legal access, the recognition of degrees, language and vocational support, childcare, and broader social inclusion to strengthen sustainable career development and labor market integration.

title: Groundwork for human nature developmentalism
abstract: This article introduces Human Nature Developmentalism (HND), a normative framework that views human beings as creative purposive agents and assesses the moral permissibility of biomedical interventions based on their contribution to human flourishing. Positioned between transhumanism and bioconservatism, HND recognises human nature as both fixed and dynamic. It argues that what matters is not the means by which we alter our nature, but the ethical considerations involved. Accordingly, HND upholds the principle that biomedical interventions are morally permissible if and only if they increment our developmental power or otherwise contribute to our flourishing as creative purposive agents.

title: Cross-ideological sharing and counterargument
abstract: Exposure to different perspectives can foster tolerance, a fundamental principle in democratic societies. Whether social media facilitates the exchange of diverse views is subject to debate. Specifically, it is unclear how often content is shared by diverse users and whether users accompany cross-ideological content with counterarguments. To address this, we collected tweets containing URLs posted on days during which four major events took place in the summer of 2021: the Biden-Putin summit, COVID-19, the #FreeBritney movement, and the MLB All-Star Game. We analyze 1,274,792 tweets across 80,130 active U.S.-based users who tweeted about these topics. We find that a lack of diversity was the modal sharing pattern for partisan topics, the Biden-Putin summit and COVID-19, compared to non-partisan topics, baseball and Britney Spears. Sharing patterns further reveal that URLs related to the more partisan topics tend to circulate among politically like-minded users, whereas non-partisan topics are predominantly shared by users with moderate political leanings. Overall, cross-ideological sharing is rare, but when users share cross-ideological content, they tend to include counterarguments. The findings highlight the need for strategies that promote diverse and constructive information exchange on social media platforms.

title: Study on environmental adaptability of prehistoric settlements in the Northern of Jianghan Plain, China
abstract: The northern part of the Jianghan Plain is at the intersection of lacustrine and marshy plains and mountain foothills, and the distribution of prehistoric settlements is obviously influenced by the natural environment. Data such as digital surface models of settlement sites obtained by unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photography and 3D reconstruction can be used to extract the microgeomorphic features of prehistoric settlement sites, analyze their formation processes, and find that the distribution of prehistoric settlements is significantly influenced by the natural environment. The ways in which prehistoric ancestors knew and transformed the natural environment and the human–land relationship should be revealed, and issues such as the mechanism of water control and the environmental adaptability of prehistoric settlements should be raised. This study reveals that prehistoric people in the northern part of the Jianghan Plain mastered rice cultivation and farmland irrigation techniques. They continuously expanded the construction of water conservancy facilities and the scale of rice planting, leading to a steady increase in grain production. This, in turn, promoted the social division of labor, class differentiation, and the birth and development of prehistoric civilization. It provides a series of typical Chinese case for the study of the formation and development of early civilizations in the major river basins at 30° north latitude.

title: A human-centric approach for responding to online soft hate speech: the effect of AI-based persuasion on the comment modification intention of commenters
abstract: The development of digital technology has facilitated the 'democratisation' of the internet, but it has also provided opportunities for online hate speech, which can have negative effects on individuals, groups, and society. Therefore, addressing online hate speech is crucial. However, owing to the paradox between free speech and the regulation of hate speech, soft hate speech, which is morally unacceptable but not directly constrained by law, as hard hate speech is, can result in harmful consequences in more subtle forms. In response, this study proposes shifting the focus of online hate speech research to individuals, with the objective of influencing the comment modification intention of soft hate speech commenters through AI-based persuasion and its associated strategies. Specifically, Study 1 establishes baseline effects by comparing AI-based persuasion against no-persuasion and irrelevant-persuasion controls. A pilot study examines how participant perspective moderates strategy effectiveness, providing the empirical basis for Study 2’s design. Study 2 further examines the comparative effects of emotional labelling and reason-explanation strategies and the mediating role of perceived persuasiveness under higher ecological validity conditions. In summary, this study explores a human-centric approach to responding to online soft hate speech and, through controlled scenario-based experiments, provides preliminary evidence that AI-based persuasion has a positive effect on scenario-based comment modification intention, with perceived persuasiveness identified as a psychological mechanism underlying this effect.

title: Five core themes of intentional team formation
abstract: Cohesive group dynamics and innovative scientific ideas are essential components of successful research collaborations. However, the group dynamics (i.e., the “people”) and the scientific process and outcomes (i.e., the “science”) are often considered separately and with unequal emphasis, such as when the focus on the science comes at the expense of individual team members. This results in a loss of team energy, motivation, and direction. Innovative ideas will only arise and thrive if team members feel psychological safety to propose, take ownership of, and pursue new project directions. As a case study, we describe a large collaborative and crossdisciplinary project team navigating the proposal development process. These efforts were carried out with design grant funding, and the sudden onset of the COVID-19 pandemic necessitated a fully virtual collaboration. This experience led us to identify Five Core Themes of Intentional Team Formation to develop and align teams and ideas: Team Development, Effective Communication, Perspective Alignment, Team Management, and Project Workflow. Here, we use the experience gained from our own crossdisciplinary proposal project to: (1) explain the importance of each theme to team formation, (2) describe our team’s approach to each theme in terms of process and interventions, and (3) evaluate the extent to which these approaches contributed to team formation and function with an emphasis on multiple metrics of success. We found that when individual contributions and expectations are aligned through psychological safety, mutual trust, and respect, idea generation and contributions can launch a team towards achieving goals and objectives. In this article, we discuss limitations, future directions, and crossdisciplinary team applications of our five core themes for team formation. Ultimately, these five core themes provide teams with the team formation tools they need to set a strong foundation to effectively tackle big challenges.

title: Cross-industry risk contagion early warning system: a machine learning framework
abstract: An effective early warning system at the company level is crucial for preventing financial distress. Traditional warning models mainly rely on internal financial indicators of enterprises, ignoring the transmission of systemic risks from external sources. This limitation frequently leads to poor performance in predicting corporate financial distress, particularly during complex cross-industry risk propagation. This study constructs a novel intelligent risk warning model that integrates a newly developed ASR-FDP (Accounting-Systematic Risk Financial Distress Prediction Model) hybrid model with advanced machine learning techniques to warn of corporate financial crises. Utilizing a dataset spanning from 2011 to 2021, we developed the ASR-FDP predictive model, incorporating both cross-industry systemic risk exposure indicators and company-level financial indicators. The results indicate that the ASR-FDP model, based on random forests, exhibits exceptional performance (accuracy of 93%, F1 score of 0.96), significantly outperforming traditional single-indicator models. Our research highlights two key findings: (1) systemic risk indicators possess substantial predictive power independent of financial information indicators, contributing 19% to the predictive ability in financial distress prediction. This addresses the limitation of traditional models, which focus solely on internal risks while neglecting external risks. The ASR-FDP model more accurately predicts financial distress compared to models relying solely on financial indicators. (2) The intelligent early warning system based on machine learning identifies early warning thresholds capable of achieving a 11-month advance prediction, with prediction lead time and accuracy far exceeding traditional methods. This methodological advancement offers regulators a dynamic monitoring tool for preventive risk mitigation, while also providing theoretical insights into nonlinear risk propagation paths in interconnected markets.

title: Algorogenic thumbprints in literary translation: an epistemic network analysis of LLM translations of classical Chinese fantasy
abstract: Abstract This study investigates algorogenic thumbprints, defined as consistent and reproducible stylistic patterns generated by large language models (LLMs) in literary translation. Using epistemic network analysis (ENA) across seven decision-making domains, lexical choice, syntactic structure, cultural adaptation, stylistic register, semantic fidelity, narrative flow, and intertextual reference, we examine translations of two classical Chinese fantasy novels produced by Claude Opus 4.5, ChatGPT 5.2 Pro, and Gemini 3 Pro, alongside published human translations and a Western fantasy reference corpus. The findings show that each LLM exhibits a stable, model-specific epistemic architecture oriented toward narrative coherence, whereas human translators structure decisions more strongly around semantic fidelity. This architectural divergence persists across texts and models. The study therefore suggests that Baker’s framework of translator thumbprints can be meaningfully extended to algorithmic translation and demonstrates the usefulness of ENA for modeling the relational structures underlying translation decision-making.

title: To be slowly killed is still to be killed: necropolitics and slow violence in Imbolo Mbue’s How Beautiful We Were
abstract: The novel How Beautiful We Were by Imbolo Mbue portrays the effects of oil extraction on the everyday lives of people living in the fictional village of Kosawa. This paper contends that the multinational corporation, through its extractive activities, destroys the environment of the village, causing the communities to endure sickness, death, and insecurity. This study places Mbue’s novel within existing discussions of environmental justice and postcolonial critique. It examines how intergenerational trauma is enacted over time through ecological destruction, and how resistance is slowly generated from that destruction. Using Mbembe’s idea of necropolitics and Nixon’s idea of slow violence, the paper maintains close analytical engagement with Mbue’s narrative voice. It pays attention to the collective perspective of the novel and everyday experiences of people facing environmental problems. The paper demonstrates how fiction represents long-term environmental harm and everyday forms of violence that often remain unrecognized within legal frameworks. It further explains how resource extraction produces environmental damage that disproportionately affects certain communities and becomes normalized within everyday life.

title: What drives continuous use of AI-generated music? Insights from a hybrid SEM–ANN approach
abstract: AI-generated music is lowering barriers to creation and reshaping music production. As AI music-generation platforms become increasingly capable and human-like, understanding the factors associated with sustained user engagement is increasingly important. Anthropomorphic characteristics may evoke admiration and wonder but may also evoke threat and unease. Integrating the stimulus–organism–response framework with cognitive appraisal theory, this study examines the relationships between anthropomorphic characteristics and continuous use intention through positive and threatened awe and assesses whether these relationships vary according to AI literacy. Survey data from 435 users in China were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling and PROCESS, complemented by artificial neural networks. All 11 hypotheses were supported. Anthropomorphic characteristics were positively associated with positive awe and negatively associated with threatened awe. Positive awe was positively associated with continuous use intention, whereas threatened awe was negatively associated with it. AI literacy strengthened the positive relationship between anthropomorphic characteristics and positive awe and attenuated the negative relationship between anthropomorphic characteristics and threatened awe. The moderated mediation indices were also statistically significant. The structural model explained 44.8% of the variance in continuous use intention, while ANN analysis assigned the highest normalised importance to threatened awe in predicting continuous use intention, followed by positive awe and anthropomorphic characteristics. These findings suggest that anthropomorphic characteristics are related to continued engagement through contrasting emotional pathways and that AI literacy conditions how users appraise AI music-generation platforms.

title: Reconstructing the tourist gaze in heritage landscapes: evidence from online reviews of Jiangnan classical gardens
abstract: This study examines how the textual tourist gaze is expressed in online reviews of Jiangnan classical gardens through ABSA-inspired dominant-aspect classification and review-level sentiment analysis of 30,478 reviews from 28 sites. We develop an eight-dimensional Landscape Aesthetic Attribute Taxonomy (LAAT), grounded in classical Chinese garden theory, particularly Yuanye, and Attention Restoration Theory. One fine-tuned MacBERT classifier assigns each review to its dominant LAAT dimension, while a second, independently fine-tuned model identifies overall sentiment polarity. The findings reveal a highly uneven distribution of dominant themes in the review corpus, providing a textual indication of how tourist attention is selectively represented in online reviews, with Atmosphere & Conception accounting for 33.0% of all reviews. Sentiment also varies significantly across dimensions. Core esthetic dimensions, including Architecture & Construction and Rockery & Waterscape, maintain positive-sentiment rates above 88%, whereas Service & Facility records a negative rate of 36.0%. An adapted Importance-Performance Analysis heuristically suggests that Service & Facility may warrant priority attention in future improvement efforts. Hierarchical clustering further grouped the gardens into four clusters based on their dimension-specific sentiment profiles. Theoretically, the study conceptualizes the textual gaze as the selective, evaluative, and culturally mediated act of writing about a landscape and shows how review text can provide an empirical articulation of the tourist gaze. We further conceptualize the textual gaze as the outcome of a five-stage textualization process and organize the LAAT as a two-level hierarchy, enabling analysis at both fine-grained and broader categorical levels.

title: Centralized money, fragmented labor: wage bargaining and asymmetric adjustment in EMU
abstract: Abstract This paper develops an analytical framework for analyzing how the interaction between the centralized monetary authority of the European Monetary Union (EMU) and nationally diverse wage bargaining institutions shapes asymmetric macroeconomic adjustment across member states. We draw on the literature of central bank credibility, collective bargaining, and EMU governance, and we argue that the interaction between a common monetary regime and heterogeneous labor-market institutions reallocates adjustment pressures toward labor markets. This, in turn, generates different employment and reform trajectories. A comparative overview of selected EMU member states provides the institutional context within which our framework highlights how bargaining coordination, employer organization, economic openness, and economic size shape the transmission of monetary policy. The paper also discusses the limitations of the monetary credibility and wage bargaining framework in light of recent inflationary dynamics, distributive conflict, and structural change. By integrating this literature, the paper conceptualizes wage bargaining as a key transmission channel through which centralized monetary policy generates heterogeneous adjustment outcomes across the euro area.

title: Bridging sustainability and health: the role of food literacy in shaping eating practices
abstract: The growing global population, environmental challenges, and unsustainable consumption habits have heightened the importance of sustainable food consumption. While sustainable food literacy (SFL) is recognized for fostering healthy eating and ecological awareness, holistic and empirically robust studies on its multifaceted impact remain limited. This study aims to examine the effect of sustainable food literacy on individuals’ sustainable and healthy eating behaviors. A quantitative research method was employed, and data were collected from 204 participants via an online survey. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) implemented in SmartPLS 4. Sustainable food literacy was operationalized as a second-order construct based on the Turkish adaptation of Teng and Chih’s (2022) instrument, in which the knowledge domain is represented by conceptual and practical knowledge components. The findings indicate that sustainable food literacy has a significant positive impact on sustainable and healthy eating behavior. Furthermore, sustainable food literacy was found to significantly influence behavioral subdimensions, including healthy and balanced eating, reading food quality labels, choosing local foods, preferring low-fat foods, and expressing concern for animal welfare. These results offer actionable insights for targeted policy and educational interventions, moving beyond general recommendations to address specific behavioral facets that promote responsible food consumption and public health. Beyond food and health research, this study contributes to the broader behavioral change literature by demonstrating that literacy functions as a proximal determinant, translating sustainability-related knowledge and attitudes into everyday consumption behavior. By linking individual food literacy to sustainable and healthy eating practices, this study also informs systems-oriented perspectives on sustainability transitions, where aggregate consumer behavior plays a critical role in shaping food systems.

title: The novel therapeutic role of self-compassion and self-coldness in bullying perpetration: cultural impact on the mediating role of compassion for others
abstract: Abstract Current bullying prevention efforts primarily focus on victims, lacking a more effective upstream approach targeting perpetrators. This study evaluated the potential culturally specific associations of self-compassion and self-coldness with traditional and cyberbullying perpetration, focusing on whether these associations showed indirect effects via compassion for others and coldness for others. In a cross-sectional design, 2313 adolescents (aged 13–17) from Hong Kong ( n = 852) and the United States ( n = 1461) self-reported levels of self-compassion, self-coldness, bullying behaviors, compassion for others, and coldness for others. Moderated mediation analyses assessed whether compassion/coldness for others mediated the associations between self-compassion, self-coldness and bullying perpetration, with culture as a moderator. The indirect effects via compassion for others and coldness for others were significant in the Hong Kong sample but not in the United States sample, indicating moderated mediation by culture. Follow-up path comparisons suggested that cross-culture differences were primarily attributable to the self-to-mediator links, which were significant in Hong Kong but near-zero in the United States, whereas the mediator-to-outcome links were robust and comparable across cultures. This study leads to a significant advancement in understanding the potential of fostering self-compassion and mitigating self-coldness in bullying prevention. Moreover, these findings highlight culturally contingent mechanisms linking self-compassion/self-coldness to bullying perpetration via other-oriented responding, underscoring the potential value of culturally sensitive prevention efforts.

title: Gamification in digital education: engagement, retention, and equity assessing the transformative potential of game-based learning in virtual classrooms
abstract: The integration of gamification in digital education has attracted significant attention as a strategy to enhance student engagement and learning outcomes. However, empirical evidence concerning its effects on retention and educational equity in real-world classroom settings remains limited. This study examines whether a gamified learning environment can improve engagement, retention-related outcomes, and academic performance compared with a non-gamified digital platform, and explores differences across diverse learner profiles. A total of 100 secondary school students were divided into a gamified group ( n = 50) and a non-gamified group ( n = 50) and observed over an eight-week instructional period. The gamified system incorporated progression tracking, adaptive challenges, real-time feedback, and digital rewards within an existing learning management system. Engagement and retention-related outcomes were estimated using platform interaction logs and academic performance indicators. Results indicate that students in the gamified group showed higher engagement, including greater login frequency, task completion, and interaction levels. Improvements were also observed in selected retention-related measures, including assignment completion and participation consistency. The findings further suggest that adaptive challenges and feedback may provide responsive support for learners with lower initial performance or engagement. However, the effect of personalisation was not statistically isolated. Equity-related analyses indicated reduced disparities across selected socio-economic and demographic groups. Overall, it is concluded that well-designed gamification can strengthen student engagement and persistence while potentially contributing to more inclusive and responsive digital learning environments. These findings provide empirical evidence that gamification can support engagement and retention-related outcomes in secondary education, while highlighting the need for larger, multi-school, and longitudinal studies to establish the sustainability of these effects and assess implications for educational equity.

title: Decoding technology transition process through consumer behavior: experience from China’s electric vehicle evolution
abstract: The competition between electric vehicles (EVs) and internal combustion engine vehicles is fundamentally shaped by how heterogeneous consumers respond to technological and market change. This study develops a decision-based framework that links micro-level adoption behavior with macro-level fleet dynamics. Using China as the core case, we identify three consumer segments: new, replacement, and renewal buyers, and show that they react differently to purchase cost, usability, and charging conditions. Embedding these segments in a dynamic simulation suggests a conditional phased transition under the baseline scenario: EV stock may overtake ICEVs around 2030, and the expansion of the secondhand EV market after 2035 could reshape buyer composition and strengthen the role of replacement demand. A cross-national comparison of 51 countries further shows that economic development stages and institutional capacity mediate how these behavioral logics translate into market outcomes, from infrastructure and affordability constraints in emerging EV markets to norm-driven, autonomous adoption in advanced EV markets. The findings highlight that EV transitions are driven by the interaction between consumer heterogeneity and market development, providing a behavioral basis for stage-specific policies and infrastructure strategies worldwide.

title: From “curse” to “gospel”: how can industrial relocation lead cities to cross the resource dependence gap
abstract: Industrial relocation offers a novel solution to help mitigate the “resource curse” by reducing dependence on natural resources and fostering diversified economic systems, thereby optimizing the industrial structure. This paper explores the mechanism and economic consequences of industrial relocation’s dependence on the host country’s resources, focusing on the National Industrial Relocation Demonstration Zones (NIRDZ). Theoretical analysis using urban panel statistics from 2006 to 2022 investigates the relationship between industrial relocation and the host’s resource dependence through a multi-period Difference-in-Differences. The heterogeneity of the policy effect is analyzed from a three-dimensional urban attribute perspective encompassing “location-feature-scale.” The results indicate that: (1) Industrial relocation can significantly restrain resource dependence and thereby help alleviate the “resource curse,” a conclusion that remains valid following multiple robustness tests. (2) Industrial relocation mainly inhibits urban resource dependence by reducing energy consumption, increasing the level of foreign investment, and enhancing technological innovation. (3) Heterogeneity analysis demonstrates that the NIRDZ policy exerts a more pronounced inhibitory effect on resource dependence in central cities, non-provincial-capital cities, and cities with smaller populations. Unlike the cracking strategy proposed by most previous studies on resource management, this paper reveals that central cities can provide a viable pathway to alleviating the “resource curse” by developing industries in the eastern region. This not only establishes a foundation for decision-making regarding the green transformation and sustainable development of resource-rich cities but also contributes to new empirical evidence to the “resource curse” governance literature.

title: Exploring emotional responses and learning effectiveness in gamified educational settings: insights from digital escape rooms
abstract: This study investigates the emotional dynamics experienced by students in digital escape rooms as a gamified learning tool. The research addresses three main questions: how digital escape rooms (DERs) overcome the limitations of physical escape rooms, the manifestation and interaction of positive and negative emotions during problem-solving, and the impact of these emotional interactions on learning English. A total of 233 university students participated. The study used an online escape room and a revised version of the Achievement Emotions Questionnaire to assess emotions, including enjoyment, hope, pride, anger, anxiety, shame, hopelessness, and boredom. Findings revealed that students experienced mixed emotions, with positive emotions coexisting with negative ones. Inter-emotional correlations and participants’ open-ended responses indicated that these emotional experiences were associated with perceived engagement and persistence, whereas individual emotions were not significantly associated with immediate performance gains. The findings further suggest that hope may be an important emotion to consider when designing supportive gamified learning experiences. Overall, this research contributes to the understanding of emotional dynamics in digital escape-room learning while avoiding causal claims that are not supported by the study design.

title: ‘Basic’ democracy, ‘platinum pro’ democracy and the ‘features nobody wants to build’: a critical interpretive review of the Civic Tech space
abstract: Abstract Information Systems (IS) designed to support formal participatory practices, commonly termed Civic Technologies, are proliferating. This expansion is accompanied by the encoding of new material constitutions of democracy through technical features and the political economies shaping their development, maintenance, and distribution. This article presents a Critical Interpretive Review of the Civic Tech landscape. By systematising the functionalities offered by Civic Tech ISs and mapping their distribution across the participatory cycle, we contend that perceived saturation in the field stems from a concentration of tools addressing similar practitioner needs. Most Civic Tech ISs operate as credentialed forums, offering basic features such as commenting, voting, and polling. Conversely, more politically consequential phases, such as the reflective design of methods and the translation of outputs into institutional systems, remain markedly underserved. These neglected features expose the participatory imaginaries rendered invisible within the field. We also identify a bifurcation in political economies: some initiatives adopt commons-based models, offering open-source tools and relying on consultancy or grants; others pursue commercial models with tiered pricing and premium services. The latter introduces tensions between democratic rhetoric and its commodification. We advocate for a more situated understanding of Civic Tech and urge critical, constructive engagement from STS.

title: Longitudinal associations between neighborhood built environment and self-rated health accounting for social capital
abstract: With the advancement of the “Healthy China 2030 Initiative”, increasing attention has been paid to health outcomes in China amid rapid urbanization and population ageing. Among various factors, Built Environment (BE) and Social Capital (SC) play important roles in shaping individuals’ Self-Rated Health (SRH). However, prior studies mainly relied on cross-sectional design, with limited attention to age and urban-rural differences in these associations. We aimed to examine the longitudinal associations between BE and SRH accounting for SC, and to investigate heterogeneity in the associations by age and urbanicity. Data came from the 2010 and 2014 waves of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), including 15,570 respondents in the final analytical sample. Participants reported better SRH in neighborhoods characterized by more appealing environment, stronger social relationships and higher levels of social trust. Further, we observed distinct differences among age groups: Enhanced neighborhood aesthetics was more strongly related to better SRH for those aged 45 and above. Individuals under 60 with higher social trust reported better SRH. In addition, enhanced neighborhood aesthetics had a stronger association with improved SRH in urban areas, whereas strengthening social relationships and social trust played a more significant role in shaping positive SRH among rural residents. Overall, our findings suggest that improving neighborhood aesthetics and enhancing social relationships and social trust may contribute to better self-rated health. Further, our findings could inform policymakers that intervention strategies need to be tailored to meet the specific needs of different age groups and those across urban and rural areas.

title: Who’s engaging in political discussions on social media? Comparing the effects of self-monitoring and moral certainty
abstract: This study explores the role certain personality traits, specifically self-monitoring and moral certainty, play in one’s propensity to post about politics online, including engaging in potentially contentious exchanges. Using data from the ANES 2020 Exploratory Testing Survey, I examine the effects of self-monitoring and moral certainty on posting political comments online and using social media to shame another user for posting something offensive. Results show that high self-monitoring scores are correlated with increased probability of both posting political comments and calling out another user. However, moral certainty scores only produce significant results in the case of shaming someone on social media for offensive comments. These results suggest the following: 1) high self-monitors engage in both types of behaviors on social media to reflect positively on other users who share their views, (2) those high in moral certainty are driven to post on social media to address a perceived moral offense.

title: Automated assessment and cross-system benchmarking of Chinese reading text difficulty via multi-model analysis
abstract: Abstract Text difficulty assessment is a significant task in natural language processing (NLP) and language education, providing an important basis for reading material selection and curriculum articulation. Using computational models as analytical tools, this study develops and evaluates a multidimensional automated framework for assessing the difficulty of Chinese reading texts in the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP), with the aim of investigating the construct of reading text difficulty and its cross-system correspondences. We extracted 173 features across five linguistic dimensions (character, lexical, syntactic, discourse, and affective features) and compared machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and large language model (LLM) approaches in terms of predictive performance, interpretability, and applicability. The findings indicate that Chinese reading text difficulty within the IBDP context examined in this study is multidimensional and continuous, with partly overlapping boundaries between adjacent levels. Lexical and character features made the strongest contributions to level differentiation, while syntactic, discourse, and affective features provided complementary evidence. The three computational approaches offered complementary methodological evidence: raw-text BERT achieved the highest accuracy (91.18%), feature-based XGBoost combined relatively high accuracy (85.00%) with interpretability, and the LLM showed potential for preliminary screening in zero-shot settings. The selected model was then applied to HSK reading texts, and its predictions were triangulated with external expert judgments and linguistic-feature analysis. HSK Level 4 (L4) texts were generally below the IBDP Ab Initio range; HSK L5 formed a transitional range between Ab Initio and SL; and HSK L6 was closest to HL while retaining some overlap with SL. Together, these findings show that cross-system benchmarking can reveal not only approximate correspondences but also differences in difficulty ranges and proficiency-progression patterns across assessment systems. The framework thereby provides a transparent text-level basis for reading-material selection, curriculum articulation, and future cross-system benchmarking.

title: Diplomacy in the digital abyss: how populism and misinformation are reshaping statecraft
abstract: A profound paradox characterizes the contemporary international system; unprecedented digital connectivity coincides with a deepening crisis of trust, creating what this paper terms a “digital abyss” for traditional diplomacy. This paper examines how populist politics and disinformation use language through framing and delegitimization to challenge traditional diplomacy and principles of statecraft. This study adopts a Constructivist theoretical approach, arguing that these forces function as a form of epistemological warfare, completely undermining the institutional legitimacy and shared realities that underpin diplomatic interaction. Findings demonstrate a fundamental shift from confidential negotiation to contested reality, challenging the possibility of international cooperation, which evades and delegitimizes international institutions. This paper concludes by proposing pathways for institutional adaptation, including cognitive immunity. By laying out a roadmap for diplomatic innovation that utilizes the conceptual and technological information landscape of 21st-century statecraft, this study advances the domains of digital diplomacy and international relations.

title: Architectural characteristics and preservation status of traditional dwellings in Luoshan County, Henan
abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization has placed Chinese traditional dwellings at growing risk of loss. Luoshan County, a representative area of southern Henan culture, retains a substantial stock of such dwellings, partly because the northern foothills of the Dabie Mountains have offered geographical protection. However, most remain lack formal grading and are therefore highly vulnerable to natural decay and human disturbance. Using primary data from the Fourth National Census of Cultural Heritage, this study investigates 55 groups of traditional dwellings in Luoshan County. It examines their architectural characteristics at two scales, courtyard complexes and individual building units, and develops a hierarchical assessment of preservation status. Based on this assessment, the study proposes targeted conservation strategies linked to architectural grading. The study contributes a regionally grounded framework for understanding and managing vulnerable heritage in rapidly transforming rural China.

title: Environmental, social, and governance disclosure and stock valuation
