abstract: This paper examines the causal effect of ESG disclosure transparency on stock valuation of Chinese listed companies, distinguishing ESG disclosure from the ESG performance scores commonly used in prior studies. Exploiting the first-time release of Bloomberg’s ESG disclosure scores as an exogenous information shock, we employ a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) model on non-financial listed firms from 2009 to 2023. Our results show that ESG disclosure significantly improves stock valuation by reducing information asymmetry. To strengthen causal identification, we complement the estimates with the Callaway-Sant’Anna estimator and a stacked DID design, and the results are robust across these specifications. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the valuation effect is more pronounced for firms with greater ESG investor participation, analyst attention, less negative media coverage, tighter financing constraints, and executive financial expertise. ESG disclosure improves valuation by obtaining external support, easing financing costs, and alleviating agency problems.

title: Does AI literacy enhance employee work engagement by boosting work self-efficacy or reducing job burnout? A one-year longitudinal study
abstract: In the AI era, the importance of AI literacy has become increasingly prominent, particularly among employees. Although preliminary research suggests that AI use may enhance employee work engagement, the relationship between AI literacy and work engagement remains underexplored—especially its longitudinal effects and underlying mechanisms. We conducted a one-year longitudinal study consisting of three waves of surveys with a sample of 1,108 employees aged between 21 and 60 years. At Time 1 (T1, baseline), we measured demographic information, AI literacy, and work engagement; at Time 2 (T2, 6 months later), we assessed work self-efficacy and job burnout; and at Time 3 (T3, 1 year later), we re-evaluated work engagement. Results showed that, after controlling for gender, age, AI use intensity, and T1 work engagement, T1 AI literacy significantly and positively predicted T3 work engagement. When mediators were included, T1 AI literacy not only directly predicted T3 work engagement but also exerted indirect effects through three pathways: (1) the independent mediating effect of T2 work self-efficacy, (2) the independent mediating effect of T2 job burnout, and (3) the chain mediation of T2 work self-efficacy and T2 job burnout. These findings confirm the long-term predictive role of AI literacy on work engagement and clarify the complex mechanisms behind its sustained influence, offering practical insights for organizations and individuals to better leverage AI for career development.

title: Short version of the Odor Awareness Scale (OAS-6): Turkish validity and reliability study
abstract: Odor awareness is currently trending topic, and significant measurement tools have recently been developed in this field. The Odor Awareness Scale Short Form (OAS-6) is one of these assessment instruments. To promote research on olfaction in Türkiye, there is a need to adapt this scale into Turkish. Thus, we aimed to adapt the OAS-6 into Turkish and test its validity and reliability. This study was designed as cross-sectional study. Data were collected online using convenience sampling between 19 September and 31 October 2025. The adaptation process of OAS-6 involved content validity, exploratory (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), validity evidence, and test–retest with 2-week intervals analysis. These analyses were conducted using JASP and p value set at p < 0.05. All stages of the study adhered to the Helsinki Declaration. The study was completed with 450 participants (60% female). Ages ranged from 18 to 63 years (M = 26.2, SD = 11.4). EFA revealed a unidimensional structure explaining 47.1% of the total variance, while CFA confirmed an acceptable model fit (χ2/df = 1.56, RMSEA = 0.027, CFI = 0.975, TLI = 0.958, SRMR = 0.041). Additionally, the scale’s internal consistency proved to be good (McDonald’s ω = 0.811; Cronbach’s α = 0.807). This study suggests that the Turkish version of the OAS-6 has acceptable validity and reliability as a unidimensional instrument within the Turkish cultural context. The scale may be useful for research and clinical settings where subjective odor perception is relevant (e.g., psychology, neurology, psychiatry, otorhinolaryngology, public health). Beyond clinical applications, the scale offers potential for humanities and social sciences research, including studies on attention, emotion, social interaction, and cultural differences in sensory awareness. Its concise six-item format reduces respondent burden and administrative time, making it adaptable to various data collection modalities, including digital platforms. The Turkish OAS-6 is promising for use in future epidemiological and interdisciplinary studies, although further validation with diverse samples is encouraged.

title: How culture promotes the social integration of migrants
abstract: Rural-to-urban migration in China has intensified, highlighting the critical challenge of social integration, as migrants’ marginalization often leads to adverse socioeconomic outcomes. This study investigates how development and entertainment-type cultural consumption influence migrant social integration. By utilizing data from the 2011 China Migrants Dynamic Survey and employing instrumental variable approaches to address endogeneity, we found that development and entertainment-type cultural consumption significantly promote social integration. We identified three mechanisms affecting this result: development activities enhance social participation, entertainment activities increase happiness, and both types of cultural consumption enhance integration willingness. The heterogeneity analysis revealed that the effects of cultural consumption vary across migrant groups, highlighting the importance of tailored policies. Development-type consumption is more beneficial for migrants with larger families, and both types of consumption have stronger effects on older migrants. Migrants with higher education experience diminishing marginal returns from cultural consumption because they possess higher cultural capital. At the regional level, migrant discrimination does not significantly moderate these relationships, while the association between entertainment-type cultural consumption and integration is weaker in cities with greater migrant-origin diversity. This study contributes to the literature by examining the role of culture in promoting the social integration of migrants.

title: Does public transport fare discount policy affect travel choices of the elderly? An empirical study based on Chongqing, China
abstract: As population aging accelerates, public transport fare discounts have become a crucial tool for cities to address the mobility needs of the elderly. This study aims to optimize such policies by examining the psychological decision-making process of elderly bus users, using survey data from Chongqing, China, collected in 2022 ( N = 556) and validated with a second cross-sectional survey conducted in 2026 ( N = 174). It investigates how socioeconomic characteristics and subjective attitudes influence travel decisions under different discount scenarios. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) is applied to confirm the impact paths of elderly transit policy acceptance, bus travel dependency, and discount schemes on travel mode choice. In addition, Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) are employed to explore the non-linear interactions among individual attributes and subjective attitudes in the context of varying discount scenarios. The results reveal that higher discount rates significantly encourage elderly individuals to choose public transport. Bus travel dependency emerges as the most robust predictor of mode choice, validated across both survey waves. The older elderly (over 75 years) show higher sensitivity to discounts despite lower baseline travel willingness. Furthermore, discount policies have a stronger incentive effect on groups with non-rigid travel demands. The findings suggest that tailored discount strategies, combined with enhanced service quality and targeted policy promotion, can increase public transport use among the elderly. Such refinements are expected to improve social participation, enhance quality of life, and provide empirical guidance for optimizing elderly bus fare discount policies.

title: Does the rich man’s club employ social media to advance digital public diplomacy? Mapping the interactional network dynamics and influence hierarchies of OECD leaders’ cross-border communication on X
abstract: This study investigates how OECD leaders utilize X (formerly Twitter) for digital public diplomacy, treating leader-to-leader interactions as a site where symbolic power through platform-specific practices and diplomatic hierarchy are negotiated. Employing directed network analysis, RoBERTa-based sentiment analysis, and TF-IDF profiling across 21,716 tweets from 38 OECD leaders during the 2023–2024 OECD Ministerial Council Meeting cycle, the study develops a tripartite typology of diplomatic engagement strategies—Proactive (PDES), Reserved (RDES), and Strategic (SDES)—operationalized through engagement rate, breadth, focus ratio, and mentions per diplomatic post. Findings indicate hierarchically patterned, uneven engagement despite broad platform connectivity. Network centrality correlates with crisis salience and alliance structures, with Zelenskyy and #Ukraine being the most mentioned figure and hashtag. Sentiment analysis indicates predominantly positive and neutral tones (78.82% combined), suggesting X primarily facilitates coalition maintenance and reputational governance rather than confrontation, with neutrality functioning as a strategic diplomatic stance rather than an absence of meaning. Integrating Castells’ network power theory, Bourdieu’s symbolic capital and framing-based meaning construction, the study conceptualizes digital diplomacy as a field of networked recognition where network position, framing capacity, and engagement strategy collectively produce visibility, making hierarchy more observable yet contingent on private platform infrastructures. Diplomatic recognition thus operates as the mechanism through which network position and symbolic capital become mutually constitutive.

title: I deserve rewards! Exploring the effect of employees’ reputation for effective AI usage on turnover intention
abstract: Although existing research generally acknowledges the positive effects of general reputation, this study argues that prior research has overstated the benefits of reputation while neglecting its potential drawbacks. We introduce a domain-specific reputation—employees’ reputation for effective AI usage, referring to positive evaluations of an individual’s ability to effectively use AI by others. Based on the social comparison theory, this research examines the negative effects of employees’ reputation for effective AI usage. The findings from both an experiment and a three-wave study reveal that employees’ reputation for effective AI usage is positively associated with turnover intention through psychological entitlement. Moreover, we identify rewards for effective AI usage as an essential boundary condition. Specifically, the positive relationship between employees’ reputation for effective AI usage and psychological entitlement and the indirect impact of employees’ reputation for effective AI usage on turnover intention through psychological entitlement are weaker when rewards for effective AI usage are high. The study also explores theoretical and practical implications, as well as outlines future research directions.

title: Pathways and challenges of sport for social integration of refugees: a narrative review
abstract: Sport is a double-edged sword for the social integration of refugees, with the potential to both facilitate and hinder this process. The findings of this study are as follows: First, sport may act as an intercultural medium, facilitating non-verbal coordination, shared ritual and trust-building, and creating “third spaces” for identity reconstruction. Second, sport may promote physiological-psychological synergy, reducing trauma symptoms and supporting emotional regulation. Third, sport can function as a temporary surrogate home that supports wellbeing. On this basis, we further explore three challenges of sport for refugees’ social integration: “tension of cross-cultural media practice”, “shortcomings of concrete effect evaluation”, and “creation of relational silos”. Accordingly, we identify key considerations for future research, to provide theoretical and practical support for subsequent studies on sport’s role in promoting refugees’ social integration.

title: A hybrid human-AI collaborative workflow for digital heritage interpretation: a case study on the “Dongdong Push” Nuo mask
abstract: Abstract With the development of generative artificial intelligence (AIGC), its application in human–AI collaborative design has attracted increasing attention. However, in the process of intangible cultural heritage (ICH) digital revitalisation and cultural product design, systematic research on balancing traditional cultural characteristics with contemporary market aesthetics while avoiding AI-generated cultural bias and visual homogenisation remains limited. Taking the “Dongdong Push” Nuo mask of the Dong ethnic group in China as a case study, this paper proposes an AIGC-assisted ICH IP design workflow based on human–AI collaboration. By integrating the Double Diamond design model, large language models, and AI image-generation tools, the study reconstructs the traditional ICH IP design process. Consumer preference analysis and cultural feature extraction are employed to establish semantic constraints for AI generation, while an AHP-FCE-based multi-stakeholder evaluation framework is constructed to assess design effectiveness through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews. The results indicate that the proposed workflow supports efficient trend extraction, style exploration, and visual ideation while achieving overall performance comparable to traditional manual design. The quantitative comparison revealed only small differences across evaluation dimensions, while the qualitative findings highlighted potential benefits of AIGC in visual exploration and iterative ideation. At the same time, the application of AIGC remains subject to challenges such as visual homogenization, AI hallucinations, and aesthetic inertia. These findings suggest that the value of AIGC in ICH design lies not in replacing human designers, but in supporting and expanding their cognitive and creative exploration through human–AI collaboration.

title: Probing language teacher creativity and its interplay with emotions in lesson study projects
abstract: This study examines how language teacher creativity emerges and interacts with emotions in university–school collaborative lesson study (LS) projects in China. Drawing on sociocultural theory, it conceptualizes creativity as a socially mediated and emotionally infused learning process. Using a qualitative design, it collected multiple sources of data from LS cycles through interviews, reflections, collective discussions, teaching documents, and classroom observations. The thematic analysis revealed four interconnected manifestations of language teacher creativity and a fifth theme illustrating the dual role of emotions in enabling and constraining creative practice. Findings show that creativity is negotiated between structure and freedom, emotionally regulated through both integral and context-contingent emotions, and mediated by language content as a key resource for pedagogical innovation. The study reconceptualizes emotions beyond a positive–negative dichotomy and highlights the pedagogical role of language content. It suggests that teacher educators (TEs) balance structure and autonomy, attend to power dynamics, and harness emotions constructively to foster teacher creativity.

title: Does low-carbon transition policy improve water–energy–land–food nexus performance considering ESG practice?
abstract: As the global climate crisis intensifies, the interplay between low-carbon transition policies and the sustainable management of critical resources has gained increasing scholarly and policy interest. This study investigates whether the implementation of low-carbon transition policies improves the performance of the water–energy–land–food (WELF) nexus in the context of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices in China. Drawing on provincial panel data from 2007 to 2023, we employ fixed effects models, heterogeneity tests, mediation effect analysis, and a PSM–DID approach to evaluate the net impact and underlying mechanisms. The results reveal that low-carbon policies significantly enhance the coupling and coordination degree of the WELF nexus, particularly in regions with stronger ESG governance and higher environmental regulation intensity. By 2023, the regional average coupling degree had increased by 2.021% compared to 2007. During the 17-year period, the mean coupling degree across all provinces and municipalities was 0.947. Mechanism analysis indicates that improvements in energy efficiency, industrial upgrading, and technological innovation are key pathways through which low-carbon policies strengthen nexus performance while aligning with ESG objectives. However, the effects vary by regional economic development level, population size, regulatory context, and market openness. These findings underscore the importance of integrating ESG principles into policy design to maximize synergies between decarbonization and holistic resource management. The study provides empirical evidence to support more targeted and adaptive low-carbon and ESG governance strategies that foster coordinated progress towards sustainability and climate goals.

title: Division and interconnection between spirit and the world: Karoline von Günderrode’s reception of Soliloquies
abstract: This paper explores philosopher and writer Karoline von Günderrode’s reception of Soliloquies . Günderrode receives certain aspects of Schleiermacher’s thought. However, she distances herself from the central thesis of the soliloquy that she comments upon (“Die Reflexion”), in which Schleiermacher maintains that the spirit is the foundation of everything, including the external or corporeal. Günderrode understands spirit and world to be in a polar relationship, where the two terms are irreducible and inseparable. Both emerge from a “primordial foundation” or “Urgrund,” which is neither purely spiritual nor purely corporeal. Günderrode’s position depends on an argument aimed at solving a problem to which the first edition of Soliloquies has no answer, namely the difficulty of explaining a totality that is mysterious and beyond determination, on which the interior and exterior depend, starting from what is only one of its parts: the interior or spirit.

title: Local creative culture environment and corporate digital transformation: evidence from cultural and creative industry parks in China
abstract: Based on a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we investigate the influence of the local creative culture environment on corporate digital transformation (DT). The results show that a vibrant creative culture environment is positively related to firms’ DT, primarily through three channels: higher R&D investments, lower financing constraints and higher regional digital talent agglomeration. Moreover, heterogeneity analyses reveal that this effect is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, in regions with weaker Confucian cultural traditions, and in firms with a higher proportion of female executives. We enhance the literature on the drivers of DT from the perspective of the local creative culture environment. The findings also provide policy implications for promoting the synergies between cultural development and the digital economy.

title: Promoting urban-rural modernization from the perspective of the digital economy
abstract: In an era defined by the digital divide, the digital economy has emerged as a pivotal force driving urban-rural modernization. This study analyzes China’s digital economy from 2011 to 2023, evaluating its influence on equitable regional development across 30 provinces, municipalities, and autonomous regions. We develop an index system to assess the modernization of urban and rural areas, quantify their developmental levels, and elucidate the mechanisms through which the digital economy drives urban-rural modernization. A novel digital economy index is constructed via the entropy weight method, and Moran’s I statistic is employed to detect spatial clustering. To address endogeneity, we apply a two-stage least squares (2SLS) model. While the Spatial Durbin Model captures spatial spillover effects, the results reveal pronounced regional disparities and spatial interdependencies. Digital economic growth generates regional spillovers, promoting modernization, yet simultaneously induces adverse local disruptions—unveiling a critical paradox between diffusion and disruption. Robustness tests substantiate our findings, reinforcing the study’s validity and reliability. Consequently, policy interventions should strategically harness digital dividends while mitigating institutional and distributive challenges. This research contributes novel empirical insights into spatial dynamics within digital transformations, guiding policymakers in economies experiencing similar digital evolution.

title: Rethinking green transport infrastructure: indirect emissions, mediated impacts, and decarbonization pathways in South Korea
abstract: This study examines the relationship between green transport infrastructure and indirect greenhouse gas emissions, focusing on emissions that arise not from vehicle operations themselves but from energy use, thermal demand, and waste generation associated with infrastructure maintenance and service provision. In doing so, it revisits the conventional assumption that electric rail systems are environmentally neutral and highlights the need for a broader accounting framework for transport-related emissions. The study distinguishes between unmediated infrastructure-related associations and mediated associations operating through socio-structural change. To examine these relationships, the study combines a spatio-temporal Durbin model with mediation analysis using 12 years of panel data from 227 Korean cities and counties. The results suggest that expressways are associated with higher indirect GHG emissions mainly through mediated pathways, particularly those related to population concentration and traffic volume, while their unmediated association is not statistically significant. By contrast, urban and metropolitan railways are associated with lower indirect emissions, with the clearest lower-emission association observed for urban railway. Intercity railway does not show a broad-based significant association, suggesting that its environmental relevance may be more selective and context-dependent. These findings indicate that “green” transport infrastructure should not be evaluated through a single universal pathway. Rather, transport-related carbon evaluation should consider both infrastructure type and the socio-economic pathways associated with it. From a policy perspective, road-related investment may need to be assessed together with land-use management, travel-demand management, and energy-efficiency considerations, while rail-based systems may be more consistently linked to lower-emission outcomes when combined with station-area planning and commercial structures that support concentrated and less carbon-intensive urban activity.

title: Staged digital transformation and firms’ total factor productivity: evidence from Chinese cultural firms
abstract: This study explores the effects of digital transformation (DT) on firms’ total factor productivity (TFP) across the digital technology application (DTA) stage and digital business model innovation (DBMI) stage. Using a sample of 245 Chinese listed cultural firms from 2011 to 2022, we examine how DT impacts TFP differently across these stages. The results show that DT significantly enhances firms’ TFP in both the DTA and DBMI stages. However, productivity gains materialize only after firms reach the transformation threshold in both stages. Moreover, the threshold for the DTA stage is higher than that for the DBMI stage. In the DTA stage, DT improves firms’ TFP by enhancing their core production capabilities and specialization. In the DBMI stage, DT affects firms’ TFP through improved operational efficiency and financial efficiency. Furthermore, during the DTA stage, larger firms experience stronger TFP gains, while smaller firms benefit more in the DBMI stage. In the DTA stage, the positive impact of DT on TFP is similar for firms with and without government subsidies. In the DBMI stage, however, the impact of DT is more pronounced for firms without subsidies. Across both stages, firms in regions with a better digital financial environment achieve greater productivity gains from DT.

title: Artificial intelligence use, creative thinking disposition, and metacognitive awareness among EFL learners: a structural equation modelling approach
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in English as a foreign language (EFL) learning, yet its cognitive implications depend on how learners engage with it rather than on its use alone. This study examined the structural relationships among differentiated patterns of AI use, creative thinking disposition, and metacognitive awareness among undergraduate EFL learners. Using a quantitative cross-sectional correlational design, data were collected from 713 learners and analysed through structural equation modelling. AI use was conceptualised as cognitive-support use, creative-extension use, reproductive or substitutive use, and ethical and critical awareness. The findings indicate that the use of cognitive-support and creative-extension AI is positively associated with both creative thinking disposition and metacognitive awareness. In contrast, reproductive or substitutive use is negatively associated with these outcomes. Creative thinking disposition demonstrates a strong positive relationship with metacognitive awareness and mediates the effects of constructive AI use on regulatory awareness. Ethical and critical engagement with AI moderates these relationships, strengthening the positive associations between constructive AI use and both creative and metacognitive outcomes. The results clarify that the cognitive value of AI in EFL learning is shaped by learner agency, reflective judgement, and responsibility for meaning-making. The study advances a cognitively grounded account of AI-mediated EFL learning and provides empirical support for differentiating AI engagement patterns in both research and instructional design.

title: Growing a new profession: evaluating occupational therapy education in Mongolia
abstract: Mongolia’s healthcare system is experiencing growing demand for rehabilitation services, yet occupational therapy (OT) education programs in the country have rarely been formally evaluated. The undergraduate OT program at the Mongolian National University of Medical Sciences (MNUMS), launched in 2014 in accordance with World Federation of Occupational Therapists guidelines, is Mongolia’s only such program. Although the program has undergone minor revisions over time, no comprehensive evaluation has yet been conducted. This study evaluated the program using the Context, Input, Process, and Product (CIPP) framework to identify strengths and areas for improvement in relation to national health and social care priorities. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. In phase one, 82 stakeholders: students, alumni, faculty, and program administrators completed a cross-sectional survey analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests, and one-way analysis of variance. Phase Two involved semi-structured interviews with 28 purposively selected participants, analyzed thematically using both inductive and deductive approaches. Survey findings showed higher ratings for the context and product domains ( M ≈ 4.0–4.3), lower ratings for input ( M ≈ 2.5), and moderate ratings for process ( M = 3.41). Statistically significant differences in perceptions were found across stakeholder groups, particularly regarding resources and practical training. Four qualitative themes emerged: the growing need for OT in Mongolia, limited public and institutional awareness of the profession, insufficient policy and financial support, and the need to strengthen program organization and teaching capacity. Overall, the findings indicate that although the program was generally perceived as valuable and socially relevant by participants, ongoing limitations in resources, infrastructure, and practical training continue to affect its quality. This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of OT education in Mongolia and offers practical implications for curriculum development, faculty support, and institutional commitment, with lessons applicable to similar programs in low-resource or transitional contexts.

title: The effectiveness of block-based programming applications in secondary school: meta-thematic analysis complemented with qualitative research
abstract: Programming is becoming increasingly important today and is considered one of the advanced skills that individuals should possess in the 21st century. However, since individuals often struggle when learning programming, block-based programming (BBP) applications have begun to be used to make coding easier to learn. In this study, the effect of BBP applications at the middle school level was investigated using meta-thematic analysis supported by qualitative research. The study consists of two stages. In the first stage of the research, studies were identified through document analysis within the scope of meta-thematic analysis. Two different researchers conducted content analysis on the identified studies to identify themes and codes. A total of 121 codes were identified from 10 studies, and 5 themes were created based on these codes. The study was conducted using an interdisciplinary approach within the scope of the experimental process. Due to the suitability of coding applications for science education and the fact that one of the researchers is a science teacher, the study continued with a 4-week BBP application with 6th-grade students taking science, information technology and software courses. At the end of the process, a semi-structured interview form was administered to the students, and codes were obtained from the participants’ responses through content analysis. The results of the study showed that BBP applications contributed to students’ affective and academic characteristics, 21st-century skills, personal development, and digital literacy. Therefore, this study not only synthesises the effects of BBP but also presents experimental evidence linking programming education to digital competencies and personal development, offering a rarely explored integrative approach to the literature.

title: Frontline advancement and enemy attrition in World War II: complementary outcome measures of combat effectiveness
abstract: Quantitative research on combat effectiveness often relies on observable battlefield outcomes because many underlying capabilities--training, command quality, logistics, morale, doctrine, and technology--are difficult to measure directly and comparably. Two outcome-based families are especially common. Loss-exchange-ratio (LER) indicators summarize relative attrition exchange, whereas territorial indicators summarize changes in spatial control. This article compares these two intermediate outcome dimensions using an original dataset of 153 World War II engagements. The analysis treats LER and the two-dimensional frontline advancement rate (TFR) as complementary rather than substitutable measures: LER captures the attrition-cost dimension of battlefield performance, while TFR captures the territorial-control dimension. The empirical design is descriptive and measurement-oriented. It reports rank correlations with bootstrap confidence intervals, nonparametric context tests, multivariate models that distinguish signed territorial performance from territorial-change intensity, and measurement-error sensitivity checks for map-derived TFR values. The evidence shows that attrition and territorial outcomes are empirically related but not interchangeable. Directional attrition advantage is positively associated with signed territorial performance in the complete-case sample, whereas the relationship between attrition imbalance and absolute territorial-change intensity is weaker and more specification-dependent. Contextual variables such as war potential, force balance, weapons support, and operational environment also shape territorial outcomes. The article, therefore, argues for a measurement-matching principle: researchers should select LER, TFR, or both according to the outcome dimension implied by their theory, and should avoid treating casualty exchange as a universal proxy for operational success. The scope of the evidence is World War II conventional territorial combat; the findings should not be generalized without qualification to counterinsurgency, hybrid warfare, air-only or naval-only operations, or conflicts without identifiable territorial-control boundaries.

title: Barriers to women’s participation in STEM education: a regional study of southern Punjab, Pakistan
abstract: Despite growing global attention to gender equality in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), women in developing countries remain significantly underrepresented. In Pakistan, this disparity persists even among academically capable students. While existing studies have examined why some women pursue STEM, little is known about why most do not. This study investigates the psychological, social, and institutional factors that discourage women from selecting STEM majors. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 920 female students at the intermediate level from four tehsils in Multan District, southern Punjab, Pakistan. Using a multi-stage cluster sampling approach, participants completed a structured questionnaire that measured self-confidence in STEM abilities, teacher support, access to career counseling, exposure to female role models, perceived math difficulty, cultural restrictions on coeducation, and work-lif balance preferences. Data were analyzed using chi-square tests, correlation analysis, and binary logistic regression with diagnostic tests confirming model adequacy (Pseudo R² = 0.26, AUC = 0.818).Findings indicate that self-confidence, teacher support, career counseling access, and female role-model exposure significantly increase the likelihood of intending to choose a STEM major, whereas perceived math difficulty, cultural restrictions on coeducation, and work-life balance preferences significantly reduce it. The model correctly classified 85% of cases, showing strong predictive validity. These results highlight that women’s avoidance of STEM is shaped less by ability and more by psychological barriers, institutional conditions, and socio-cultural expectations that elevate the perceived cost of STEM participation.Women’s decisions not to pursue STEM majors are primarily influenced by low self-efficacy, gendered socialization, and cultural restrictions on coeducation, alongside broader environmental constraints rather than academic incompetence. Addressing these barriers requires multi-level interventions, including gender-sensitive pedagogy, co-education institutions, mentorship programs, and family awareness campaigns. Empowering women and reforming restrictive norms are crucial to achieving gender equity in STEM and sustainable development.

title: The dual mediation of flow experience and learning effectiveness: unraveling the formation mechanism of continuous intention to use online learning platforms
abstract: The swift progress and broad application of information and communication technologies (ICTs) have significantly advanced their integration into the educational sector. This research aims to address the impacts of flow antecedents, including online learning self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation for online learning, on flow experience. Furthermore, it aims to assess interactivity, flow, and course content as predictors of online learning effectiveness. It also investigates the effects of flow and learning effectiveness on the intention to continue using online learning platforms. This study collected data from 224 online learners of English learning platforms in Taiwan using an online survey. According to the findings, flow was positively and significantly impacted by online learning self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation for online learning. Furthermore, interactivity, course content, and flow were positively associated with educational effectiveness. Lastly, both flow and learning effectiveness were found to be positively and significantly associated with continuance intention. Examination of the dual mediating mechanism revealed significant indirect pathways whereby intrinsic motivation for online learning and online learning self-efficacy exert substantial influence on continuance intention through the mediating role of flow experience. Conversely, the hypothesized indirect effects of interactivity and course content on continuance intention, mediated by learning effectiveness, failed to reach statistical significance. These findings highlight the critical importance of cultivating flow states in online language-learning environments, as the psychological immersion experienced during learning activities is a more powerful determinant of continued platform use than the actual learning outcomes.

title: A corpus-based analysis of modality in legislative texts: a case study
abstract: This article investigates the use of modality in legislative discourse through a corpus-based analysis of the Malaysian Companies Act 2016. The Act, which received Royal Assent on 31 August 2016, was pre-processed by removing structural headings, resulting in a corpus of approximately 142,000 words organized into numerous clauses. Adopting a corpus-based quantitative approach, the study employs UAM Corpus Tool version 6.2 as an automated tool to identify and annotate modality features in the text. The findings indicate that verbal modality is overwhelmingly prevalent in the Act, while non-verbal modality is virtually negligible. Within the verbal domain, modal auxiliaries—particularly shall and may —are the primary devices for expressing obligation and permission, reflecting the legal text’s strong orientation toward deontic modality. Shall functions as the principal marker of mandatory obligations, whereas may encodes permission and choice, thus mediating between coercive force and regulatory flexibility. Other auxiliaries ( would, will, should ) and semi-modals (e.g. need not ) occur only sporadically, mainly to signal the absence of obligation. Lexical items such as required, require, requiring, requires , and necessary further dominate the expression of deontic meaning, reinforcing the obligation-centred character of the discourse. In contrast, adjectives such as likely and possible contribute only marginally to epistemic modality, and able and unable express dynamic modality in a similarly limited manner. Overall, the study elucidates key characteristics of modality in legislative texts and points to the value of extending such analyses to larger corpora to deepen their scientific contribution.

title: Agenda-setting relations between Chinese state media reports and public social media posts: focusing on COVID-19
abstract: This study explores differences and cross-arena relations in agenda construction between the People’s Daily , the official publication of the Chinese Communist Party, and Weibo, a widely used social media platform, by analyzing the structural similarities of attribute networks within media reports and Weibo posts about COVID-19 in China. Drawing on network agenda-setting theory, the study assesses how agenda attributes co-occur and exhibit similar structural patterns across arenas and stages of the COVID-19 issue life cycle. By revealing a statistically significant positive relation between the two arenas’ attribute networks, as well as variance in strength and configuration similarities across stages, this study deepens our understanding of the roles and interactions between traditional and platform media in China and provides key insights into factors driving public opinion formation in China.

title: Aligning climate policy with energy justice through remedial stakeholder theory
abstract: We contribute to this special issue by exploring climate policy and energy justice through the lens of remedial stakeholder theory. While stakeholder theory traditionally focuses on present and forward-looking relationships, we argue that climate change and the energy transition provide a compelling case to examine the nexus of past, present, and future organisational action. Many energy companies, which are legally incorporated entities (in some cases with more than one hundred years of existence), have accumulated substantial profits through business models that externalised the environmental costs of greenhouse gas emissions, with particularly negative effects on the countries that contributed the least to them. These emissions have significantly contributed to human-induced climate change, which is projected to plunge millions further into climate-related poverty, particularly in vulnerable and low-income communities. To address this challenge, we propose an extended view of stakeholder theory—remedial stakeholder theory—as a normative framework that spotlights organisational responsibility for historical environmental harms. This model urges firms, especially in the energy sector, to acknowledge and remediate past contributions to climate change by centring reparative practices in their transition strategies. Remedial stakeholder theory connects with climate policy by offering a foundation for designing policies and corporate responses that go beyond distributive fairness in the present to include procedural and restorative justice over time. In doing so, our paper provides a lens to assess how climate and energy policies can more equitably address the burdens and benefits of the energy transition.

title: Home from school: University graduates become technology leaders in their smallholder communities
abstract: Every year, thousands of young Latin Americans leave their smallholder households to attend university, yet some aspire to return as technology leaders. To understand this overlooked segment of youth, we analyzed data from 3670 applicants to Ayllu AgTech, an FAO training program, including 67 autobiographical videos and 15 in-depth interviews. Our findings reveal that these youth remain rooted in their places of origin. Their farming experience and technical training equip them to combine scientific and local knowledge to address rural challenges like food insecurity and climate change. While some graduates do return to their home villages, others act as change agents from a nearby provincial city. Each young professional devises their own way to balance social service with professional growth. However, this group faces systemic barriers—a lack of capital, weak institutional support, and scarce job opportunities. We call for a rethinking of rural youth policy: just as governments support the return of internationally trained talent, they should invest in the development of educated youths as technology leaders for smallholder communities. This is an overlooked development strategy hiding in plain sight.

title: A dual-modal hotel recommendation method utilizing the generalized Shapley-Choquet integral
abstract: This paper examines hotel management and consumer decision-making within the platform economy. Online reviews serve as key instruments for analyzing complex consumer behavior. The new method converts computational techniques—such as natural language processing, multimodal sentiment analysis, and fuzzy mathematics—into quantitative analytical tools. The analytical framework systematically explores consumers’ latent interactive psychology. First, a data-driven hotel rating indicator system provides detailed characterization of service experiences. Second, sentiment scores, derived from textual and image-based analyses, integrate cross-modal sensory experiences through confidence levels, thereby reducing cognitive biases in emotional expression. The method accounts for heterogeneous consumer preferences and psychological interactions among attributes. A 2-additive measure, based on sentiment scores, dynamically determines attribute importance. The generalized Shapley value and Choquet integral comprehensively capture compensation patterns across attribute subsets. Personalized demands are mined from consumers’ historical accommodation records. A triple-hybrid similarity method screens candidate hotels and enables personalized recommendations. The case study demonstrates that the proposed method effectively captures consumers’ multisensory and multi-attribute decision-making characteristics. The findings offer robust managerial implications and support precise hotel service design and dynamic supply-demand alignment within the platform economy ecosystem.

title: Sentiment analysis in rural areas: a systematic review of applications and approaches
abstract: Rural depopulation and territorial imbalances are ongoing challenges that require innovative tools for understanding community needs and informing evidence-based policy. Sentiment Analysis (SA) has emerged as a promising methodology for extracting emotional information from large volumes of digital text data. However, despite its growing methodological relevance across the social sciences, its application to rural contexts is limited, and no prior systematic review has examined the application of SA within rural research. This article aims to assess the usefulness and potential of SA in rural research through a systematic review of existing applications and a critical analysis of its methodological contributions. The systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies applied SA to textual or social media data and focused on rural areas or explicitly compared rural and urban contexts. Searches were performed in Scopus and Web of Science (WOS) up to March 2025. A total of 47 studies were included and analysed. Data extraction was performed from the reviewed studies, collecting information on the location, study type, authors’ discipline, and methodological quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and a consensus review by the research team. Key results were extracted, including areas of application of SA, methodologies employed, and data sources. Additionally, a thematic analysis was conducted considering the main areas of application of SA and its limitations. The studies reveal a developing field where SA is increasingly applied across various domains, particularly in rural tourism and public health, as well as in agriculture, food policy and social well-being. A significant geographic concentration of research is observed in China and the United States. The studies employ various SA processing methodologies (lexicon-based, machine learning, deep learning and hybrid approaches) and diverse data sources (social media, surveys, digital reviews). Methodological quality was generally high, with 85% of the studies scoring 7 or higher on the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Furthermore, the analysis identified notable differences in perceptions between rural and urban areas, emphasizing the importance of considering local contexts in public policy discussions. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the role of SA in rural development and offer valuable insights for future research and policy formulation aimed at addressing the specific needs of rural communities.

title: Online sexual exploitation and grooming in inclusive settings: school response mechanisms and the first 24 h
abstract: The increasing integration of digital technologies into inclusive school settings may heighten the vulnerability of students with special educational needs to online child sexual exploitation and abuse (OCSEA) and online grooming. This study examines schools’ capacity to identify and respond to these risks, with a focus on the initial response in the first 24 h after a concern is raised. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 school professionals in Türkiye (15 teachers; 15 school administrators) working in inclusive settings. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Seven themes were identified: (1) digital risks encountered by students within inclusive school settings, (2) early warning signs, (3) schools’ initial response process in suspected cases, (4) schools’ technical safety measures, (5) gaps in student-facing education, (6) teachers’ professional development needs, and (7) recommendations for families. Risks were most frequently linked to unmoderated interactions on social media and in online games. Concerns were commonly recognised through behavioural indicators. Although referral to the school guidance/counselling service was typical, participants reported uncertainty about legal reporting requirements and referral pathways and described feeling insufficiently prepared. Overall, the findings suggest that technical measures alone are inadequate and underscore the need for a comprehensive school safety approach that includes clear reporting protocols, structured staff training, and sustained collaboration with families.

title: Gender pay equity in public sector employment: An analysis of compensation disparities and overtime allocation across municipal departments
abstract: The public sector maintains official salary systems and equality policies yet women and men continue to experience pay differences when total compensation is evaluated. The research conducts a thorough examination of gender pay equity throughout a large municipal workforce by studying both base salary and overtime and longevity pay. The research uses administrative data from more than 10,000 employees spread across 42 departments to analyze compensation disparities through a theoretical framework that includes Human Capital Theory and Discrimination Theories and Institutional Theory and Gender Stratification. The research shows that unequal overtime distribution creates more than 60% of the total pay difference between genders. The departmental level shows substantial differences because cultural elements together with structural aspects determine how equity outcomes develop. The departments that demonstrate strong equity performance provide practical examples which organizations can use to develop reform strategies. The research demonstrates that meaningful gender pay equity in public sector organizations requires specific data-based interventions together with enhanced organizational responsibility. Note: This analysis is cross-sectional in design; therefore, the findings reflect associations rather than causal relationships, and longitudinal replication is recommended to establish causality.

title: Orchestrating connective value cocreation through online communities: a mixed-method investigation
abstract: Abstract In the digital age, online communities have revolutionized firms’ value-creation processes. However, how firms orchestrate interactions among heterogeneous users to enable connective value cocreation (CVC), a digitally mediated form of value cocreation based on sustained interaction, remains unexplored. To bridge this gap, this study investigates CVC mechanisms through a mixed-method investigation of Xiaomi’s online community, combining a qualitative case study with online community interaction analysis. Drawing on resource orchestration theory, we identify three orchestration actions—accessing, categorizing, and aligning—and show how they structure user roles and coordination dynamics in practice. The findings advance the understanding of the governance of crowd-based innovation and offer practical insights for firms seeking to manage online communities for sustained innovation outcomes.

title: Dynamics of urban wetland ecosystem service values in China
abstract: Although urbanization has profound ecological consequences, quantitative evidence on how socio-economic factors in this process affect China’s urban wetland ecosystem services (UWES) remains limited. We present a comprehensive systematic review of UWES valuation in China and develop a meta-analysis database integrating urban wetland valuation studies with city-level characteristics to examine the temporal dynamics and drivers of UWES across stages of urbanization. We identify a structural shift around 2015 and an urbanization-rate threshold of approximately 82.3%, beyond which the determinants of urban wetland value change substantially in both magnitude and direction. This pattern suggests a transition from expansion-driven urbanization to a more mature phase where ecological conditions, governance capacity, and city-level characteristics play a greater role. Drawing on evidence from residents’ willingness-to-pay for non-use UWES and nationwide projections of UWES values, we derive policy implications for stage-specific wetland conservation strategies and integrated management.

title: “We need urbanization that is good to older people”: the sense of belonging of Chinese rural older adults experiencing in-situ urbanization
abstract: Many developing countries are prioritizing age-friendly urbanization in their policy agendas in response to two major demographic shifts: population ageing and urbanization. This qualitative study explored variations in the sense of belonging (SOB) among rural older adults undergoing in-situ urbanization and how these variations were related to their subjective well-being (SWB). Drawing on in-depth interviews with 35 older adults and three focus group discussions involving 16 community gatekeepers in a county in western China, the analysis identified three recurring patterns of SOB: clan-centric belonging, integrated dual belonging, and community-centric belonging. Participants whose accounts reflected integrated dual or community-centric belonging more often described positive well-being and attitudes toward urbanization. The thematic analysis related these patterns to (1) the contained influence of village clans, (2) discrepancies between expectations and the realities of urbanization, and (3) different coping responses. The findings suggest that urbanizing communities should consider both built and social infrastructure when supporting older residents’ participation and belonging.

title: Ecological wisdom of settlement heritage from the perspective of climate adaptability: a case study
abstract: As urbanization advances and environmental challenges like global warming become more pronounced, the traditional wisdom in constructing rural settlement spaces has garnered increasing attention. This study focuses on the dispersed branches of the Tujia ethnic group in northeastern Sichuan Province, China. It comprehensively analyzes the spatial characteristics of their settlements and their adaptive relationship with the environment, comparing these features to those in the core distribution area of the Tujia people. Through field investigations, spatial mapping, and microclimate measurements, the study accurately identifies the adaptation strategies of traditional settlements to harsh climatic conditions. Consequently, it summarizes spatial patterns that can be applied to similar climate environments. Research findings indicate that: (1) Traditional settlements of the Tujia ethnic group in northeastern Sichuan exhibit strong adaptability to the region’s unique climate characterized by hot summers; (2) Numerous ventilation corridors are observed within architectural courtyards, and the resulting spatial configurations are associated with variations in wind circulation and indoor thermal-humidity conditions; (3) The indoor microclimate has been significantly improved. Both wooden board walls and brick-stone walls effectively mitigate the harsh climatic conditions, with brick-stone walls demonstrating superior performance compared to wooden board walls.

title: Transformational leadership and service innovation performance: the role of knowledge sharing and innovation culture in the hospitality sector employees
abstract: Abstract This research examines how Indian hotels can systematically create “wow” moments for guests by translating transformational leadership (TL) into frontline employees’ service innovation performance (SIP) rather than treating innovation as ad hoc or leader‑driven in a vacuum. Drawing on social exchange theory, organizational learning theory, and the job demands–resources (JD–R) model, we develop and test a conditional process model in which TL shapes SIP through two distinct yet complementary mechanisms: knowledge sharing (KS) as a proximal learning behaviour and innovation culture (IC) as a deeper normative infrastructure, while psychological safety (PS) functions as a contextual resource that regulates how strongly these pathways operate. Survey data from 492 frontline employees in Indian hotels and resorts were analyzed using covariance‑based structural equation modeling (AMOS 29) and bootstrapped conditional process analysis (SPSS 29). The results indicated that TL is linked to SIP through its relationship with KS and IC, and KS emerged as the stronger conduit. Moreover, PS strengthens the direct TL–SIP link once a minimum safety threshold is reached and simultaneously attenuates the TL → KS → SIP and TL → IC → SIP pathways, potentially reducing employees’ dependence on leader-driven KS mechanisms while enabling the translation of leader-driven cultural norms into SIP. These findings extend existing leadership–innovation theory in hospitality by distinguishing behavioural and cultural routes from TL to SIP, which are most consequential for SIP when PS acts as a booster vs a contextual ceiling, offering actionable guidance on how hospitality practitioners can align leadership development, knowledge systems, and PS‑building practices to achieve sustained, perceptible innovation outcomes.

title: Cybernetics, the Anthropocene, and education: student learning in conjunction with AI
abstract: This article develops a speculative and empirically inflected account of how university students are learning in conjunction with artificial intelligence (AI). It brings together three interlocking fields: cybernetics, the Anthropocene and education. Cybernetics is central because the communicative and control processes through which students engage AI for research, writing and study raise fundamental questions about agency, authorship and the capacity to think otherwise within machine-mediated capitalism. The Anthropocene provides a second axis of analysis, naming the planetary consequences of human technological development, economic acceleration and ecological damage. Education forms the third axis, because universities are key sites in which these cybernetic and Anthropocene dynamics are materialised through everyday practices of study, assessment and writing. The article combines philosophical analysis with empirical data from education students learning with AI. These data are organised as “data portals”: analytic thresholds that interrupt, extend and test the conceptual argument. Drawing on Deleuze’s transcendental empiricism, the article argues that students do not encounter AI as an external tool alone, but as part of a wider student-AI-university assemblage. The article concludes that agency persists in this assemblage, but is increasingly modulated by feedback, acceleration, assessment pressure, economic precarity and machinic cognition.

title: ‘I finally switched from the teaching course to a business one’: a serendipitous longitudinal study of a TESOL student-teacher’s resignation
abstract: Teacher attrition remains a persistent challenge, particularly among early-career educators, with language teachers facing distinct systemic barriers such as job insecurity, undervaluation, and emotional labour. While existing studies predominantly focus on in-service teachers, pre-service teacher attrition remains underexplored, limiting the development of effective interventions to support student-teachers. This study addresses this gap by examining the case of a pre-service teacher from China, who was enroled in a Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages programme at a Malaysian university and later left teacher education for business studies. Adopting a longitudinal qualitative approach, we thematically and temporally analysed 13 semi-structured interviews conducted over nearly two years. The findings reveal that the participant’s departure was driven by a mismatch between teaching realities and initial aspirations, psychological strain and burnout, inadequate skill development and support, concerns over the recognition and transferability of the degree, and the relocation of career identity. These factors were contextualised through the interplay of human, social, structural, and psychological capital constraints, alongside relational, comparative, and agentic capital influences, manifesting through contradictory, socialising, dislocating, and evolutionary routines in careership. The study has significant implications for teacher education programmes and the broader educational community in fostering teacher retention and promoting a more sustainable teaching profession.

title: Social networks, social support, and loneliness among older urban Indians: a mediation analysis
abstract: Rapid population ageing is transforming family structures in India, which have traditionally been considered as the primary source of care and support for older persons. As a result, older persons experience emotional and financial insecurity, which in turn increases the prevalence of psychological distress in later life. Considering this, the presence of social networks and the provision of social support may serve as a form of social resilience that helps cope with psychological distress in old age. The present study examines the association between social network types and loneliness, and explore the intermediary role of reciprocal social support in this relationship among older urban Indians. An adequate sample of 378 older individuals was drawn from a cross-sectional primary survey in the Kalyani Municipal Area of West Bengal, an eastern state of India. Both hierarchical and K-means cluster analyses were employed to derive distinct social network types. Hierarchical linear regression models were performed to assess the impact of specific social network types on loneliness after adjusted for control variables. Baron and Kenny’s ‘Causal Step Approach’ was used to explore the mediational impact. Cluster analyses identified five distinct social network types: ‘Other,’ ‘Friend,’ ‘Children (living away),’ ‘Spouse and Children (living together),’ and a specific family type, i.e., ‘Distant Family.’ Compared to the ‘Other’ network type, only the ‘Spouse and Children’ and ‘Children’ networks were significantly negatively associated with loneliness after controlling for adjusted variables. Further, social support partially mediates the relationships between social network types and loneliness. Specifically, giving social support is more favourable to prevent loneliness compared to receiving social support. The study findings underscore the need to promote social awareness regarding intergenerational responsibility towards the care and support of elderly members. Additionally, construction of geriatric unit and urban community centres may promote leisure activities and good knowledge about health and well-being.

title: An integrated model of executive function, AI literacy, and Chinese L2 reading comprehension among ethnic minority adolescents in Hong Kong
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in second language (L2) learning, yet the cognitive demands of AI-mediated environments, particularly for logographic languages such as Chinese, remain underexplored. This study investigated the interrelationships among executive function (EF), reading-related linguistic skills, AI literacy, and Chinese L2 reading comprehension in 155 Form 4 Southeast Asian ethnic minority students in Hong Kong. Using a quantitative design, we validated a three-factor EF model (working memory, cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control) and examined how these components, together with orthographic and morphological skills, relate to L2 reading outcomes. Structural equation modeling showed that all three EF components significantly predicted reading comprehension, underscoring the importance of executive control for processing a complex logographic script. AI literacy significantly supported both foundational reading skills and overall reading comprehension. A key finding of the integrated model is that cognitive flexibility significantly predicted AI literacy, which in turn significantly predicted reading comprehension, indicating an indirect pathway from EF to reading via AI literacy. This pattern highlights the cognitive underpinnings of digital engagement in L2 learning. The study extends the Reading Systems Framework by positioning AI literacy as an external scaffold that interacts with learners’ cognitive resources, and offers practical implications for designing cognitively supportive, AI-enhanced Chinese L2 instruction for ethnic minority learners.

title: Social simulations with large language model risk Utopian illusion
abstract: Reliable simulation of human behaviour is essential for explaining, predicting, and intervening in our society. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in emulating human behaviours, interactions, and decision-making, offering a powerful new lens for social science studies. However, the extent to which LLMs diverge from authentic human behaviour in social contexts remains underexplored, posing risks of misinterpretation in scientific studies and unintended consequences in real-world applications. This study introduces a systematic framework for analysing LLMs’ behaviour in social simulation. Our approach simulates multi-agent interactions through chatroom-style conversations and analyzes them across five linguistic dimensions, providing a simple yet effective method to examine emergent social cognitive biases. We conduct extensive experiments involving eight representative LLMs across three families. The results show that LLMs do not faithfully reproduce genuine human behaviour but instead reflect overly idealised versions of it, shaped by the social desirability bias. In particular, LLMs show social role bias, primacy effect, and positivity bias, resulting in “Utopian” societies that lack the complexity and variability of real human interactions. These findings suggest that LLM-based simulations reproduce how people wish others to behave rather than how people themselves behave, a divergence that amplifies through multi-agent interaction and, if uncritically adopted in social analysis, may produce an artificially narrowed representation of social life. This paper calls for more socially grounded LLMs that better capture the diversity of human social behaviour.

title: A century of party congress elections in China and the Soviet Union
abstract: Ruling parties are thought to sustain autocracies by facilitating elite power-sharing. If so, authoritarian party institutions must be reasonably resilient. We evaluate this thesis by studying dissenting votes against leader-nominated candidates in party congress elections—among the most pervasive yet least examined forms of elections in twentieth-century autocracies. We combine Chinese Communist Party election data (1945–2017), estimated through a new heuristic method, with Soviet Communist Party records from declassified Russian archives (1934–1986) to provide the first comparative analysis of elections in the two major communist states. We further validate the heuristic method against Soviet records, providing the first direct evidence for this increasingly adopted tool. Both regimes exhibited active dissent in their early periods, but dissent eventually declined—though far more gradually in China until a precipitous drop after 2012. These findings cast doubt on the party-sustaining-autocracy thesis and open a new frontier in authoritarian election studies.

title: From digital to real: The technology convergence and its impact on corporate employment expansion
abstract: Promoting the deep integration of digital and real economy technologies and achieving high-quality full employment are important tasks in China’s high-quality economic development strategy. Based on panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2014 to 2023, this paper measures technology convergence between digital and real economy industries (TCDR) from a micro perspective and empirically examines its employment effects. The results show that, first, TCDR significantly increases employment quantity and has a non-linear effect on employment quality, and the findings remain robust after endogeneity and robustness tests. Second, the mechanism analysis shows that TCDR promotes growth in employment quantity through production scale expansion, indicating a positive linear relationship in which the creation effect outweighs the inhibition effect. Meanwhile, TCDR has a non-linear effect on employment quality, initially suppressing and then improving it through productivity improvement, factor substitution, and enhanced market competitiveness. Finally, the heterogeneity analysis indicates that the employment effects of TCDR are shaped by internal firm characteristics, such as executives’ backgrounds and digital-technology bias; external conditions, such as government subsidies and digital infrastructure; and digital knowledge sources. Firms with a stronger digital-technology bias, as well as those that absorb more digital knowledge from the digital product services sector during the TCDR process, are more likely to achieve coordinated growth in employment quantity and employment quality.

title: Work-family bidirectional conflicts and their impact on working mothers’ job satisfaction in Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract Married women’s employment rates have significantly increased in recent decades, especially for mothers of small children. Mothers’ increased labour market participation has worsened the conflicts between their jobs and family obligations, negatively impacting their employment results. The primary assumption made throughout this study is that time and stress are the leading predictors of work-family conflicts in both directions, e.g., from family to work and work to family. The analysis is predicated on a sample of 307 full-time employed mothers with at least one child under the age of 8. Findings indicate that both time-based and strain-based family-work conflict (FWC) and strain-based work-family conflict (WFC) significantly adversely impact working mothers' job satisfaction in Bangladesh. Conversely, our study demonstrated no substantial effect of time-based work-family conflicts on mothers’ job satisfaction. Thus, the current research simultaneously supports and contradicts the prevailing literature on work-family conflict (WFC) and family-work conflict (FWC). This study recommends that organisations and management adopt strategies that promote a gender-neutral workplace, enabling working mothers to strive and realise their full potential. The current study further stresses that addressing the ubiquities of gendered norms and structural barriers is imperative to delving into WFC & FWC for maximising mothers’ labour market outcomes.

title: The value of a family dinner from the perspective of subjective well-being
abstract: Based on data from the China Family Panel Studies ( CFPS ) 2014 and 2018 surveys, this paper investigates the association between family dinners and subjective well-being ( SWB ), analyzing it through the dual lenses of material and spiritual needs. The findings reveal that sharing meals with family members significantly enhances SWB —and that this positive effect has strengthened over time. Moreover, the magnitude of this effect exhibits notable heterogeneity across urban versus rural residence and across income groups. Employing the life satisfaction approach ( LSA ), the study further monetizes the value of family dinners. On average, residents are willing to pay CNY 11,585 annually for one additional family dinner per week—a willingness-to-pay figure that has also increased over time, again reflecting pronounced urban–rural and income-based disparities. Additional analysis uncovers a threshold effect in the relationship between family dinner frequency and SWB improvement, with the threshold varying by survey year, gender, marital status, and residential location (urban vs. rural).

title: A study of the “Breakthrough of Localized Influence” in regional sports events: agenda, emotion, and cultural identity
abstract: The rapid development of social media has profoundly transformed how cultural and sports events are disseminated, enabling regional sports events to overcome geographical constraints and attract nationwide attention--a phenomenon referred to as “breakout” (chū quān). Such events, rich in local cultural symbols, have become important vehicles for spreading regional culture and fostering local identity. This study explores the dynamics and differentiated pathways underlying this phenomenon. We collected comprehensive data on the “Jiangsu City Football League” (“Su Chao”), a phenomenal regional sports event in China, including 222,027 posts and comments from Weibo and 743,794 video titles and comments from TikTok. Using a mixed-method framework that integrates LDA (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) topic modelling, social network analysis, and sentiment analysis, we examined the agenda networks (i.e., cognitive associative structures formed by co-occurring issue attributes) constructed by official media, opinion leaders, and the public, as well as the structural associations among them. We further propose a triple linkage pathway of “agenda network construction - emotional resonance stimulation - cultural identity reinforcement”: agenda network construction provides the cognitive framework, emotional resonance injects affective energy, and cultural identity reflects deeper social outcomes; the three dimensions co-evolve. The results suggest that: (1) the agenda networks of Weibo and TikTok are oriented around different cores--Weibo focuses on “cultural honour,” while TikTok emphasizes “commercial confrontation-fusion”; (2) transmission pathways diverge across platforms--Weibo exhibits hierarchical collaboration (a top-down, orderly flow pattern from official media to opinion leaders to the public), whereas TikTok suggests competitive public reconstruction (the public’s active deconstruction and re-creation of established agenda frameworks); (3) breakout depends on the triple linkage pathway, manifesting as a gradual pathway on Weibo and a carnival-like pathway on TikTok. This study offers a new theoretical framework for understanding complex communication of regional sports events in social media ecosystems and provides practical guidance for coordinating cross-platform strategies.

title: From textbooks to classrooms: how climate change is represented and taught in Chinese high schools
abstract: This study investigated how climate change was represented in Chinese senior high school textbooks and how teachers interpreted and taught climate change in the classrooms. Focusing on geography, biology, and chemistry textbooks published by the People’s Education Press in 2019, this study combined a qualitative content analysis of textbook materials with semi-structured interviews with 30 senior teachers from Zhejiang Province. The findings indicated that climate change content was moderately represented and unevenly distributed across disciplines. Geography provided the most integrated coverage, connecting scientific mechanisms, socioenvironmental impacts, and policy responses, whereas biology emphasised ecological consequences and chemistry focused on explaining the underlying mechanisms. Teacher interviews revealed that climate change topics were given low academic priority, largely because of their minimal presence in high-stakes examinations, leading to textbook-centred, shallow instruction. Nevertheless, teachers consistently highlighted environmental awareness and civic responsibility as key instructional goals. This study demonstrates that while textbooks provide foundational knowledge, disciplinary silos, exam-oriented content selection, and national policy priorities, such as carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, shape classroom enactment, resulting in fragmented climate-change learning experiences. These findings underscore the importance of curriculum alignment, assessments, and teacher support to foster more coherent, interdisciplinary, and action-oriented climate change education.

title: Livelihood vulnerabilities among women in the bushmeat trade in Ghana during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The bushmeat trade is a significant source of employment for women in Ghana; providing income-generating opportunities and supporting household livelihoods. However, there is a paucity of research on how the COVID-19 affected these women. Using qualitative data, this paper examines the livelihood vulnerabilities of women bushmeat traders during the COVID-19 pandemic. Drawing on their lived experiences, the study highlights interrelated factors shaping their vulnerability, including the association of the commodities with zoonotic diseases, the perishable nature of the commodity, limited economic resources, and weak protection systems. Despite these challenges, the women demonstrated resilience and agency in sustaining their livelihoods. The paper recommends that policy makers incorporate the needs of women bushmeat traders into interventions aimed at reducing vulnerability and sustaining their livelihoods.

title: Hauntological ecologies and temporalities of post-socialism: Disco Elysium between Estonia and China
abstract: This paper examines the video game Disco Elysium (ZA/UM, 2019) as a pivotal cultural text for understanding the hauntological dimensions of post-socialist experience. The game’s transnational journey and profound reception from Estonia to China reveal a shared, yet differentially articulated, structure of feeling shaped by the aftermath of collapsed socialist projects and the ascendancy of neoliberal capitalism.
