These groups often struggle to recognise scam tactics due to technological and language barriers, rendering them susceptible to cyberfraud victimisation. By comparing 106 phishing text messages in Australia with legitimate text messages sent by frequently imitated organisations, this study examined the threat of phishing text messages, which account for substantial financial losses and reduced wellbeing globally. Using systemic-functional linguistics (SFL), a framework that ties language choices to context and function, specific linguistic features that manipulate receivers of phishing messages were identified. Results of the analysis showed that different clause types; time, location, and manner markers; high modality; and conjunctive use, were influential in creating urgency and authority, and eliciting emotional responses to phishing messages. Many current advisory resources offer generalised advice and explanations of scam tactics, yet fail to include concrete examples of such communications. By aligning linguistic analysis with human behavioural constructs and public policy, the results of this study have implications for the protection of vulnerable community groups from growing cyber threats through enhancing advisory content, and by developing automated scam detection systems.

title: AI-generated content-plagiarism versus institutional silence: comparative insights on responses of higher education to rapid technological changes in China and Japan
abstract: This study seeks to elucidate how the higher education systems of China and Japan have addressed the issue of plagiarism exacerbated by generative artificial intelligence (AIGC-plagiarism) and the insights gained from these responses. As generative AI becomes increasingly integrated with higher education, the age-old problem of plagiarism has resurfaced with greater intensity and elusiveness, sweeping across universities worldwide. Although no definitive consensus exists regarding the precise definition of AIGC-plagiarism, this conceptual ambiguity does not preclude its broad recognition as prohibited academic conduct. The relationship between cutting-edge technologies and higher education appears to have reached an impasse, yet the majority of Chinese institutions have maintained a stance of silence, while the Chinese government has shown concern but refrained from taking formal action. This research comparatively examines the response strategies to AIGC-plagiarism by the Japanese government and 359 universities, which share similar systemic and institutional contexts with their Chinese counterparts, and reaches a conclusion that the practice of “No Copy + Exceptions” emerges as a particularly instructive approach. A micro-level comparative analysis reveals that this regulatory inertia is shaped by both technological and political factors, and represents a pragmatic strategy in the face of technological uncertainty. Regardless of the underlying rationale, such silence constitutes an unacceptable form of de facto endorsement or passive acquiescence. Higher education systems must develop more proactive, responsive, and agile mechanisms to cultivate morally anchored, innovation-capable students amidst technological and geopolitical turbulence. Key components of this mechanism include, but are not limited to a unified national benchmark and implementation rule, a dynamic AI impact assessment structure, autonomy of faculty and academic councils, and student participation with feedback channels.

title: Bridging competitiveness and sustainability in tourism: a multistage network DEA approach aligned with the SDGs
abstract: Enhancing tourism competitiveness while addressing environmental constraints and post-pandemic recovery challenges has become a critical issue for sustainable development. This study employs a multistage network data envelopment analysis (NDEA) to assess the sustainable tourism effectiveness of 117 countries across five dimensions: transportation infrastructure, information technology, service activity, tangible benefits, and sustainability governance over three interconnected developmental stages. To capture post-pandemic changes, this study uses TTCI 2019 as the pre-pandemic baseline and TTDI 2021 and 2024 as recovery-period benchmarks. The results reveal substantial continent-specific effectiveness gaps, with North America, Europe, and Oceania showing stronger performance in transportation, digital infrastructure, and service effectiveness, whereas Africa and South America require further improvement in transforming tourism resources into tangible economic benefits. By integrating the tangible benefit and sustainability governance dimensions, the NDEA framework provides a diagnostic tool for identifying stage-specific areas for improvement. The findings offer practical implications for enhancing destination competitiveness, promoting responsible resource use, and supporting SDG 8 and SDG 12 in the post-pandemic tourism context.

title: Environmental stress and well-being in OECD countries: testing EKC, LCC, and PHH models
abstract: This study investigates the interaction between economic growth, environmental stress, and well-being in OECD countries from 1990–2022. Using the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) and Load Capacity Curve (LCC) hypotheses, alongside the Pollution Haven Hypothesis (PHH), the analysis explores the roles of renewable energy consumption, globalization, population density, financial development, and foreign direct investment. Panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE) and Driscoll-Kraay standard errors confirm the EKC and LCC hypotheses; they reject PHH under LCC but accept it under EKC, albeit statistically weakly. Results show that renewable energy significantly improves ecological capacity and reduces CO₂ emissions, whereas globalization exerts a negative effect on environmental quality. Population growth weakens ecological capacity but has no significant impact on emissions. Financial development exhibits mixed effects, with weak evidence of environmental harm. OECD economies, which account for over 60% of global GDP yet remain heavily reliant on fossil fuels, represent a critical test case for sustainability. Policy recommendations emphasize prioritizing renewable energy adoption, integrating environmental safeguards into globalization processes, and channeling financial flows toward green technologies. These findings contribute to the literature by combining traditional and innovative models, offering actionable insights for policymakers seeking to balance economic growth with ecological resilience.

title: Legislative revisions to attendance mandates in german higher education and the experiences of academics: a case study informed by self-determination theory
abstract: This study investigates the impact of a legal regulation that relaxes mandatory attendance requirements in university courses in certain German states on academic practices. This study employed a descriptive design within a qualitative framework. The study group comprised six academics affiliated with Johannes Gutenberg University in Germany during the 2023–2024 academic year. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews and analyzed using descriptive methods. The findings reveal that the legal regulation operates within a multi-layered structure. First, it was determined that higher education policies vary among the states in accordance with Germany’s federal structure, and that participation policies are shaped within this decentralized governance framework. Second, the emergence of the regulation was influenced by the positioning of students as autonomous and adult individuals, as well as by political and institutional pressure dynamics. Third, regulation enhances student autonomy and self-regulation skills, supports intrinsic motivation, and fosters innovation and academic competition in teaching processes. However, it was also determined that the regulation has led to significant negative consequences, such as a decline in faculty motivation, weakened classroom interaction, reduced course quality, and a diminished sense of responsibility among students. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that attendance policies in higher education encompass both pedagogical opportunities and structural risks, highlighting the necessity of balanced policies that strike a balance between student autonomy and the quality of teaching processes.

title: Demand information sharing strategies in supply chains with green services and consumer-to-manufacturer
abstract: Abstract This paper constructs a game-theoretical model to investigate demand information sharing strategies in a supply chain consisting of a single manufacturer and a green service platform, while considering the manufacturer’s adoption of the Consumer-to-Manufacturer (C2M) strategy. The green service platform determines whether to disclose demand information. If the platform discloses information, the manufacturer may adopt the C2M strategy to adjust pricing and product decisions based on the shared demand information. We analyze three decision scenarios: no information sharing and no C2M, information sharing and no C2M, and information sharing and C2M. Different from conventional studies that focus on pricing or operational decisions alone, this work innovatively integrates platform green services, demand information asymmetry, and C2M into a unified analytical framework, revealing how C2M strategy efficiency reshapes the platform’s information sharing incentives and the supply chain’s operational outcomes. Contrary to traditional wisdom, our results show that the platform is inclined to share demand information when C2M investment efficiency is at a moderate level. Adopting the C2M strategy can incentivize the platform to share information, thereby creating a mutually beneficial outcome for both supply chain members. We further quantify the impacts of information sharing and C2M strategy choices on consumer surplus and social welfare, which depend closely on C2M investment efficiency. This study fills the research gap regarding the interactive mechanism among platform green services, demand information sharing, and the C2M strategy, and enriches the theoretical system of supply chain information management and digital business model research.

title: Talent policy attention and online public response: a nonlinear association across 232 Chinese cities
abstract: Digital platforms are now central to local policy communication, but greater visibility does not always produce a more favorable public response. This study examines talent-policy news attention in Chinese cities, where competition for talent is increasingly conducted online. The analysis draws on a balanced panel of 232 cities from 2014 to 2023. Talent Policy Attention (TPA) is measured from talent-related news coverage. The talent policy sentiment-interaction (TPSI) index is constructed from messages posted on the Message Board for Leaders and combines sentiment composition with the intensity of institutionalized interaction. Two-way fixed-effects models with a quadratic term show a U-shaped association between TPA and TPSI. The estimated turning point corresponds to about 94 talent-related news reports per city-year in this sample. The pattern holds for alternative specifications of TPSI and for the participation dimension taken alone. Measures built on sentiment composition alone do not turn within the observed range, which places the reversal in participation rather than in sentiment polarity: sustained attention is associated with more talent-policy messages, not with a more favorable balance of expression. Mediation and heterogeneity results are consistent with possible conditioning roles for digital economy development and public service capacity in the association between TPA and TPSI. The design is observational at the city level, so the estimates describe associations rather than causal effects.

title: Speech act realization patterns of requests and refusals in English among Nigerian university students: a focus on Hausa, Igbo, and Yoruba speakers
abstract: Nigeria’s multilingual landscape provides a rich context for investigating cross-cultural variations in pragmatic behavior. However, existing research has not sufficiently explored speech act production among Hausa, Igbo, and Yoruba speakers. To address this gap, the current study examines request and refusal strategies among Nigerian undergraduate students, aiming to identify pragmatic similarities and differences across these three ethnolinguistic groups in both L1 and L2 contexts. A total of 90 participants across four Nigerian universities were selected for the study. To investigate the students’ linguistic, pragmatic, and socio-pragmatic competence, two instruments were used: a written discourse completion task (WDCT) developed by the researchers and a rating scale. The results reveal numerous similarities among Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba participants in their use of all speech act strategies for requests and refusals. However, significant differences in linguistic, pragmatic-linguistic, and socio-pragmatic competence are found between Igbo and Hausa, as well as between Yoruba and Hausa. Overall, these findings illustrate how cultural norms shape pragmatic choices in Nigeria’s multilingual settings and highlight the importance of integrating pragmatic awareness into ESL curricula and indigenous language instruction to support culturally appropriate communication.

title: Spatial distribution patterns and influencing factors of traditional villages in southwest China: an integrated MGWR-XGBoost approach
abstract: Traditional villages in Southwest China exhibit complex spatial distribution patterns, yet comprehensive quantitative analysis of their clustering characteristics and influencing factors remains limited. This study integrates Multi-scale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR) with eXtreme Gradient Boosting-SHapley Additive exPlanations (XGBoost-SHAP) models to analyze spatial distribution patterns and influencing factors of 2,177 traditional villages across Southwest China. Results reveal: (1) significant hierarchical clustering with high-density concentrations in northwestern Yunnan and southeastern Guizhou, (2) pronounced spatial non-stationarity in factor influences across different geographical scales, (3) intangible cultural heritage density as the primary influencing factors with the highest SHAP importance value, and (4) complex nonlinear relationships and synergistic interactions among cultural, environmental, and accessibility factors. This integrated methodological framework advances heritage science by providing interpretable machine learning tools for spatial pattern analysis, offering scientific foundation for differentiated conservation strategies in mountainous regions.

title: Socioeconomic drivers of the declining Igbo apprenticeship scheme (Igba Boyi) and sustainable pathways of its reinvigoration
abstract: The Igbo apprenticeship scheme (Igba boyi ) of Southeastern Nigeria, once celebrated as a transformative entrepreneurial incubator, is experiencing a notable decline, yet this trend remains under-examined through a sustainability lens. This study investigates the socioeconomic drivers of this decline and proposes pathways for reinvigoration to attract younger generations. Framed by the triple helix model (industry, government, academia), the research employed a concurrent mixed-methods design with 2401 survey respondents (1201 masters, 1200 apprentices) and qualitative data from in-depth interviews, key informant interviews and focus group discussions in Onitsha markets. Findings revealed that 77% of masters and 68.7% of apprentices perceive the scheme as declining, driven predominantly by negative public perception of apprenticeship as ‘servitude’ among educated youths, a preference for formal education, a get-rich-quick mentality, and systemic failures in oral agreements and settlement practices. To reverse this trajectory, we propose reconceptualizing Igba boyi as ‘apprenticeprenureship’ or ‘nkwado-ogranya’ (preparation for wealth creation), operationalized through the triple helix framework: government providing legal backing and certifications, academia delivering tailored business curricula and digital skills training, and industry adopting standardized codes of conduct. This integrated model offers a sustainable pathway for preserving a vital indigenous economic institution.

title: Exploring the impact of AI, peer, and teacher feedback on university students’ L2 writing feedback literacy
abstract: Abstract Student writing feedback literacy (FL) has emerged as a critical competence in second language (L2) education, yet most studies focus mainly on teacher or peer feedback, overlooking how feedback from different sources may differentially shape studnets’ FL development. This mixed-methods study explores changes in Chinese university students’ L2 writing feedback literacy across AI-generated, peer, and teacher feedback during a 10-week quasi-experimental intervention. Three intact classes (N = 126) completed pre- and post-tests using the L2 Student Writing Feedback Literacy Scale (L2-SWFLS), and qualitative interviews were conducted with a subsample to understand their perceptions and the processes involved in engaging with these feedback sources. Quantitative findings showed significant improvements in writing feedback literacy for the AI and peer feedback groups, with the AI group showing advantage in acknowledging different feedback sources and the peer group in appreciating feedback, acknowledging different feedback sources, and making judgments. While the teacher feedback group showed limited improvement, with no significant changes in all dimensions. Qualitative data revealed that AI and peer feedback enhanced students’ autonomy and criticality in interpreting and using feedback compared to teacher feedback. These findings highlight the differentiated effects of AI, peer, and teacher feedback on L2 writing feedback literacy and suggest that integrating multiple feedback sources can optimize writing instruction.

title: Digital literacy, employment choices, and income disparities among migrant agricultural workers
abstract: The investigation of the impact of digital literacy on the income growth and income disparities of migrant agricultural workers is of significant importance for advancing common prosperity among rural farmers. Based on China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) data, this study empirically tests the effect of digital literacy on migrant agricultural workers’ income and income disparities. The results show that improving digital literacy significantly increases the per capita income of migrant agricultural workers’ households and reduces the income gap. These findings remain valid after a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. Mechanism analysis suggests that digital literacy contributes to income growth and narrowing the income gap by influencing migrant agricultural workers’ formal employment, occupational choices, and industry transitions. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the income growth and gap reduction effects among migrant agricultural workers are more pronounced in the eastern region. However, it is noteworthy that, compared to the new generation and higher-educated migrant agricultural workers, the income growth and gap reduction effects are more pronounced among the older generation and lower-educated migrant agricultural workers. RIF unconditional quantile regression further finds that the income growth effect of digital literacy is strongest at the low-income end and weakens as income quantiles increase, while its effect on reducing income disparities is also concentrated at lower quantiles. Based on these findings, recommendations are proposed, such as improving the incentive mechanism for inclusive digital economy development and enhancing mechanisms for preventing income polarization among the rural migrant population.

title: From vision to value: sustainable leadership and project sustainable performance through employee engagement and organizational culture
abstract: This research investigates a novel model in the context of sustainability and examines how sustainable leadership affects sustainable project performance in NGO construction projects in federally administered tribal areas (FATA), Pakistan, through the mediating role of employee engagement and the moderating role of organizational culture. Based on social exchange theory, the proposed model was tested using time-lagged data collected from 361 workers in NGO projects, using hierarchical regression and Hayes’ PROCESS macro. The findings reveal that sustainable leadership significantly enhances sustainable project performance and positively influences employee engagement. Employee engagement partially mediates the relationship between sustainable leadership and sustainable project performance, while organizational culture strengthens the relationship between sustainable leadership and employee engagement, as well as the indirect effect of sustainable leadership on project performance. This study contributes to the sustainable leadership and project management literature by introducing a moderated mediation framework within the underexplored NGO context of FATA, Pakistan. The findings provide practical insights for NGOs seeking to improve the long-term sustainability of projects through leadership practices, employee engagement, and a supportive organizational culture. They also significantly advance the literature on project management, leadership, and sustainable development goals and contribute practical guidance for the Government and NGOs working in challenging environments.

title: The power of framing: how pro- and anti-conflict media discourses shape attitudes and behaviours towards left-wing extremism in india
abstract: Humans assess media discourses on violent political conflicts to either endorse or oppose it. In the largest democracy, India, media significantly depicts the Left-wing extremism (LWE aka Naxalism) with a rejectionist stance to uphold national security and developmental democracy. Nevertheless, no experimental research on perceptual mechanisms regarding pro- or anti-Naxal discourse exists in social and political psychology. This study investigates how people perceive and process anti-Naxal discourse at cognitive and behavioural levels. To explore this, two priming experiments measured the response accuracy (%) and response time (msc) in context of anti- and pro-Naxal discursive stimuli. Findings indicated that anti-extremist discourses were processed with greater speed and higher accuracy than pro-extremist sentential stimuli. Participants showed strong disagreement with pro-Naxal discourses and agreement with anti-Naxal stimuli. The delayed response time for pro-Naxal discourses suggest that participants actively reject the violent ideology of the radical communists. These findings were contextualized within the attentional paradigm, peace journalism, and theories of positive psychology.

title: Socioeconomic disadvantage and health in later life: associations and potential pathways in rural China
abstract: Socioeconomic status (SES) is a key determinant of health. Its relationship with health among older adults in rural China—particularly among vulnerable subgroups—remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the association between SES and multiple health dimensions among rural older adults, assessed subgroup disparities, and explored mediating pathways involving physical exercise, nutrition, and living conditions. Data was drawn from 1077 rural older adults in Shaanxi Province, including both general and vulnerable welfare-recipient groups. Health outcomes covered self-rated health (SRH), cognitive function, and depressive symptoms. Multivariable regression combined with propensity score matching was used to improve comparability between SES groups, and exploratory mediation analysis was conducted to examine potential pathways. Lower SES was associated with poorer SRH (β = 0.367, P < 0.001), poorer cognitive function (β = 1.927, P < 0.001), and more severe depressive symptoms (β = −0.471, P < 0.001). The SES-cognitive function association was stronger among the vulnerable population, whereas SES associations for SRH and depressive symptoms were larger in the general population. Living conditions accounted for the largest share of the observed SES-health association (8.3–25.1%), followed by physical exercise (3.9–9.8%) and nutrition (3.2–13.2%). The association between SES and depressive symptoms appeared stronger among those living alone (β = −0.587, P < 0.001), with no gender differences. SES is strongly associated with multiple health outcomes among rural older adults in China, with physical exercise, nutrition, and living conditions potentially contributing to these associations. Efforts to reduce the health costs of poverty in later life may benefit from comprehensive policies that improve living environments, promote healthy behaviors, and prioritize support for vulnerable groups such as welfare recipients and those living alone.

title: The influence of college students’ mathematical literacy and information literacy on the ability to pose creative mathematical problems: based on the moderating-mediated effect of critical thinking tendency
abstract: Abstract The ability to pose creative mathematical problems rooted in real-world contexts — closely connected with mathematical modelling practice — is an important manifestation of creative thinking. In this study, 196 college students were surveyed to explore the effects of mathematical literacy, information literacy, and critical thinking tendency on the ability to pose creative mathematical problems. Different from pure intra-mathematical problem-posing tasks, our situational paradigm integrates real-life quantitative scenarios, which echoes the assessment orientation of mathematical literacy advocated by OECD. The results show that: (1) The overall situation of college students’ ability to pose creative mathematical problems is relatively good, but there are significant differences in the high-and-medium-score rate of thinking fluency, flexibility, and originality; (2) The main effect of the category ‘major’ is significant, while the main effects of grade and gender are not obvious; (3) Mathematical literacy, information literacy, and critical thinking tendency have a significant positive impact on the ability to pose creative mathematical problems, and there are significant positive correlations between mathematical literacy and information literacy and critical thinking tendency; (4) Critical thinking tendency shows a significant moderated-mediation effect in the influence of mathematical literacy and information literacy on the ability to pose creative mathematical problems.

title: Research on the interaction effects and coordinated relationship between digital agriculture and high-quality agricultural development in China
abstract: In the digital era, the development of digital agriculture (DA) serves as an effective pathway to achieve high-quality agricultural development (HQAD). Although both DA and HQAD are current research hotspots, the interaction and coordination mechanisms between them still urgently require exploration. This study constructs a theoretical analytical framework for the coordinated interaction between DA and HQAD. Utilizing data from 31 Chinese provinces from 2013 to 2023, it empirically analyzes the dynamic interactive effects, coordinated development levels, and the influencing mechanisms of regional disparities between them. The findings reveal that: (1) The development levels of both have been steadily improving, yet significant imbalances and inadequacies persist in their advancement. (2) There exists a mutually reinforcing dynamic interactive effect between DA and HQAD, and their own development exhibits cumulative effects and path dependence. (3) The coupling coordination degree between DA and HQAD has continuously increased, but overall remains at a primary coordination stage, exhibiting a spatial evolution pattern characterized by “eastern regions leading, central regions stable, and western regions catching up.” (4) Human resources, financial services, government support, and transportation logistics are the primary factors influencing the regional differences in the degree of coordination between the two. These findings provide policy guidance for fostering a virtuous cycle between China’s DA and HQAD. They also offer valuable insights and Chinese practices for other countries promoting agricultural modernization.

title: Between pixels and emotions: semiotic-NLP deconstruction of cultural heritage’s social media image
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how digital transformation reshapes the representation and perception of cultural heritage within contemporary tourism by analysing social media narratives of three key urban heritage attractions in Ankara: Hamamönü, Ankara Castle, and the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research integrates visual semiotic analysis—examining colour schemes, compositional patterns, and symbolic codes—with NLP-based sentiment classification of user-generated content from X, Instagram, and Facebook. Findings show Hamamönü is primarily represented through traditional architecture (41%) and gastronomy-focused experiences (34%), emphasizing its cultural and experiential identity. Ankara Castle highlights archaeological heritage (38%) and the urban landscape (29%), underscoring historical and spatial dimensions. The Museum of Anatolian Civilizations is associated with educational value (45%) and interactive exhibition practices (27%), reflecting its strong role in digitally mediated museum experiences. Sentiment analysis indicates polarization: museum-related posts are overwhelmingly positive (82%), whereas critiques focus on Castle infrastructure (28%) and visitor management issues (19%). Overall, the study provides a data-driven framework demonstrating how social media analytics can guide evidence-based strategies for digital transformation, effective promotion, and sustainable communication of cultural heritage sites.

title: Spatial differentiation and driving mechanisms of Tibetan and Qiang traditional villages in northwestern Sichuan, China
abstract: Abstract Northwestern Sichuan Province in China, characterized by its unique geography and rich ethnic culture, hosts numerous Tibetan–Qiang Traditional Villages (TTVNS) of significant conservation value. These villages exhibit pronounced macro-level spatial inequalities, making the study of their spatial differentiation and the quantification of driving mechanisms essential for implementing targeted conservation strategies. This study examines 412 TTVNS using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE), accessibility-based clustering, Optimal Parameter Geographical Detector (OPGD), Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR), and Random Forest with SHAP (RF–SHAP) to identify spatial patterns and quantify the mechanisms influencing them. The results indicate that: (1) TTVNS display a “multi-core clustering with contiguous distribution” pattern, forming two northeast–southwest aggregation belts, with significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran’s I = 0.175); (2) in single-factor detection, Cultivated Land (X3, q = 0.3019), Population (X19, q = 0.2510), and Road Density (X13, q = 0.2303) are the strongest explanatory factors, while the strongest interaction occurs between Temperature (X9) and Population (X19, q = 0.406), demonstrating that spatial differentiation is driven by the coupling of environmental suitability and social support rather than any single factor; (3) model comparison shows that MGWR substantially outperforms OLS and GWR, with R² increasing from 0.3049 and 0.3246 to 0.6568, confirming pronounced spatial non-stationarity in the driving mechanisms of TTVNS; (4) different categories of drivers exhibit distinct pathways: nature and geography influence aggregation through cultivated land, river systems, and temperature; location and transportation shape a “node–corridor” settlement pattern along valley corridors; humanities and religion affect clustering through the coupling of religious nodes and local social structures; society and economy reshape contemporary spatial patterns primarily via tourism development and population dynamics. These findings demonstrate that the spatial differentiation of TTVNS emerges under long-term natural constraints and religious-cultural networks, and continues to be reshaped by modern transportation and tourism development. The study provides a quantitative basis for designing differentiated and context-specific conservation strategies.

title: Research on the impact of artificial intelligence on the pollution governance mechanism and pathways in border regions
abstract: Abstract Boundary pollution poses obstacles to environmental governance and industrial upgrading, while traditional monitoring methods fail to provide a fundamental solution. Drawing on data from boundary prefecture-level cities between 2016 and 2022, this paper delves into the governance effect of artificial intelligence (AI) on boundary pollution. The research reveals that AI significantly improves the situation of boundary pollution, breaking down market segmentation, enhancing supervision, and addressing negative externalities through positive spillover effects. Furthermore, the development of AI suppresses pollution in adjacent regions through economic ties, mitigating the negative impact of competition among local governments. This suppressive effect is particularly pronounced in regions with low levels of regional collaboration and contiguous poverty-stricken regions. Consequently, the government should attach great importance to the role of digital technology in boundary pollution control, strengthen cooperation with the market, foster regional economic ties, and promote green and high-quality economic development in boundary regions, ultimately achieving sustainable development goals.

title: Early disaster response to extreme heat in modern Shanghai, 1873–1949: limited preparedness and unequal protection
abstract: As extreme heat has become one of the most deadly climate risks in cities today, a fundamental question is rarely asked: where does a city’s heat-disaster response capacity actually come from? Taking Shanghai from 1873 to 1949 as a case study, this study reconstructs summer extreme heat events by integrating Xujiahui Observatory temperature observations with modern newspapers and municipal archives. Focusing on three representative years (1894, 1934, and 1942), this study compares how heat shocks were transformed into social impacts and governance responses under different institutional contexts. The findings show that the early heat response in modern Shanghai did not arise from a mature policy system, but was rather a patchwork of limited preparedness cobbled together from existing channels of public communication, public health, municipal coordination, social relief, and administrative control. More importantly, this seemingly evolving response system was consistently accompanied by deep-seated unequal protection. Different social groups and urban districts faced vastly different levels of risk exposure and access to relief in the face of heatwaves. There was no linear relationship between heat intensity and social impact; governance interventions could buffer risk in some contexts, but unequal protection remained the norm. Limited preparedness and unequal protection, therefore, constituted the central features of early heat-disaster response in modern Shanghai. The historical experience uncovered in this study reminds us that the legacy of heat-disaster response is not merely a story of technological evolution, but also a long-term challenge concerning equity and governance capacity.

title: Encountering a newcomer attenuates shared evaluative standards: experimental evidence of rapid emergence and partial persistence
abstract: Abstract Collective activity requires individuals to converge on common yardsticks for judging the world; however, it remains unclear how these evaluative standards (ES) respond when a group encounters unfamiliar members. Using a newly developed dot-estimation task informed by Sherif’s classic norm-formation studies, this study experimentally tracked (a) how shared ES emerge through dyadic interactions and (b) how they respond to a newcomer whose judgements systematically diverge. Participants first completed rounds with a partner whose estimates gradually aligned with their own, with perceptual bias shifting reliably toward that partner’s standard within a single block of thirty trials. However, when a newcomer with divergent estimates entered, participants partially shifted toward the newcomer’s standard, while their responses suggested carryover from the prior interaction. Impressions of the divergent newcomer did not depend on whether participants had previously established a shared standard with another partner, indicating that brief behavioural alignment does not by itself generate derogation of a divergent other. Taken together, these findings show that shared ES form quickly through dyadic interaction and, although attenuated by exposure to a newcomer, persist in part within individuals. Understanding the micro-dynamics of their formation and partial persistence helps explain how groups negotiate common standards and how those standards may attenuate—without fully unravelling—when group composition changes.

title: Digital fiscal transfers, macroeconomic stability, and credit risk in frontier financial systems: evidence from Uganda’s microfinance deposit-taking institutions
abstract: The expansion of digital fiscal transfers across developing economies since the COVID-19 pandemic has transformed access to finance for marginalized communities, yet their macro financial implications for institutional risk remain underexplored. This study provides novel empirical evidence on how macro financial dynamics and digital fiscal transfers jointly influence credit risk in Uganda’s microfinance deposit-taking institutions (MDIs) using monthly data from September 2022 to July 2025 and an Autoregressive Distributed Lag model. Results show that, in the short run, higher MDI capital, customer deposits, and E-money inflows reduce credit risk, highlighting the stabilizing role of institutional liquidity buffers and digital fiscal inflows, while increased loan loss provisions signal heightened portfolio vulnerability. Inflation temporarily eases credit risk by lowering real debt burdens. In the long run, the system exhibits cointegration, but only economic activity exerts a significant influence on credit risk. Stronger economic activity is associated with higher credit risk, implying procyclical risk behavior, with 14.7 percent of disequilibrium adjusted monthly. The evidence suggests that Uganda’s MDIs benefit from strong institutional liquidity, digital fiscal inflows, and moderate inflation as short-term stabilizers, but remain vulnerable to procyclical risk taking during periods of economic expansion. This highlights the importance of digitally sound, forward-looking, countercyclical risk-sensitive prudential regulation and coordinated oversight among fiscal, monetary, and digital finance authorities to ensure digital innovation supports inclusive and resilient financial systems in the post-pandemic era. These insights show that fiscal digitalization can enhance financial stability and foster inclusive, sustainable credit growth in frontier markets.

title: Outcomes of a year 3 and year 4 STEM professional development program: teachers’ successes, challenges, and insights
abstract: Amid growing pressure for science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) integration in primary education, many classroom teachers continue to face uncertainty in teaching STEM with confidence. Traditional Professional Development (PD) models often fall short in translating new knowledge into sustainable practice. This study responds to these challenges by investigating a contextually embedded community “outreach” STEM PD program, situated, facilitated, and designed in a university, by university STEM facilitators, to support regional teachers. Uniquely positioned in a regional setting, the PD supported Year 3 and Year 4 teachers through collaborative learning, reflective dialogue, and context-aligned resources. Drawing on focus group interviews with participating teachers, thematic analysis revealed three key themes: the teacher’s successes, challenges, and insights. Teachers also shared critical insights about the need for contextual relevance, time to experiment, and ongoing support. Challenges identified included limited access to resources, curriculum constraints, and systemic barriers to innovation. Rather than offering a one-size-fits-all solution, this study presents a model of outreach PD that is adaptive, collaborative, and responsive to local, regional classroom needs. The findings contribute to current debates on how to design equitable, meaningful STEM PD, particularly in regional areas. By centring teacher voice and pedagogical practice, this research offers a replicable and scalable model for advancing STEM capacity for teachers in primary schools.

title: Hedonic pricing of wine attributes in Hungarian online retail: the Tokaj noble rot wines
abstract: Tokaji Aszu (a botrytised noble rot wine) is one of Hungary’s most renowned wine styles and an essential part of its viticultural heritage. This paper investigates the determinants of wine prices in the Hungarian online retail market, focusing on Tokaj wines. A hedonic pricing framework and a quantile regression approach are employed to analyse how the main wine attributes (e.g. origin or quality classifications) influence online retail prices across different market segments. The analysis is based on a cross-sectional dataset comprising 1,216 observations, including Hungarian and imported products. The findings indicate that vintage, import status, Tokaj-related characteristics, organic certification, and wine classification are significantly associated with observed retail prices, although the magnitudes vary across quantiles. The negative vintage coefficient indicates that earlier vintages are associated with higher observed prices, implying higher premiums for aged wines. Wines produced in the Tokaj wine region and classified as Tokaj botrytised noble rot wine demonstrate positive price differentials, confirming the quality and terroir-driven reputation of this Hungarian appellation. Moreover, organic-certified and superior quality (Premier/Grand Cru) wines exhibit positive price associations, whereas Selection labels show smaller effects across specifications. The most pronounced price effects are concentrated in the upper quantiles, indicating that in high-end wines, exceptional value is placed on heritage, scarcity, and symbolic quality cues. The research provides new empirical evidence on wine price differentiation in the Hungarian online retail market. It highlights how historical reputation, sustainability, and quality signals jointly influence wine pricing, reflecting heterogeneity across conditional price distribution.

title: Insurance, risk, and society: understanding earthquake insurance uptake in a high-risk country
abstract: Abstract This study aims to examine the supply and demand dynamics of disasters, insurance, particularly earthquake-focused policies, through a qualitative analysis of Türkiye. Despite being located in a region with a high earthquake risk, Türkiye faces significant challenges due to insufficient public awareness and participation in the insurance system. The primary motivation of this research is to understand the current state of the insurance framework designed to mitigate the devastating impacts of earthquakes and to identify areas for improvement. Employing a qualitative research approach, the study conducted in-depth interviews with two key stakeholders in the insurance sector: insurance agents and households, which represent policyholders. This method allowed for a comprehensive analysis of the economic, social, cultural, and structural factors influencing both the supply and demand for earthquake insurance from multiple angles. The findings reveal that, especially in developing countries, increasing the prevalence of disaster insurance depends not only on legal regulations but also critically relies on raising social awareness and building trust within communities. Based on these insights, the study offers concrete recommendations aimed at policymakers and industry representatives to strengthen the insurance system. The results obtained from the Turkish context are expected to serve as a guiding reference for other countries facing similar risk profiles.

title: Dialectical reflections on collectivism: Does the Long March Imprint of executives influence financial decisions?—Empirical evidence from China
abstract: The Long March constitutes a significant cultural symbol in modern Chinese history; however, its influence on micro-level corporate behavior remains underexplored. Grounded in imprinting theory, this study exploits the 80th anniversary commemoration of the Long March victory as an exogenous shock to construct a natural experiment. Using data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2021 and employing a difference-in-differences approach, the impact of executives’ Long March imprint on corporate earnings management is examined. The findings reveal that, from 2016 onward, firms whose executives were born in regions along the Long March route exhibit a significant reduction in earnings management, indicating that the Long March imprint suppresses earnings manipulation behavior. Further analysis demonstrates that the Long March spirit curbs earnings management through two channels: the cultivation of corporate culture and the restraint of managerial self-interest. Heterogeneous effects are observed with respect to external cultural shocks, market attention, government-market relations, and executives’ educational attainment. By introducing cultural memory into the analytical framework of executive decision-making, this study offers a novel perspective on the cultural determinants of corporate earnings management.

title: The influence of transformational teacher leadership behaviours on student self-determination moderated by institutional support and classroom climate: a self-determination theory perspective
abstract: Student self-determination is widely recognised as a critical factor in enhancing learning outcomes in higher education. Although prior research has identified key drivers of perceived self-determination, limited attention has been given to how teachers demonstrating transformational leadership behaviours interact with classroom- and institutional-level dynamics to shape students’ motivational driven learning processes. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory, this study examines the influence of transformational teacher leadership behaviours on student self-determination, with particular emphasis on the moderating roles of classroom climate and institutional support. In doing so, a sequencial explanatory mixed-methods research design was employed involving 436 undergraduate students. Quantitative data were collected from 420 participants using self-reported structured questionnaires, while qualitative insights were obtained from 16 participants through semi-structured interviews. The collected quantitative and qualitative data were then analysed through structural equation modelling and thematic analysis, respectively. The findings indicate that transformational teacher leadership is significantly associated with students’ perceived self-determination. Classroom climate also emerged as both a strong direct predictor and a significant moderating factor, enhancing the positive relationship between transformational teacher leadership and student self-determination. In contrast, institutional support did not demonstrate a significant direct or moderating effect. Qualitative findings further reveal that students’ motivation is primarily shaped by immediate classroom interactions, while institutional factors are perceived as more distant and less impactful. This study contributes to the literature by proposing a contextually grounded model of student self-determination that highlights the importance of proximal classroom dynamics over distal institutional conditions. It provides theoretical and practical insights into how teachers exhibiting transformational leadership behavioursand supportive classroom environments jointly foster students' self-determened learning motivation in higher education.

title: Haji Bushra of Gata and the making of Islamic education in nineteenth-century South Wollo, Ethiopia: institutional formation and community agency
abstract: Abstract Scholarship on Islam in Ethiopia has examined religious authority, scholarly networks, and Muslim communities, but has paid less attention to how local centres of Islamic learning were established and sustained. This article examines Gata Majlis in nineteenth-century South Wollo, focusing on how Haji Bushra’s scholarly authority shaped its formation, how learning continued after his death, and how later generations remembered his role. It also considers the centre within the social and political context of nineteenth-century Wollo and distinguishes its institutional history from later traditions of religious memory and pilgrimage. The study draws on 20 manuscripts, institutional and historical records, 12 semi-structured interviews, two focus-group discussions, and published scholarship. Eight manuscripts were selected for detailed analysis based on provenance, relevance, and textual accessibility, while twelve provided contextual evidence. Historical criticism, textual and thematic analysis examined institutional development, knowledge transmission, community participation, and historical memory. The findings indicate that Haji Bushra was central to Gata Majlis’s formation, but its continuity depended on teachers, students, custodians, families, and local supporters, who sustained instruction, preserved manuscripts, provided material support, and maintained community relationships. The surviving manuscripts provide stronger evidence of Gata’s intellectual tradition and its transmission over time. The article contributes to Ethiopian Islamic historiography by showing how Islamic learning was sustained through community participation, educational practices, and manuscript preservation beyond the lifetime of a prominent scholar. Gata Majlis offers a close example of why the history of Islamic education must account not only for influential scholars but also for the people and practices that carried their traditions across generations.

title: The role of Engicha Nekela ritual in facilitating social and cultural integration in Gojjam, Ethiopia
abstract: The Engicha Nekela festival, a regional variant of the Amhara Ashenda celebration in Gojjam, Ethiopia, serves as a key mechanism for social cohesion and cultural continuity in an agrarian, multi-ethnic community prone to resource disputes. This ethnographic study examines its role in fostering identity, solidarity, and integration through enhanced communication, tension resolution, and intergenerational value transmission. Using qualitative methods (participant observation, in-depth interviews, and focus groups; n ≈ 25–30) in Debre Markos (August 2015–September 2016), data were thematically analyzed. Findings show the ritual promotes integration via communal participation, symbolic cleansing (uprooting/burning “evil weeds” as metaphors for disputes/bad behaviors), hair adornment/shaving (marking transitions), and intergenerational bonding. These elements purge negativity, reinforce shared norms, and balance individual/collective interests in a dispute-prone setting. This paper contributes to ritual studies and the documentation of Ethiopian intangible cultural heritage by demonstrating how seasonal festivals in rural, dispute-prone settings actively foster social resilience.

title: Between transgressive intervention and transboundary coordination: quasi-meta-governance in China’s environmental public interest litigation for sustainable development
abstract: In China’s procuratorate-led Environmental Public Interest Litigation (EPIL) system, the procuratorate has to navigate the dilemma between transboundary coordination and transgressive intervention to achieve effective collaborative governance. To conceptualize this distinctive role, this paper extends meta-governance theory by introducing the concept of the “quasi-meta-governor” to explain how a judicially embedded actor can coordinate fragmented governance networks without possessing fully transcendent authority. Building on this framework, the paper develops a four-party evolutionary game model involving procuratorial organs, administrative departments, polluting enterprises and the public, followed by an empirical examination of its equilibrium dynamics using the institutional evolution of EPIL in Zhoushan, Zhejiang Province. The findings show that quasi-meta-governance strategies, including network activation, resource integration, and agenda cultivation, can promote the transition from fragmented governance toward collaborative equilibrium by reducing coordination costs, integrating governance resources, and reshaping environmental cognition among multiple actors. The paper makes three main contributions. Theoretically, it extends meta-governance theory into the field of judicial supervision through the concept of the quasi-meta-governor and explains how cross-boundary coordination can be achieved under institutional embeddedness without undermining existing authority structures. Methodologically, it introduces a four-party evolutionary game framework into EPIL research to analyze dynamic multi-actor interactions. Empirically, it identifies the institutional mechanisms through which procuratorate-led coordination can transform fragmented environmental governance into a more stable collaborative governance arrangement, offering implications for EPIL institutional optimization.

title: The positive impact of electricity spot trading on ESG performance in energy-intensive enterprises
abstract: Electricity market reforms are vital for global energy transition. Using a firm-level panel dataset of listed companies from 2012 to 2020 and taking China’s electricity spot market pilot project as a quasi-natural experiment with a difference-in-differences-in-differences method, we examine its impact on ESG performance in energy-intensive enterprises. Drawing on a modified Coasean perspective that acknowledges transaction costs and government intervention, we propose both positive and negative pathways. Results show that electricity spot trading (EST) significantly enhances ESG performance through optimized resource allocation, improved employee governance, and enhanced operational stability, while we find no evidence that EST induces managerial short-termism. The positive effect is stronger in regions with higher marketization, particularly those with developed non-state economies, and among enterprises facing greater supplier competition. Both city-level and firm-level evidence further reveal that EST reduces carbon emission intensity, mitigating greenwashing concerns. This study provides Chinese evidence on the micro-level effects of EST and offers policy insights for advancing energy transitions through market mechanisms.

title: Empowering elementary school leaders for inclusive learning: integrating cultural diversity, digital competence, and academic optimism
abstract: Education is a cornerstone for building a more inclusive and equitable society in today’s interconnected and rapidly evolving world. Over the past 20 years, multicultural and inclusive education has become integral to the educational paradigms employed by several education systems worldwide, due to the epistemological emphasis on equal interaction and participation of groups and individuals who, for various reasons, experience marginalization. In culturally diverse educational systems, elementary school leaders play a pivotal role in shaping inclusive learning environments that integrate digital competence and sustain academic optimism. This qualitative study examines how elementary school administrators in North Cyprus support teachers’ digital competence, foster inclusive teaching and learning environments, and conceptualize academic optimism within multicultural school contexts. Using purposive sampling, data were collected through group-based unstructured interviews with 30 public elementary school administrators affiliated with the Ministry of National Education and Culture. Thematic analysis was employed to identify leadership practices that enable inclusive and academically focused schooling. The findings reveal that administrators support teachers’ digital competence indirectly through trust-based, motivational, and collaborative leadership rather than through stand-alone technical interventions. Administrators understand digital competence as a culturally responsive pedagogical capacity designed to equip teachers for the specific instructional demands of culturally diverse classrooms. They also see the creation of an inclusive environment as a normative commitment that should be visible in every dimension of their daily administrative behavior, from the quality of their listening to the fairness of their recognition to the principled universality of their trust advocacy. In addition, administrators understand academic optimism as a dynamic institutional achievement that should be actively cultivated through differentiated recognition, resilient goal management, democratic governance, and collective accountability, an ongoing process.

title: From difference to danger: algorithmic amplification and the digital construction of autism in violence narratives
abstract: Abstract This study examines how autism is constructed as a perceived marker of danger within digitally mediated violence narratives. Drawing on qualitative content analysis as the primary analytical method, complemented by a non-participant digital ethnographic perspective, the article analyzes 40 videos (18 primary and 22 response videos) and 620 user comments from high-visibility content on TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts. The analysis identifies interrelated processes of stigma, labeling, affective intensification, and platform-mediated visibility; algorithmic amplification is treated as an interpretive dimension of the platform context rather than as a directly measured causal effect. To conceptualize this process, the article introduces cyber totemization as a process of symbolic-affective condensation through which complex and internally heterogeneous identities are reduced to simplified, emotionally charged, and circulable markers of risk. Within the sampled high-visibility material, stigmatizing narratives emerged rapidly under conditions of uncertainty, while corrective responses appeared less prominent and more fragile. By integrating sociological theory with contemporary platform scholarship, the study contributes to communication and digital media research by providing a process-oriented account of how stigma is constructed, circulated, contested, and rendered visible in platform-mediated environments. The article further advances a rights-based ethical framework, emphasizing the need to address not only misinformation but the structural conditions that enable the persistence of stigmatizing representations.

title: From green to digital-sustainable HRM: a bibliometric and empirical synthesis toward employee engagement and employee-perceived organisational performance
abstract: Abstract This study integrates bibliometric and empirical evidence to explain how green human resource management (GHRM) and digital readiness are associated with employee engagement and employee-perceived organisational performance. A hybrid design was used. In the bibliometric phase, an initial Scopus search identified 49 records published between 2015 and 2025; after screening for relevance and data quality, 26 publications were retained for analysis to map the convergence of green and digital HRM themes. The empirical phase tested the proposed Green–Digital–Engagement Framework (GDEF) using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) based on 280 valid responses obtained through purposive sampling from selected green-oriented organisational settings in Indonesia. The findings indicate that both GHRM and digital readiness are positively associated with employee engagement, with digital readiness showing the stronger relationship in the present sample. Employee engagement is also positively associated with employee-perceived organisational performance and significantly mediates the relationships of GHRM and digital readiness with that outcome. These results support the role of employee engagement as a behavioural mechanism linking sustainability-oriented HR practices and digital readiness with employees’ perceptions of organisational functioning and effectiveness. The study contributes to digital-sustainable HRM by integrating bibliometric evidence, theoretical reasoning, and employee-level empirical findings within a single explanatory framework. Practically, the findings suggest that organisations may benefit from aligning green-oriented HR practices with digital readiness initiatives and implementing both in ways that strengthen employee participation, clarity, and involvement. The findings should be interpreted within the study’s purposive, context-specific, and employee-perception-based design rather than as evidence of objective firm-level performance or unrestricted generalisability.

title: Service preservation from matching non-matching socks under stochastic loss
abstract: Abstract Socks are produced and replaced at a massive scale, yet their paired use makes them unusually vulnerable to service loss, as the disappearance of a single sock can leave usable wear-capacity stranded and create sockless days even when functional socks remain available. In this study, we examine whether pairing non-matching “orphan” socks can preserve daily sock service under stochastic loss, and how this benefit trades off against perceived social discomfort. We formalize sock ownership as a sequential decision problem under uncertainty in which socks wear out and disappear stochastically during laundering, while public exposure induces a person-specific mismatch penalty. We conducted an in-person study to estimate mismatch sensitivity and diversity preference, linking behavioral heterogeneity to interpretable mixing policies. Using these results, an exact benchmark on small tractable instances, and a simulation-based evaluation of pairing policies, we show that strict matching can appear resource-frugal largely because it generates many sockless days. In contrast, controlled tolerance for mismatch sustains service and reduces stranded wear-capacity across loss regimes. The ecological-cost term is treated as a proportional embodied-cost proxy rather than an independent life-cycle assessment measure, so the environmental interpretation is suggestive and mechanism-based rather than a direct estimate of environmental savings. This study establishes the feasibility and limitations of matching non-matching socks as a simple strategy for preserving service from already-owned garments.

title: From narrative generation to interpretive stabilization: generative AI and the mechanism of ethical understanding
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly reshaping narrative practices through character monologues and emotionally guided storytelling on digital platforms such as Bilibili and Chinese TikTok. While existing AI ethics scholarship has primarily focused on issues of bias, transparency, and governance, it offers limited explanatory power for understanding how generative systems reorganize the interpretive conditions under which moral judgment is formed. To address this gap, this study develops Generative Interpretive Mediation (GIM) as a mechanism-based framework for analyzing how GenAI intervenes in interpretive processes prior to explicit ethical evaluation. Based on an interpretive research design, the article examines widely circulated AI-generated character monologues as analytically selected cases of platform-mediated narrative production. The analysis identifies three interrelated operations: interpretive selection, interpretive pre-structuring, and interpretive orientation. Together, these operations do not simply produce narratives, but stabilize interpretation by reducing narrative ambiguity and guiding users toward coherent psychological trajectories. In doing so, GenAI often replaces sustained interpretive effort with pre-shaped explanatory closure, thereby reshaping how understanding is formed in everyday engagement with digital narratives. By bringing narrative hermeneutics into dialogue with behavioral accounts of the “illusion of understanding” and “decisional inertia,” the article situates GIM within an emerging epistemic turn in AI ethics. It argues that the central ethical concern of GenAI lies not primarily in biased outputs, but in its capacity to reorganize interpretive environments in ways that subtly condition the formation of public moral judgment.

title: Dionysus in China: cultural transmission and transformation in Dunhuang’s Grape Harvest Worshipping Festival
abstract: During China’s medieval period (Wei 魏 to Song 宋 Dynasties), the Silk Road facilitated vibrant cultural exchanges, exemplified by Dunhuang’s Grape Harvest Worshipping Festival 敦煌結葡萄賽神節 under the Tang Dynasty’s Guiyi Army 歸義軍. This festival, focused on agricultural abundance and the ritual worship of grapes, appears to reflect distant resonances of Greek Dionysian practices, possibly transmitted via Sogdian intermediaries. Through a comprehensive study of Dunhuang manuscripts, visual iconography, and comparative ritual analysis, this paper argues that the festival represents a localized rearticulation of Dionysian symbolism within the Chinese agrarian and cosmological system. By incorporating both textual and material sources, and engaging recent scholarship on ritual hybridization, transculturation, and symbolic translation, this research situates Dunhuang’s ritual culture within a broader matrix of Silk Road exchanges.

title: Beyond AI detection: traceable assessment design for generative AI-supported professional coursework
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) challenges final-product-only coursework assessment: a polished report or design proposal may no longer show how students used AI, which claims they checked, how they attributed sources and AI contributions, or what they revised. This study examined traceable assessment design as a practical response. Rather than relying on AI detection or broad permission rules, assessment tasks were redesigned to collect evidence of students’ AI use, verification, attribution, feedback-mediated revision, and reflective judgement. Using a multi-cycle action research design with an embedded mixed-methods approach, we studied two professional courses: anatomy and physiology as the main evaluation setting and modern microscopy as a secondary adaptation setting. Data sources included coursework, AI-use statements, verification logs, assessment records, student interviews, teacher redesign logs, and traceability-related process indicators. In the main setting, the redesign class recorded higher cumulative report scores than the comparison class (21.59 vs 17.91/30; mean difference = 3.68, 95% CI [1.80, 5.56], Welch t (63.1) = 3.91, p < 0.001, d = 0.96). Of this difference, 3.29 points (89.4%) were concentrated in the redesign-targeted disclosure/citation, verification, and reflection dimensions, compared with 0.39 points across physiology accuracy and the data/evidence chain. The redesign class also recorded higher scores on a design-aligned ethics-focused assessment (14.53 vs 12.36/20; mean difference = 2.17, 95% CI [1.08, 3.26], Welch t (63.9) = 3.99, p < 0.001, d = 0.98), which was not independent evidence of broader ethical learning. Neither OSPE comparison was statistically significant ( p = 127 and 0.334). Across implementation phases, AI-use statement uptake was 88.2% and 91.2%, and verification-log completeness was 1.44 and 1.74. In microscopy, group report scores across three technically different assignments (7.60, 8.03, and 8.60/10) were interpreted descriptively, not as longitudinal improvement. Traceable assessment thus made students’ documented GenAI use, verification, attribution, and revision more inspectable without establishing improved disciplinary learning.

title: Digital transformation in healthcare: a systematic and bibliometric review of strategies, policies, barriers, and benefits
abstract: Digital transformation (DT) in healthcare has traditionally been conceptualized through models that privilege either technological or organizational perspectives. However, this study shows that DT cannot be understood as a linear or purely technical process but rather as a dynamic adjustment among policy frameworks, organizational capabilities, and technological change. To capture this complexity, we conducted a systematic and integrative review that combined bibliometric mapping and a grounded qualitative synthesis of literature published between 2010 and 2025, guided by three research questions: (RQ1) What are the key themes and trends in healthcare DT? (RQ2) What policy-level barriers and enablers shape its development? and (RQ3) What strategic challenges and benefits influence DT in healthcare institutions? Findings reveal that prevailing models—such as the HIMSS EMRAM and McKinsey 7S frameworks—offer valuable benchmarks but remain limited by static and technocentric assumptions. Building on these insights, this study proposes an integrated framework grounded in Social Systems Theory, which conceptualizes DT as an adaptive system characterized by iterative feedback, learning, and recalibration across policy, organizational, and technological domains. The framework contributes both a theoretical advancement toward an evolutionary understanding of DT and a practical roadmap for policymakers and healthcare managers aiming to build sustainable, interoperable, and human-centered health systems.

title: Mapping interdependencies among challenges to artificial intelligence adoption in drug discovery
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) offers significant potential to accelerate drug discovery, yet its adoption remains constrained by interdependent technical, organizational, and regulatory barriers. This study applies Fuzzy DEMATEL to analyze twelve challenges and uncover their causal structure using expert judgments expressed as triangular fuzzy numbers. Following normalization and CFCS defuzzification, Resistance to Change, Lack of Standardization, Limited Trust in AI Outputs, Talent Shortage, and Lack of Clinical Validation emerge as the primary causal drivers. These upstream barriers exert strong influence on downstream effects, including Regulatory Barriers, Biological Complexity, Integration with Legacy Systems, and Poor Data Quality. The findings indicate that several constraints commonly viewed as external are, in practice, manifestations of internal organizational and technical shortcomings. By providing a structured causal prioritization of barriers, this study offers actionable guidance for targeting high-leverage interventions in AI-enabled drug discovery. Findings reflect expert judgment within a North Cyprus context and should be interpreted as indicative organizational signals rather than universal prescriptions.

title: Combating linguicide through pronunciation and voice reclamation: shadowing as an identity practice
abstract: This study investigates voice reclamation as a countermeasure to linguicidal processes that erode speakers’ confidence in their phonological identity. Using a mixed-methods quasi-experimental design, we examined how a shadowing-based intervention, embedded in sociophonetic awareness workshops, shaped the interplay between pronunciation, identity, and agency among 120 undergraduate English majors in Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Quantitative data included a Voice Confidence Scale (VCS) and acoustic analysis of speech rate, pitch range, and pausing patterns; qualitative evidence was drawn from reflective voice diaries and semi-structured interviews. Voice confidence increased significantly in both cohorts (a mean gain of approximately 30%), accompanied by modest, non-significant prosodic shifts that participants framed as more intentional pausing and individualized pitch adjustment. The findings suggest that shadowing, when reframed within a Voice Reclamation Framework rather than a native-speaker imitation paradigm, can reposition the learner’s voice as a site of self-recognition and cultural negotiation. The study contributes to applied linguistics, sociophonetics, and World Englishes research by showing how embodied voice practices may support identity ownership and contest deficit-based narratives in global English, while acknowledging that acoustic change over a four-week intervention remained limited.

title: Decentralization in Ghana: noble intentions under harsh realities in the agricultural sector
abstract: Abstract In Ghana, decentralisation has gained significant importance as a strategy to address localized challenges and ensure effective public service delivery. The Agriculture Department is an integral part of the Metropolitan, Municipal, and District Assemblies (MMDAs), with the underlying vision to foster decentralised agricultural extension services. Underpinned by the Soufflé theory of decentralization, the study utilised a qualitative research approach to gain insights into governments efforts to strengthen decentralization and the harsh realities militating against decentralized agricultural extension service delivery in Ghana. It revealed that governments have introduced institutional reforms and legal frameworks to strengthen decentralisation. However, severe challenges, including irregular funding, recentralization of central government procurement, and the actions of some development partners undermine the decentralization process. The study argues that the capping of the DACF and persistent delay in the disbursement of same render the MMDAs ineffective and underscore the predicaments that circumscribe agricultural extension services delivery in Ghana.

title: Exploring intentions to adopt GenAI in academia: perceived usefulness and attitudes among scholars and researchers
abstract: This study aims to investigate scholars’ and researchers’ perceptions, attitudes, and intentions toward using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in academic research. Employing a cross-sectional survey, data were collected from 1,283 participants in China. After removing missing values, 1150 valid responses were analyzed. Results indicate that perceived usefulness of GenAI was positively associated with attitudes (β = 0.489, p < 0.001) and directly associated with usage intention (β = 0.385, p < 0.001). Furthermore, attitudes toward GenAI had a positive effect on usage intention (β = 0.323, p < 0.001) and mediated the association between perceived usefulness and intention (indirect effect = 0.157, Boot95% CI [0.120, 0.199]). These findings underscore that positive perceptions of GenAI’s usefulness are associated with more favorable attitudes and stronger intentions to adopt it in research. By applying the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to GenAI adoption, this study highlights the need for academic institutions to promote responsible use through ethical guidelines, training programs, and awareness campaigns, which may facilitate effective integration into research practices.

title: Market risks, varietal diversification, and operating income among China’s peach farmers
abstract: This study examines the drivers of varietal selection by peach farmers and the operating income consequences of varietal diversification using a 2022 farm survey of 924 producers in Jiangsu, Hubei, Anhui, and Shandong. We develop a conceptual framework linking markets, farmer behaviour and income, estimate count models for varietal number alongside income regressions with quadratic terms, complemented by quantile and heterogeneity analyses and robustness checks. The evidence shows that nursery stock risk, sales channel dependence, and hiring difficulty each significantly increase the number of varieties cultivated, with farmer age moderating the labour constraint effect in an inverted U pattern. These results are robust across ordinary least squares and maximum likelihood estimations and after winsorisation. Diversification exhibits an inverted U relationship with operating income in the full sample, with the turning point lying within the observed range and shifting upward with farm size. Quantile regressions indicate that the marginal income gain from additional varieties declines along the income distribution. Market conditions shape payoffs: in high risk segments, the positive income effect of diversification weakens while the negative effect strengthens. Heterogeneity tests show that a higher share of early-maturing peaches dampens the benefits of adding varieties, whereas a higher share of late-maturing peaches enhances them; farmers specialising in flat peaches gain more from diversification than those focusing on honey peaches. Planting locally leading cultivars allows farmers to hedge risks while leveraging regional spillovers. These findings clarify the behavioural logic of varietal diversification in a perennial fruit sector and inform policies on seedling market governance, marketing infrastructure, labour services, and regional varietal layout.

title: How balance, contour, symmetry, and complexity predict the perceived emotions in Chinese traditional music
abstract: Understanding how musical structure shapes emotion perception remains a central question in music psychology, yet the role of mid-level structural features in Chinese traditional music is underexplored. This study investigated how balance, contour, symmetry, and complexity (BCSC framework) predict perceived emotions in Chinese traditional music using both linear (Lasso-selected multiple regression) and nonlinear (random forest regression) modeling approaches. Analyses included dimensional emotions (valence, arousal) and seven discrete emotions (anger, gentleness, happiness, peacefulness, sadness, solemnness, transcendence). Linear regressions showed that BCSC features explained 35.1% of variance in valence and 37.1% in arousal. For valence, Total Asymmetry (β = 0.266, p < 0.001), Average Local First-Order Entropy (β = 0.862, p < 0.001), Third-Order Duration Entropy (β = 0.511, p = 0.022), and Event Density (β = −0.890, p < 0.001) were among the strongest predictors.
