For arousal, Duration Abruptness, Total Asymmetry, Average Local First-Order Entropy, and Third-Order Duration Entropy were significant positive predictors (all ps < 0.01), while Rhythmic Abruptness, Event Density, and First-Order Duration Entropy showed significant negative effects (all ps < 0.001). For discrete emotions, predictive power ranged from adjusted R² = 0.157 (peacefulness) to 0.386 (happiness), with emotion-specific patterns: e.g., Bi-Unbalance (β = 0.316, p < 0.001) predicted anger, while First-Order Duration Entropy had opposing effects for anger (β = −0.252, p < 0.001) and peacefulness (β = 0.403, p < 0.001). Nonlinear models confirmed feature importance patterns, highlighting the roles of temporal irregularity, melodic interval size, and structural imbalance. Overall, these findings demonstrate that mid-level structural features provide systematic elements that serve as emotional cues for perceived emotions in Chinese traditional music.

title: Data is not knowledge: Hayek’s epistemological challenge to artificial intelligence
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is routinely described as a knowledge technology. This paper argues that the description misplaces a boundary Hayek drew in 1945, between “scientific knowledge”—codifiable, statistical, articulable—and “knowledge of the particular circumstances of time and place.” Kiesling (2015) reconstructs part of the latter as the contextual knowledge problem: knowledge that does not exist outside the interaction producing it, as against the complexity problem of aggregating knowledge that exists dispersed but can in principle be codified. The reconstruction is interpretive and identifies a generative subset of Hayek’s category rather than its whole content; much of the remainder is knowledge agents already possess, and AI dissolves a good deal of it. The argument is not that machine systems cannot discover novel alternatives, nor that their search spaces are closed; both are conceded. It is that discovering means does not originate the ultimate ends by reference to which alternatives acquire economic significance, and that current systems receive those ends rather than constituting them. Under a Misesian account of evaluative agency—a premise the paper declares rather than derives—better aggregation, prediction and optimisation therefore cannot by themselves resolve the generative subset, so neither Polanyian tacit knowledge in large language models nor microstructure price discovery by high-frequency traders reaches it. The taxonomy is applied at three levels—the data pipeline, the tacit-knowledge debate, and the institutional conditions of price generation—as three applications of one classification rather than three independent demonstrations. Its products are a set of operational tests, none of which has been run and which are here read against a published Q-learning pricing architecture, and a criterion distinguishing context-preserving from context-suppressing deployment at the level of the market.

title: Demand structure transition, policy interventions and China’s grain security: A DSGE-based investigation of self-sufficiency dynamics
abstract: Confronted with the transformation of grain demand structure and the risks of short-term demand surges induced by the upgrading of residents’ dietary patterns, as well as the frequent occurrence of geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters, how to stabilize the grain self-sufficiency rate through precise policy interventions has emerged as a pivotal issue in China’s grain security governance. This study first employs the random forest approach for variable selection. On this basis, we construct a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) model comprising heterogeneous households (farm households and general households) and multiple production sectors (staple food, soybean, and non-grain sectors). The model systematically incorporates a total of seven categories of exogenous shocks: demand shocks for staple food and soybean, production technology shocks for the two grain types, production subsidy shocks, and agricultural machinery purchase subsidy shocks for farm households. Simulation analysis reveals that: (1) Sudden demand shocks are the primary factor driving short-term fluctuations in grain prices and affecting the real purchasing power of residents, while also eroding grain self-sufficiency rate; (2) Production technology shocks represent the fundamental force underlying the long-term evolution of grain output and self-sufficiency rate. Positive technology shocks can significantly raise the grain self-sufficiency rate and improve residents’ consumption welfare, which highlights the core role of technological progress in safeguarding national grain security. (3) Both production subsidies and agricultural machinery purchase subsidies are effective in coping with external shocks. The former delivers direct and rapid effects in stabilizing grain output and ensuring supply in the short run, whereas the latter focuses more on enhancing systemic resilience through long-term capital accumulation. The two policies are heterogeneous in terms of their mechanism and time effectiveness. This study provides a dynamic quantitative basis for optimizing the agricultural support policy system and systematically enhancing grain security capacity in a complex and volatile domestic and international environment.

title: Tensions in integration: a qualitative exploration of clinical psychologists’ integration of various knowledge types in psychotherapy
abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to gain knowledge about how peer-nominated clinical psychologists describe their use of different knowledge types in psychotherapy practice. This may miigate the knowledge gap concerning clinical expertise and how clinical experts integrate various knowledge types in practice. Clinical psychologists ( N = 16) who had been recommended by their co-workers were included. The participants were interviewed using semi-structured qualitative interviews. The transcripts of the interviews were subjected to hermeneutic phenomenological thematic analysis. Most of the therapists in the sample described tensions in how they integrated different knowledge types in psychotherapy practice. These tensions in integration were expressed through four themes: (a) Evidence is not carved in stone; (b) The individual beyond categories: (c) Embodied professional practice; and (d) Psychotherapy’s contextual dimension. This study provides empirically grounded insight into these real-world decision-making processes, contributing to a debate previously shaped primarily by theoretical and normative accounts. The participants did not reject research evidence. Tensions arose when evidence derived from group-level trials were applied to individual patients and when clinical guidelines encountered patients who did not fit the categories for which the guidelines had been developed. The results suggest a conception of knowledge that differs from the one commonly associated with evidence-based practice in psychology. Whereas evidence-based practice in psychology describes integration in terms of bringing together three forms of knowledge, the participants’ accounts portray integration as sustained engagement with tensions among them that cannot be fully resolved. Drawing on previous research and literature, we discuss how understanding integration in terms of tension may preserve a space for clinical judgment that an emphasis on unification risks constraining. We conclude that integration is not a straightforward process of combining different elements but a dynamic, dialectical practice requiring continuous reflection and adjustment.

title: Layered transitions: the strategic evolution of scripted content in European premium television (2002–2019)
abstract: Abstract The paper analyzes the evolution of premium television in Europe from 2002 to 2019 through an institutionalist lens, emphasizing the layered and incremental transformation of programming strategies. Drawing on a manually curated dataset of 1134 television series distributed by premium operators, we combine longitudinal analysis of programming catalogs with log-linear growth models and bootstrap resampling to examine shifts in the balance between scripted and unscripted content, and between original productions and broadcast-originated series. Our findings support two hypotheses: first, that scripted content gradually gained prominence without displacing unscripted formats, exemplifying a process of institutional layering; and second, that the growth of scripted programming rested throughout on a combination of original commissioning and licensed acquisition, with neither superseding the other. The shift proceeded without identifiable phase boundaries: scripted content remained below a quarter of new titles until 2006, passed half from 2014, and reached 80% by 2019, while unscripted output continued to grow throughout. This study reveals how European premium operators strategically adapted within existing institutional structures, offering a new framework for understanding contemporary television production in transnational, multi-platform contexts.

title: Blackmail, economic efficiency and libertarianism
abstract: Abstract The present paper deals with the economics of blackmail, having assumed – in line with the most recent libertarian scholarship—that certain blackmail exchanges would constitute fraud and would be therefore impermissible. It is for that reason that our economic analysis is narrowed down to permissible (i.e., non-fraudulent) blackmail exchanges. First, we tackle the allocative efficiency of a regime wherein blackmail exchanges would be legal. Here, our argument is Coasean in nature. Given negligible transaction costs and ignoring any external costs and benefits, permitting blackmail would produce private efficiencies and would be under the said assumptions superior to a regime with blackmail banned. However, onḍce we start considering both positive and negative externalities, our simplified models can at most yield an agnostic verdict. That is, we cannot determine purely economically whether delegalizing would, all in all, increase or decrease social welfare . Finally, we argue that permitting blackmail seems to fare, everything else equal, worse than banning it as far as dynamic efficiency is concerned. More specifically, with blackmail being legal, some actors would be incentivized to invest some resources in digging up the information that they might in the end decide not to reveal for money, with discovering the information thus transpiring to be wasteful.

title: The contemporary dispute over personhood: ontological roots and ethical implications
abstract: The concept of person holds a pivotal role in contemporary ethical, legal, and philosophical debates, yet its meaning has become increasingly fragmented. A notable feature of this fragmentation is the conceptual separation between “human being” and “person,” particularly in bioethical and legal contexts, where personhood is often defined in functionalist or psychological terms—such as self-awareness, autonomy, or relational capacity. These redefinitions resonate with broader cultural currents, including posthumanist tendencies that challenge the boundaries and identity of the human itself. This article argues that such views reflect a deeper philosophical rupture: the weakening of realist ontological accounts of the person. As a result, dignity is no longer viewed as intrinsic, but as contingent and variable, undermining moral protections for the most vulnerable human beings. In response, this study advocates a return to an ontologically grounded account of the person. Building upon the classical tradition of Boethius and Thomas Aquinas, and enriched by Leonardo Polo’s notion of the personal act of being, it proposes a framework in which personhood is understood as a subsistent reality rooted in being—not in capacities or social recognition. Polo’s metaphysical approach deepens the classical view by highlighting the structural link between being, freedom, and transcendence. The article defends the thesis that human dignity presupposes being: personhood is grounded in what a human being is rather than in what a human being is capable of doing. It argues that a realist metaphysical anthropology offers a stable and inclusive foundation for human dignity in contemporary bioethical discourse.

title: Characterizing diverse student behaviors, interactions, and perceptions with GAI-augmented learning analytics tool
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI)-enhanced learning analytics tools can support programming education by combining personalized assistance with access to individual and peer learning information. However, little is known about how students engage with self- and peer-oriented resources in these environments or how different patterns of engagement relate to the quality of their interactions with GAI and their perceptions of it. This study adopted a multi-method approach to examine students’ behavioral patterns while using a learner-facing learning analytics tool associated with a GAI-supported programming platform, along with the corresponding interaction qualities and perceptual evaluations. Using fine-grained behavioral trace data, stage-specific clustering identified three initial profiles (Deep, Self-Oriented, and Peer-Oriented Explorers), and an additional final-stage profile, Limited Explorers. Peer-generated information was examined as a social reference frame for comparison and reflection, and the clusters exhibited distinct patterns of engagement with self- and peer-generated content. Although perceptions of GAI were generally favorable, they did not differ significantly across the final-stage profiles. These findings underscore the importance of tailoring pedagogical support to learners’ stage-specific engagement profiles and current task status. The study concludes by proposing profile-informed, adaptive feedback and GAI-supported scaffolding, while calling for longitudinal research to trace individual transitions between engagement profiles in GAI-augmented programming education.

title: Vertical spatial mismatch of cropland: assessment of gains and losses, driving factors, and governance strategies
abstract: Driven by urban expansion, land-finance dependence, and agricultural restructuring, traditional grain croplands are increasingly displaced into high-slope zones, creating a global vertical spatial mismatch known as the slope-climbing of cropland (SCCL). However, fine-grained, process-based assessments of its productivity and ecological losses, as well as its multi-dimensional causal mechanisms, remain poorly understood. This study couples a “cropland slope-climbing index” with “micro-plot tracking” to dynamically quantify net changes in cropland productivity (CLP) and habitat quality. We further establish a three-dimensional “forcing-inducing-pushing” framework to disentangle SCCL’s underlying drivers. Empirical results from China’s Two Lakes Region (2000–2020) indicate that SCCL intensified over time, generating substantial net deficits in both CLP and ecological services. The share of high-slope cropland rose from 15.87% to 17.40%, with net ecological degradation observed in more than 84% of administrative units. Factor detection reveals that the explanatory power of fixed asset investment, the urban construction land growth rate, and the added value of secondary and tertiary industries strengthened continuously, while local government land transfer revenue consistently exerted a dominant structural influence. These findings demonstrate how rigid requisition–compensation balance mandates, driven by land-finance dependence, fuel this unsustainable vertical mismatch. Crucially, our dynamic analysis reveals that ex-post engineering remediation cannot fully offset the baseline losses induced by SCCL. Consequently, we propose a systemic policy framework that integrates cause-based source prevention and loss-type-differentiated correction to mitigate this vertical spatial conflict.

title: The role of religiosity in labour pain management among Orthodox Christian and Muslim women in Greece
abstract: Religiosity is increasingly recognised as a factor associated with psychological resilience; however, its specific role in the subjective appraisal of childbirth pain remains underexplored. Set within the sociocultural context of Greece, a predominantly Orthodox Christian country with a diverse Muslim minority, this cross-sectional study has a dual aim: to compare self-reported labour pain perceptions between Orthodox Christian and Muslim women, and to evaluate individual religiosity as an independent predictor of pain intensity. A convenience sample of 121 postpartum women assessed within 24–48 h of delivery was recruited, comprising 63 Orthodox Christian and 58 Muslim participants who had undergone spontaneous vaginal deliveries without the use of epidural analgesia. Individual religiosity was measured using a scale based on the Sethi and Seligman model. Pain perception was evaluated using the Perception of Labour Pain Questionnaire, a multidimensional self-report rating scale. Data were analysed using group comparisons and linear regression models. Muslim women reported lower overall pain scores compared to Orthodox Christian participants (p < 0.001). While overall religiosity scores were comparable between groups, higher individual religiosity emerged as an independent predictor of lower perceived pain (B = −0.18, p = 0.038). Higher educational attainment was associated with higher pain scores (B = 2.18, p = 0.008). Group differences emerged in specific pain dimensions, with Orthodox Christian women reporting higher scores regarding the physical nature of pain and external medical stressors. Individual religiosity was associated with lower perceived labour pain, while group differences by religious affiliation appeared intertwined with migrant and cultural background. Rather than implying a direct causal effect on physiological pain expression, it is argued that sociodemographic and theological factors provide distinct cultural scripts for navigating childbirth.

title: Knowledge and meaning in a technology-driven world: a rapid review
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), virtual and augmented reality, the Internet of Things (IoT), and the Internet of Everything (IoE), has reshaped human life, raising existential questions and challenging traditional sources of meaning. This study addresses the problem of how these technological transformations affect individuals’ processes of meaning-making and the management of knowledge in the digital era. The aim of this study is to examine the relationship between digital technologies, digital literacy, and knowledge management, with a particular focus on their implications for existential inquiry and meaningful engagement with technology. A rapid review methodology was applied to analyze 18 peer-reviewed studies indexed in Scopus, published between 2010 and 2024. The analysis explored their relevance to existentialism, meaning-making, and human existence in the context of digital technologies. The thematic analysis identified five key themes: AI and existential concerns, technology and human experience, embodied cognition and technology, digital literacy and knowledge management, and technology and meaningful interaction. The findings indicate that digital technologies substantially reshape identity, autonomy, and individuals’ search for meaning, while digital literacy emerges as a central capability for navigating these changes and supporting effective knowledge management. The study highlights important implications for research and practice, suggesting that strengthening digital literacy is essential to foster more meaningful interactions with technology and to mitigate potential negative existential and cognitive effects. Limitations include potential selection biases, reliance on self-reported data, and cultural and socioeconomic constraints that may affect the generalizability of the results.

title: Balancing internal and external: decoupling carbon emissions from economic growth in China through the lens of economic circulation structure
abstract: Globalization is being reconfigured, decarbonization at the national level requires a deeper understanding of the domestic and international circulations. This study proposes a new decoupling analysis framework for China, examines the decoupling dynamics and driving effects of different economic circulations during 1995–2022. The results show that:(1) China’s economic pattern is characterized by a predominantly domestic circulation, and the evolution of domestic circulation dependence shows a “U-shaped” curve. (2) The changes in the decoupling indices for China overall and for different economic circulations all show an “N-shaped” curve, reflecting significant reversals between different stages. (3) Domestic circulation and international circulation exerted a competitive driving effect on China’s overall economic growth in the early stage, while both tended toward “Expansive coupling” in the later stage. (4) The driving effects from international circulations play a dominant role in the shift of China’s overall decoupling index between 2008 and 2013 compared with that between 2001 and 2008. (5) The own decoupling effect of the economic circulation shows a positive driving effect on China’s overall decoupling index. The growth decoupling effect of the domestic and international circulations due to the slowdown in economic growth gradually inhibits the rise of China’s overall decoupling index. It is recommended that the Chinese government focus on the decoupling status of different economic circulations and the complex impacts of economic structure transformation on decoupling.

title: From Beijing to Brussels: pathways to the integration of gender in research and development (IGIRD)
abstract: Abstract This article offers a first consolidated historical account of the institutionalisation of the Integration of Gender in Research and Development (IGiRD). We use IGiRD as an analytical umbrella term for policies, instruments and research practices that integrate sex and gender analysis into the content, design, evaluation and governance of research and development. The article centres on how sex and gender analysis became institutionally anchored as a question of research quality, responsibility and societal relevance, while treating gender representation in research careers as a related but distinct issue. Drawing on an event-based historical reconstruction of 186 policy and institutional events from 1957 to 2024, the article traces how IGiRD developed across four partially overlapping pathways: gender equality and anti-discrimination frameworks, women’s advancement in science and technology, health and medical research, and broader integration of sex and gender analysis across research fields and governance structures. Comparing the EU, US, Canada and South Korea, the analysis shows that IGiRD has not followed a single linear trajectory. The EU pathway is distinctive because gender mainstreaming became layered onto supranational research funding and evaluation structures, while North America demonstrates strong sectoral anchoring in health and biomedical research, and South Korea illustrates rapid formal-legal anchoring with incomplete operational embedding. The article contributes to historical-institutionalist science policy research by conceptualising IGiRD institutionalisation as layered, recursive and politically reversible. Formal anchoring in laws, strategies or funding rules matters, but durable change depends on operational embedding through review expertise, guidance, training, monitoring and feedback mechanisms, and on substantive methodological integration in research practice. This perspective clarifies why IGiRD can be stabilised, narrowed or reactivated under changing political conditions and offers policy implications for strengthening gender-sensitive R&I in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence.

title: The play in the mirror: examining mirror-stage queerness in Farewell My Concubine
abstract: Abstract The development of queer identity which appears in Farewell My Concubine (1993) follows a path that differs from models based on personal desires and Western-style coming-out stories because it emerged from the unique cultural practice of Beijing Opera. The global acclaim of the film does not illuminate why Cheng Dieyi experiences intense mental entrapment through his stage role because his situation requires a thorough psychoanalytic examination. The research develops a queer psychoanalytic extension of Jacques Lacan’s mirror stage theory to examine how forced artistic indoctrination reshapes processes of gendered subject formation beyond Western identity-based models of queer selfhood. Farewell My Concubine manifests how an opera performer spends his life as a dan role while his identity merges with his continuous performance of this female character. The article employs Lacanian theory to study the film which demonstrates how Beijing opera rituals and disciplinary systems and ideological frameworks create a queer reflective self. The article argues that Cheng Dieyi’s subjectivity emerges through what this study terms a “queer mirror-stage arrest”: a historically intensified form of fractured identification in which the theatrical image of femininity becomes compulsively internalized as the ego ideal. Queer subjectivity in the film emerges through aesthetic discipline, theatrical performance, and historical violence thus making it impossible to match the fixed gender expectations of a conventional social system.

title: Climate change as a health crisis: Mental health, non-communicable diseases, and health system resilience as neglected dimensions of national adaptation plans
abstract: Recent assessments including the World Health Organization COP29 special report on climate change and health (2024) the Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) 2023, and the 2025 Lancet Countdown on health and climate change confirm that climate change is a present and accelerating threat to human health with wide-ranging consequences for populations and health systems worldwide. Yet, while global mitigation efforts have gained momentum including through World Health Assembly Resolution WHA75.8 (2022) and the WHO Alliance for Transformative Action on Climate and Health (ATACH), the dominant adaptation response remains narrowly focused on infectious disease and acute disaster impacts. This commentary argues that the true health toll extends far beyond these immediate threats, encompassing three dimensions that remain systematically underrepresented in general National Adaptation Plans (NAPs): the mental health consequences of climate-driven displacement; the exacerbation of non-communicable diseases through food insecurity, air pollution, and disrupted care; and the fragility of health systems under repeated climate shocks. Critically, these dimensions remain underrepresented in general NAPs, the whole-of-government instruments through which cross-sectoral climate investments are directed, even as Health National Adaptation Plans (H-NAPs) have made greater progress in addressing them. Fewer than half of countries have developed H-NAPs, and their implementation and financing remain uneven, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where climate vulnerability is greatest. This commentary calls for urgent integration of these overlooked burdens into climate policy through a multisectoral, whole-of-society approach coupling ambitious mitigation, which delivers immediate health co-benefits through cleaner air, active transport, and sustainable diets, with adaptation strategies that explicitly address mental health, chronic disease, and health system resilience. Only by expanding climate-health policy to explicitly address mental health, chronic disease burden, and health system resilience alongside the more visible acute impacts can we build adaptation responses that are both just and effective.

title: Understanding users’ intention to adopt AI avatars in online learning: an integrated model of TAM and DOI
abstract: This research examines the key factors associated with users’ intentions to adopt AI avatars within online learning environments. By combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory, a comprehensive model was proposed to assess the relationships between four primary design elements—perceived personalization, feedback quality, transparency, and interactivity—on five key constructs: observability, relative advantage, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust, as well as users’ attitudes and willingness to adopt. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire using convenience sampling, yielding 653 valid responses from participants experienced with AI-powered online education platforms. Structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis was used to examine the proposed TAM–DOI framework and the relationships among the study variables. Notably, trust is closely associated with transparency and other design perceptions, as well as users’ attitudes and behavioral intentions. These findings offer practical guidance for the design of AI-powered educational tools, emphasizing transparent, personalized, and feedback-driven systems that support user trust in online learning.

title: The ecology of blame: conflicts beyond the encounter, diffused responsibility, and governance of delay in South India
abstract: Abstract Human–wildlife conflict (HWC) is often approached through the immediate encounter between humans and animals and its material consequences, including crop loss, injury, compensation, deterrence, and habitat management. This paper argues that the encounter is only one moment within a longer temporality of conflict. Drawing on narrative-based qualitative fieldwork in forest-fringe regions of South India, it examines how wildlife-related conflicts are shaped by conditions that precede particular encounters, including histories of dispossession, ecological change, unequal conservation authority, and the marginalisation of local ecological knowledge, and how they continue beyond them through waiting, compensation procedures, infrastructural failure, bureaucratic delay, and contested responsibility. The paper uses human–human conflict (HHC) not to replace the ecological dimensions of HWC, but to identify the social and institutional conflicts through which wildlife-related risk is produced, interpreted, distributed, and governed. The “problem of many hands” is used as a bounded ethical lens to examine a particular governance paradox: authority may remain concentrated while responsibility for response is dispersed across administrative offices and levels, producing difficult-to-locate answerability and consequential delay. Through three narratives, the paper shows that HWC is simultaneously ecological, social, institutional, and historical. Its contribution is therefore to shift analysis from the encounter as a discrete event toward conflict as an extended trajectory whose antecedents and consequences shape vulnerability, responsibility, institutional trust, and possibilities for coexistence.

title: Decomposing the gender gap in subjective well-being: evidence from a machine learning-based switching framework
abstract: Human well-being has received increasing attention as an indicator of individual and social health and as a consideration in public policy. Gender differences in subjective well-being (SWB), a widely accepted indicator of human well-being, have long been documented. However, explanations of these gender differences remain varied and inconclusive. This study utilizes Gallup World Poll data comprising 1,911,212 observations from 2009 to 2022. Employing advanced machine-learning techniques within an Exogenous Switching Treatment Effect Model (ESTEM) framework, we decompose the gender gap in SWB into differences in characteristics and differences in regime-specific returns. Conditional on observed characteristics and under a common predictive regime, the model predicts higher SWB for men. In contrast, the regime-specific returns component is associated with lower predicted well-being under the male regime. This component also increases over time, widening the estimated gender gap in SWB, while its magnitude varies across countries. The results suggest the potential relevance of institutional flexibility and reduced gender-role pressures for addressing gender disparities in human well-being.

title: Why exclude others from democracy? Obstinate partisanship, conspiracy mentality, and political intolerance
abstract: Wide-ranging and heterogeneous participation within political processes has been theorized as the foundational spirit of healthy democracies. Individual lack of support for large and diverse public participation remains at the core of that premise. This study extends existing research on the antecedents of political intolerance toward ‘others.’ To do so, this study introduces three understudied concepts in this context: Obstinate partisanship, conspiracy mentality, and political intolerance. Drawing on partisan motivated reasoning and group identity theories, this study hypothesizes that these three concepts are interrelated. Using a two-wave diverse online panel survey data in the United States, this study shows that obstinate partisanship and conspiracy mentality significantly predict political intolerance. Those who develop unreasonable, unconditional party loyalty and those who are more likely to hold conspiratorial mentalities will embrace repressive political attitudes toward outgroups when they participate in politics. Furthermore, a mediation model test suggests that conspiracy mentality significantly mediates the influence of obstinate partisanship over political intolerance. The study provides relevant theoretical implications about political intolerance in democracy and adds to the understanding of its antecedents. Limitations and future research directions are also discussed in the manuscript.

title: Too much or too little? Unpacking the curvilinear relationship between telework extent and creativity
abstract: As telework has become increasingly prevalent, understanding its implications for employees has received growing scholarly attention. In particular, how telework affects employee creativity is an important question, given the central role of creativity in organizational innovation and competitiveness. Grounded in the conservation of resources theory, we developed and tested a model examining a potential curvilinear relationship between telework extent and creativity. We further examined the mediating role of workplace anxiety (employees’ feelings of nervousness, uneasiness, and tension regarding work) and the moderating role of temporal leadership (leaders’ behaviors that help subordinates improve their time management and coordination). Our analyses revealed a U-shaped relationship between telework extent and workplace anxiety, and this relationship became nonsignificant under low temporal leadership. Moreover, workplace anxiety mediated the inverted U-shaped relationship between telework extent and creativity. Overall, our findings provide important theoretical and practical implications for understanding the relationship between telework and creativity and underscore the important role of workplace anxiety.

title: This is just between us: understanding the cooperation between village authorities and folk religious NGOs in China’s rural governance
abstract: Abstract Despite the temptation to view it as such, rural governance in China is not always organized through unilateral state control. Several folk religious NGOs are now active in rural China, some of which informally cooperate with village authorities in rural governance. To understand the forms of such cooperation and the opportunity space that sustains it, this research introduces a 'behavioural logic–action strategy' framework and employs a qualitative approach combining methods such as participant observation and semi-structured interviews with village cadres and religious leaders. For village authorities with limited governance resources, leveraging the social capital of folk religious NGOs can enhance the effectiveness of rural governance, but vigilance should also be exercised against challenges to their authority; for folk religious NGOs, participating in rural governance can increase their local influence and consolidate their legitimacy. Based on their autonomous action strategies, the two parties have engaged in non-institutionalised and unequal cooperation in rural governance. In the long term, as state capacity expands in rural areas, folk religious NGOs may face unforeseen development opportunities. This research challenges conventional perspectives based on the corporatist framework and provides original empirical insights into the relationship between the state and NGOs.

title: The cognitive-emotional pathway to information dissemination: source and content effects on Weibo during natural disasters
abstract: This study examines the dynamic relationships between information sources, information content, and dissemination behavior on social media during natural disasters. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework and dual-process theory, we analyze 68,166 Weibo posts related to the 2025 Tibet earthquake using a vector autoregression model with exogenous variables (VARX). The results reveal systematic differences in how source-related and content-related cues shape dissemination dynamics. In the short term, source credibility and source activity are associated with decreases in dissemination behavior, whereas source influence, information severity, and information susceptibility are associated with increases. Over time, the influence of source characteristics weakens, while content-related cues continue to be linked with dissemination dynamics. Collective cognitive and emotional expressions also play important intermediary roles in these relationships. Cognitive expressions are more strongly associated with content-related cues, whereas emotional expressions are more closely linked with source-related cues. These findings contribute to a better understanding of how source-related and content-related cues shape aggregate cognitive-emotional expression and dissemination dynamics during natural disasters, offering implications for emergency communication practices in social media environments using time-series evidence from large-scale Weibo data.

title: Instructional application of BYOD in K-12 in the context of the digital transformation of education: a systematic literature review
abstract: BYOD is an instructional approach in which students use personal digital devices to participate in learning activities. Although a growing body of research has examined BYOD, systematic evidence remains limited on how BYOD arrangements relate to students’ opportunities to participate in learning in K-12 education. This study systematically synthesizes 32 articles that met the inclusion criteria and identifies patterns in their reported hardware, software, configuration mechanisms, instructional applications, and evaluations: (1) Among the included studies, the most frequently reported hardware devices were tablets, smartphones, and laptops, with tablets being the most common, followed by smartphones and laptops. Further analysis was conducted from grade level allocation, application type, and configuration method. (2) Regarding instructional applications, BYOD is reported in five major categories of courses: basic science, social science, mathematics, language, and interdisciplinary courses. Inquiry-based learning, collaborative learning, and flipped learning are the most common teaching methods, and related technology applications are mainly at the enhanced level of the SAMR framework. Further analysis was conducted from the perspective of grade level to examine its subject configuration and teaching method applications. (3) Regarding evaluation, this study employs topic coding analysis to further analyze the positive and negative effects of BYOD on learning and potential problems. Finally, the review offers context-specific insights for school policies and teaching practices aimed at supporting equitable participation in BYOD-supported learning and identifies directions for future research.

title: The longitudinal relationships among loneliness, source-specific perceived social support, and depressive symptoms in Chinese children and adolescents: a three-wave cross-lagged panel network analysis
abstract: Loneliness, perceived social support, and depressive symptoms are closely linked in childhood and adolescence; however, less is known about how depressive symptoms, loneliness, and source-specific deficits in perceived support are prospectively associated at different levels of measurement. Prior studies using aggregate scores have limited insights into how specific symptoms interact with distinct support sources over time. This three-wave cross-lagged panel network (CLPN) study examined these relationships in a large school-based sample of ~5000 Chinese children and adolescents. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), loneliness was measured with a single item, and perceived social support was evaluated across four sources: parents, teachers, classmates, and close friends. We estimated both cross-sectional and cross-lagged panel networks to examine centrality indices, bridge expected influence, and longitudinal predictive pathways. Network structures remained stable across waves. Fatigue consistently emerged as a central depressive symptom, and low classmate support was central within the support domain. Loneliness showed the strongest bridge effect, linking depressive symptoms with low perceived social support. Longitudinally, fatigue and loneliness showed relatively high outward expected influence and prospectively predicted later increases in low perceived support, although these temporal pathways should not be interpreted as causal effects. The associations between suicidal ideation and support were similar for parent and teacher sources but differed for peer support during a specific time period, demonstrating source-specific interpersonal correlates. These findings suggest that fatigue, loneliness, and source-specific support deficits may be important targets for hypothesis generation and future intervention research, while causal mechanisms require further confirmation using designs specifically suited for causal inference.

title: Digital transformation and urban land expansion: how E-commerce reshapes urban space in Quanzhou, China
abstract: E-commerce has become a major force driving industrial upgrading, urban expansion, and urban–rural integration. Yet it remains unclear whether classical theories of urban land expansion can adequately explain the digital era, particularly in terms of when and at what scale E-commerce begins to reshape urban space in traditional manufacturing cities. Using Quanzhou as a case study, this research integrates firm-level E-commerce data (2008–2023) with impervious-surface land-use datasets to examine how digital economic activities influence urban land expansion. Spatial analyses show that both E-commerce activity and built-up land expanded southeastward, although with different local trajectories. Urban growth in Quanzhou increasingly shifted toward infill development, while E-commerce expanded more rapidly from the southeast-central urban area into distant suburbs. Over time, the spatial alignment between transportation networks and E-commerce activity strengthened: although E-commerce initially had limited influence on urban structure, its rapid growth later promoted transport expansion toward suburban areas, reinforcing sprawl while also encouraging infill development. Threshold regression results further reveal the nonlinear effects of E-commerce on urban land expansion. Small and compact E-commerce clusters improve land-use efficiency and reduce land demand, whereas development beyond critical quantity and density thresholds generates agglomeration effects that drive outward expansion. Transportation accessibility, population, and industrial foundations significantly shape these processes, while public services show limited influence. This study extends theories of urban land expansion and digital economy–urban spatial interaction.

title: Constructing and performing Jia in short study abroad: a case study of Chinese minor students in homestays
abstract: Homestay arrangements are integral to short-term transnational study tours, yet the construction and performance of Jia (home) centered on minor participants remain critically underexplored. This study addresses this gap by examining the homestay experiences of Chinese middle school students in California, USA. Drawing on qualitative data, this paper analyses the homestay as a multi-dimensional, negotiated field. Findings reveal that: (1) The material Jia is pre-constructed by the commercial logic of intermediaries and the remote risk management of parents, and is subsequently co-constructed through on-site interactions between hosts and students. (2) The emotional Jia is remade through reciprocal interactions with hosts and tour leaders, yet is simultaneously shaped by the virtual co-presence of parents, whose digital support provides a crucial, transnational emotional safety net. (3) The cultural Jia functions as a site for the collision, negotiation, and fusion of ‘home’ concepts, extending beyond the physical dwelling to the community and enabling students to form multi-scalar cultural meanings of Jia. This study contributes a multi-participant perspective on the commercial home, revealing it as a complex field negotiated by both present and remote actors. These findings hold practical implications for study tour agencies.

title: Generative inference model reveals political and economic motivations for road construction in past societies
abstract: Abstract The construction of roads in past societies reflects a trade-off between a preference for straightness and the influence of slope gradient. This trade-off is, however, also conditioned by other factors, principally the political and economic motivations of a past society. Our understanding of this trade-off and its relationship to these motivations is poor, hindered by qualitative studies that fail to explain variability in road construction, and non-comparative quantitative approaches. Here, we introduce a hierarchical, generative inference model that simulates roads using explicit decision rules to estimate the influence of slope gradient on 62 well-evidenced Roman roads in modern-day Wales. Our results reveal substantial variability, with Roman roads not conforming to a single unifying straightness-gradient trade-off. We relate this trade-off to political and economic motivations to provide a unified, comparative framework for inferring motivations for road construction, both within the Roman Empire and across past societies more broadly.

title: Coparenting relationship quality and parenting satisfaction, concerns, and strain among Japanese mothers and fathers in early parenthood
abstract: Abstract Coparenting relationship quality is a key interpersonal context in which parents’ emotional experiences of childrearing take shape. In Japan, where traditional gendered expectations of ‘mothers as primary caregivers’ coexist with growing norms of paternal involvement, little is known about how multidimensional coparenting relates to parents’ affective attitudes towards parenting or whether these associations differ for fathers and mothers. This study explored patterns of association between multiple facets of coparenting and affective attitudes towards parenting among fathers and mothers in Japan during early parenthood from a gender-informed perspective. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 547 parents (261 fathers, 286 mothers) whose oldest child was aged 3 years or younger. Six dimensions of coparenting were analysed: agreement, closeness, exposure to conflict, support, undermining, and endorsement of partner parenting. Affective attitudes towards parenting were assessed as three subjective affective evaluations: parenting satisfaction, parenting concerns, and parenting strain. Multiple-group path analysis was used to estimate associations while adjusting for socio-demographic covariates. On balance, model comparisons favoured the constrained-equal structural path model over the unconstrained structural path model, suggesting that fathers and mothers shared a broadly similar association structure. Correspondingly, gender differences in individual paths were limited. Within this shared structure, closeness and support were positively associated with parenting satisfaction, agreement was negatively associated with parenting concerns, and exposure to conflict was positively associated with both parenting concerns and parenting strain; undermining and endorsement of partner parenting showed no unique associations. These findings suggest that, in Japan’s transitional context of shifting gender norms and institutional conditions surrounding childrearing, fathers and mothers may share similar patterns linking coparenting dynamics to their affective attitudes towards parenting, highlighting the importance of couple-level processes in family support.

title: Reexamining the nonlinear effects of public services on housing prices from the lenses of proximity, availability and quality
abstract: Understanding the complex interplay between public services and housing markets is essential for building inclusive and sustainable cities. However, existing studies on the housing price effects of public services are limited because they overlook multidimensional public service characteristics. In this study, the nonlinear effects of public services on housing prices are reexamined within a three-dimensional framework that considers proximity, availability and quality. The gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) algorithm is applied to infer the nonlinear effects of four types of public services (education, healthcare, parks and metros) on housing prices in Beijing. The results reveal that (1) the quality and availability of public services are the primary influencing factors of housing prices, whereas the importance of proximity to facilities might be overstated in existing studies. (2) Generally, the proximity to and the quality of public services positively influence housing prices, but the “not in my backyard” (NIMBY) effect occurs within a relatively short distance from healthcare facilities and middle schools. The association between availability and housing price shows an “M-shaped” relationship. (3) Interactive effect analyses reveal that high quality and high availability can amplify the effect of proximity on housing prices. The findings have implications for equitable urban public service provision and the planning of inclusive and sustainable cities.

title: Does teleworking adoption improve employee productivity? A new insight from the post-pandemic hybrid working world
abstract: Despite growing significance of teleworking, its effective activation is resisted by users’ perceptions affecting adoption behaviors and productivity. This study evaluates how teleworking perceptions affect employee adoption behavior and productivity. The theoretical underpinnings of the technology acceptance model (TAM), theory of planned behavior (TBP), data from 443 employees, and the structural equation modeling (SEM) technique were used to estimate the factors affecting teleworking adoption behaviors and productivity. The findings indicate that perceived ease of use, organizational culture, education, and job position significantly influence employees’ teleworking adoption behaviors and productivity. However, personal attitude, perceived behavioral control, and gender did not predict changes in employees’ teleworking adoption behaviors and productivity. Our findings contribute to the analysis of the factors limiting the activation of teleworking across institutions. These factors can be used to design and modify existing teleworking policies for businesses looking to thrive in the post-pandemic era.

title: Addressing global environmental degradation: examining the role of financialization and trade globalization on reducing carbon emissions
abstract: The pressing challenge of achieving environmental sustainability hinges on financialization and trade globalization. These dynamics are central to strategies aimed at mitigating ecological degradation. Effective financial and policy decisions are crucial in managing the interplay between finance, trade, and environmental outcomes. This study investigates the relationship between financialization and ecological degradation by employing three dimensions of financialization financial development, financial markets, and financial institutions within the framework of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC). Using a two-step system generalized method of moments (GMM) on a balanced panel of 129 developed and developing countries covering the period 2000 to 2022, the analysis provides robust evidence on the heterogeneous roles of financialization. The findings reveal that trade and financial development are associated with higher emissions in both developed and emerging economies, while financial markets significantly reduce emissions. Financial institutions also demonstrate a negative association with emissions, underscoring their role in supporting sustainable investment. The squared term of trade openness indicates significant emission reductions, consistent with the EKC’s inverted U-shaped hypothesis. However, the interaction effects of financialization and trade on emissions are essentially insignificant, suggesting weak synergies between these forces. Overall, the study highlights that financial development and trade can initially exacerbate ecological pressures. Still, financial markets and institutions, when supported by regulatory and governance frameworks, play a critical role in advancing sustainability. These results offer theoretical contributions to the finance–environment nexus and provide policy insights for aligning financial systems and trade with the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Capital under the shadow of stupa: a study of crony capitalism in Theravāda Buddhist countries of Southeast Asia
abstract: Abstract Within the framework of Marxist political economy, and through an analysis of state power, military structures, and international relations, this article argues that crony capitalism, as a politico-economic model in which wealth accumulation and resource allocation are highly dependent on political power, represents an alienated and distorted form of contemporary capitalism under specific historical conditions. In contexts where political systems remain underdeveloped and institutional environments are not yet fully consolidated, crony capitalism can facilitate rapid vertical political integration and economic mobilization in the short term for Third World countries. Southeast Asia has been profoundly shaped by crony capitalism. In the processes of state formation, capital accumulation, and integration into the global economic system, Myanmar, Cambodia, and Thailand have developed distinct forms of crony capitalism, namely “military-predatory crony capitalism,” “family-authoritarian crony capitalism,” and “alliance-based monopolistic crony capitalism.” Within these systems, the military and its networks play a crucial role in sustaining crony capitalism; the influence of international capital is likewise significant; and Theravāda Buddhism, as a historical and ideological resource, is incorporated into the process of power reproduction. While crony capitalism may contribute to short-term political and economic stability through elite alliances, in the long run its inherent exclusivity and mechanisms of resource misallocation exacerbate structural contradictions and systemic oppression, thereby constraining social development and rendering the paths toward modernization in Myanmar, Cambodia, and Thailand increasingly difficult.

title: Belief to behavior: how AI self-efficacy shapes AI acceptance through AI literacy
abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into higher education has raised important questions regarding students’ acceptance of AI and the psychological and cognitive factors shaping their engagement with these systems. This study aimed to examine how university students’ AI self-efficacy influences their acceptance of AI, whether AI literacy helps explain this relationship, and whether greater AI acceptance is associated with lower AI anxiety. For the present study, data were obtained from 622 undergraduate students at a public university. Empirical analyses were based on validated scales measuring AI self-efficacy, AI literacy, AI acceptance, and AI anxiety, and conducted using correlation analyses and regression-based mediation models via the PROCESS Macro. The results showed that AI self-efficacy was positively associated with AI acceptance, both directly and indirectly through AI literacy. Higher AI acceptance was also associated with lower AI anxiety; however, this relationship should not be interpreted as causal. These findings support a sequential motivational, cognitive and affective model of AI engagement and highlight the importance of integrating confidence-building interventions with literacy-focused instructional strategies to promote psychologically adaptive and sustainable AI integration in higher education contexts.

title: The impact of the data factor platform on the urban green innovation: evidence from China
abstract: Abstract With the rapid expansion of the digital economy, data elements have emerged as a pivotal force shaping urban green development. This study offers a novel perspective by examining how the construction of data factor platform influences urban green innovation. From the channel of artificial intelligence (AI) development and human capital accumulation, we propose a mechanism framework. Based on the city-level data from 2010 to 2022 in China, using the multi-period Difference-in-Difference (DID) model, we explore the impact of the data factor platform construction on urban green innovation. The results reveal that data factor platform construction can stimulate urban green innovation. The data factor platform construction stimulates urban green innovation through the channel of promoting AI development and accelerating human capital accumulation. The impact of the data factor platform construction on the urban green innovation is heterogeneous. The data factor platform construction has a larger effect on the urban green innovation in the low-carbon pilot city situation and cities with larger economic scales. The further analysis results reveal that the data factor platform construction in the surrounding areas effectively promotes local green innovation. According to the above conclusions, in the green transition process, the government should pay attention to data factor platform programs and make a combination of policies to stimulate green innovations.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of eco-tourism competitiveness in countries along the belt and road
abstract: The ecological environment serves as a pivotal factor in ensuring the sustainable development of the tourism industry, which, in turn, acts as a crucial link in stimulating economic growth and fostering deeper understanding and trust among countries and regions along the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Consequently, an increasing number of nations are prioritizing eco-tourism development to bolster international tourism collaboration and partnerships. To foster tourism collaboration along the BRI, this study analyzed data from 50 countries along the route spanning 2000 to 2021, employing the Entropy Weight-TOPSIS method to assess their respective weights in economic, social, tourism resource, and environmental dimensions. Furthermore, spatial autocorrelation and Local Indicators of LISA maps were utilized to unravel the spatio-temporal evolution patterns and clustering characteristics of eco-tourism competitiveness among these countries. Additionally, the Spatial Durbin Model was employed to explore the influencing factors. The primary result showed that: (1) China’s eco-tourism competitiveness index significantly outpaces that of other countries; (2) The eco-tourism competitiveness index of countries along the BRI demonstrates an overall steady upward trend in spatial distribution; (3) The majority of countries along the route exhibit insignificant spatial clustering, lacking both high-high and low-low clusters; (4) Regarding influencing factors, EF, PPP, and the degree of openness are found to have significant positive impacts on eco-tourism competitiveness, while the informatization rate and population structure have significant negative effects. Moreover, industrial structure exerts a negative but insignificant influence on eco-tourism competitiveness, and the spillover effect is evident.

title: Negotiating masculinity in a feminized profession: a systematic review of male teachers in early childhood education
abstract: To better understand male teachers in Early Childhood Education (ECE) in China, where gender roles are firmly established in professional life, this study presents a systematic review following the PRISMA protocol. It combines findings from 16 carefully chosen qualitative studies published between 2013 and 2025. The review focuses on two main research questions: (1) how male teachers develop and navigate their personal and professional identities in ECE settings, and (2) how key stakeholders, such as female colleagues, parents, leaders, and community members, view and react to men in this field. The findings show that male ECE teachers often face complex identity challenges in mostly female-dominated work cultures. They deal with suspicion, gender stereotypes, and restrictive role expectations, which can harm their sense of professional legitimacy and belonging. In China and other Confucian-influenced societies, deeply rooted cultural norms and moral debates further label ECE as “women’s work,” making it harder for men to enter, stay, and advance in this profession. Beyond China, this review adds to global discussions on gender diversity in ECE. It shows how specific cultural norms intersect with broader structural and institutional barriers that also affect male teachers’ experiences across different educational systems. The findings indicate that issues related to gender expectations, professional identity, and societal trust are not just local concerns but also resonate worldwide, albeit in different contexts. By highlighting these common trends, the study promotes a more comparative and globally relevant view of gender imbalance in ECE. The review advocates coordinated policy and institutional changes, including fair pay, gender-inclusive professional standards, and leadership practices that challenge gender bias. Ultimately, it emphasizes the need to redefine early childhood education as a gender-inclusive profession worldwide, recognizing diversity as essential for improving workforce sustainability and the overall development of young children.

title: Pedagogical affordances for professional communication development: a mixed-methods comparison of active learning approaches
abstract: Professional communication is an important learning outcome in higher education, yet different active learning pedagogies may provide different communicative affordances for its development and enactment. This study comparatively examined how four active learning pedagogies-group discussion, role play, case study analysis, and student-led seminars-were associated with professional communication across five dimensions: clarity and precision, logical structuring, adaptability and tone, active listening, and persuasive expression. Using a mixed-methods, within-subject repeated-measures design, data were collected from 72 postgraduate management students across two cohorts. All participants experienced the four pedagogies through a Latin Square rotation. Data were drawn from pre-post self-reports, instructor-rated session-level communication performance, and qualitative reflections. Findings were examined across three analytical levels. At the aggregate level, pre-post results indicated significant gains in students’ self-perceived communication competence across both cohorts. These findings indicate perceived development rather than objective gains in demonstrated competence. At the session level, observed communication performance varied across pedagogical conditions, with group discussion and role play associated with higher performance scores than case study analysis and student-led seminars. At the dimension level, qualitative findings revealed distinct pedagogy-dimension linkages. Group discussion was associated with clarity, logical structuring, active listening, and persuasive expression, whereas role play was particularly associated with adaptability and contextual responsiveness. The findings suggest that active learning pedagogies should not be treated as interchangeable approaches to communication development. Instead, their communicative affordances may be considered in relation to specific instructional objectives and desired dimensions of professional communication. The study contributes a differentiated account of how pedagogical structures shape opportunities for communication enactment and provides an evidence-informed basis for aligning active learning design with professional communication objectives in higher education.

title: Attracting and retaining high-level talents in higher education institutions: a Kano analysis
abstract: Abstract Brain drain in higher education has emerged as a global sustainability challenge, necessitating nuanced talent retention strategies. This study defines high-level talents (HLTHE) in higher education as an operational dual construct: established academic professionals with doctoral degrees or associate senior professional titles, and emerging PhD candidates with outstanding research potential and demonstrated academic productivity (e.g., published papers in core journals or participation in provincial-level or above research projects). This cohort is distinguished from general skilled employees by its possession of domain-specific advanced human capital, irreplaceable academic research capabilities, and core roles in disciplinary construction and scientific innovation. Employing Kano’s Theory of Attractive Quality, combined with the theoretical underpinnings of Social Exchange Theory and Job Embeddedness Theory, we classify 36 retention-related attributes via 40 interviews and a survey of 203 professionals (supplemented by 102 PhD candidates for subgroup comparisons). Based on the professional subsample, this exploratory Kano analysis categorizes 19 attributes into Must-be, One-Dimensional, Attractive, and Indifferent types. The Total Satisfaction Index (TSI) identifies “flexible work arrangements” (0.42), “offering international academic exchange opportunities” (0.38), and “organizing high-level meetings” (0.36) as the most influential. One-Dimensional attributes exhibit higher average satisfaction coefficients (mean ASC = 0.57) than Attractive ones (mean ASC = 0.45). Subgroup analyses reveal career-stage moderation (e.g., scientific evaluation mechanism shifts from Attractive for professionals to Must-be for PhD candidates) and selective gender differences (e.g., interesting work appeals more to males, while cross-disciplinary platforms appeal more to females). These exploratory findings provide a classification-based perspective for understanding talent retention in central and western Chinese universities, contributing to context-specific strategy development.

title: An analytical model for multi-modal argumentation
abstract: Traditional argumentation theory has primarily centered on logical reasoning, often overlooking other modes that also contribute to argumentative practice. Michael Gilbert’s multi-modal argumentation theory represents an important advancement by integrating these neglected modes into argumentation analysis, and it has accordingly attracted substantial attention within argumentation studies. Yet, a systematic model for the analysis and evaluation of multi-modal argumentation remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, this paper proposes a path-based model, taking an important step toward the systematic model. In our account, we take the goal of argumentation to be the resolution of disagreement through the presentation of arguments whose premises are intended to justify a conclusion that expresses the arguer’s standpoint. We treat a mode as a way through which information is expressed, and we employ the notion of path to represent the justificatory connection between premises and the conclusion.

title: Gender differences in effective feedback practices of computer science teachers in programming education
abstract: Abstract Programming education has become an important component of K–12 curricula worldwide. A key element of this educational transition is feedback, which facilitates the identification of misconceptions and supports iterative learning processes underlying coding mastery. Framed by Wiggins’ keys and sociocultural theory, this research investigates the influence of teacher gender on programming feedback practices among CS teachers in Saudi Arabia. Using mixed-methods research design, the study employed a semi-structured questionnaire to analyze the intersection of gender and feedback strategies. Findings indicate that while both male and female educators utilize Wiggins’ Seven Keys to feedback, female teachers report significantly higher implementation across all dimensions. Data shows no significant gender variance in the use of group, electronic, AI, or self-feedback; however, female teachers utilize individual and peer feedback more frequently. Qualitative analysis further categorizes these practices into three primary domains: teacher-based, student-based, and technology-based strategies. By highlighting the varied approaches CS teachers use to scaffold student learning, this study contributes to the global discourse on CS pedagogy and demonstrates how adaptable feedback strategies can enhance the effectiveness of the K–12 programming environment.

title: Untying the soul in techgnosis? an isomorphic examination of the metaverse and gnosticism
abstract: Abstract Gnosticism has repeatedly returned in modern and contemporary thought as more than a historical object. It names a persistent way of thinking the crisis in which the given world no longer appears sufficient for meaning, authority, embodiment, and worldliness. The metaverse, emerging within contemporary digital culture, gives this older problematic a new technological form. It does not revive ancient Gnosticism in any literal or doctrinal sense, yet it restages several of its formal motifs: estrangement from the given world, the salvific privilege of knowledge, the elevation of another order, and the desire to loosen the limits of embodied existence. This study argues that the metaverse can therefore be read as a contemporary scene of techgnosis, grounded in a hierarchical dualism that differentially values body and soul, materiality and transcendence, physical and virtual existence. Through hermeneutic and comparative analysis, the article brings Western discussions of Gnosticism and techgnosis into dialogue with the Chinese semantic field of lingjing and lingzhi, treating these terms as mediated conceptual resonances that widen the vocabulary through which spirit, knowledge, and technological world-making can be understood. The paper further shows that the ethical stakes of the metaverse lie not simply in immersion or simulation, but in the revaluation of embodiment, nature, and moral imagination under digital conditions. Against both rationalist instrumentality and fantasies of disembodied escape, it suggests that moral imagination remains necessary for keeping technological mediation answerable to the fragile conditions of embodied and shared life.

title: Learning to nurture: associations between parents’ self‑directed learning investment and children’s human capital
abstract: Against the backdrop of intense educational competition in China, an increasing number of parents are turning from direct investment in children toward self-directed learning aimed at improving their own educational capabilities. This study examines the associations between parents’ self-directed learning investment and children’s academic achievement and non-cognitive skills using micro-survey data from 1166 primary-school students and their families. The results show that parental learning expenditure and both fathers’ and mothers’ learning frequency are positively associated with children’s academic achievement, while the association with aggregate non-cognitive skills is concentrated mainly in parental learning frequency. Pathway analyses suggest that parental support represents a more consistent potential pathway across outcomes, whereas the parental-anxiety pathway is weaker and mainly evident for non-cognitive skills. Children’s prior academic achievement strengthens the positive associations of fathers’ and mothers’ learning frequency with current academic achievement. Heterogeneity analyses further indicate that structured and sustained forms of parental learning are more consistently associated with better child outcomes than fragmented forms, while school-level differences are concentrated primarily in fathers’ learning frequency. By shifting attention from parents’ direct investment in children to parents’ own learning and capability development, this study extends research on family educational investment and provides new evidence on parental self-directed learning as a dynamic component of the family educational environment.

title: Revolutionary transformation of digital art:ontological reconstruction and paradigm shift driven by technology
abstract: Abstract This study examines changes in digital art’s creative mechanisms, subject relations, and conditions of existence through the lens of the philosophy of technology. Tracing the evolution from mechanical and electronic media to algorithmic systems, the paper argues that technology no longer functions merely as an external tool but increasingly intervenes in artistic cognition, creative processes, and the conditions under which works are generated. The paper outlines three notable dimensions of change in digital art: technologically mediated existence, distributed creative relations, and algorithmically shaped aesthetic processes. The paper also examines three tensions: Western aesthetic dominance via biased training data, NFT-driven value paradoxes, and destabilized artistic subjectivity under generative AI. Drawing on process philosophy, complexity theory, and technological phenomenology, it proposes a techno-cognitive framework positioning digital art as a dynamic interface between technology and human cognition. The study proposes evaluative and ethical discussion frameworks better suited to contemporary digital art, with the aim of supporting further theoretical analysis.

title: Urban ecological resilience in the digital era: the role of data factor marketization and spatial spillovers
abstract: As data becomes an increasingly important production factor in the digital economy, its role in shaping environmental outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how data factor marketization affects urban ecological resilience. Using a spatial difference-in-differences model and panel data from 282 Chinese cities between 2010 and 2022, we find that data factor marketization significantly enhances ecological resilience and generates positive spatial spillovers, although these effects are mainly concentrated within a relatively short geographic range. The effect operates through three main pathways: green innovation, efficient resource allocation, and industrial upgrading through digital transformation. The results also reveal substantial heterogeneity: eastern and western cities benefit more than central ones, and resource-based cities respond more strongly, likely due to their stronger demand for structural transformation. In addition, cities with stronger digital foundations derive greater ecological benefits from the reform, highlighting the conditioning role of digital development in shaping policy effectiveness. These findings advance understanding of how data factor allocation supports environmental adaptation and underscore the importance of digital infrastructure and institutional capacity. Policy efforts should prioritize data institutionalization, digital inclusion, and targeted support for digitally lagging and resource-dependent cities to better translate data reforms into ecological gains.

title: Resource rents, institutions and growth in Sub-Saharan African OIC countries: a panel quantile analysis
abstract: Abstract This research investigates the nexus among natural resource rents, control of corruption, and GDP per capita growth in 21 Sub-Saharan African OIC member states for the period 2005–2024. Applying panel Fixed Effects estimation as well as panel quantile regression (25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles), the study assesses heterogeneities along with the growth distribution. The findings suggest that control of corruption is positively associated with growth in all specifications. The interaction variable of natural resource rents and corruption control is found to be negative and significant, implying that the marginal effect of corruption control on growth decreases with increases in resource reliance. Quantile regression results indicate that the negative relationship between resource rents and growth is most pronounced at the lowest end of the growth scale, while foreign direct investment has a positive association with growth mostly in the median and upper quantiles. These results indicate that there is distributional diversity in the resource, governance, and growth nexus across SSA-OIC countries.

title: Investigating the nexus between technological innovations and trade in low carbon technology products in BRI economies: Do environmental taxes matter?
abstract: Technological innovations, environmental taxes and low-carbon technologies are essential for transitioning to a carbon-free economy. However, the significant role of technological innovations and environmental taxes in shaping trade in low-carbon technology products still requires further investigation within the BRI context.
