To address this research gap, the study assessed the potential impact of technological innovations and environmental taxes on TLCTPs using panel data from 31 BRI economies spanning 1994 to 2021, utilizing the CS-ARDL, robustness and IV 2SLS methods. The findings exhibit that technological innovations significantly enhance TLCTPs. Whereas ecological taxation not just enhances trade in low carbon technology products but also reinforces the relationship between technological innovations and TLCTPs, it sustains the Porter Hypothesis. In addition, control variables, i.e., FDI, lnGDP, REC, R&D expenditures, institutional quality and human capital have substantial impacts on TLCTPs. Contrarily, CO2 emissions and dependency on non-renewable energy hamper the low carbon technology trade. Hence, study outcomes emphasize the significance of a complementary policy framework, encouraging research and development subsidies, green taxation strategies and trade liberalization to foster technological transfer, low-carbon trade and green growth in BRI economies.

title: Going online for work: global evidence of ICT access and its association on youth employment by gender (1991–2022)
abstract: This study examines the association between Information and Communication Technology (ICT) access and youth unemployment rates by gender across up to 166 countries from 1991 to 2022. Using a comprehensive cross-national time-series analysis, we evaluate three dimensions of ICT access: internet usage, fixed broadband subscriptions, and mobile phone penetration. Employing two-way fixed effects (2WFE), panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE), and system generalized method of moments (System GMM) models, the findings suggest that increased ICT access is significantly and negatively associated with youth unemployment rates, with a stronger and more consistent association observed for female youths compared to male youths. This gendered pattern highlights the potential of ICT to address structural barriers that disproportionately hinder young women’s labor market participation. Additionally, heterogeneity analysis reveals that these associations are substantially stronger in developing countries compared to developed economies, suggesting that the marginal returns to ICT development may be higher in contexts where baseline connectivity remains low. These findings provide actionable insights for policymakers, emphasizing the need to expand digital infrastructure and implement gender-sensitive interventions to promote inclusive youth employment in the digital age.

title: More than falsehood: conceptualising ‘the moral economy of misinformation’ in the post-truth era
abstract: This article theorises misinformation as morally and affectively meaningful storytelling embedded within what it conceptualises as a moral economy of misinformation. Rather than treating falsehood as cognitive failure or epistemic breakdown, it argues that misinformation endures because it acquires symbolic force: it affirms identities, resolves grievance and offers emotionally satisfying interpretations of contested social realities. The analysis draws on a qualitative thematic study of 426 posts and comments responding to the viral and largely false Achraf Hakimi divorce narrative, which circulated widely across African and diasporic digital platforms in 2023. The findings show that the narrative gained traction less through factual credibility than through moral plausibility. It circulated as a parable of masculine foresight and resistance to perceived female financial entitlement, resonating with anxieties about divorce, economic vulnerability and shifting gender relations. The article identifies three mechanisms through which misinformation becomes durable: value coherence, whereby narratives align with pre-existing moral worldviews; affective intensity, through which emotion transforms misinformation into an object of attachment, pleasure and identification; and premediated scripts, which render stories legible in advance of verification by activating familiar cultural templates of grievance, entitlement and moral retribution. These dynamics are intensified by platform infrastructures, including algorithms, influencer economies, meme cultures and short-form video, that privilege emotionally charged and morally legible content over empirical accuracy. Bringing moral economy theory into dialogue with feminist media studies, affect theory and digital sociology, the article develops a framework for explaining why misinformation can remain socially persuasive even after factual correction, particularly when it continues to satisfy moral expectations and affective investments. It argues that post-truth culture is less a collapse of truth than a struggle over which truths become morally persuasive in digital spaces.

title: Digital employment pathways for Ukrainian refugees in Romania: an exploratory study of remote job offers
abstract: Abstract The 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine triggered the largest displacement crisis in Europe since World War II, resulting in millions of refugees, primarily women with children, seeking safety across the continent. As the crisis continues, the transition from emergency response to long-term integration, and labor market inclusion has emerged as a critical priority. Remote or digital work, which proved essential during the COVID-19 pandemic, presents a potentially transformative solution, especially for displaced individuals facing mobility, caregiving, or legal constraints. This article seeks to answer what types of digital job opportunities are available to Ukrainian refugees in Romania, and how are these opportunities distributed across sectors, experience levels, and contract types, in order to identify the major trends and limitations of such labour integration measures. Drawing on a developed web scraping and real-time data analysis approach on data from Jobs4Ukraine platform, the study identifies the dominance of full-time and permanent roles, and the positive correlation of entry-level positions, positive for refugees´ integration prospects, but also significant limitations. The digital labor market remains concentrated in high-skills sectors like IT, with a strong bias toward mid-level experience and a lack of flexible, part-time, or freelance opportunities, which are paramount for the majority of Ukrainian refugees with caregiving responsibilities. These trends indicate an exacerbation of the problem of exclusion among this group, as well as other groups with similar vulnerability characteristics. The findings highlight the need for more inclusive digital employment strategies that address structural barriers through policy reform, upskilling programs, and adaptive job design. Ultimately, digital work holds substantial potential as a pathway for economic integration and resilience, but realizing this promise requires intentional efforts to make the digital labor market more accessible, equitable, and responsive to the diverse realities of displaced populations.

title: Investigating the impact of money growth and exchange rate shocks on inflation in Turkey: a time-varying causality analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic relationships between money supply, exchange rates, and the consumer price index in Turkey from 1960 to 2024 using time-varying Granger causality techniques, including rolling window and recursive evolving algorithms. Our analysis shows a significant structural shift following the 2001 policy reforms. Contrary to the pre-2001 era, we find a strengthened causal influence of money supply on inflation, signaling the emergence of a consistent monetarist trend under the inflation-targeting regime initiated, implicitly, in January 2002. Concurrently, we document a rising and more prolonged exchange rate pass-through effect, challenging the prevailing belief that the post-2001 floating exchange rate regime curbed transmission. This points to a potential depreciation-inflation spiral, particularly evident after 2017. Our results, robustly confirmed by a supplementary wavelet coherence analysis, underscore that inflation in Turkey is now driven by a dual-channel mechanism, with significant implications for monetary policy.

title: A sociological investigation into doctoral students’ perinatal experiences in Hong Kong
abstract: Several policy discourses link low fertility levels to increased educational opportunities, particularly for women. However, the structural constraints within higher education that hinder the combination of parenthood and academic achievement have received little attention. This study aims to illuminate the perinatal experiences, including both pregnancy and postpartum, of doctoral student-parents at public universities in Hong Kong. Specifically, it explores how pregnancy and parenthood influence doctoral students’ journey in the perinatal period. Additionally, the study evaluates the accessibility and effectiveness of existing institutional and social support systems in addressing the needs of pregnant and first-time parenting doctoral students in Hong Kong. The study engaged and interviewed 20 participants who were selected from diverse disciplines and public universities in Hong Kong. A significant contribution of this study is its inclusion of the experiences of male students with pregnant or postpartum partners, and the implications of these experiences for their academic performance. The study revealed that maternity policies for students are often “gray areas” in most universities, with pregnancy and postpartum support primarily available to female faculty members and staff. Psychologically, students reported experiencing stress and depression, with some receiving clinical diagnoses that affected their overall well-being and academic journey. International doctoral students faced greater stress, sometimes leading them to defer their programs. The findings of this study have important implications for the development of comprehensive maternity and paternity policies for students at universities in Hong Kong, and potentially in other parts of the world.

title: A corpus-assisted textual analysis of the framing of domestic violence in the Chinese translations of W.S. Maugham’s Liza of Lambeth
abstract: Abstract Research on the translation of gendered violence has concentrated on texts in which gender politics and sexual violence are explicitly foregrounded, and much less is known about how such violence is reframed in literary works that advance no explicit feminist position. This study addresses this gap through a corpus-assisted comparative analysis, drawing on Baker’s narrative framing framework to examine domestic violence (DV) in Xian Yangyang’s 2013 and Yu Kangyong’s 1995 Chinese translations (the latter reprinted in 2016) of W. S. Maugham’s Liza of Lambeth . Quantitative and qualitative analyses examine four narrative framing strategies — selective appropriation, repositioning of participants, framing by labelling, and temporal-spatial framing — and compare representations of physical violence, psychological abuse, and sexual assault. The findings reveal systematic differences in the textual prominence and framing of DV. Xian’s translation devotes proportionally greater textual space to DV, particularly psychological abuse, and more frequently repositions participants in representations of physical violence, while Yu’s allocation of textual space to DV remains broadly proportional to the overall expansion of the translation. Close analysis reveals a more complex pattern: both translations alternately foreground, mitigate, or redistribute perpetrator agency and the force of violence across different episodes. Paratextual analysis further shows that the two editions contextualise Liza’s tragedy differently: TT1 foregrounds family deprivation, romantic desire, and fate, whereas TT2 places greater emphasis on moral categorisation, class, and socio-economic environment. These findings demonstrate that the reframing of gendered violence cannot be reduced to a simple opposition between amplification and mitigation but operates unevenly across textual strategies, episodes, and paratextual contexts. The study highlights the value of combining corpus-assisted, close textual, and paratextual analysis for examining how translation mediates representations of domestic violence, gender ideology, agency, and responsibility across cultures.

title: Demystifying the nexus between spiritual leadership, innovative work behavior and sustainable economic performance
abstract: The quest for sustainability has garnered immense attention in recent years, driven by the relentless need to embrace sustainable practices and ensure the enduring resilience and longevity of healthcare services. Existing literature has recognized leadership as a potential driver for fostering sustainable performance. However, there has been a dearth of research on the application of higher-level leadership paradigms, such as spirituality, in rejuvenating sustainable performance within organizations. One hundred ninety-five valid responses were collected from healthcare professionals across South India using a simple random sampling technique. The data were analyzed using multiple regression and mediation analysis to investigate the direct and indirect effects within the proposed conceptual framework. The findings indicate that spiritual leadership exerts a significant positive influence on sustainable economic performance. Furthermore, the results ratify the role of spiritual leadership in fostering sustainable economic performance, mediated by innovative work behavior. This maiden investigation enriches the literature on healthcare management by fostering novel work practices through the integration of spiritual leadership, innovative work behavior, and sustainable economic performance.

title: Cognitive mechanisms of AI agent behavioral intention among design graduate students: an integrated TAM–TTF perspective
abstract: AI agents are reshaping educational systems and transforming teaching and learning in design disciplines. However, the psychological mechanisms underlying AI-agent use among design graduate students remain underexplored, as does the interaction between design-specific tasks and AI agents. To address this gap, this study integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Task–Technology Fit (TTF) theory to explain how technological cognition and task-fit perceptions jointly shape behavioral intention to use AI agents. Because conventional structural modeling mainly captures hypothesized linear relationships, MLP-ANN was added to assess nonlinear patterns and predictor importance. Using 405 valid questionnaire responses, the model was tested through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), a Multilayer Perceptron Artificial Neural Network (MLP-ANN), and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA). PLS-SEM supported nine of ten hypotheses. Self-efficacy positively affected perceived usefulness (β = 0.458, p < 0.001) and perceived ease of use (β = 0.394, p < 0.001). Perceived enjoyment enhanced perceived ease of use (β = 0.220, p < 0.001), but its effect on perceived usefulness was negative and nonsignificant (β = −0.033, p = 0.483). Perceived usefulness (β = 0.376, p < 0.001), perceived ease of use (β = 0.185, p < 0.001), and task–technology fit (β = 0.224, p < 0.001) positively influenced attitude. Task characteristics (β = 0.322, p < 0.001) and technology characteristics (β = 0.266, p < 0.001) positively affected task–technology fit, while attitude promoted behavioral intention (β = 0.388, p < 0.001). Ten-fold cross-validated MLP-ANN models produced mean RMSE values of 0.3263–0.4203 across training and testing and broadly confirmed the PLS-SEM predictor-importance patterns. NCA further identified self-efficacy (d = 0.125, p = 0.015) and attitude (d = 0.132, p < 0.001) as necessary conditions for perceived usefulness and behavioral intention, respectively. This study extends the integrated TAM–TTF framework to design education and offers theoretical and practical implications for effective AI-agent use in design disciplines.

title: Optimizing e-referral reward programs in the presence of uncertain conversion rate
abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of e-referral reward programs by enterprises, existing research provides limited insights into their optimal design, particularly in the context of recommendation uncertainty. This study develops a unified framework to investigate the design of optimal referral programs among three strategies: the no-referral-consideration strategy, the no-reward-offering strategy, and the referral reward strategy. Specifically, we consider conversion rate uncertainty as the driving mechanism of strategic consumer behavior. Counter-intuitively, we find that the no-referral-consideration strategy is not always detrimental to firms. When consumers’ psychological cost for failed recommendations is relatively high, the no-referral-consideration strategy outperforms the no-reward-offering strategy. Only when the discount factor of perceived value is high, and the psychological cost is moderate, does the e-referral reward strategy emerge as the optimal strategy. Overall, this study highlights the effect of conversion rate uncertainty on consumer behavior and provides valuable guidance for firms in designing optimal referral programs.

title: Geocentric spatial concepts in Mandarin: comparing empirical evidence with theoretical models
abstract: The goal of this paper is to analyse geocentric spatial concepts in Mandarin, i.e. spatial relations defined via reference to salient locations (“anchors”) in the geographic environment. We connect this analysis to the SocioTopographic Model, which introduces a complex taxonomy of spatial relation types. We show that Mandarin expresses cross-linguistically well-documented geocentric relations (e.g. Béi ‘North’, Dōng ‘East’), but also language-specific concepts (e.g. yán-hǎi lit. ‘around-sea’ for ‘seaside’). We then show that in previous works on these relations, their role in Mandarin has received little analysis. To ameliorate this situation, we provide a mixed-methods study. First, we verified the existence of possible words expressing geocentric relations via a dictionary analysis of compound forms potentially expressing these relations. Second, we retrieved sentences including these compound forms to verify their grammatical (i.e. morpho-syntactic) properties and distribution, and their use in conversation. Third, we administered an exploratory online questionnaire to native speakers (N = 77; average age = 35.0 years) to assess whether these compound forms can introduce unique anchors in context. The central findings of our mixed-methods study are as follows. First, compound forms can express a wide array of geocentric relations, though the number of forms potentially expressing spatial relations is considerably larger (116/418). Second, compound forms expressing geocentric relations can occur in any sentential position, and regularly introduce reference to anchors. Third, the responses from the questionnaire provided preliminary support for compound forms referring to unique anchors in context. We discuss how these findings are consistent with the language-general predictions of the SocioTopographic Model. We also highlight the language-specific nature of our findings, and how these findings individuate theoretical gaps in the model. We conclude the paper by sketching possible avenues of future research on geocentric spatial concepts, and possible contributions of our study to the SocioTopographic Model.

title: Impact of artificial intelligence on the task structure of tourism practitioners
abstract: Although artificial intelligence (AI) is extensively applied in tourism, empirical insights into its nuanced impacts on specific work tasks are still emerging. Utilizing Chinese General Social Survey data (2010–2023), this paper examines how AI is associated with different task types and explores the underlying mechanisms. Results suggest that AI is associated with an emerging shift in the occupational composition among tourism practitioners, leaning toward greater routine cognitive task intensity and lower non-routine cognitive task intensity—primarily in hospitality and travel agencies—while no significant effects are observed on manual tasks. Mediation analyses indicate that reduced job autonomy represents a potential pathway associated with this adjustment. Further analysis shows that this constraint on job autonomy exhibits significant nonlinear and dynamic characteristics: it strengthens after AI penetration crosses a specific threshold and demonstrates a staged temporal evolution—transitioning from early assistance to subsequent constraint before stabilizing. We attempt to conceptualize this phenomenon as the “re-routinization” of tourism employment, whereby AI is associated with greater routine cognitive task intensity and lower non-routine cognitive task intensity, with reduced job autonomy emerging as a potential partial pathway.

title: Queer masculinities with pain and love: embodied experiences from Black Myth: Wukong to its danmei fanfiction
abstract: Previous scholarship has established that videogames and fan communities serve as sites where queer representations are reproduced, altered, and challenged. Employing critical discourse analysis, this article examines the embodied experience of masculinity in the Chinese role-playing game Black Myth: Wukong , and how the game’s fanfiction reconfigures this experience. While the game compels players to enact a complex form of Chinese hegemonic masculinity characterized by implicit homosexuality and the downplaying of pain, fanfiction reconceptualizes this ideal. This new form is defined by a vulnerable yet powerful body that embraces pain, and a mind that integrates explicit homosexuality, intellectual prowess, and a sexuality rooted in intense, equal, and reciprocal love. This article therefore contributes to game studies, fan studies, and queer studies by examining the embodied experiences of masculinity in both the game and its fanfiction.

title: Feminism and emotional persuasion in social media beauty advertising: a multimodal critical genre analysis of Douyin
abstract: Beauty influencer advertising (BIA) has emerged as a distinctive form of digital advertising and an increasingly valuable strategy for beauty brand promotion. This study focuses on a highly commercialised subset of BIA produced by mega beauty influencers on Douyin. On this platform, promotional messages in such elite influencer advertising are woven into everyday sharing, tutorial performance, and low-pressure participation, while the aesthetic practices promoted in this content may intensify appearance anxiety among young Chinese women. Drawing on Bhatia’s framework of advertising rhetorical structure and Kress and van Leeuwen’s visual grammar, this study examines 25 beauty advertising videos posted by five mega beauty influencers on Douyin. It explores how this form of mega-influencer BIA is rhetorically organised, how multimodal resources are deployed to realise persuasion, and what ideological logic underpins this advertising discourse. Findings show that, within this elite sample, BIA blurs the commercial boundaries of advertising through more interactive, entertaining, and de-commercialised rhetorical strategies. Influencers also enact multiple discursive identities across rhetorical moves through the strategic use of visual semiotic resources, thereby producing different forms of emotional alignment with audiences. Finally, this form of Douyin BIA reconstructs a responsibilised, relationalised, and knowledge-based mechanism of body governance in the Chinese context, through which dominant aesthetic norms are further legitimised. Overall, this study sheds light on the discursive practices of highly commercialised mega-influencer BIA as a platformised advertising genre and contributes to understanding multimodal communication and postfeminist body governance in China.

title: Strengthening global health security through prioritizing interdependent logistics and supply network indicators
abstract: Abstract This study analyzes the interdependencies among logistics and supply network indicators from the Global Health Security (GHS) index to understand their combined impact on GHS preparedness. The study contributes to the literature by identifying both the most predictive indicators of GHS performance and the indicators with the greatest potential to improve preparedness outcomes through a probabilistic network modeling approach. Using a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) model, twelve logistics and supply network indicators relevant to GHS are examined to determine their influence, ranking, and interactions. Sensitivity and mutual value of information analyses are applied to assess the relative importance and predictive strength of each indicator. The findings reveal strong interconnections, particularly involving laboratory cooperation and coordination, and transportation security. Sensitivity results indicate that improving laboratory cooperation and coordination substantially enhances health security, resulting in the largest increase in the percentage of countries classified within the high-performance tier of the GHS Index (61 percentage points) when this indicator transitions from low to high performance. Furthermore, laboratory capacity and routine health care and laboratory system supply are identified as the most informative predictors of the GHS index. These findings provide critical insights for guiding investments, refining preparedness strategies, and strengthening the overall resilience of global health systems.

title: On different roads: reconciling Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities with healthcare provision in the UK
abstract: Addressing ongoing health disparities between the UK’s Gypsy, Roma, and Traveller (GRT) communities and the general population is a critical concern for healthcare services. These groups face poorer health outcomes and significant barriers to access, driven by historical discrimination and structural inequalities. In this Comment, we argue that current policy and practice often misinterpret GRT health attitudes and practices as ‘deprivations’ rather than adaptive cultural responses. We propose the application of cultural evolutionary theory to reframe these behaviors as sophisticated adaptations developed within unique environmental and social contexts. We then outline the utility of agent-based modeling as a methodological tool to explore these cultural dynamics and inform more effective, culturally sensitive healthcare interventions, fostering co-enrichment between communities and services.

title: A study of the impact of climate transition risk on the profitability of commercial banks
abstract: Abstract Climate transition risk has become an increasingly important challenge for commercial banks during the low-carbon transition process. Using carbon dioxide emissions from six carbon-intensive industries and industry-level bank loan data, this study constructs a climate transition risk indicator for Chinese listed commercial banks from 2010 to 2022 and examines its impact on bank profitability. Employing a two-way fixed effects model, heterogeneity analysis, moderating effect tests, and a series of robustness checks, the study finds that climate transition risk significantly reduces bank profitability. The negative effect is more pronounced among state-owned and large commercial banks, while it is relatively weaker for joint-stock banks, regional banks, as well as small and medium-sized banks. Further analysis reveals that bank size and non-performing loan ratios partially mitigate the adverse impact of transition risk on profitability. The findings suggest that banks with high exposure to carbon-intensive industries should strengthen climate-related risk management and gradually optimize their credit structure during the green transition process. The study also provides evidence for regulators to implement differentiated climate finance policies across different types of banks.

title: Beyond self-efficacy: the distal-proximal motivational hierarchy of knowledge transfer in fitness short videos
abstract: Abstract While fitness short videos have become a pivotal medium for health dissemination, the mechanism translating content quality into knowledge transfer remains insufficiently understood. We propose a distal-proximal motivational framework to examine how knowledge expressiveness facilitates transfer through the sequential mediating roles of self-efficacy and outcome expectations. Based on a survey of 337 regular viewers, structural equation modeling reveals a complete mediation mechanism. Findings indicate that knowledge expressiveness enhances transfer effectiveness, yet self-efficacy does not directly predict knowledge transfer. Instead, it functions as a distal precursor that remains inert until converted into proximal outcome expectations. Only when initial confidence is anchored in perceived instrumental value does it drive the persistent learning behavior necessary for technical mastery. These results challenge the assumption that self-efficacy directly facilitates learning in digital media, highlighting that motivation in fitness communication operates through a hierarchical activation process. Practically, creators should prioritize the strategic alignment of instructional clarity with the communication of tangible outcomes to ensure self-belief results in effective knowledge internalization.

title: Dynamic mechanism of digital technology empowering green innovation in manufacturing enterprises
abstract: Although the dual digital and green transformation has become a strategic imperative for manufacturing firms, whether and how digital technology effectively drives green innovation remains contested. This debate largely stems from concerns regarding digital divides and the potential for diminishing returns caused by excessive investment. To address this theoretical gap, this study develops a differential game model to examine the dynamic mechanisms through which digital technology enables green innovation across three distinct stages of the product lifecycle: research and development focused on green knowledge accumulation, manufacturing focused on product greenness, and post-sale operations focused on green service. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate three primary findings. First, digital technology, knowledge accumulation, product greenness, and service quality all exert positive effects on overall green innovation performance, with the marginal effects being stronger in the initial period. Second, green knowledge accumulation plays a dominant role relative to product greenness and green service. Third, the relationship between digital input and green innovation benefits follows an inverted U-shaped trajectory, which is regulated by a critical threshold determined by the ratio of technology sensitivity to application costs. These findings offer theoretical explanations for the digital divide phenomenon in green innovation and provide practical guidance for manufacturing firms seeking to optimize their digital investments and avoid overinvestment traps during sustainability transitions.

title: Screen kiss in China: kissing performance and its social acceptability in Chinese feature films during the “Seventeen Years” period (1949–1966)
abstract: The claim that the “first kiss” on the screen in the People’s Republic of China (P.R.C.) appeared in Romance on Lushan Mountain (1980) needs to be corrected. This study argues that the first kiss on screen in the P.R.C. should be in the film Caravans with Ring, produced by Shanghai Film Studio in 1954. Besides, under the dual influence of traditional Chinese culture and mainstream ideology at that time, the depiction of kissing on screen, while broadening the scope of film expression, exceeded the cultural limits that the era could bear and construct. The portrayal of kissing in the production field, composed of writers, screenwriters, directors, and actors, and the audience field, including political leaders, film critics, media, and the public, created an intriguing arena of contention and perception. This highlighted the tension between artistic rules, subjective intentions, cultural traditions, and ideology, thus leading to a unique social acceptability of kissing performances.

title: Older adults’ intention to use extended reality in China’s Yellow River Basin: an extended Technology Acceptance Model with intergenerational support
abstract: As older adults become an important segment of China’s tourism market and family-based multigenerational travel becomes more prevalent, extended reality (XR)-enabled cultural heritage tourism raises a broader question about older adults’ access to technology-mediated cultural participation. Although XR may enrich cultural heritage tourism, older adults’ engagement with XR may be shaped by digital barriers and varying levels of family-based support. However, limited research has examined older adults’ intention to use XR in tourism through an integrated framework that considers intergenerational support and XR characteristics. Addressing this gap, this study develops an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to examine older adults’ behavioral intention to use XR in the cultural heritage tourism context of China’s Yellow River Basin. A scenario-based survey was conducted in this pre-adoption context. Using a standardized written-and-video scenario depicting XR applications in cultural heritage tourism, data were collected from 413 Chinese adults aged 60 and above and analyzed using SPSS 25 and partial least squares structural equation modeling in SmartPLS 4, with a supplementary confirmatory factor analysis conducted in AMOS 23. The results show that perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and anticipated satisfaction are directly associated with behavioral intention, with anticipated satisfaction showing the strongest direct association. Intergenerational support and XR characteristics are indirectly associated with behavioral intention through distinct cognitive and evaluative pathways. By clarifying these pathways, this study extends TAM and contributes to discussions of ageing, family-mediated digital inclusion, and potential inequalities in access to technology-mediated cultural heritage experiences.

title: Can integrated legal and administrative governance reduce corporate carbon emissions?
abstract: Traditional environmental governance often relies on a single regulatory form, necessitating the exploration of more comprehensive integrated governance models. Utilizing the pilot program of procuratorial public interest litigation in China as a quasi-natural experiment, this study investigates the impact of integrated legal and administrative governance on corporate carbon emissions and the underlying mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that this governance model significantly reduces corporate carbon emissions. Mechanism tests reveal that the policy functions by strengthening institutional constraints, incentivizing green investments, mobilizing public environmental supervision, and heightening corporate litigation risks. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that factors such as executives’ environmental experience, industry pollution attributes, regional rule of law levels, and market competition exert differential effects on the policy’s impact. Additionally, our analysis reveals that the policy further enhances firms’ overall ESG performance. These findings confirm that integrating judicial oversight with administrative supervision is a viable pathway for achieving carbon neutrality, offering valuable insights for constructing a multi-stakeholder environmental governance system.

title: Whose Anthropocene? Disciplinary shifts and global asymmetries in a changing knowledge system
abstract: The term “Anthropocene” captures humanity’s profound impact on Earth’s geology and ecosystems, and it has become central to understanding the relationship between human societies and the Earth system. This study investigates the evolution of Anthropocene research over the period 2001–2024, covering more than two decades since Paul Crutzen first introduced the concept. Using a multi-method computational framework integrating bibliometric indicators, network analysis, and spatial mapping, we analyzed 4575 articles indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection. Our analysis reveals not merely a quantitative growth of the field, but also a profound structural reorganization of its intellectual landscape. Early Anthropocene research was anchored in geology and Earth system science, with climate change and stratigraphic debates occupying central positions. Over time, however, keyword co-occurrence networks and disciplinary correlations indicate a shift toward a more heterogeneous structure. While institutions in the Global North dominate publication output, comparative network analysis reveals systematic differences in problem framing between developed and developing countries. We argue that the Anthropocene has evolved into a heterogeneous knowledge system characterized by both disciplinary divergence and novel forms of cross-disciplinary integration, shaped by persistent geopolitical asymmetries. In this context, the recent rejection of the Anthropocene as a formally defined geological epoch should be understood not as a setback, but rather as an opening for more reflexive and inclusive forms of knowledge production.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and topological connectivity of the global platinum group metals trade network: a multiscale network perspective
abstract: Platinum group metals (PGMs) are critical raw materials for diverse industries, including automotive, chemical, electronics, and hydrogen energy sectors. Research on the spatiotemporal evolution of global PGMs trade networks is essential for understanding global supply-demand dynamics and supply chain systems. This study constructs a comprehensive long-term dataset of the global PGMs trade networks and employs advanced network analysis methods to characterize their spatiotemporal evolution and topological structures. The findings include: (1) Since 2001, both the trade value and volume of global PGMs have exhibited fluctuating growth trends, notably responsive to international events such as financial crises and the COVID-19 pandemic. (2) The overall structure of the global PGMs trade network has remained stable, with continual growth in trade scale and network density, showing clear hierarchical and spatial imbalances. This structure features South Africa and Russia at its core, surrounded by major trade groups in Europe-America and Asia. (3) At the macro level, the connectivity of the global PGMs trade network has significantly improved, reflected in fluctuating trends in network clustering and transmission efficiency. At the meso level, the backbone structures have continuously expanded, demonstrating a multi-centralized nature. At the micro level, South Africa and Russia emerge as influential global PGMs exporters, while the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Italy, Japan, and others maintain core positions. China is progressively becoming a pivotal trade hub in Asia and globally. Building on these findings, this paper proposes policy recommendations to enhance international trade cooperation in PGMs and ensure supply security.

title: Caught in cultural lag: exploring health anxiety of China’s first-generation modern older adults
abstract: Health anxiety among older adults has attracted growing attention globally as the ageing population increases. In previous studies, health anxiety has largely been understood as a biomedical and psychological concern. This study conceptualizes health anxiety as a culturally mediated experience, embedded in socially shared ideals of what it means to age “well,” remain valuable, and feel morally adequate in later life. From September 2022 to December 2023, the authors conducted life story interviews with 28 first-generation modern older adults in China who were socialized under collectivist moral frameworks yet have aged amid rapid modernization. These findings suggest a process in which participants initially seek to align themselves with dominant ideals of progress, autonomy, and successful ageing, but subsequently come to experience health anxiety when encountering bodily uncertainty, fragmented care arrangements, and weakening intergenerational and community support. Through this socialized shift, these external constraints and vulnerabilities are interpreted through moral expectations and internalized as personal inadequacies. By foregrounding these cultural dynamics, the study challenges individualistic accounts of health anxiety and demonstrates how contemporary norms and policy discourses of ageing escalate emotional distress in later life.

title: Sectoral analysis of female employment and economic growth: evidence from OIC countries
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between sectoral female employment and economic growth in 56 member countries of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) from 1998 to 2024. Utilizing panel data and various econometric models, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), 2SLS, fixed effects, and Generalized Method of Moments (GMM), the research suggests that, once endogeneity and dynamics are controlled for, female employment in industry is positively and significantly associated with GDP growth, while female employment in agriculture, services, and self‑employment become statistically insignificant. Lagged GDP and foreign direct investment are the most consistent drivers of growth. The findings highlight the need for targeted policies to address sector‑specific challenges, enhance productivity, and support female employment in alignment with cultural and religious norms to optimize economic development in OIC countries. This study is limited by its reliance on panel data, which may not fully capture country‑specific nuances and cultural factors affecting female employment and economic growth in OIC countries. For academia, the findings challenge aggregate‑level analyses by demonstrating that sectoral decomposition (industry vs. agriculture/services) fundamentally alters conclusions about female employment and growth, and that dynamic GMM with collapsed instruments is essential to avoid instrument proliferation. For practice, policymakers in OIC countries should prioritize industrial formalisation and export‑oriented FDI for female workers, while improving productivity in agriculture and services through skills training and access to credit, rather than relying on sectoral reallocation alone.

title: Social networking amid China’s Double Reduction Policy among Chinese private tutoring entrepreneurs: a sensemaking perspective
abstract: This article critically investigates the networking practices, known as guanxi in China, employed by private tutoring entrepreneurs amid China’s Double Reduction Policy that strictly regulates the private tutoring industry. Drawing from a 16-month narrative study in Chongqing municipality, this article examines the role of sensemaking in the initiation, maintenance, and termination/mutation of guanxi networks among private tutoring entrepreneurs, a process shaped by dynamic interactions embedded in cultural, institutional, and structural contexts. The findings reveal previously under-researched mechanisms within the guanxi networking process, highlighting its multifaceted and evolving nature. Theoretically, we contribute to guanxi scholarship by reframing it as a dynamic interpretive process rather than a static resource and extend sensemaking theory beyond intra-organizational to multiple inclusions. Practically, our distinction between legitimate reciprocity, ethically ambiguous favors, and regulatory evasion implies that policy efforts should target specific misconduct rather than guanxi as such.

title: When circular economy barriers stir emotions: how SME leaders respond
abstract: Emotions shape how small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) leaders respond to barriers in the transition to a circular economy (CE); however, the emotional dimension of CE leadership remains under-explored. To understand how SME leaders engaged in CE appraise and cope with barriers that hinder the adoption of circular business models, this study explores emotions in organisational behaviour. A qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological approach is adopted, drawing on 17 in-depth semi-structured interviews with Spanish SME leaders. The interview data are analysed via interpretative phenomenological analysis to capture the links between leaders’ cognitive appraisals, emotions and subsequent coping actions when they face salient CE-related barriers. The findings show that leaders experience emotions such as anger, frustration, fear, powerlessness, sorrow and vicarious embarrassment. These emotions are associated with three response patterns: inspiration, deliberation, and no coping; the first two are active coping strategies, whereas the latter reflects withdrawal or inaction. Inspiration reflects an approach-oriented strategy in which negative emotions are channelled into purpose-driven and creative efforts to overcome barriers. Deliberation involves a reflective pause and calculated decision-making in response to emotionally charged situations. No coping captures withdrawal or inaction, particularly when emotions such as sorrow and vicarious embarrassment are triggered. By clarifying how specific emotional appraisals shape leaders’ capacity to engage with CE barriers, this study advances the understanding of CE leadership at the micro level. The findings also offer practical implications for policy design, support mechanisms, and training and coaching programmes aimed at helping SME leaders recognise, regulate, and more effectively channel emotions during the circular transition.

title: Land degradation compromise drought risk financing across Africa, impacting pastoralist welfare
abstract: Drought and land degradation threaten pastoral livelihoods in Africa, particularly in the Horn of Africa (HoA), where livestock losses can undermine household resilience, local economies, and the effectiveness of climate-risk financing mechanisms. Index-Based Livestock Insurance (IBLI) offers an important means of reducing pastoral vulnerability by linking indemnity payouts to satellite-derived forage indices. However, its effectiveness depends on the assumption that vegetation-rainfall relationships and historical ecological baselines remain sufficiently stable over time. Increasing climate variability, land degradation, and other human-induced changes may violate these assumptions, creating basis risk and misaligned payouts for both pastoralists and insurers. We examine the implications of these changing environmental conditions for drought risk management and IBLI performance by integrating about 20 years of satellite-derived vegetation Indices (VIs) and precipitation data with linear and nonlinear modeling and Residual Trend (RESTREND) analysis. Across Africa, ~25% of the land area exhibits significant long-term changes in vegetation productivity, including 19% greening and 6% browning. Our analysis indicates that only 7% of these changes are primarily associated with rainfall variability, whereas 18% are linked to non-climatic factors such as agricultural expansion, bush encroachment, and invasives. These findings demonstrate that vegetation dynamics increasingly reflect interacting climatic, ecological, and anthropogenic processes, rather than rainfall variability alone. Consequently, drought indices based on historical vegetation-precipitation relationships may not adequately represent contemporary forage conditions or pastoral risk, with implications for the accuracy, equity, and financial sustainability of climate-risk financing systems. In IBLI operational regions within the HoA, ~20% of IBLI units (n = 124) exhibit significant changes in vegetation productivity that influence payout trends, highlighting the potential for changing ecological baselines to alter insurance performance and the correspondence between measured index risk and pastoralists’ realized exposure. The results suggest that environmental change can affect not only drought monitoring but also the distribution and reliability of climate-risk protection available to pastoral households. We therefore argue that robust drought-risk management in pastoral systems requires insurance and adaptation frameworks that account for land use/cover changes, shifting climatic baselines and degradation-sensitive vegetation dynamics, incorporate ground-based validation, and periodically reassess index-risk relationships. By linking long-term environmental change to insurance performance and pastoral vulnerability, this framework advances understanding of how ecological change can reshape risk measurement, climate-risk financing, and adaptation decision-making in drought-prone pastoral systems.

title: Multiscale spillovers and portfolio management in major assets: insights from a Jump, Oscillation and Trend decomposition
abstract: This study develops an integrated multi-scale framework for structurally decomposing major financial asset prices, including stocks, bonds, currencies, commodities, and precious metals, into trend, oscillation, and jump components. This decomposition provides the basis for examining cross-market spillovers and evaluating dynamic portfolio allocation strategies. Empirical results reveal regime-dependent spillover mechanisms: (1) Trend-based spillovers demonstrate high persistence and structural stability, closely corresponding to the Merrill Lynch Investment Clock, and support the macro-fundamental transmission channel. (2) Oscillation components capture medium-term behavioral sentiment and liquidity cycles, providing potential early-warning signals during market transitions. (3) Jump components dominate during systemic shocks, with equities and precious metals acting as primary transmitters of instantaneous contagion. Portfolios that use these component-specific spillover dynamics exhibit stronger benchmark performance than traditional strategies in the pre-transaction-cost setting, particularly in trend- or jump-dominated regimes. By integrating structural decomposition with dynamic asset allocation analysis, this study contributes to the understanding of heterogeneous spillover mechanisms and provides a structured reference for adaptive, multi-layered portfolio strategies.

title: Ethical-efficiency balance of AI in international Chinese teacher development
Sacred waters, broken systems: community experiences of traditional water body renovations in Braj, India
abstract: Abstract Traditional Knowledge Systems and community participation have historically sustained water management practices across the Indian subcontinent for centuries. Communities developed sophisticated methods rooted in cultural practices while addressing practical requirements. However, colonial interventions and post-independence policies have systematically marginalised local knowledge and community participation in water management decisions. Replacing them with centralised technocratic approaches that prioritise technical efficiency over cultural continuity. In the Braj region of India, Traditional Water Bodies (Kunds) serve as both cultural anchors and ecological resources, embodying practical knowledge and spiritual meaning within sacred geography. Today, many of these Kunds are facing degradation due to pollution, encroachment, and state-led renovation interventions. That often destroys their essential socio-ecological qualities. This research investigates how communities remember and value traditional water management systems, navigate tensions between religious significance and physical degradation of transformed water bodies, and reveal unintended consequences of development interventions in culturally significant water systems. This study involves field observation, semi-structured interviews, and thematic analysis across the Braj region. This research documents the lived experiences of communities whose traditional water management systems have been altered by state-led development interventions. Findings reveal a fundamental contradiction between official narratives celebrating renovation success and communities' experiences of environmental and cultural degradation. The water that once embodied purity and reverence has become brackish and undrinkable due to deep boring accessing saline aquifers, yet communities continue performing ritual practices requiring direct water contact. Community memories preserve sophisticated ecological knowledge about natural water purification and adaptive management, but contemporary interventions prioritise standardised technical solutions while systematically excluding local knowledge from decision-making processes. This research contributes to understanding how high modernist development projects encounter and transform complex local systems, revealing gaps between development aspirations and everyday experiences of environmental change.

title: Investigation of restaurant customers’ behavioral intentions with goal-directed behavior theory
abstract: Behavioral intentions are critical determinants of customer loyalty and competitive advantage in the highly competitive restaurant sector. Understanding these intentions requires an integrated view of psychological, emotional, and cognitive processes, combining motivational theory with memory-related mechanisms in gastronomic decision-making. Existing studies often overlook the dynamic interplay between attitudes, social influences, anticipated emotions, perceived control, past experiences, and cognitive recall in shaping restaurant choices. This three-wave longitudinal study applies the Model of Goal-Directed Behavior (MGB) to a sample of 386 restaurant customers in Istanbul, Türkiye, incorporating memory as a novel moderating variable to illuminate cognitive dimensions of consumer choice. Structural Equation Modeling results showed positive associations of perceived behavioral control, positive anticipated emotions, attitudes, subjective norms, and frequency of past behavior with desire. Desire and frequency of past behavior were positively associated with behavioral intentions, whereas the direct association between perceived behavioral control and intentions was not statistically significant. Memory moderation received differing levels of support across the examined pathways: the interaction involving past behavior was positive and statistically significant, whereas evidence for the desire intention interaction was borderline. The interaction involving perceived behavioral control was not statistically significant. Negative anticipated emotions were not significantly associated with desire in this sample. These findings provide support for selected MGB relationships among the surveyed restaurant customers and suggest that self-reported memory vividness and accessibility warrant further investigation in relation to behavioral intentions. Their causal and practical implications require additional evidence.

title: Assessing life skills education in online learning environments through a case study in China
abstract: This study presents the first application and psychometric validation of a Capability Approach-based life skills scale in a Chinese open-university context, revealing distinct challenges in the implementation of these skills in practice. An attempted census invited all eligible instructors across disciplines at an open university in China, and 187 completed an online survey. Analyses comprised Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), association rule learning (Apriori), and Friedman tests with Nemenyi post hoc comparisons. CFA supported a 13-dimension structure. Ranking analyses indicated stronger implementation for practical reason, body integrity, affiliation, emotions, and digital accessibility/usability, and weaker implementation for soft skills integration, environmental awareness, body health, and creativity. Association rules revealed robust links between digital skill integration, health, and perceived control with cybersecurity, and between affiliation, environmental awareness, perceived control, and positive emotions. The findings extend validity beyond European settings, identify capability areas requiring targeted improvement, and offer actionable guidance for program design in comparable open university contexts.

title: Digital policies and environmental regulations: does policy synergy achieve greater urban ecological resilience?
How stars’ persona reformulations shape audience preferences: insights from ERP evidence
Informality in business from a gender perspective: a literature review
Navigating external conflicts, technological innovations, and financial risks for sustainable development: evidence from the EKC and ecological footprints in the next eleven
abstract: Abstract To achieve sustainable development, ongoing research needs further investigations in detail for stronger environmental protection. For this purpose, several studies have investigated the factors of ecological footprints (EF), but very few of them have taken external and internal conflicts with technological innovations in the context of EKC. Against this backdrop, this study applies some advanced techniques like wavelet plots and augmented mean group (AMG) methods over the panel data of 1984-2022 for the Next Eleven nations. The results find strong linkages among the variables. Moreover, reducing external conflicts can stimulate environmental quality. The results validate that the EKC, technological innovations, and financial risk are environmentally friendly. GDP is contributing to environmental degradation, while the population shows a mixed impact on environmental sustainability. The wavelet plots also show that there is a direct linkage between financial risk and ecological footprints.
